body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_1. nakṣatrakalpaḥ)
(AVParis_0,0.0) śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ || oṃ namo 'tharvātmane vāmadevāya śivāya || śrīsarasvatyai namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 1. <s>Nakṣatrakalpa</s>) Salutation to Śrī <s>Gaṇeśa</s>! Oṃ, salutation to <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the <s>Ātman</s> of the <s>Atharvan</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>! Salutation to Śrī <s>Sarasvatī</s>!

body.text: (AVParis_1,1.1) atha nakṣatrakalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now we shall expound the <s>Nakṣatrakalpa</s> (ritual procedure of the lunar mansions).

body.text: (AVParis_1,1.2) kṛttikā rohiṇī mṛgaśira ārdrā punarvasū puṣyāśleṣā maghā(ḥ) phālgunī phalgunyau hasta(ś) citrā svāti(r) viśākhe anurādhā jyeṣṭhā mūla(m) pūrvāṣāḍhā uttarāṣāḍābhijic chravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhā śatabhiṣaḥ pūrvaproṣṭhapadottaraproṣṭhapadau revaty aśvayujau bharaṇyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Phālgunī</s>, the two <s>Phalgunī</s>s, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Viśākhe</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, <s>Pūrva Proṣṭhapadā</s>, <s>Uttara Proṣṭhapadā</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, the two <s>Aśvayuj</s>s, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_1,2.1) ṣaṭ kṛttikā ekā rohiṇī tisro mṛgaśira ekārdrā dve punarvasū ekaḥ puṣyaḥ ṣaḍ āśleṣāḥ ṣaṇ maghāḥ catasraḥ phalgunyaḥ pañca hasta ekā citrā ekā svātir dve viśākhe catasro 'nurādhā ekā jyeṣṭhā sapta mūlam aṣṭāv aṣāḍhā eko 'bhijit tisraḥ śravaṇaḥ pañca śraviṣṭhā ekā śatabhiṣā catasraḥ proṣṭhapadau ekā revatī dve aśvayujau tisro bharaṇyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Six are in <s>Kṛttikā</s>, one in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, three in <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, one in <s>Ārdrā</s>, two in <s>Punarvasu</s>, one in <s>Puṣya</s>, six in <s>Āśleṣā</s>, six in <s>Maghā</s>, four in <s>Phalgunī</s>, five in <s>Hasta</s>, one in <s>Citrā</s>, one in <s>Svāti</s>, two in <s>Viśākhe</s>, four in <s>Anurādhā</s>, one in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, seven in <s>Mūla</s>, eight in <s>Aṣāḍhā</s>, one in <s>Abhijit</s>, three in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, five in <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, one in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, four in the <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, one in <s>Revatī</s>, two in <s>Aśvayuj</s>, three in <s>Bharaṇī</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,2.2) iti saṃkhyāparimitaṃ brahma ||
body.translated_text: Thus is the <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) delimited by number.

body.text: (AVParis_1,3.1) āgniveśyaḥ kṛttikā rohiṇy ānurohiṇī śvetāyinaṃ mṛgaśira ārdrā bārhadgavī vātsyāyanau punarvasū bhāradvājaḥ puṣyo jātūkarṇyo 'śleṣā vaiyāghrapadyo maghā(ḥ) pārāśaryau pūrve phālguṇyāv aupaśivyā uttare māṇḍavyāyano hastaś citrā gautamī kauṇḍinyāyanaḥ svātiḥ kāpile viśākhe maitreyy anurādhā kauśikī jyeṣṭhā kautsaṃ mūlaṃ hāritayajñī pūrvāṣāḍhā kāśyapy uttarā śaunako 'bhijid ātreyaḥ śravaṇo gārgyaḥ śraviṣṭhā dākṣāyaṇī śatabhiṣag vātsyāyanyau pūrve proṣṭhapade āgastyāv uttare śāṅkhāyanī revatī kātyāyan(y)āv aśvayujau mātṛbhyo bharaṇyaḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapa ādityaś candramā brahmāṇo nakṣatreṣu ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Āgniveśya</s> [lineage belongs to] <s>Kṛttikā</s>; <s>Rohiṇī</s> [belongs to] <s>Ānurohiṇī</s>, <s>Śvetāyin</s>; <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> [to] <s>Ārdrā</s>; <s>Bārhadgavī</s> [and] the <s>Vātsyāyana</s>s [to] <s>Punarvasu</s>; <s>Bhāradvāja</s> [to] <s>Puṣya</s>; <s>Jātūkarṇya</s> [to] <s>Āśleṣā</s>; the <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>s [to] <s>Maghā</s>; the two <s>Pārāśarya</s>s [to] the former <s>Phālgunī</s>s; <s>Aupaśivyā</s> [to] the latter; <s>Māṇḍavyāyana</s> [to] <s>Hasta</s>; <s>Citrā</s> [to] <s>Gautamī</s>; <s>Kauṇḍinyāyana</s> [to] <s>Svāti</s>; <s>Kāpila</s> [to] <s>Viśākhe</s>; <s>Maitreya</s> [to] <s>Anurādhā</s>; <s>Kauśikī</s> [to] <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>; <s>Kautsa</s> [to] <s>Mūla</s>; <s>Hāritayajñī</s> [to] <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>; <s>Kāśyapa</s> [to] <s>Uttarā</s>; <s>Śaunaka</s> [to] <s>Abhijit</s>; <s>Ātreya</s> [to] <s>Śravaṇa</s>; <s>Gārgya</s> [to] <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>; <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> [to] <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>; the <s>Vātsyāyana</s>s [to] the former <s>Proṣṭhapada</s>; the <s>Āgastya</s>s [to] the latter; <s>Śāṅkhāyanī</s> [to] <s>Revatī</s>; the <s>Kātyāyana</s>s [to] the <s>Aśvayuj</s>s; the Mothers [to] <s>Bharaṇī</s>s; <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Candramā</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> [preside] over the <s>nakṣatra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.1) kṛttikā agnidevatyā rohiṇyāṃ tu prajāpatiḥ | saumyaṃ mṛgaśiraṃ vidyān marutaś cātra daivatam ||
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛttikā</s> has <s>Agni</s> as its deity; in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>; one should know <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> as belonging to <s>Soma</s>, and here the <s>Marut</s>s are the deity.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.2) rudrasyārdrāditeḥ punarvasū puṣye vidyād bṛhaspatim | aśleṣā[[ḥ]] sarpadaivatyā maghāsu pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>'s is <s>Ārdrā</s>; <s>Aditi</s>'s are the <s>Punarvasu</s>s; in <s>Puṣya</s> one should know <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; the <s>Āśleṣā</s>s have serpents as deities; in <s>Maghā</s>, the ancestors (<s>Pitṛ</s>s) are recorded.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.3) bhagas [tu] pūrvayoḥ phalgunyor aryamottarayor api | haste ca savitā daivaṃ citrā tu tvaṣṭṛdaivatā ||
body.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s> [presides over] the former <s>Phalgunī</s>s, <s>Aryaman</s> over the latter also; in <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s> is the deity; and <s>Citrā</s> has <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> as its deity.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.4) svātau tu daivataṃ vāyur indrāgnī tu viśākhayoḥ | anurādhāsu mitro vai jyeṣṭhāyām indramahādevau ||
body.translated_text: In <s>Svāti</s>, the deity is <s>Vāyu</s>; in the <s>Viśākhe</s>s, <s>Indrāgnī</s> (Indra and Agni); in <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Mitra</s> indeed; in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Mahādeva</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.5) ahir budhnyaś ca mūlasya nirṛtiś cātra daivatam | āpaḥ pūrvāsv aṣāḍhāsu viśve devās tathottare ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> (the Serpent of the Deep) and <s>Nirṛti</s> are the deities of <s>Mūla</s>; the Waters [preside over] the former <s>Aṣāḍhā</s>s; the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) over the latter.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.6) abhijid brahmadevatyaḥ śravaṇe viṣṇur ucyate | śraviṣṭhā vasudevatyā śatabhiṣag varuṇendrayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Abhijit</s> has <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity; in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is declared; <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> has the <s>Vasu</s>s as deities; <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> [belongs to] <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Indra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.7) aja ekapād diśaś ca ādityaś ca tathottare | revatī pūṣadaivatyā aśvinyām aśvinau smṛtau ||
body.translated_text: <s>Aja Ekapād</s> (the One-footed Goat) and the directions, and <s>Āditya</s> over the latter; <s>Revatī</s> has <s>Pūṣan</s> as its deity; in <s>Aśvinī</s>, the <s>Aśvin</s>s are recorded.

body.text: (AVParis_1,4.8) bharaṇyo yamadevatyā devatāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bharaṇī</s>s have <s>Yama</s> as their deity — thus the deities have been proclaimed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.1) kṛttikā maghā mūlaṃ [[ca tathā]] pūrvāṇi dvandvinām | etāni purastādbhāgāny ahaḥpūrvāṇi jānīyāt ||
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, and the former ones of the paired [mansions] — these are the portions that face eastward, to be known as belonging to the day.

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.2) ārdrāṃ śatabhiṣajaṃ svātim āśleṣā bharaṇīr api | naktaṃbhāgāni bruvate jyeṣṭhayā saha brahmāṇam ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>s — these are declared as belonging to the night portion, together with <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Abhijit</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.3) punarvasū viśākhe ca uttarāṇi ca dvandvinām | rātrīm ubhayataḥ pakṣau bhajante yā ca rohiṇī ||
body.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Viśākhe</s>, and the latter ones of the paired [mansions] — these partake of the night on both sides, as also <s>Rohiṇī</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.4) mṛgaśiraḥ puṣyo hastaś citrā tu sahānurādhaiḥ | śravaṇaś ca śraviṣṭhāś ca revaty aśvayujau nava ||
body.translated_text: <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Citrā</s> together with <s>Anurādhā</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, and the <s>Aśvayuj</s>s — nine.

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.5) etāny upariṣṭādbhāgāni rātrīpūrvāṇi jānīyāt | muhūrto 'bhijid ucyate ||
body.translated_text: These are the portions facing upward, to be known as belonging first to the night. <s>Abhijit</s> is called a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment).

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.6) purastādbhāgāny anāgatenopariṣṭādbhāgāny atikrāntena ubhayatobhāgāni vartamāne[[na]] naktaṃbhāgāni samaṃ candreṇa vā ||
body.translated_text: The eastward-facing portions [are reckoned] by [the moon] yet to come; the upward-facing portions by [the moon] that has passed; the portions on both sides by [the moon] in the present; the night portions in conjunction with the moon.

body.text: (AVParis_1,5.7) [[ṣaḍ a]]nāgatayogīni sthitayogīni dvādaśa | navātikrāntayogīni tathā yogaḥ pradṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: Six have conjunction yet to come; twelve have conjunction while stationary; nine have conjunction already passed — thus conjunction is observed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.1) bahūni jātāni graho hinasti kṛttikāsu tiṣṭhann uta dīrgham āyuḥ | ajāvayo mūṣikāś ca vyathante viśo brahmaṇaḥ saha mlecchavāṃś ca ||
body.translated_text: When a planet stands in <s>Kṛttikā</s>, many who are born it afflicts, and also [grants] long life; goats, sheep, and mice suffer, as do the communities of <s>Brahmā</s> together with the <s>Mleccha</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.2) kaliṅgānāṃ vyathate nanu rājā hiraṇyakārāṃś ca nihanti kṛtsnam | ayaskārā lohakārā āhitāgniś ca kṛtsnaṃ niyanti sahāgnitaptaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: The king of the <s>Kaliṅga</s>s surely suffers, and it completely destroys the goldsmiths; the ironsmiths, coppersmiths, and the fire-maintainers are all afflicted along with those heated by fire.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.3) ayo lohaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ hiraṇyamiśraṃ [yac] ca patanti sāram | kāśāḥ kuśā yac ca suvarṇavarṇaṃ yac cāgnivarṇaṃ phalamūlapuṣpam ||
body.translated_text: Iron, copper, silver, gold, and whatever mixed with gold falls as essence; <s>kāśa</s> grasses, <s>kuśa</s> grasses, and whatever is gold-colored, whatever is fire-colored — fruit, root, and flower.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.4) [ye tatra jātāḥ] sarāṃsi śuṣyanty apayanti nadyaḥ prajā vyathante paśavo mṛgāś ca || prajāpater hṛdaye pīḍyamāne sarvaṃ jagad vyathate sapradeśam ||
body.translated_text: Those born there — lakes dry up, rivers recede, people suffer, as do cattle and wild animals. When the heart of <s>Prajāpati</s> is afflicted, the whole world suffers with its regions.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.5) mahābhaumo rājā mariṣyatīti vidyād ekāriṇāṃ chavakām invakāsu | nakṣatrabhāge niyanti yojadhānāḥ tathā hi nūnaṃ triṇavena sṛṣṭam ||
body.translated_text: One should know that the great earth-king will die; [observe] the single-enemy [planets] in <s>Kṛttikā</s>; in the division of the <s>nakṣatra</s>, the allotters of grain proceed — for thus indeed it was created in triads.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.6) tathā sa ninye nidhānadarśanāya tatra teṣāṃ sahākṣemaṃ tasya vidyāt | paritya ye pūrvapadān balena uttiṣṭhanti vīryavanto mṛgānām ||
body.translated_text: Thus he was led to the showing of the treasure; there one should know their welfare together. Those who, having surpassed the first positions by strength, arise — the mighty ones among the animals.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.7) bhagena devy upayanti divyam ārdrābhāge sahino bhavanti | tatra daivān mānuṣyāṃś ca punarvasvor nakṣatra bhāge niniyoja dhānāḥ ||
body.translated_text: By <s>Bhaga</s> the goddesses attain the divine; in the portion of <s>Ārdrā</s> they become powerful; there, by divine and human [conjunction], in the portion of the <s>Punarvasu</s> <s>nakṣatra</s>, the allotters of grain were established.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.8) tathā hi nūnaṃ puṣyo bhāga ekadhā brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā vidur nakṣatraveditāraḥ tathā hi nūnam ||
body.translated_text: For thus indeed, in the single portion of <s>Puṣya</s>, so do the knowers of <s>nakṣatra</s>s know it for the Brahmins — for thus indeed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.9) śatadrayaḥ kaiśikā dakṣiṇārdhā āndhrāś ca yogahāsayā pravṛddhāḥ || aśleṣābhāge sahino bhavanti tatra ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Śatadrayu</s>s, <s>Kaiśika</s>s, the southern half, the <s>Āndhra</s>s, and those who prosper through the conjunction of <s>yoga</s> — in the portion of <s>Āśleṣā</s>, they become powerful therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,6.10) veṇūn pitṝṃs trirujāhur devatām | maghābhāge aṣṭame devasṛṣṭam | saṃyujyante devaprasādanena tatra ||
body.translated_text: They declare the bamboos, the ancestors, the three-fold disease as the deity; in the eighth portion of <s>Maghā</s>, [it is] created by the gods; they are joined by the grace of the gods therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.1) rājñāṃ rākāyām atha madrakaikayā manomāpāyanasahaparisunniyojasahāntau | tunyam atha saptamātraṃ pūrvabhāge navake phalgunīṣu ||
body.translated_text: Of kings, at the full moon, and <s>Madra</s> and <s>Kekaya</s>, together with <s>Manomāpāyana</s> and the companions — [they meet] the end; [there is] injury, then seven measures in the first portion of the ninth, in <s>Phalgunī</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.2) matsyā māgadhāś cedayaś ca śālvā matsyā ubhe phalgunīṣu | saṃyujyante devaprasādanena tatra ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Matsya</s>s, <s>Māgadha</s>s, <s>Cedi</s>s, <s>Śālva</s>s, and <s>Matsya</s>s [belong to] both <s>Phalgunī</s>s; they are joined by the grace of the gods therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.3) pūrvācāryā icchamānāś ca sarve yakṛt kloma saha bhāgena haste | saṃyujyante devaprasādanena tatra ||
body.translated_text: The ancient teachers and all who desire — the liver and lung together with the portion in <s>Hasta</s>; they are joined by the grace of the gods therein.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,7.4) ye pūrvārdhe nijīhate carantaḥ śāntā mṛgā [jantu]paśavo apagāminas te | paśavo bhavatāś ca sarve citrāyā bhāge sahino bhavanti || tatrā-
(AVParis_1,7.5) -cyutakeśaṃ vāhanaṃ jayārthaṃ kumāryo anaḍvān sahate atra ye | vijñāyate devasṛṣṭaṃ purāṇaṃ svātiṃ bhajante tṛṇavaś ca sarve ||
body.translated_text: Those who wander, departed in the first half — peaceful deer, creatures, and cattle that go away — all cattle in the portion of <s>Citrā</s> become powerful. Therein — unshorn hair, a vehicle for victory, young women, an ox endures there; the ancient creation of the gods is known; all the grass-eaters resort to <s>Svāti</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.6) vṛkṣā vṛkṣamūlam ikṣvākavaś ca viśākhāyāṃ yojitāḥ sāṃpadena | tasmin gṛhīte bhayam eva teṣāṃ daivopasṛṣṭe tu balena kāryam || ye tatra jātāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Trees, tree-roots, and the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s are yoked in <s>Viśākhā</s> with prosperity; when that is seized, fear indeed is theirs; when sent by fate, action must be done by force. Those born therein [share the fate].

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.7) ye paścārdhe nijīhate caranta āsavo mṛgā uttarārdhāś cāndhrāḥ | anūrādhāsu magadhavaṅgamatsyāḥ sarve samagrāḥ sahino bhavanti tatra ||
body.translated_text: Those who wander, departed in the latter half — vital spirits, deer, and the southern <s>Āndhra</s>s; in <s>Anurādhā</s>, the <s>Magadha</s>s, <s>Vaṅga</s>s, and <s>Matsya</s>s — all together become powerful therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,7.8) pañcaikadhā janapadā bhavanti sayujaḥkāsaubaladādauṣyadhāḥ | bāhlīkā jyeṣṭhā upayanti bhaktyā tatra ||
body.translated_text: The peoples are fivefold: <s>Sayuja</s>, <s>Kāsaubala</s>, <s>Dāuṣyadha</s>s; the <s>Bāhlīka</s>s resort to <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> with devotion, therein.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,7.9) ikṣvākūṇāṃ nirmathyā mūlam āhuḥ | tathā vidur nakṣatraveditāras tathā hi nūnam
(AVParis_1,7.10) kāmbojāḥ kālamṛṣāś ca krandā ucchuṣmāṇaḥ śvānaś cāvadhūmamarkaṭāś ca pūrvāṣāḍhā upayanti bhaktyā tatra ||
body.translated_text: They declare <s>Mūla</s> to be the root of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s; thus the knowers of <s>nakṣatra</s>s know — for thus indeed. The <s>Kamboja</s>s, <s>Kālamṛṣa</s>s, <s>Kranda</s>s, the furious ones, dogs, and smokeless monkeys — they resort to <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> with devotion, therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,8.1) viśve devāḥ saha pañcālajyeṣṭhā āpaś ca yāḥ pāntu bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyat | uttarāṣāḍhā upayanti bhaktyā tatra ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) together with the foremost of the <s>Pañcāla</s>s, and the Waters that protect what has been and will be — they resort to <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> with devotion, therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,8.2) nārkavindā nārvvidālā nasṛṅgāvau naiṣadhā jantavo mataṅgāḥ | abhijitaṃ hārthavijñāya bhejire tatra ||
body.translated_text: Not of lotus-born, not of split [nature], not of horned [creatures], the <s>Naiṣadha</s>s, creatures, and the <s>Mataṅga</s>s — they resorted to <s>Abhijit</s>, having understood the purpose, therein.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,8.3) pāñcālāḥ śravaṇam upaiti bhaktyā sunvantaś cobhe vidvān bhūtā niniyoja devaḥ || pūrvakartā bhūtabhaviṣyakālas tathā ni nūnam
(AVParis_1,8.4) kurūn śraviṣṭhās tathā śivās tathāhur nakṣatrabhāge niniyoja dhānāḥ || tathā hi nūnam
(AVParis_1,8.5) aṅgādayo janapadā guhāśayā apsu ca ye kṣipanti śatabhiṣaji bheṣajasya bhejire tatra ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Pañcāla</s>s resort to <s>Śravaṇa</s> with devotion, pressing <s>Soma</s>, both [kinds], the wise god established in both past and future — the primeval creator, the time of past and future — for thus indeed. The <s>Kuru</s>s [resort to] <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, likewise auspicious — thus they say, in the portion of the <s>nakṣatra</s>, the allotters of grain were established — for thus indeed. The <s>Aṅga</s>s and other peoples, cave-dwellers, and those who hurl into the waters, in <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, resorted to the remedy therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,8.6) khaḍgā hastino gavayā varāhā ahīnarā kuntayaś cāpi sarve | pūrvau proṣṭhapadā upayanti bhaktyā tatra ||
body.translated_text: Swords, elephants, <s>gavaya</s> (wild oxen), boars, snake-men, and spearmen — all these resort to the former <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s> with devotion, therein.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,8.7) uśīnarā uttarayoḥ proṣṭhapadayor nakṣatrabhāge niniyoja dhānāḥ | tathā hi nūnam
(AVParis_1,8.8) āvṛtāḥ śūdrāḥ saha kāravaś ca dakṣiṇapūrve yūkabhiḥ saha revatīṃ hārthavijñāya bhejire tatra ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Uśīnara</s>s [belong] to the latter <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, in the portion of the <s>nakṣatra</s> the allotters of grain were established — for thus indeed. The enclosed <s>Śūdra</s>s together with artisans, in the south-east, together with lice, resorted to <s>Revatī</s>, having understood the purpose, therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,8.9) acyutakeśaṃ vāhanaṃ ca padārtham ucāvacajanapadā mahāntaḥ | aśvayujau hārthavijñāya bhejire tatra ||
body.translated_text: Unshorn hair, vehicle, and substance — the great and various peoples — they resorted to the <s>Aśvayuj</s>s, having understood the purpose, therein.

body.text: (AVParis_1,8.10) ubhaye kīkaṭāḥ kauśalāś ca rahaś ca[vo] ye ca prasuptāś caranti bharaṇīḥ sahārthavijñāya bhejire tatra teṣāṃ sahākṣayam asya vidyāt ||
body.translated_text: Both the <s>Kīkaṭa</s>s, the <s>Kośala</s>s, and the secretive ones, and those who wander as if asleep, resorted to <s>Bharaṇī</s> having understood the purpose, therein — one should know their complete destruction.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.1) kariṣyamāṇaḥ saṃgrāmaṃ pratirājena kṣatriyaḥ | brāhmaṇaṃ pūrvam anvicched vidvāṃsaṃ śāstravittamam ||
body.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> about to engage in battle with an opposing king should first seek a Brahmin who is learned and most versed in the scriptures.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.2) utpātān yas tu yān vidyād divyāntarikṣapārthivān | taṃ vai lipsitum arhati rājā rāṣṭre jijīviṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text: One who knows the portents — celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial — him indeed the king who desires to live long in his kingdom should seek to obtain.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.3) grahāṇāṃ yaḥ sthitiṃ vidyān nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca sāṃpadam | anabhyaktam upāsīta nakṣatrasamatāṃ ca yat ||
body.translated_text: One who knows the positions of the planets and the prosperity of the <s>nakṣatra</s>s should attend upon one who is not anointed [as king], and [know] what constitutes equality of <s>nakṣatra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.4) āyudhīyān bibhrad rājā kṛttikāsu na riṣyati | tad dhi tejasvi nakṣatraṃ bahulaṃ divi rocate ||
body.translated_text: A king bearing weapons under <s>Kṛttikā</s> is not harmed; for that is a brilliant <s>nakṣatra</s>, shining abundantly in the sky.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.5) atho hi kṛttikā iti nakṣatraṃ bhānumattamam | āgneyam agninakṣatraṃ rājā hy asmin pravardhate ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kṛttikā</s> is the most luminous <s>nakṣatra</s>; it belongs to <s>Agni</s>, it is the fire-<s>nakṣatra</s> — under it a king prospers.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.6) rohiṇyā[ṃ] sārdham āsīta rajjupalyāni kārayet | mṛgaśirasy aśvān bibhṛyāt sāsya senā na riṣyati ||
body.translated_text: One should sit together with <s>Rohiṇī</s> and should have ropes and coverings made; under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> one should maintain horses — then his army is not harmed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.7) saumyaṃ somasya nakṣatraṃ rājā hy asmin pravardhate | ārdrāyāṃ mṛgayāṃ yāyād amitrebhyaś ca hāvayet ||
body.translated_text: It is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Soma</s>, belonging to <s>Soma</s>; under it a king prospers. Under <s>Ārdrā</s> one should go on a hunt and should have offerings made against enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.8) punarvasvābhiyuñjīta puṣyenaitāṃ prayojayet | iṣīkāṃ chedayan rājā aśleṣāsu na riṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Punarvasu</s> one should undertake [action]; under <s>Puṣya</s> one should employ it. A king cutting reeds under <s>Āśleṣā</s> is not harmed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.9) maghābhiḥ sārdham āsīta na yāyād ucchrayaṃ cana | phalgu dvārāṇi kārayet paricārāṃś ca vāhayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,9.9) One should sit together with the <s>Maghā</s> [nakṣatra]; one should not go to any elevated place. Under <s>Phalgunī</s>, one should have doors constructed and conveyances driven.

body.text: (AVParis_1,9.10) toraṇāni ca saṃhanyuḥ phalakāni ca takṣayet | ..... uttarābhyāṃ ca hāvayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,9.10) They should construct arches and have panels carved. [...] And under the two <s>Uttarā</s>s, one should have [offerings] conveyed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.1) hastena citrām ākāṅkṣen nakṣatrasya parigraham | anekadarśī syāc citrāyāṃ purā svāter abhiplavāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.1) With one's hand, one should observe the <s>Citrā</s> [nakṣatra] and the extent of the constellation. One who sees manifold [signs] under <s>Citrā</s>, before the conjunction of <s>Svāti</s> —

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.2) svātau śiśūn niyojayej javārthān rathavāhinaḥ | athāsmin [kanyām] upavāsayet kṣipraṃ sā labhate patim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.2) Under <s>Svāti</s>, one should set children to swift tasks as chariot-drivers. And under this [nakṣatra], if one makes [a maiden] fast, she quickly obtains a husband.

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.3) pradatīn kārayan rājā viśākhāyāṃ na riṣyati | lepayet pradatī rājā anūrādhāsu kṣatriyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.3) A king who has ramparts constructed under <s>Viśākhā</s> is not harmed. The king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, should have the ramparts plastered under <s>Anurādhā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.4) jyeṣṭhāyāṃ hastinaṃ paśyed abhiṣekāṃś ca kārayet | ..... rājaputrāṃś ca yodhayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.4) Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, one should behold an elephant and have consecration ceremonies performed. [...] And one should train princes in combat.

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.5) mūlena parikhāṃ khānayet puraṃ citena yojayet | nairṛtaṃ rājanakṣatraṃ vadhyān anena ghātayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.5) Under <s>Mūla</s>, one should have a moat excavated; under <s>Citra</s>, one should fortify a city. <s>Nairṛta</s> is the royal <s>nakṣatra</s> — under it one should have the condemned executed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.6) trirātraṃ sārdhaṃ dīkṣayitvā āṣāḍhāsu vrataṃ caret | abhijity abhiyuñjīta śravaṇena cikīrṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.6) Having consecrated [the sacrificer] for three nights together, under the <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>s one should observe the vow. Under <s>Abhijit</s>, one should engage [in ritual]; under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, one should undertake [action].

body.text: (AVParis_1,10.7) śraviṣthābhiḥ sṛjed rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.7) Under the <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>s, one should release the ritual juices.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,10.8) śatabhiṣaji bhiṣakkarma bhaiṣajyaṃ cātra kārayet | prācīnaproṣṭhapadayor yāyād ...
(AVParis_1,10.9) uttarābhyām abhiyuñjīta gṛheṣu revatyāṃ vaset | vi senāṃ kārayed rājā aśvinyāṃ bharaṇīṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,10.8) Under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, one should have medical work and healing performed. Under the two <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, one should set out... (AVParis_1,10.9) Under the two <s>Uttarā</s>s, one should engage; under <s>Revatī</s>, one should dwell at home. The king should have the army disbanded under <s>Aśvinī</s> and the <s>Bharaṇī</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_1,11.1) citrāṇi sākaṃ divi rocanāni sarīsṛpāṇi bhuvane javāni | turmiśaṃ sumatim icchamāno ahāni gīrbhiḥ saparyāmi nākam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,11.1) The brilliant [stars] shining together in the sky, the swift creeping ones in the world — desiring good counsel and the <s>Turmiśa</s> [rite], I honor the heavens with hymns for the [auspicious] days.

body.text: (AVParis_1,11.2) suhavam agne kṛttikā rohiṇī castu bhadraṃ mṛgaśiraḥ śam ārdrā | punarvasū sūnṛtā cāru puṣyo bhānur āśleṣā ayanaṃ maghā me ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,11.2) May <s>Agni</s> be well-invoked; may <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s> be [auspicious]; may <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> be blessed; may <s>Ārdrā</s> bring peace; may <s>Punarvasu</s> be true-spoken and beautiful; may <s>Puṣya</s> [be auspicious]; may <s>Āśleṣā</s> be the radiance and the course for me, and may <s>Maghā</s> [be mine].

body.text: (AVParis_1,11.3) puṇyaṃ pūrvā phalgunyau cātra hastaś citrā śivā svāti sukho me astu | rādhe viśākhe suhavā anurādhā jyeṣṭhā sunakṣatram ariṣṭamūlam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,11.3) May the two <s>Pūrva Phalgunī</s>s be meritorious, and here <s>Hasta</s>; may <s>Citrā</s> be auspicious; may <s>Svāti</s> be blissful for me; may <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Viśākhe</s> be well-invoked; may <s>Anurādhā</s> [be auspicious]; may <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> be a good constellation, and <s>Mūla</s> be free from calamity.

body.text: (AVParis_1,11.4) annaṃ pūrvā rāsatāṃ me aṣāḍhā ūrjaṃ dehy uttarā ā vahantu | abhijin me rāsatāṃ puṇyam eva śravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhāḥ kurvatāṃ supuṣṭim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,11.4) May the first <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> grant me food; may the latter <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> give strength and bring [blessings]; may <s>Abhijit</s> grant me true merit; may <s>Śravaṇa</s> and the <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>s bestow great nourishment.

body.text: (AVParis_1,11.5) ā me mahac chatabhisag varīya āme dvayā proṣṭhapadā suśarma | ā revatī cāśvayujau bhagaṃ ma ā me rayiṃ bharaṇya ā vahantu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,11.5) May great <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> [bring] me excellence; may the two <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s [bring] me good shelter; may <s>Revatī</s> and the two <s>Aśvayuj</s>s [bring] me fortune; may the <s>Bharaṇī</s>s bring me wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_1,12.1) kṛttikā rohiṇī mṛgaśira ārdrā punarvasū puṣyāśleṣā maghāḥ pūrve phalgunyau tan navamam agnir daśamam ahorātre edādaśadvādaśe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,12.1) <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and the two <s>Pūrva Phalgunī</s>s — that is the ninth; <s>Agni</s> is the tenth; day and night are the eleventh and twelfth.

children.text: (AVParis_1,12.2) etāny evāsmai nakṣatrāṇi śriyaṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyaṃ samindhata iti veda
children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,12.2) These very <s>nakṣatras</s> kindle for him glory, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, cattle, food, and the eating of food — thus he knows.

children.text: (AVParis_1,12.3) atha yaṃ kāmayaty etāny evāsmai nakṣatrāṇi śriyaṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyaṃ samindhīrann iti tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt
children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,12.3) And for whomever he desires that these very <s>nakṣatras</s> should kindle glory, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, cattle, food, and the eating of food — therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

children.text: (AVParis_1,12.4) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya [[parisamuhya paryukṣya]] paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyāc citrāṇi sākaṃ divi rocanāni svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,12.4) Having placed the fuel facing east, having swept and sprinkled around, having spread the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), having placed the ritual juices on the <s>barhis</s>, having touched [them], then one should offer into the fire [saying]: 'The brilliant [stars] shining together in the sky — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire, having brought the residual drops into the juices, having established the oblations, then one causes him to partake of the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,12.5) evaṃ ced asmai karoty etāny evāsmai nakṣatrāṇi śriyaṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyaṃ samindhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,12.5) If one performs thus for him, these very <s>nakṣatras</s> kindle for him glory, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, cattle, food, and the eating of food.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,13.1) uttare phalgunyau hasta[[ś]] citrā svāti[[r]] viśākhe anūrādhā jyeṣṭhā mūlaṃ pūrvāṣāḍhā tan navamam ādityo daśamaṃ [nāmarūpa] pūrvapakṣāparapakṣāv ekādaśadvādaśe
(AVParis_1,13.2) etāny evāsmai = 1,12.2.
(AVParis_1,13.3) atha yam = 1,12.3.
(AVParis_1,13.4) prāñcam idhmam = 1,12.4.
(AVParis_1,13.5) evam = 1,12.5.
(AVParis_1,14.1) uttarāṣāḍhābhijic chravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhā śatabhiṣak proṣṭhapadau revaty aśvayujau bharaṇyas tad daśamam ... paurṇamāsyamāvāsye dvādaśatrayodaśe
(AVParis_1,14.2) etāny evāsmai = 1,12.2.
(AVParis_1,14.3) atha yam = 1,12.3.
(AVParis_1,14.4) prāñcam idhmam = 1,12.4.
(AVParis_1,14.5) evam = 1,12.5.
(AVParis_1,15.1) ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo brahmavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣam itihāsapurāṇaṃ vākovākya[[m]] idāvatsaraḥ parivatsaraḥ saṃvatsaro daśamaṃ śītoṣṇe ekādaśadvādaśe
(AVParis_1,15.2) etāny evāsmai = 1,12.2.
(AVParis_1,15.3) atha yam = 1,12.3.
(AVParis_1,15.4) prāñcam idhmam = 1,12.4.
(AVParis_1,15.5) evam = 1,12.5.
(AVParis_1,16.1) prāṇo apāno vyānaḥ samāna udānaś cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vāṅ manas tan navamam ... daśamaṃ nāmarūpe ekādaśadvādaśe
(AVParis_1,16.2) etāny evāsmai = 1,12.2.
(AVParis_1,16.3) atha yam = 1,12.3.
(AVParis_1,16.4) prāñcam idhmam = 1,12.4.

children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,16.5) [The same formula as 1,12.5 applies.]

children.text: (AVParis_1,17.1) ajany ajanir yaśo ajanir varco ajanis tejo ajaniḥ saho ajanir maho ajanir brahmā ajanir brāhmaṇavarcasam ajaniḥ sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarvāsāṃ sravantīnāṃ janitādhipatir ajanir bhavatīti veda
children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,17.1) Glory was born, fame was born, splendor was born, radiance was born, force was born, greatness was born, <s>Brahman</s> was born, the luster of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was born. He who knows [this] is the begetter and overlord of all worlds, all gods, all <s>Vedas</s>, all beings, and all flowing rivers.

children.text: (AVParis_1,17.2) atha yaṃ kāmayeta sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarvāsāṃ sravantīnāṃ janitādhipatir ajaniḥ syād iti tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_1,17.2) And for whomever he desires that he should become the begetter and overlord of all worlds, all gods, all <s>Vedas</s>, all beings, and all flowing rivers — therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,13.1) The two <s>Uttara Phalgunī</s>s, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Viśākhe</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> — that is the ninth; <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is the tenth; [name and form,] the bright and dark fortnights are the eleventh and twelfth. (AVParis_1,13.2-5) [The same formulae as 1,12.2-5 apply.] (AVParis_1,14.1) <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, the two <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, <s>Revatī</s>, the two <s>Aśvayuj</s>s, <s>Bharaṇī</s>s — that is the tenth... the full-moon and new-moon days are the twelfth and thirteenth. (AVParis_1,14.2-5) [The same formulae as 1,12.2-5 apply.] (AVParis_1,15.1) The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (Atharvaveda), <s>śikṣā</s> (phonetics), <s>kalpa</s> (ritual), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar), <s>nirukta</s> (etymology), <s>chandas</s> (meter), <s>jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy), <s>itihāsa-purāṇa</s> (history and mythology), <s>vākovākya</s> (dialectics) — the first year, the second year, the [full] year are the tenth; cold and heat are the eleventh and twelfth. (AVParis_1,15.2-5) [The same formulae as 1,12.2-5 apply.] (AVParis_1,16.1) <s>Prāṇa</s> (outbreath), <s>Apāna</s> (inbreath), <s>Vyāna</s> (diffused breath), <s>Samāna</s> (equalizing breath), <s>Udāna</s> (ascending breath), sight, hearing, speech, mind — that is the ninth... the tenth is name-and-form; the eleventh and twelfth [as before]. (AVParis_1,16.2-4) [The same formulae as 1,12.2-4 apply.]

body.text:
(AVParis_1,17.3) prāñcam idhmam = 1,12.4.
(AVParis_1,17.4) evaṃ ced asmai karoti sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarvāsāṃ sravantīnāṃ janitādhipatir ajanir bhavati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,17.3) [The same ritual procedure as 1,12.4 applies.] (AVParis_1,17.4) If one performs thus for him, he becomes the begetter and overlord of all worlds, all gods, all <s>Vedas</s>, all beings, and all flowing rivers.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,18.1) viṣṭhitaśravā vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yat pūrvāhne adhi[[tiṣṭhati vi]]tiṣṭhaty asya puṇyā kīrtir ainaṃ puṇyā kīrtir gacchaty upainaṃ puṇyā kīrtis tiṣṭhati nāsmāt puṇyā kīrtir apakrāmati kīrtimān prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena bhavatīti veda
(AVParis_1,18.2) atha yaṃ kāmayeta vitiṣṭhed asya puṇyā kīrtir [[ainaṃ puṇyā kīrtir]] gacched upainaṃ puṇyā kīrtis tiṣṭhen nāsmāt puṇyā kīrtir apakrāmet kīrtimān prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena syād iti tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,18.1) 'Widely-heard' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which presides in the forenoon. Auspicious fame extends to him, auspicious fame comes to him, auspicious fame abides with him, auspicious fame does not depart from him. He becomes famous, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — thus he knows. (AVParis_1,18.2) And for whomever he desires that auspicious fame should extend, that auspicious fame should come, that auspicious fame should abide, that auspicious fame should not depart, that he should become famous with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,18.3) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyād viṣāsahiṃ sahamānaṃ svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,18.3) Having placed the fuel facing east, having spread the <s>barhis</s>, having placed the ritual juices on the <s>barhis</s>, having touched [them], then one should offer [saying]: 'O vanquisher, conquering — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire, having brought the residual drops into the juices, having established the oblations, then one causes him to partake of the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,18.4) evaṃ ced asmai karo[[ti vitiṣṭha]]ty asya puṇyā kīrtir [[ainaṃ puṇyā kīrtir]] gacchaty upainaṃ puṇyā kīrtis tiṣṭhati nāsmāt puṇyā kīrtir apakrāmati kīrtimān prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair bhavati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,18.4) If one performs thus for him, auspicious fame extends to him, auspicious fame comes to him, auspicious fame abides with him, auspicious fame does not depart from him. He becomes famous, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,19.1) varco vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yan madhyāhnainaṃ varco gacchaty upainaṃ varcas tiṣṭhati nāsmād varco apakrāmati varcasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena bhavatīti veda
(AVParis_1,19.2) atha yaṃ kāmayetainaṃ varco gacched upainaṃ varco tiṣṭhen nāsmād varco apakrāmed varcasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena syād iti tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,19.1) 'Splendor' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] at midday. Splendor comes to him, splendor abides with him, splendor does not depart from him. He becomes splendorous, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — thus he knows. (AVParis_1,19.2) And for whomever he desires that splendor should come, that splendor should abide, that splendor should not depart, that he should become splendorous with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,19.3) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyād varco asi varco mayi dhehi svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,19.3) Having placed the fuel facing east, having spread the <s>barhis</s>, having placed the ritual juices on the <s>barhis</s>, having touched [them], then one should offer [saying]: 'You are splendor; place splendor in me — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire, having brought the residual drops into the juices, having established the oblations, then one causes him to partake of the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,19.4) evaṃ ced asmai karoty ainaṃ varco gacchaty upainaṃ varcas tiṣṭhati nāsmād varco apakrāmati varcasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena bhavati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,19.4) If one performs thus for him, splendor comes to him, splendor abides with him, splendor does not depart from him. He becomes splendorous, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,20.1) tejo vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yad aparāhṇainaṃ tejo gacchaty upainaṃ tejas tiṣṭhati nāsmāt tejo apakrāmati tejasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena bhavatīti veda
(AVParis_1,20.2) atha yaṃ kāmayetainaṃ tejo gacched upainaṃ tejas tiṣṭhen nāsmāt tejo apakrāmet tejasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena syād iti tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,20.1) 'Radiance' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] in the afternoon. Radiance comes to him, radiance abides with him, radiance does not depart from him. He becomes radiant, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — thus he knows. (AVParis_1,20.2) And for whomever he desires that radiance should come, that radiance should abide, that radiance should not depart, that he should become radiant with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth — therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,20.3) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyād tejo asi tejo mayi dhehi svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,20.3) Having placed the fuel facing east, having spread the <s>barhis</s>, having placed the ritual juices on the <s>barhis</s>, having touched [them], then one should offer [saying]: 'You are radiance; place radiance in me — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire, having brought the residual drops into the juices, having established the oblations, then one causes him to partake of the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,20.4) evaṃ ced asmai karoty ainaṃ tejo gacchaty upainaṃ tejas tiṣṭhati nāsmāt tejo apakrāmati tejasvī prajayā paśubhiḥ śriyā gṛhair dhanena bhavati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,20.4) If one performs thus for him, radiance comes to him, radiance abides with him, radiance does not depart from him. He becomes radiant, with offspring, cattle, glory, houses, and wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_1,21.1) viṣṭhitaśravā vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yat pūrvāhne ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,21.1) 'Widely-heard' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] in the forenoon.

body.text: (AVParis_1,21.2) varco vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yan madhyāhne ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,21.2) 'Splendor' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] at midday.

body.text: (AVParis_1,21.3) tejo vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yad aparāhṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,21.3) 'Radiance' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] in the afternoon.

body.text: (AVParis_1,21.4) akāle tv evāprayuktāni bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,21.4) But when employed out of their proper time, they are ineffective.

body.text: (AVParis_1,22.1) viṣṭhitaśravā vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yat pūrvarātre ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,22.1) 'Widely-heard' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] in the first watch of the night.

body.text: (AVParis_1,22.2) varco vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yad madhyarātre ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,22.2) 'Splendor' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] at midnight.

body.text: (AVParis_1,22.3) tejo vai nāmaitan nakṣatraṃ yad apararātre ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,22.3) 'Radiance' indeed is the name of that <s>nakṣatra</s> which [presides] in the last watch of the night.

body.text: (AVParis_1,22.4) svesve kāle [[prayuktāni]] bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,22.4) When employed in their respective proper times, they become effective.

body.text: (AVParis_1,22.5) [[yo vai rātriyānv evāprayuktāni bhavanti]] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,22.5) Those which are employed at night are indeed ineffective [if misapplied].

body.text: (AVParis_1,23.1) yo vai ahnaḥ puṇyāhaṃ veda puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,23.1) He who knows the auspicious day of the daytime becomes one of auspicious days; the day becomes auspicious for him; he indeed performs on an auspicious day.

body.text: (AVParis_1,23.2) sūryo vāhnaḥ puṇyāhaṃ tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,23.2) The sun is the auspicious day of the daytime; therefore, one who knows thus should perform [the rite] under this <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,23.3) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyād viṣāsahiṃ sahamānaṃ svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_1,23.3) Having placed the fuel facing east, having spread the <s>barhis</s>, having placed the ritual juices on the <s>barhis</s>, having touched [them], then one should offer [saying]: 'O vanquisher, conquering — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire, having brought the residual drops into the juices, having established the oblations, then one causes him to partake of the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,23.4) evaṃ ced asmai karoti puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.23.4) If one thus performs for him, he becomes one of auspicious days; the auspicious day comes to him; he indeed makes the day auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_1,24.1) yo vai rātryāḥ puṇyāhaṃ veda puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.24.1) He who knows the <s>puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day) of the night becomes one of auspicious days; the auspicious day comes to him; he indeed makes the day auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_1,24.2) candro vai rātryāḥ puṇyāhaṃ tasmād etasmin nakṣatra evaṃvidvān kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.24.2) The moon is indeed the <s>puṇyāha</s> of the night; therefore, one who knows thus should perform the rite under this <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion).

body.text: (AVParis_1,24.3) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī rasān barhiṣy ādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyād yad rājānaṃ svāhety agnau hutvā raseṣu saṃpātān ānīya saṃsthāpya homāṃs tata enaṃ prāśayati rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.24.3) Having placed the firewood facing east, having spread the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) around, having placed the ritual essences upon the <s>barhis</s>, having touched them, then one should offer oblations with 'To the king, <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered into the fire and brought the remainders into the essences, having assembled them, from the oblations one then feeds him the essences.

body.text: (AVParis_1,24.4) evaṃ ced asmai karoti puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.24.4) If one thus performs for him, he becomes one of auspicious days; the auspicious day comes to him; he indeed makes the day auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_1,25.1) yo vā ahoratrayoḥ puṇyāhaṃ veda puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.25.1) He who knows the <s>puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day) of day-and-night becomes one of auspicious days; the auspicious day comes to him; he indeed makes the day auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_1,25.2) brāhmaṇo vā ahorātrayoḥ puṇyāham

children.text: (AVParis_1,25.3) taṃ pṛcchet kenājiteti
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.25.3) One should ask him: 'By whom was it unconquered?'

children.text: (AVParis_1,25.4) sa ced brūyāt kartavyam iti tathā kuryāt
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.25.4) If he should say 'It is to be done,' then one should do so.

children.text: (AVParis_1,25.5) puṇyāhī bhavati puṇyāham asmai bhavati puṇyāha eva kurute ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.25.5) He becomes one of auspicious days; the auspicious day comes to him; he indeed makes the day auspicious.

body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.25.2) The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed the <s>puṇyāha</s> of day-and-night.

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.1) yāni nakṣatrāṇi divy antarikṣe apsu bhūmau yāni nageṣu dikṣu | prakalpayaṃś candramā yāny eti sarvāṇi mamaitāni śivāni santu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.1) Whatever <s>nakṣatra</s>s (constellations) are in the sky, in the atmosphere, in the waters, on the earth, in the mountains, and in the directions — all those through which the moon passes as it arranges them — may they all be auspicious for me!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.2) aṣṭāviṃśāni śivāni śagmāni saha yogaṃ bhajantu me | yogaṃ prapadye kṣemaṃ ca kṣemaṃ prapadye yogaṃ ca namo 'horātrābhyām astu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.2) May the twenty-eight auspicious and beneficent ones share in my prosperity! I take refuge in prosperity and well-being; I take refuge in well-being and prosperity. Homage be to day and night!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.3) svastitaṃ me suprātaḥ susāyaṃ sudivaṃ sumṛgaṃ suśakunaṃ me astu | suhavam agne svasty amartyaṃ gatvā punar āyābhinandan ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.3) May there be blessing for me, a good morning, a good evening, a good day, auspicious animals, and auspicious birds! O <s>Agni</s>, may the oblation be auspicious! Having gone to immortality and returned, may I rejoice!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.4) anuhavaṃ parihavaṃ parivādaṃ parikṣavam | sarvair me riktakumbhān parā tānt savitaḥ suva ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.4) The counter-offering, the surrounding offering, the censure, the diminution — O <s>Savitṛ</s> (Sun), impel away all those empty vessels of mine!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.5) apapāpaṃ parikṣavaṃ puṇyaṃ bhakṣīmahi kṣavam | śivā te pāta nāsikāṃ puṇyagaś cābhimehatām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.5) Removing evil, diminution — may we enjoy the auspicious and worthy! May the auspicious one protect your nostril, and may the one going to merit urinate upon it!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.6) imā yā brahmaṇaspate viṣūcīr vāta īrate | sadhrīcīr indra tāḥ kṛtvā mahyaṃ śivatamās kṛdhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.6) O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> (Lord of Sacred Speech)! These [forces] that blow in various directions like the wind — O <s>Indra</s>, having made them converge, make them most auspicious for me!

body.text: (AVParis_1,26.7) svasti no astv abhayaṃ no astu namo 'horātrābhyām astu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.26.7) May there be well-being for us, may there be fearlessness for us! Homage be to day and night!

body.text: (AVParis_1,27.1) dadhyodanaṃ bhuktvā kṛttikābhir abhyudiyāt siddhārtho haiva punar āgacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.27.1) Having eaten rice with curds, one should set forth under the <s>Kṛttikā</s>s (Pleiades); one returns having accomplished one's purpose.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,27.2) ārṣabhena māṃsena rohiṇyāṃ mṛgamāṃsair mṛgaśirasi rudhiram ārdrāyāṃ gṛhapatibhaktaṃ punarvasvoḥ ghṛtapāyasaṃ puṣye sarpir māṃsair aśleṣāsu
(AVParis_1,27.3) etāni khalu prāgdvārāṇi nakṣatrāṇi bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.27.2-3) Under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, with bull's meat; under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, with deer-meat; under <s>Ārdrā</s>, with blood; under <s>Punarvasu</s>, the householder's food; under <s>Puṣya</s>, rice cooked in ghee and milk; under <s>Āśleṣā</s>, with clarified butter and meat. These indeed are the <s>nakṣatra</s>s of the eastern gate.

body.text: (AVParis_1,27.4) sa yatraiva prācīṃ diśam abhyutthitaḥ śastrahastena vā kaṇṭhahastena vā vadhyaghātena vā sameyān nivartetārvāk khalv etat krośād ūrdhvaṃ krośād avyāghātukam arthasya bhavati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.27.4) If, having set forth toward the eastern direction, one should encounter a person with a weapon in hand, or with hand at throat, or a slayer of those condemned to death, one should turn back. Within a <s>krośa</s> (league) this is so; beyond a <s>krośa</s>, it is not an obstruction to one's purpose.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,28.1) tailena kṛśaraṃ bhuktvā maghābhir abhyudiyāt siddhārtho haiva punar āgacchaty
(AVParis_1,28.2) āvikair māṃsair bhuktvā pūrvayoḥ phalgunyor abhyudiyād rasair uttarayoḥ praiyaṅgavaṃ haste citraṃ bhaktaṃ bhuktvā citrayābhyudiyāt yāni jyeṣṭhāni teṣāṃ bhuktvā svātāv abhyudiyād apūpān viśākhayor
(AVParis_1,28.3) etāni khalu dakṣiṇadvārāṇi nakṣatrāṇi bhavanti
(AVParis_1,28.4) sa yatraiva dakṣiṇāṃ diśam abhyutthitaḥ śayanahastena vāstaraṇahastena vāsandīhastena vā nīvīhastena vā jānuhastena vā sameyān nivartetārvāk khalv etat krośād ūrdhvaṃ krośād avyāghātukam arthasya bhavati
(AVParis_1,29.1) khalakulair bhuktvānurādhābhir abhyudiyāt siddhārtho haiva punar āgacchati
(AVParis_1,29.2) jyeṣṭhaṃ bhaktaṃ bhuktvā jyeṣṭhayābhyudiyān mūlair bhuktvā mūlenābhyudiyād [[.... bhuktvā pūrvābhir aṣāḍhābhir abhyudiyād]] rasair uttarābhir navanītena pāyasaṃ bhuktvābhijity abhyudiyād [[.... bhuktvā śravaṇenābhyudiyād]]
(AVParis_1,29.3) etāni khalu paścimadvārāṇi nakṣatrāṇi bhavanti
(AVParis_1,29.4) sa yatraiva pratīcīṃ diśam abhyutthitaḥ pāśahastena vā jālahastena vā matsyabandhena vā sameyān nivartetārvāk khalv etat krośād ūrdhvaṃ krośād avyāghātukam arthasya bhavati
(AVParis_1,30.1) vidalasūpena bhuktvā śraviṣṭhābhir abhyudiyāt siddhārtho haiva punar āgacchati
(AVParis_1,30.2) śākaṃ śatabhiṣaji godhā gavyair māṃsair bhuktvā pūrvayoḥ proṣṭhapadayor abhyudiyād rasair uttarayor gṛhiṇībhaktaṃ bhuktvā revatyābhyudiyād akṣatamāṣair bhuktvāśvinyor abhyudiyāt tilataṇḍulān bhakṣayitvā bharaṇībhir abhyudiyād

children.text: (AVParis_1,30.3) etāni khalūdagdvārāṇi nakṣatrāṇi bhavanti
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.30.3) These indeed are the <s>nakṣatra</s>s of the northern gate.

children.text: (AVParis_1,30.4) sa yatraivodīcīṃ diśam abhyutthitaḥ pānahastena vā kiṇvahastena vākṣīveṇa vā sameyān nivartetārvāk khalv etat krośād ūrdhvaṃ krośād avyāghātukam arthasya bhavati
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.30.4) If, having set forth toward the northern direction, one should encounter a person with a drinking vessel in hand, or with ferment in hand, or an intoxicated person, one should turn back. Within a <s>krośa</s> this is so; beyond a <s>krośa</s>, it is not an obstruction to one's purpose.

children.text: (AVParis_1,31.1) atha rājño 'bhiprayāṇasyānayanti pradakṣiṇamukhaṃ śvetam ajaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śuklavāsasam ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.1) Now, for a king setting forth on an expedition, they bring: a white goat facing clockwise, and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> clad in white garments.

body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.28.1-4) Having eaten rice-gruel mixed with sesame oil, one should set forth under the <s>Maghā</s>s; one returns having accomplished one's purpose. Under the former <s>Phālgunī</s>s, having eaten with meat of sheep; under the latter, with ritual essences; under <s>Citrā</s>, having eaten millet in hand with the householder's food; under <s>Svātī</s>, one should set forth; under <s>Viśākhā</s>, with cakes. These indeed are the <s>nakṣatra</s>s of the southern gate. If, having set forth toward the southern direction, one should encounter a person with bedding in hand, or with a cover in hand, or with a stool in hand, or with a girdle in hand, or with hand on knee, one should turn back. Within a <s>krośa</s> this is so; beyond a <s>krośa</s>, it is not an obstruction to one's purpose. (1.29.1-4) Having eaten with <s>khalakulā</s> grains, one should set forth under <s>Anurādhā</s>; one returns having accomplished one's purpose. Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, having eaten the chief food; under <s>Mūla</s>, with roots; under the former <s>Aṣāḍhā</s>s, one should set forth; under the latter, with essences; under <s>Abhijit</s>, having eaten rice-pudding with fresh butter; under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, one should set forth. These indeed are the <s>nakṣatra</s>s of the western gate. If, having set forth toward the western direction, one should encounter a person with a rope in hand, or with a net in hand, or a fish-catcher, one should turn back. Within a <s>krośa</s> this is so; beyond a <s>krośa</s>, it is not an obstruction to one's purpose. (1.30.1-2) Having eaten with split-pulse soup, one should set forth under <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>; one returns having accomplished one's purpose. Under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, vegetables; under the former <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, with monitor-lizard and cow's meat; under the latter, with essences; under <s>Revatī</s>, having eaten the wife's food; under <s>Aśvinī</s>, with unbroken rice and black gram; under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, having eaten sesame and rice grains.

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.2) supratiṣṭhitam avibhrāntaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ śṛṅginaṃ harim | sa cen nadati saṃsṛṣṭas tām āhuḥ siddhim uttamām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.2) A well-established, unfrightened bull, horned and tawny — if it bellows when brought together, they call that the supreme success.

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.3) gajaṃ dhvajaṃ rathaṃ chattraṃ varma yodhān alaṃkṛtān | bhūṣaṇāni ca sarvāṇi praśastāny āyudhāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.3) An elephant, a banner, a chariot, a parasol, armor, warriors adorned,

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.4) vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi patākā vividhās tathā | śuklāḥ sumanaso lājā akṣatā gaurasarṣapāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.4) And all musical instruments, and various flags; white flowers, parched grain, unbroken rice, and white mustard seeds.

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.5) phalāni pūrṇapātrāṇi dhūpagandhān jalaṃ tilāḥ | arcayitvā devatāḥ sarvā brāhmaṇān pratipūjya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.5) Fruits, full vessels, incense, perfumes, water, and sesame; having worshipped all the deities and honored the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s,

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.6) purohitaṃ puraskṛtya suhṛdo mantriṇas tathā | evaṃ prayāto labhate vijayaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.6) Placing the <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain) in front, together with friends and ministers — one who sets forth thus obtains victory; there is no doubt in this.

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.7) kalyāṇanāmadheyaṃ ca gajam avyaṅgadarśanam | kumārīṃ dadhipātreṇa gṛhītena svalaṃkṛtām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.7) And an elephant of auspicious name, of unblemished appearance; a maiden well-adorned, holding a vessel of curds.

body.text: (AVParis_1,31.8) yadi ced adhigo jālmi sūryācandramasor gṛhe | aśvinā rāsabhendreṇa yānaṃ kuryāt pradakṣiṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.31.8) If indeed one should encounter a cow [or] an intelligent person in the house of the sun and moon, one should make a circumambulation with a donkey-lord at the <s>Aśvinī</s> [constellation].

body.text:
(AVParis_1,32.1) prādakṣiṇyam agner gavāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ rājño rathasya [naravāhanasya śakaṭasya] caturyuktasya ṣaḍyuktāṣṭayuktasya ca
(AVParis_1,32.2) hradasya dakṣiṇāvartasya kumārasyābhyutthitasya ca | manuṣyapūrṇapiṭakasya pṛthivyā utthitasya ca || prabaddhasyaikapaśoḥ
(AVParis_1,32.3) ulūcī kālaśakuniḥ kṣipraśyeno 'tha vartikā | ete dvijāḥ prādakṣiṇyāś cāṣaś cātra pradṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.32.1-2) Circumambulation should be of fire, cows, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the king's chariot, a chariot yoked with four, six, or eight [horses]; of a pool with a clockwise whirl, of a boy who has risen up, of a basket full of people, and of the earth that has risen; of a single bound animal. (1.32.3) The owl, the black bird, the swift hawk, and the quail — these are the auspicious birds for circumambulation, and the blue jay is also observed here.

body.text: (AVParis_1,32.4) krauñcanakulapriyavṛkṣacaityānāṃ nityaṃ vayasām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.32.4) Of cranes, mongooses, beloved trees, and sacred groves — always, of birds.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,32.5) tiryag nyag vādhipatitaṃ viparītaṃ hīnāṅgāṅgātiriktaṃ vikṛtanagnamuṇḍabaṇḍaś citraśyāmaśyāvadantakunakhijaṭila[[ḥ]] kāṣāyāvikayoś [carmā]brāhmaṇayor
(AVParis_1,32.6) eteṣāṃ kiṃ cid dṛṣṭvā na gacched
(AVParis_1,32.7) yadi gacched arthino yanti ced arthaṃ gacchān id daduṣo rātim | vavṛjyus tṛṣyataḥ kāmam ity etāṃ japet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.32.5-6) What has fallen sideways, downward, or above, what is inverted, with deficient or extra limbs, deformed, naked, shaven-headed, eunuch; spotted, dark-complexioned, dark-toothed, one with bad nails, matted-haired, wearing saffron robes or woolen garments — of leather-clad <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s. Having seen any of these, one should not proceed.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,32.8) ni ṣajyato dasyūṃś chādayann indreti vā
(AVParis_1,32.9) stuhi śrutam iti vā
(AVParis_1,32.10) devīṃ vācam ajanayanta devās tāṃ viśvarūpāḥ paśavo vadanti | sā no mandreṣam ūrjaṃ duhānā dhenur vāg asmān upa suṣṭutaitu iti gardabhamukhena pratinadati pratilomapratikṛtyāsya
(AVParis_1,32.11) sarvāś ca pāpikā vāco neṣṭā<ḥ> | kuceladarśanaṃ ca | anarthā hiṃsārtham | taddarśanāya | pāpaṃ vā jihīrṣatāṃ siddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.32.7-11) If one does proceed, one should recite: 'Those who desire wealth go, they who go [reach] their goal; givers give the gift; may they fulfill the desire of the thirsty.' Or: 'O <s>Indra</s>, sitting down, covering the brigands...' Or: 'Praise the famous one.' Or: 'The gods generated divine speech; all-formed creatures speak it; may that speech, yielding us strength and nourishment like a wish-fulfilling cow, approach us well-praised' — one should sound back with the face of a donkey as a counter-ritual against the adverse. And all inauspicious words are undesirable. And the sight of one in dirty garments. Misfortunes are for the purpose of harm. For the one who sees them. Or success for those who wish to steal evil.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,33.1) atha rogaparimāṇāny
(AVParis_1,33.2) uttarāsv aṣāḍhāsūttarayoḥ proṣṭhapadayor māsam |
(AVParis_1,33.3) rohiṇyāṃ viṃśatirātram |
(AVParis_1,33.4) punarvasor ūnaviṃśatirātraṃ pūrvāṇi dvandvinām |
(AVParis_1,33.5) mṛgaśirasi ṣoḍaśarātram abhijiti śravaṇe ca
(AVParis_1,33.6) ārdrāyāṃ pañcadaśarātram anūrādhāśraviṣṭhābharaṇīṣu ca |
(AVParis_1,33.7) puṣye dvādaśarātraṃ haste svātau ca |

children.text: (AVParis_1,33.8) śatabhiṣaji navarātraṃ māse vākālaṃ kurute |
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.33.8) Under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, nine nights, or a month — it makes the time.

children.text: (AVParis_1,33.9) jyeṣṭhāyāṃ mūle cāṣṭarātram |
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.33.9) Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> and <s>Mūla</s>, eight nights.

children.text: (AVParis_1,33.10) revatyāṃ saptarātram |
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.33.10) Under <s>Revatī</s>, seven nights.

children.text: (AVParis_1,33.11) kṛttikāśleṣā maghā uttare phālgunyau citrā viśākhe aśvayujau ca saptasv eteṣu daśarātram ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 1.33.11) Under <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, the latter <s>Phālgunī</s>s, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and the <s>Aśvinī</s>s — in these seven, ten nights.

body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.33.1-7) Now, the durations of diseases: Under the latter <s>Aṣāḍhā</s>s and the latter <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s, one month. Under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, twenty nights. Under <s>Punarvasu</s>, less than twenty nights — these are the former ones of the paired [nakṣatras]. Under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, sixteen nights; under <s>Abhijit</s> and <s>Śravaṇa</s> likewise. Under <s>Ārdrā</s>, fifteen nights; under <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s> likewise. Under <s>Puṣya</s>, twelve nights; under <s>Hasta</s> and <s>Svātī</s> likewise.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,34.1) atha balayaḥ
(AVParis_1,34.2) śukla upaśurasṛpeśuklosaptamūnmodanaḥ | aṣṭamaḥ palalodano dhānāḥ saktavo 'tha śaṣkulī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.34.1-2) Now, the <s>bali</s> (ritual offerings): White [offering]; then the subsidiary, serpent, and white seventh-day rice offering with jaggery; the eighth, rice with dried meat; grain, barley grits, and then fried cakes.

body.text: (AVParis_1,34.3) citraś ca kṛkavākuś ca śuklaḥ kambūkapiṇḍakaḥ | sarvabījāni mūlāni udapātraṃ ca pāyasau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.34.3) A spotted one and a wild cock, a white one, and cowrie-shell cakes; all seeds, roots, a vessel of water, and two milk-puddings.

body.text: (AVParis_1,34.4) paśu ghṛtaṃ kaśīkā ca ārdramāṃsāni pāyasau | pathyāyāṃ māṣasaktavaḥ pāyaso 'tha tilodanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.34.4) An animal, ghee, and a <s>kaśīkā</s> (cloth); fresh meats and two milk-puddings. For [the rite of] the auspicious path, barley and black gram grits, then milk-pudding, and then rice with sesame.

body.text: (AVParis_1,34.5) sarvatra gandhapuṣpāṇi lājānulepikās tathā | anudvāraṃ ca nakṣatraṃ daivataṃ cātra yojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.34.5) Everywhere, fragrant flowers, parched grains, and ointments likewise. And the <s>nakṣatra</s> proper to the door, and the deity should be assigned here.

body.text: (AVParis_1,34.6) dīpāś ca maṇḍale dīptāḥ śuciś cāpi baliṃ haret | yo 'smin yas tvā mātur iti vipariharet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.34.6) And lamps kindled in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram); and one who is pure should offer the <s>bali</s>. With the [hymn] 'He who of you, who of your mother' — one should make the circumambulation.

body.text: (AVParis_1,35.1) saśvetasaktu kaṃsaś ca prācīnārthasya maṅgalam | sravaṃ ca māṃsapeśī ca dakṣiṇārthasya maṅgalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.35.1) A vessel with white barley-flour is the auspicious [sign] for one whose purpose lies to the east. A stream and a piece of meat are the auspicious [signs] for one whose purpose lies to the south.

body.text: (AVParis_1,35.2) kumārī dadhikaṃsaś ca pratyagarthasya maṅgalam | anaḍvān brahmacārī ca udagarthasya maṅgalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.35.2) A maiden and a vessel of curds are the auspicious [signs] for one whose purpose lies to the west. A draft-ox and a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) are the auspicious [signs] for one whose purpose lies to the north.

body.text: (AVParis_1,35.3) kumārīṃ dadhipātreṇa gṛhītena svalaṃkṛtām | pradakṣiṇāṃ tu tāṃ kuryād dhruvaṃ syāt siddhir iṣyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.35.3) One should circumambulate a well-adorned maiden holding a vessel of curds; surely the desired success will be firm.

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.1) senāṃ ced abhyutthitāṃ mandraḥ pratigarjed rājā vāmātyo vā mariṣyatīti vidyāt tatra vāruṇīṃ japet | ud uttamaṃ varuṇa pāśam iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.1) If, when an army has arisen, a deep sound thunders back, the king or his minister will die — thus one should know. There one should recite the <s>Vāruṇī</s> [formula]: 'Rise up the highest, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, the noose...'

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.2) senāṃ ced adbhyutthitāṃ dhūmo 'nugacched vijeṣyatīti vidyāt | tveṣas te dhūma ity anumantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.2) If, when an army has arisen, smoke follows it, one will be victorious — thus one should know. One should consecrate with the <s>mantra</s>: 'Fierce is your smoke...'

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.3) senāṃ ced abhyutthitāṃ vāto 'nuvāyād vijeṣyatīti vidyād vāta ā vatv ity anumantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.3) If the wind blows after [behind] an army that has marched forth, one should know that it will be victorious. One should recite the <s>mantra</s> 'vāta ā vatu' (Let the wind blow hither).

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.4) senāṃ ced abhyutthitāṃ mṛgo vyabhimṛśed arthaṃ tasyā vinaśyatīti vidyāt | mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhā ity anumantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.4) If an animal should cross the path of an army that has marched forth, one should know that its purpose will be destroyed. One should recite the <s>mantra</s> 'mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ' (Like a fearsome beast, roaming in hollows, dwelling on mountains).

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.5) senāṃ ced abhyutthitāṃ pakṣiṇo vyatipateyur māṃsodanaṃ ca tatra dadyāt | aliklavā jāṣkamadā gṛdhrā ity anumantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.5) If birds should fly across [the path of] an army that has marched forth, one should offer a rice dish with meat there. One should recite the <s>mantra</s> 'aliklavā jāṣkamadā gṛdhrāḥ' (The aliklavas, the jāṣkamadas, the vultures).

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.6) senāṃ ced abhyutthitāṃ kapiñjalaḥ prativaded bhadraṃ vadeti tisraḥ kāpiñjalāni stavanāni vadanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.6) If a francolin partridge should call back to an army that has marched forth, [one should recite] 'bhadraṃ vada' (Speak auspiciously) — the three <s>kāpiñjala</s> (francolin) hymns of praise.

body.text: (AVParis_1,36.7) yo abhy u babhruṇāyasi svapantam atsi puruṣaṃ śayānam agasvalam | ayasmayena brahmaṇāśmamayena varmaṇā pary asmān varuṇo dadhad || ity abhyavakāśe saṃviśati | abhyavakāśe saṃviśati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.36.7) 'You who approach with a tawny one and consume the sleeping man, the one lying down, the wanderer — with a brazen spell, with a stony armor, may <s>Varuṇa</s> place [protection] around us.' With this [<s>mantra</s>] one sleeps in the open. One sleeps in the open.

body.text: (AVParis_1,37.1) agnir devo yajvanaḥ kṛṣṇavartmā vaiśvānaro jātavedā rasāgrabhuk | sa nakṣatrāṇāṃ prathamena pāvakaḥ kṛttikābhir jvalano no 'nuśāmyatām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.37.1) May <s>Agni</s>, the god, the sacrificer's [deity], of dark path, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Jātavedas</s>, the consumer of essence, he the purifier, foremost among the <s>nakṣatra</s>s (lunar mansions), blazing with the <s>Kṛttikā</s>s (Pleiades), be appeased for us.

body.text: (AVParis_1,37.2) prajāpatir yaḥ sasṛje prajā imā devānt sa sṛṣṭvā viniyoj[[y]]a karmasu | sa sarvabhuk sarvayogeṣu rohiṇī śivāḥ kriyāḥ kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.37.2) <s>Prajāpati</s>, who created these beings — having created the gods and assigned them to their duties — he, the all-consumer, in all undertakings, may <s>Rohiṇī</s> (Aldebaran) make auspicious rites for the accomplishment of action.

body.text: (AVParis_1,37.3) vidyāvido ye abhiśocamānavā arcanti śakraṃ saha devatāgaṇaiḥ | sa no yoge mṛgaśiraḥ śivāḥ kriyāḥ śreṣṭharājaḥ kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.37.3) Those who, possessing knowledge and burning with zeal, worship <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) together with the host of deities — may he, the best of kings, at the conjunction, may <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> (Orion's head) make auspicious rites for the accomplishment of action.

body.text: (AVParis_1,37.4) devaṃ bhavaṃ paśupatiṃ haraṃ kṛśaṃ mahādevaṃ śarvam ugraṃ śikhaṇḍinam | sahasrākṣam aśaniṃ yaṃ gṛṇanti sa no rudraḥ paripātu na ārdrayā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.37.4) To the divine <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Hara</s>, the emaciated one, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, the fierce one, the crested one, the thousand-eyed, the thunderbolt — whom they praise — may that <s>Rudra</s> protect us with <s>Ārdrā</s> (Betelgeuse).

body.text: (AVParis_1,37.5) ....yā vipraiḥ kavibhir namasyate dākṣāyaṇī devapurādibhir nṛbhir | sā naḥ stutā prathamajā punarvasuḥ śivāḥ kriyāḥ kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.37.5) ...she who is worshipped by sages and poets, <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, by men [dwelling in] divine cities and the rest — may she, praised, the first-born, <s>Punarvasu</s> (Pollux and Castor), make auspicious rites for the accomplishment of action.

body.text: (AVParis_1,38.1) yasya devā brahmacaryeṇa karmaṇā mahāsuraṃ tigmatayābhicakrire | taṃ subudhaṃ devaguruṃ bṛhaspatim arcāmi pusyeṇa sahābhipātu mā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.38.1) He by whose <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline) and action the gods vanquished the great <s>Asura</s> with sharp heat — that wise one, the preceptor of the gods, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, I worship — may he, with <s>Puṣya</s> (Cancri), protect me.

body.text: (AVParis_1,38.2) yā na[[ḥ]] stutaḥ parihiṇomi medhayā tapyamānam ṛṣibhiḥ kāmaśocibhiḥ | jaratkārasūnor ṛṣibhir manīṣibhis tā aśleṣā abhirakṣantu noragaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.38.2) Those whom I praise, she who is praised, I encompass with wisdom — the one heated by the seers burning with desire — the son of <s>Jaratkāru</s>, by the seers, the wise ones — may the <s>Āśleṣā</s>s (Hydrae) protect us with serpents.

body.text: (AVParis_1,38.3) ye devatvaṃ puṇyakṛto 'bhicakrire ye cāpare ye ca pare maharṣayaḥ | arcāmi sūnur yamarājagān pitṝṃś chivāḥ kriyāḥ kṛṇutāṃ ca no maghā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.38.3) Those who attained godhood by meritorious deeds, and others, and other great sages — I, the son, worship the ancestors who went to King <s>Yama</s> — may <s>Maghā</s> (Regulus) make auspicious rites for us.

body.text: (AVParis_1,38.4) yo yojayan karmaṇā carṣaṇīdhṛto bhūmiṃ ceti bhaga[[ḥ prajāḥ]] prasādayan | taddevatye śivatamām alaṃkṛte phalgunyor īḍe bhajanaṃ ca pūrvayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.38.4) He who, yoking by action, holding the people, traverses the earth, <s>Bhaga</s>, gladdening the beings — in that most auspicious deity-constellation, adorned, I praise and worship the former <s>Phālgunī</s>s (Leonis).

body.text: (AVParis_1,38.5) stutaṃ pūrvair aryamaṇaṃ manīṣibhiḥ staumi devaṃ jagati vācam erayan | taddevatye śivatamām alaṃkṛte phalgunyau na uttare devatātaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.38.5) <s>Aryaman</s>, praised by former sages, I praise — the god, raising my voice in the world — in that most auspicious deity-constellation, adorned, may the latter <s>Phālgunī</s>s [be] for divine worship.

body.text: (AVParis_1,39.1) ś[y]āvair yuktaḥ śitipād dhiraṇyayo yasya rathaḥ pathibhir vartate sukhaiḥ | sa no hastena savitā hiraṇyabhug ghiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā [no] 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.39.1) Yoked with dark steeds, white-footed, golden — he whose chariot moves on easy paths — may <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Stimulator), golden-handed, the enjoyer of gold, with <s>Hasta</s> (Corvi), protect us.

body.text: (AVParis_1,39.2) tvaṣṭre namaḥ kṣitisṛje manīṣiṇe bhūtagoptre paramakarmakāriṇe | sā na[[ḥ]] stutā kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye citrāṃ devī saha yogena rūpabhṛt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.39.2) Homage to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the creator of the earth, the wise one, the protector of beings, the doer of supreme acts — may she, praised, make for the accomplishment of action, <s>Citrā</s> (Spica) the divine one, bearing form together with conjunction.

body.text: (AVParis_1,39.3) yaḥ prāṇināṃ jīvayan khāni sevate śivo bhūtvā mātariśvā rasāgrabhuk | dhvajo 'ntarikṣasya sa sarvabhūtabhṛd vāyur devaḥ svātinā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.39.3) He who, giving life to breathing beings, pervades the openings [of the body], becoming auspicious, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, the consumer of essence, the banner of the atmosphere, he who supports all beings — may the god <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) protect us with <s>Svātī</s> (Arcturus).

body.text: (AVParis_1,39.4) yāv īḍitāv ātmavidbhir maṇīṣibhiḥ sahitau [yau] trīṇi savanāni sāmagau | indrāgnī varadau namaskṛtau viśākhayoḥ kurvatām āyuṣe śrīḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.39.4) Those two who are praised by the self-knowing wise ones, united, who at the three <s>savana</s>s (pressings) sing the <s>Sāman</s> — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, boon-givers, reverenced — may they grant prosperity for long life with <s>Viśākhā</s> (Librae).

body.text: (AVParis_1,39.5) viśve devā yam ṛṣim āhur mitraṃ bharadvājam ṛṣitaḥ prasāmavit | taṃ jagatyā gāthayā staumy ugraiḥ sa mām anūrādhābhir [bhṛtakaṇvo] 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.39.5) He whom all gods call a seer — <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, a seer and knower of the <s>Sāman</s> — him I praise with a <s>Jagatī</s> verse, with the mighty [<s>Anūrādhā</s>s] — may he protect me with the <s>Anūrādhā</s>s, [he who is] nourished by <s>Kaṇva</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.1) śatakratur yo nijaghāna śambaraṃ vṛtraṃ ca hatvā saritaḥ prasarjata[ḥ] | sa naḥ stutaḥ prītamanāḥ puraṃdaro marutsakhā jyeṣṭhayā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.1) He of a hundred powers who slew <s>Śambara</s> and, having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, released the rivers — may he, praised, with pleased mind, <s>Purandara</s> (Destroyer of citadels), friend of the <s>Marut</s>s, protect us with <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (Antares).

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.2) yā dhārayaty ojasātidevapadaṃ mātā pṛthivī ca sā sarvabhūtabhṛt | sā na[[ḥ]] stutā kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye mūlaṃ devī nirṛtiḥ sarvakarmasu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.2) She who supports with might what is beyond the divine station, Mother <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth), the supporter of all beings — may she, praised, make for the accomplishment of action — <s>Mūla</s> (Scorpii), the divine <s>Nirṛti</s>, in all rites.

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.3) parjanyasṛṣṭās tisṛṇībhir āvṛtaṃ yās tarpayanty abhitaḥ pravṛddhaye | tā[[ḥ]] staumy āpo vāruṇīḥ ... pūrvā āṣāḍhā svadhayāstu yojane ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.3) Released by <s>Parjanya</s> (the Rain-god), covered with triple [clouds], those [waters] that nourish on all sides for growth — I praise those <s>Vāruṇī</s> waters... may the former <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> (Sagittarii) be for yoking with offerings.

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.4) yās triṃśataṃ trīṃś ca madanti devā devanāmno nirmitā[[ṃ]]ś ca bhūyasaḥ | tā no 'ṣāḍhā uttarā vaso viśve [[śivāḥ]] kriyāḥ kṛṇutāṃ suramatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.4) Those thirty and three gods who rejoice, and those whose names are divine and fashioned in abundance — may the latter <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>, O <s>Vasu</s>, the <s>Viśve</s> [devas], make auspicious rites, approved by the gods.

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.5) yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛt sarvabhūtabhṛd yasmād anyan na paraṃ kiṃ canāsti | anirmitaḥ satyajitaḥ puruṣṭutaḥ sa no brahmābhijitā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.5) He who is all-knowing, all-doing, the supporter of all beings, than whom nothing higher exists — uncreated, true-conquering, greatly praised — may that <s>Brahmā</s> protect us with <s>Abhijit</s> (Vegae).

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.1) sthānācyute sthānam indrāya pātave devebhyaś ca ya īrayaṃs [trir] vicakrame | taṃ svid dhi svargaṃ nākapṛṣṭhaṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇur devaḥ śravaṇenābhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.1) He who, dislodged from his station, strode thrice to protect <s>Indra</s>'s station and [that] of the gods — that very heaven, the back of the sky, the universal one — may the god <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect with <s>Śravaṇa</s> (Altair).

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.2) aṣṭau śatāni śvetaketūnāṃ yāni tvaṃ ca sa tvaṃ nijaghāna bhūyasaḥ | anādeśenobhaya[ta]ś ca vīḍitāḥ śraviṣṭhābhir no 'bhirakṣantu vājinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.2) Those eight hundred white-bannered ones — you and he — [who] slew even more — pressed from both sides without command — may the <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>s (Delphini) protect us with their steeds.

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.3) vājā devī devamṛṇānikākubhāv ubhāv ājasya natakarmaṇā śivā | tava vrājaṃ staumasi devabhojanau pratyagbhiṣak śatabhiṣak śivau naḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.3) <s>Vājā</s>, the divine, and the two ends of divine-debt — both auspicious by the ritual of the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] — we praise your fold, O divine-nourished ones; may <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> (Aquarii) be auspicious for us, facing west.

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.4) śunāsīrau naḥ pramumūtu jihmasau tautau pitṛbhyo dadatu[[ḥ]] stanau śubhau | tau pūrvajau kṛṇutām ekapād ajaḥ pratiṣṭhānau sarvakāmābhayāya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.4) May <s>Śunāsīra</s> (Plough-deities) release us, the two crooked ones; may they give to the ancestors two auspicious breasts — may the first-born one, <s>Ekapād Aja</s> (the one-footed unborn), make the two <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s a foundation for the fulfillment of all desires and fearlessness.

body.text: (AVParis_1,40.5) sarvārthāya kṛṇomi karmasiddhaye gaviṣṭutāyānekakāriṇe namaḥ | so 'hir budhnyaḥ kṛṇutām uttarau śivau pratiṣṭhānau sarvakāmābhayāya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.40.5) For the accomplishment of all purposes, for the success of action, homage to the one praised with cattle, the doer of many deeds — may that <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> (Serpent of the Deep) make the two latter ones auspicious, a foundation for the fulfillment of all desires and fearlessness.

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.6) yaṃ mahāhemam ṛṣitaḥ prasāmavid bharadvājaś candramasau divākaram | sajuṣṭānām aśvayujau bhayāya ca sa naḥ pūṣā kṛṇutāṃ revatīṃ śivām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.6) He whom <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the great golden one, a seer and knower of <s>Sāman</s>, [praises] as the moon and the sun — may <s>Pūṣan</s>, with the two <s>Aśvayuj</s> (Equulei), for [removing] fear, make <s>Revatī</s> (Piscium) auspicious for us.

body.text: (AVParis_1,41.7) jīrṇaṃ santaṃ yau yuvānaṃ hi cakratur ṛṣiṃ dhiyā cyavanaṃ somapau kṛtau | tau naś cittibhir bhiṣajām asya satkarau .... prajām aśvinyām aśvinau śivau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.7) Those two who made the seer <s>Cyavana</s>, old as he was, young again by their wisdom, the two <s>Soma</s>-drinkers — may they, with the graces of physicians, their good deeds... progeny with <s>Aśvinī</s> (Arietis), may the two <s>Aśvin</s>s be auspicious.
