body.text: (AVParis_1,41.8) yasya śyāmaśabalau rakṣataḥ svadhā duṣkṛt sukṛd vividhā carṣaṇīdhṛtau | tau savitryā ca savitur dharmacāribhir yamo rājā bharaṇībhir no 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.41.8) He whose dark-speckled [dogs] guard the offerings, discerning the evil-doer from the virtuous, the two supporters of the people — they, with <s>Sāvitrī</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s>, among the righteous — may King <s>Yama</s> protect us with the <s>Bharaṇī</s>s (Arietis).

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.1) atha nakṣatrasnānānāṃ vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpadam | grahadaivatapūjāṃ ca yeṣu yatra yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.1) Now I shall declare the procedure of the <s>nakṣatra</s>-snāna (lunar mansion bathing) rites in order — and the worship of planets and deities, in which [constellation], where, and according to which rule.

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.2) nakṣatrayogakālajñaḥ kṛtvā tantraṃ yathāvidhi | yajed grahān haviṣyeṇa yathoktena ca devatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.2) One who knows the times of <s>nakṣatra</s> conjunctions, having arranged the ritual apparatus according to rule, should sacrifice to the planets with oblations and to the deities as prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.3) praśastalakṣaṇaṃ kumbhaṃ sasaṃbhārajalaṃ budhaḥ | saṃpātābhihitaṃ kṛtvā mantrair vidhim anusmaran ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.3) The wise one, having made a vessel of auspicious characteristics, filled with water and ritual ingredients, having recited the prescribed <s>mantra</s>s and remembering the procedure,

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.4) sāvitryā śāntisūktaiś ca mahāvyāhṛtibhis tathā | apāṃ stotraiḥ pavitraiś ca nakṣatrastutibhis tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.4) With the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [<s>mantra</s>], with the peace hymns, with the great <s>vyāhṛti</s>s (ritual exclamations), with the hymns of praise to the waters, the purifying [verses], and with the <s>nakṣatra</s> praises likewise —

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.5) nakṣatradaivatān mantrān pratinakṣatram āvapet | kāmyāṃś caivāvapen mantrān karmaliṅgavidhānavit ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.5) One should cast the <s>mantra</s>s of the <s>nakṣatra</s> deities for each <s>nakṣatra</s>; and one should also cast <s>mantra</s>s for desired objects — one who knows the rules of ritual classification and procedure.

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.6) saṃpātyāthābhimantrya vā nakṣatrasnānakovidaḥ | snāpayed arthinaṃ vāgbhiḥ puṇyābhir abhimantritam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.6) Having consecrated [the water] or having recited <s>mantra</s>s over it, one skilled in <s>nakṣatra</s>-snāna should bathe the supplicant with holy words that have been consecrated.

body.text: (AVParis_1,42.7) eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sadasyebhyaś ca dakṣiṇā | pūrvam āpyāyayed dehaṃ paścād dadyāt tu dakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.7) This is the prescribed procedure, and the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) for the officiants; first one should nourish the body, and afterward give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,42.8) anena vidhinā snātvā dadyāc caivātra dakṣiṇām | prāpnoty anunayaṃ puṃsaḥ sa vedaphalam aśnute || [prāpnoty: prāpṇoty ed. (misprint)]
(AVParis_1,42.9) ātmānaṃ nirmalīkṛtya devān iṣṭvā grahāṃs tathā | vidvadbhyo dakṣiṇā deyā dvijān annena tarpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.42.8-9) Having bathed by this procedure and having given the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, one obtains the grace of men and enjoys the fruit of the <s>Veda</s>. Having purified oneself, having worshipped the gods and the planets, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given to the learned, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s should be satisfied with food.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.1) kṛttikābhiḥ śirīṣasya aśvatthasya vaṭasya ca | snāpayet pattrabhaṅgena ya icched rājapūjitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.1) With the <s>Kṛttikā</s>s (Pleiades), one should bathe [the person] with leaf-fragments of the <s>śirīṣa</s> tree, the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), and the <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) — he who desires to be honored by a king.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.2) rohiṇyāṃ snāpayed vaiśyaṃ sarvabījair alaṃkṛtam | akṣatān antaraṃ kṛtvā tathā saubhāgyam arhati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.2) Under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, one should bathe a <s>Vaiśya</s> (merchant), adorned with all kinds of seeds; having placed unhusked rice in between, one thus becomes worthy of good fortune.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.3) yadā mṛgaśiro yujyet tadā snānaṃ vidhīyate | muktāmaṇisuvarṇena dhanārthī tena snāpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.3) When <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> is conjoined, then the bathing is prescribed; one desiring wealth should bathe [the person] with pearls, gems, and gold.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.4) śrīveṣṭakasarjarasatagarośīrapattrakaiḥ | ārdrāyāṃ vaṇijaḥ snātāḥ sulābhāṃs tu labhanti te ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.4) With <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s> (pine resin), <s>sarja</s>-resin, <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), and leaves — those bathed under <s>Ārdrā</s> obtain easily what is easily obtainable.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.5) punarvasubhyāṃ gomārgād āhared agramṛttikām | gopīṭhe snāpayed go 'rthī kṣipraṃ gomān bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.5) Under the two <s>Punarvasu</s>s, one should bring the topmost earth from a cow-path; one desiring cows should bathe [the person] on a cow-platform — quickly he shall become a possessor of cows.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.6) raktaśālisahasreṇa tāvadbhir gaurasarṣapaiḥ | sahasravīryānantyā ca madayantīpriyaṅgubhiḥ | trīn puṣyān brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ pārthivaṃ labhate yaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.6) With a thousand [grains of] red rice, with as many white mustard seeds, with <s>sahasravīryā</s> (thousand-power) herb, <s>anantyā</s> (endless) herb, <s>madayantī</s> (intoxicating) herb, and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> bathed on three <s>Puṣya</s> [days] obtains royal glory.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.7) aśleṣāsv āhārayed ubhayataḥ kūlamṛttikāḥ | [aśv]ārohaṃ snāpayet tena kṣipravāhī bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.7) Under the <s>Āśleṣā</s>s, one should gather earth from both banks [of a river]; one should bathe a horseman with that — he shall become swift-moving.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.8) maghābhis tu tilaiḥ snāyād utpalaiḥ kamalais tathā | tasmiṃs tu māse sā kanyā kṣipraṃ ca labhate patim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.8) Under the <s>Maghā</s>s, one should bathe with sesame seeds, with blue lotuses and lotuses; in that month, that maiden shall quickly obtain a husband.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.9) atha pūrvayoḥ phalgunyoḥ śatapuṣpā priyaṅgavaḥ | madhv eva ca tṛtīyaṃ syāt saubhāgyaṃ bhogavardhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.9) Under the former <s>Phālgunī</s>s, <s>śatapuṣpā</s> (dill) and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet) [are used]; and honey as the third — [this brings] good fortune and increase of enjoyment.

body.text: (AVParis_1,43.10) athottarayoḥ phalgunyor akṣatā gaurasarṣapāḥ | etat snānaṃ prayuñjīta prajāsthāpanam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.43.10) Under the latter <s>Phālgunī</s>s, unhusked rice and white mustard seeds [are used]; this bathing should be employed — it is supreme for the establishment of progeny.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.1) hastena sarvakārūṇāṃ caurāṇāṃ cāpi nityaśaḥ | nadīgiritaṭākeṣu mṛttikāsnānam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.44.1) Under <s>Hasta</s>, for all artisans and also thieves, always — bathing with earth from rivers, mountains, and tanks is supreme.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.2) citrāyāṃ citramālyais tu sarvagandhair alaṃkṛtam | yoṣārthī snāpayet tena kṣipraṃ sa labhate priyām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.44.2) Under <s>Citrā</s>, with colorful garlands and adorned with all fragrances — one desiring a woman should bathe [the person] with that — quickly he obtains his beloved.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.3) svātinā tu gandhaiḥ snāyād utpalaiḥ kumudais tathā | tasmiṃs tu māse sā kanyā kṣipraṃ nirvyūhyate tataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.44.3) Under <s>Svātī</s>, one should bathe with fragrances, with blue lotuses and water-lilies; in that month, that maiden is quickly given in marriage.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.4) khaḍgasya ca viṣāṇena gajasya ṛṣabhasya vā | viśākhābhyām abhiṣikto [rājā] pṛthivīm abhiśāsayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.44.4) With the horn of a sword[-shaped tusk], of an elephant, or of a bull — one consecrated under the two <s>Viśākhā</s>s [as] king should rule the earth.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.5) anūrādhāsv āhārayed valmīkaśatamṛttikāḥ | karṣaṇaṃ snāpayet tena dhanadhānyena vardhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 1.44.5) Under the <s>Anūrādhā</s>s, one should gather earth from a hundred anthills; one should bathe a ploughman with that — he increases in wealth and grain.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.6) jyeṣṭhāyāṃ jyaiṣṭhyakāmaṃ tu abhiṣiñcet purohitam | rasaiś ca miśradhānyaiś cābhiṣiktaḥ prāśayed rasān ||
body.translated_text: One should anoint the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) who desires pre-eminence under the <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>]; anointed with juices and mixed grains, he should eat the juices.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.7) mūlena sarvatobhadram upaviṣṭā varavarṇinī | śamīpattrasahasreṇa snānāt putraṃ prasūyate ||
body.translated_text: Under the <s>Mūla</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], a woman of excellent complexion, seated upon a <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious diagram), having bathed with a thousand <s>śamī</s>-leaves, gives birth to a son.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.8) atha pūrvāsv aṣāḍhāsu yā snāyād ahate paṭe | jātarūpeṇa kalyāṇī bhogaṃ bhuṅkte patipriyā ||
body.translated_text: Now, she who bathes under the <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] in an unworn cloth, the auspicious woman, devoted to her husband, enjoys pleasures with gold.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.9) athottarāsv aṣāḍhāsu yaḥ snāyāc ced upoṣitaḥ | mahāhrada uśīreṇa dāsīdāsena vardhate ||
body.translated_text: Now, he who bathes under the <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], having fasted, in a great lake with <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver grass), prospers with male and female servants.

body.text: (AVParis_1,44.10) vacayotpalakuṣṭhaiś ca brāhmī siddhārthakais tathā | abhijid brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ pārthivaṃ labhate yaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: With <s>vaca</s> (sweet flag), blue lotuses, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>brāhmī</s> along with mustard seeds — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> bathed under <s>Abhijit</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] obtains royal glory.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.1) śravaṇena sravantīnāṃ yaḥ snāyāt saṃgameṣu ca | sa saṃgacchati svarṇena hiraṇyena dhanena vā ||
body.translated_text: He who bathes under <s>Śravaṇa</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] at the confluences of flowing rivers — he comes together with gold, silver, or wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.2) śraviṣṭhābhir dhanakāmaṃ [tu] snāpayed yatra candanaiḥ | etat snānaṃ prayuñjāno dhanadhānyena vardhate ||
body.translated_text: Under the <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā) [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should bathe the one desiring wealth wherever [there are] sandalwoods; employing this bathing [rite], one prospers with wealth and grain.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.3) śatabhiṣag bhiṣakkāmo 'bhiṣiñcec chāntikarmasu | so 'bhiṣikto hatapāpmā sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one desiring to be a physician should perform anointment in pacification rites; thus anointed, with sins destroyed, one is freed from all diseases.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.4) [atha] pūrvayoḥ proṣṭhapadayo rocanayāñjanena ca | snātā gajaviṣāṇena rājānaṃ janayet sutam ||
body.translated_text: Under the two <s>Pūrva-Proṣṭhapadā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], with <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment) and collyrium, a woman bathed with an elephant's tusk should give birth to a son [who will be] a king.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.5) athottara[yoḥ] proṣṭhapadayoḥ prasannāpadmakaṃ madhu | gandharvaṃ snāpayet tena rājavāhī bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Under the two <s>Uttara-Proṣṭhapadā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], [with] clear lotus-honey, one should bathe the <s>gandharva</s> (musician) with that; he will become a bearer of kings.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.6) khaḍgasya ca viṣāṇena jalena madhusarpiṣā | revatyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ snāto [rājā] pṛthivīm abhiśāsate ||
body.translated_text: With a rhinoceros horn, water, honey, and clarified butter, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> bathed under <s>Revatī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] rules the earth as king.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.7) aśvinyāṃ svastikaṃ mālyaṃ madayantīpriyaṅgubhiḥ | rūpājīvāyās tat snānaṃ saubhāgyaṃ bhogavardhanam ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Aśvinī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], with an auspicious <s>svastika</s> garland, with <s>madayantī</s> and <s>priyaṅgu</s> [herbs] — that bathing is for a woman who lives by her beauty, for good fortune and the increase of enjoyments.

body.text: (AVParis_1,45.8) bharaṇībhir bhadramustais tv elāsiddharthakais tathā | snātā patikulaṃ gacched asapatnam akaṇṭakam ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Bharaṇī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], with auspicious <s>musta</s> grass, <s>elā</s> (cardamom), and mustard seeds likewise — a woman who has bathed should go to her husband's family, free from co-wives, free from thorns.

body.text: (AVParis_1,46.1) sarvajñaḥ sarvaga śaṃsa nārada prajñānam anyasmād anūnaprajñāt svargasya lokasya dehādyairyāt pathibhir upapanno manuṣyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: O all-knowing, all-pervading <s>Nārada</s>, proclaim! By what paths, endowed with wisdom no less than another's, does a man attain the world of heaven with his body and the rest?

body.text: (AVParis_1,46.2) upoṣitaḥ śuciśīlaḥ puṇyagandho yadā bhavet | prāg astaṃgamanabhojanād yad enaṃ nityam atandritaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When one has fasted, is of pure conduct, and of holy fragrance — before sunset, [partaking of] food, one who is always unwearied,

body.text: (AVParis_1,46.3) samayācārapūrvābhiḥ karmasiddhiḥ praśasyate | [taṃ] kāmadughaṃ svargakāmaḥ paretya pratipadyate ||
body.translated_text: Success in action is praised when preceded by observances and proper conduct; the one desiring heaven, departing, attains the wish-fulfilling [realm].

body.text: (AVParis_1,47.1) kṛttikābhiḥ pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā saha bhojayet | [taṃ] kāmadughaṃ svargakāmaḥ paretya pratipadyate ||
body.translated_text: Under the <s>Kṛttikā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should feed [a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] rice pudding with clarified butter; the one desiring heaven, departing, attains the wish-fulfilling [realm].

body.text: (AVParis_1,48.1) rohiṇyām akṣatair māṣaiḥ sarpirmiśraṃ sahaudanam | dugdhānnapāna[[ṃ]] maṃheta so 'kṣato yamasādane ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Rohiṇī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should offer rice mixed with clarified butter along with unbroken grains and <s>māṣa</s> (black gram); milk-food and drink — he [goes] unharmed to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

body.text: (AVParis_1,48.2) mṛgaśirasi maṃheta ajāṃ dhenuṃ payasvinīm | sāsmai sarvān kāmān dugdh[v]ā eti pūrvā payasvinī ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should offer a she-goat and a milch cow; she, having milked all desires for him, goes forth as a milch cow.

body.text: (AVParis_1,48.3) ārdrāyāṃ kṛsaraṃ dadyāt tailamiśram upoṣitaḥ | punarvasubhyāṃ maṃheta madhvapūpāṃs tv anuttamān ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Ārdrā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give <s>kṛsara</s> (a grain dish) mixed with sesame oil, having fasted; under the two <s>Punarvasu</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], one should offer unsurpassed honey-cakes.

body.text: (AVParis_1,48.4) rukmaṃ puṣyeṇa maṃheta so 'kṣato yamasādane | aśleṣā rajataṃ dadyāt saurabheyeṇa preṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should offer gold under <s>Puṣya</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] — he [goes] unharmed to <s>Yama</s>'s abode; under <s>Āśleṣā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give silver, dispatched by the <s>Surabhī</s> (divine cow),

body.text: (AVParis_1,48.5) sarpān nirhanti pretasya paripanthi sukhād bhayāt | maghābhis tu tilān dadyān madhumiśrān smaran pitṝn ||
body.translated_text: Which removes the serpents of the deceased, [protecting] from danger to comfort on the path; under <s>Maghā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give sesame mixed with honey, remembering the ancestors.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,48.6) kāmais tatropatiṣṭhanti amī ye somayājinaḥ | [phāṇiteneṣṭakā miśrā dadyāt pūrvayoḥ phalgunyor madhunottarayoḥ ||]
(AVParis_1,48.7) pūrvottarayoḥ phalgunyor duhate madhuphāṇite ||
body.translated_text: Desires attend those there who are performers of <s>Soma</s> sacrifices; [one should give bricks mixed with jaggery under the two <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>s and honey under the two <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>s;] under the two <s>Pūrva</s>- and <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], one milks honey and jaggery.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.1) bṛhaddhastirathaṃ yuktaṃ hastena tu dadan naraḥ | savituḥ sthānam āpnoti divyāṃ kāmajavāṃ sabhām ||
body.translated_text: A man who gives a great elephant-chariot, yoked, along with an elephant — he attains the station of <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), the divine assembly [moving] swift as desire.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.2) citrāyāṃ vṛṣalīṃ dadyāt sarvapuṣpair alaṃkṛtām | gandhaiḥ śuśrūṣamāṇas tu dhruve sthāne [sugandhiḥ] prapadyate ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Citrā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a <s>Śūdra</s> woman adorned with all flowers; serving with fragrances, one attains a permanent, fragrant station.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.3) svātāv ekadhanaṃ dadyād yadyad asya priyaṃ gṛhe | asajjamāno gaccheta aśarīro yathā manaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Svāti</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a single possession — whatever is dear to him in the house; unattached, he should go like the mind without a body.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.4) dhenuṃ tu rūpasaṃpannām anaḍvāhau tu vā vahau | viśākhābhyāṃ madhumanthaṃ prāpayet sthānam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: A cow endowed with beauty, or two draft oxen that carry loads — under the two <s>Viśākhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s, with] honey-drink, one attains the supreme station.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.5) anūrādhāsu prāvaraṇam annaṃ tu śuci jyeṣṭhāyāṃ ca | dadyāc cānnaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo bhakṣair uccāvacaiḥ saha ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Anurādhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], a covering-garment, and pure food under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>; one should give food to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s along with various delicacies.

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.6) surā[[ṃ]] mūlena maṃhetābrāhmaṇībhya upoṣitaḥ | mātus tenānṛṇo bhavati saṃkarāc ca vimucyate ||
body.translated_text: Having fasted, one should offer liquor with [the] <s>Mūla</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] to non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women; by that, one becomes free from debt to one's mother and is released from mixed [impurity].

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.7) udamantham aṣāḍhāsu pūrvāsu madhunottaram ||
body.translated_text: Under the <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], a water-churn [should be given]; with honey under the <s>Uttara</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>].

body.text: (AVParis_1,49.8) abhijid duhitaraṃ dadyān madhuparkapurogamām | uttame brahmaṇaḥ sthāne sarvakāmaiḥ pramodate ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Abhijit</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a daughter, preceded by a honey-offering; in the supreme station of <s>Brahman</s>, one rejoices with all desires fulfilled.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.1) kambalaṃ śravaṇe dadyād vastrāntaram upoṣitaḥ | śraviṣṭhābhir vastrayugaṃ gandhān śatabhiṣag bhavet ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Śravaṇa</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a blanket and an additional garment, having fasted; under <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, a pair of garments; under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, fragrances.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.2) ajaṃ saṃpacyodanaṃ dadyāt pūrvayoḥ proṣṭhapadayor aurabhreṇa sahottarayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should cook a goat and give rice under the two <s>Pūrva-Proṣṭhapadā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s]; with a ram under the two <s>Uttara</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s].

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.3) dhenuṃ ca rūpasaṃpannāṃ gaur gṛṣṭiḥ pūrṇadohanīm | revatyāṃ trivatsāṃ dadyāc chubhakāṃsyopadohinīm ||
body.translated_text: A beautiful cow — a cow that has calved, yielding a full pail — under <s>Revatī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a three-year-old [cow] with a good bronze milking vessel.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.4) vastreṇānaḍvāhau [saṃ]baddhvā dadyād aśvayujo<r> naraḥ | daśa varṣasahasrāṇi lomnilomni mahīyate ||
body.translated_text: A man who gives two draft oxen bound with a cloth under <s>Aśvayuj</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>] — for ten thousand years, hair by hair, he is glorified.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.5) aṣṭau varṣasahasrāṇi ajadhenvā payo 'śnute | daśa varṣasahasrāṇi godhenvā payo 'śnute ||
body.translated_text: For eight thousand years, one enjoys the milk of a goat-cow; for ten thousand years, one enjoys the milk of a cow.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.6) anaḍvāhaṃ tu yo dadyāt suhṛdaṃ sādhuvāhinam | vīraṃ prajānāṃ bhartāraṃ prāpnoti daśadhenudam ||
body.translated_text: He who gives a draft ox — a good friend, a good carrier — a hero, a sustainer of offspring, he attains [the merit of] one who gives ten cows.

body.text:
(AVParis_1,50.7) [yadā vatsasya pādau dvau śiras cāpi pradṛśyate | tadā gauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvad garbhaṃ na muñcati ||]
(AVParis_1,50.8) bharaṇībhiḥ kṛṣṇatilāṃ dadyāt [tila]dhenuṃ payasvinīm | tayā durgāṇi tarati kṣuradhārāṃś ca parvatān ||
body.translated_text: [When two feet of the calf and also its head become visible, then the cow should be known as 'Earth' as long as she does not release the embryo.] Under <s>Bharaṇī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], one should give a milch cow of black sesame [i.e., a sesame-cow]; by her, one crosses over difficulties and mountains of razor-edges.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.9) nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathā somo jyotiṣām iva bhāskaraḥ | bhāti divyaṃ divaṃ jyotiḥ pāvakaḥ śucir uttamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: As <s>Soma</s> is among the <s>nakṣatra</s>s, as the sun is among the luminaries — the divine light shines in heaven, <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire), pure, supreme.

body.text: (AVParis_1,50.10) evam uktāṃ nakṣatradakṣiṇāṃ yo dadātīha jīvaloke | [[a]]pahatya tamaḥ sarvaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate | yathā yaṣṭus tathādhyetur eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, he who gives the prescribed <s>nakṣatra</s>-gift in this world of the living — having dispelled all darkness, he is glorified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. As the sacrificer has [performed], so he should attain — this is the sacred promise of <s>Brahman</s>, this is the sacred promise of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_1b. [kṛttikārohiṇīmadhye paippalādā mantrāḥ])
(AVParis_1b,1.1) oṃ yad rājānaṃ śakadhūmaṃ nakṣatrāṇy akṛṇvata | bhadrāham asmai prāyacchan tato rāṣṭram ajāyata ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 1b: <s>Paippalāda</s> mantras [between <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>]) When the <s>nakṣatra</s>s made <s>Śakadhūma</s> king, they gave him an auspicious day; thence a kingdom was born.

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.2) bhadrāham astu naḥ sāyaṃ bhadrāhaṃ prātar astu naḥ | bhadrāham asmabhyaṃ tvaṃ śakadhūma sadā kṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: May there be an auspicious day for us in the evening; may there be an auspicious day for us in the morning; O <s>Śakadhūma</s>, always make an auspicious day for us.

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.3) yo no bhadrāham akaraḥ sāyaṃ prātar atho divā | tasmai te nakṣatrarāja śakadhūma sadā namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: You who made an auspicious day for us — evening, morning, and also by day — to you, O king of <s>nakṣatra</s>s, <s>Śakadhūma</s>, always [our] salutation!

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.4) yad āhuḥ śakadhūma[[ṃ]] mahānakṣatrāṇāṃ prathamajaṃ jyotir agre | tan naḥ śatīm abhikṛṇotu rayiṃ ca naḥ sarvavīraṃ niyacchāt ||
body.translated_text: What they call <s>Śakadhūma</s>, the first-born light of the great <s>nakṣatra</s>s, foremost — may it produce a hundredfold wealth for us and bestow upon us progeny with all heroes.

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.5) yo 'smin yakṣma[[ḥ]] puruṣe praviṣṭa iṣitaṃ daivyaṃ sahaḥ | agniṣ ṭaṃ ghṛtabodhano 'paskanda no vidūram asmat so 'nyena samṛcchāt || tasmai prasuvāmasi ||
body.translated_text: Whatever disease has entered this man, the sent divine force — may <s>Agni</s>, awakened by clarified butter, drive it away; far from us, may it join with another! To that [disease] we consign [this offering].

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.6) yas tvā mātur uta vā pituḥ parijāyamānam abhisaṃbabhūva | na tvad yam adhināsayāma so 'nyasmai sayātaiḥ praviṣṭaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever [evil] beset you as you were being born, from mother or from father — we shall not let it rest upon you; let it, having entered, depart to another.

body.text: (AVParis_1b,1.7) aliklavā gṛdhrāḥ kaṅkāḥ suparṇāḥ śvāpadāḥ patatriṇo vayāṃsi śakunayo 'muṣyāmusyāyaṇasyāmuṣyāḥ putrasyādahane carantu ||
body.translated_text: Let vultures, kites, eagles, beasts of prey, winged creatures, and birds move about at the cremation-ground of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, [born of] such-and-such [mother].

body.text: kṛttikārohiṇīmadhye paippalādā mantrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [These are] the <s>Paippalāda</s> mantras between <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_2. rāṣṭrasaṃvargaḥ)
(AVParis_2,1.1) om | brahmaṇe brahmavedāya rudrāya parameṣṭhine | namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi śeṣam ātharvaṇaṃ vidhim ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 2: <s>Rāṣṭrasaṃvarga</s> [Conquest of the Kingdom]) Oṃ. Having saluted <s>Brahmā</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme), I shall declare the remaining Atharvan rite.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.2) daivaṃ prabhavate śreṣṭhaṃ hetumātraṃ tu pauruṣam | daivena tu suguptena śakto jetuṃ vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: The divine prevails as supreme; human effort is merely an instrument. But with the divine well-guarded, one is able to conquer the earth.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.3) daivāt puruṣakārāc ca daivam eva viśiṣyate | tasmād daivaṃ viśeṣeṇa pūjayet tu mahīpatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Between the divine and human effort, the divine alone is superior; therefore the king should worship the divine with special attention.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.4) daivakarmavidau tasmāt sāṃvatsarapurohitau | gṛhṇīyāt satataṃ rājā dānasaṃmānarañjanaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore the king should always secure the <s>sāṃvatsara</s> (astronomer-priest) and the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest), who know divine and ritual action, with gifts, honors, and favors.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.5) apitā tu yathā bālas tathāsāṃvatsaro nṛpaḥ | amātṛko yathā bālas tathātharvavivarjitaḥ || arimadhye yathaikākī tathā vaidyavivarjitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: A king without a <s>sāṃvatsara</s> is like a child without a father; one deprived of Atharvan [knowledge] is like a child without a mother; one deprived of a physician is like one alone amidst enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.6) dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vijayiṣyan mahīpatiḥ | vidyālakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ bhārgavaṃ varayed gurum ||
body.translated_text: A king desiring to conquer the entire earth through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) should choose as his <s>guru</s> (preceptor) a <s>Bhārgava</s> (descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>) endowed with learning and auspicious marks.

body.text: (AVParis_2,1.7) caturvidhasya karmaṇo vedatattvena niścayam | prajāpatir athaiko hi na vedatrayam īkṣate ||
body.translated_text: For the determination of the fourfold ritual action according to the truth of the <s>Veda</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> alone [is the authority] — the three <s>Veda</s>s do not comprehend [it].

body.text: (AVParis_2,2.1) atharvabhinnaṃ yac chāntaṃ tac chāntaṃ netarais tribhiḥ | vijñānaṃ triṣu lokeṣu jāyate brahmavedataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever is pacified through the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, that is [truly] pacified — not through the other three. Knowledge in the three worlds arises from the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (Atharvaveda).

body.text: (AVParis_2,2.2) atharvā sṛjate ghoram adbhutaṃ śamayet tathā | atharvā rakṣate yajñaṃ yajñasya patir aṅgirāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Atharvaveda</s> creates the terrible, and it pacifies the wondrous likewise; the <s>Atharvaveda</s> protects the sacrifice, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> is the lord of the sacrifice.

body.text: (AVParis_2,2.3) divyāntarikṣabhaumānām utpātānām anekadhā | śamayitā brahmavedajñas tasmād rakṣitā bhṛguḥ ||
body.translated_text: The one who knows the <s>Brahmaveda</s> is the pacifier of celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents in many ways; therefore <s>Bhṛgu</s> is the protector.

body.text: (AVParis_2,2.4) brahmā śamayen nādhvaryur na chandogo na bahvṛcaḥ | rakṣāṃsi rakṣati brahmā brahmā tasmād atharvavit ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> [priest] should pacify — not the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, not the <s>Chandoga</s> (Sāmaveda priest), not the <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgveda priest). The <s>Brahman</s> protects against <s>Rākṣasa</s>s; therefore the <s>Brahman</s> is the knower of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,2.5) senāyā rakṣaṇe tasmāt svarāṣṭraparivṛddhaye | śāntyarthaṃ ca mahīpālo vṛṇuyād bhārgavaṃ gurum ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the protection of the army and the prosperity of his own kingdom, and for the purpose of pacification, the king should choose a <s>Bhārgava</s> as his <s>guru</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,3.1) gurave pārthivo dadyāt kotiṃ varaṇadakṣiṇām | ardhamardhaṃ mahībhāgaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu tribhāgataḥ ||
body.translated_text: The king should give to the <s>guru</s> a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million [coins]) as the gift of selection; half, half a portion of land, or a third in three parts.

body.text: (AVParis_2,3.2) evaṃ bhūmipramāṇena koṭibhāgaṃ vinirdiśet | yena vā parituṣyeta gurus tat pārthivaś caret ||
body.translated_text: Thus, according to the measure of the land, he should assign a <s>koṭi</s>-portion; or whatever satisfies the <s>guru</s>, that the king should do.

body.text: (AVParis_2,3.3) ghnanti daivopasargāś ca na ca devo 'bhivarṣati | vīrās tatra na sūyante yad rāṣṭram apurohitam ||
body.translated_text: Divine afflictions strike, and the god does not send rain; heroes are not born there — in a kingdom without a <s>purohita</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,3.4) na haviḥ pratigṛhṇanti devatāḥ pitaro dvijāḥ | tasya bhūmipater yasya gṛhe nātharvavid guruḥ ||
body.translated_text: The deities, ancestors, and twice-born do not accept the oblations of that king in whose house there is no <s>guru</s> versed in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,3.5) samāhitāṅgapratyaṅgaṃ vidyācāraguṇānvitam | paippalādaṃ guruṃ kuryāc chrīrāṣṭrārogyavardhanam ||
body.translated_text: One should appoint as <s>guru</s> a <s>Paippalāda</s> [priest] with well-composed limbs and sub-limbs [of knowledge], endowed with learning, conduct, and virtues — for the increase of prosperity, kingdom, and health.

body.text: (AVParis_2,4.1) tathā śaunakinaṃ vāpi vedamantravipaścitam | rāṣṭrasya vṛddhikartāraṃ dhanadhānyādibhiḥ sadā ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, a <s>Śaunaka</s> [priest], learned in Vedic mantras, who brings about the growth of the kingdom — [should be honored] always with wealth, grain, and the rest.

body.text: (AVParis_2,4.2) ātharvaṇād ṛte nānyo niyojyo 'tharvavid guruḥ | nṛpeṇa jayakāmena nirmito 'gnir ivādhvare ||
body.translated_text: None other than an <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Atharvavedic priest), a teacher learned in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, should be appointed by a king desirous of victory — like fire consecrated in a sacrifice.

body.text: (AVParis_2,4.3) bahvṛco hanti vai rāṣṭram adhvaryur nāśayet sutān | chandogo dhananāśāya tasmād ātharvaṇo guruḥ ||
body.translated_text: A <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgvedic priest) indeed destroys the kingdom; an <s>Adhvaryu</s> (Yajurvedic priest) causes the loss of sons; a <s>Chandoga</s> (Sāmavedic priest) [leads] to the loss of wealth — therefore the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> should be the preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_2,4.4) ajñānād vā pramādād vā yasya syād bahvṛco guruḥ | deśarāṣṭrapurāmātyanāśas tasya na saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He whose preceptor is a <s>Bahvṛca</s>, whether through ignorance or negligence — the destruction of his country, kingdom, city, and ministers is beyond doubt.

body.text: (AVParis_2,4.5) yadi vādhvaryavaṃ rājā niyunakti purohitam | śastreṇa vadhyate kṣipraṃ parikṣīṇārthavāhanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: If a king appoints a priest of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [school] as <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain), he is swiftly slain by weapons, with his wealth and vehicles diminished.

body.text: (AVParis_2,5.1) yathaiva paṅgur adhvānam apakṣī cāṇḍajo nabhaḥ | evaṃ chandogaguruṇā rājā vṛddhiṃ na gacchati ||
body.translated_text: Just as a lame man [cannot traverse] a road, and a wingless egg-born creature [cannot traverse] the sky, so a king does not attain prosperity with a <s>Chandoga</s> as his preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_2,5.2) purodhā jalado yasya maudo vā syāt kadā cana | abdād daśabhyo māsebhyo rāṣṭrabhraṃśaṃ sa gacchati ||
body.translated_text: He whose <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain) is a cloud-[like] (i.e., <s>Jalada</s> recension) or a <s>Mauda</s> (shaven) one at any time — within a year or ten months, he comes to loss of his kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_2,5.3) palālakam idaṃ sarvam ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃsthitam | sāraṃ sāraparaṃ dhānyam atharvāṅgiraso viduḥ ||
body.translated_text: All this, established in the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, is but chaff; the essence, the supreme essence, the grain — the knowers of the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> know.

body.text: (AVParis_2,5.4) trayo lokās trayo devās trayo vedās trayo 'gnayaḥ | ardhamātre layaṃ yānti vedaś cātharvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The three worlds, the three gods, the three <s>Veda</s>s, the three fires — they merge in the half-<s>mātrā</s> (the transcendent sound); and the <s>Veda</s> is recorded as the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,5.5) na tithir na ca nakṣatraṃ na graho na ca candramāḥ | atharvamantrasaṃprāptyā sarvasiddhir bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Neither <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) nor <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), neither planet nor moon [is needed] — by the attainment of <s>Atharvan</s> <s>mantra</s>s, all success will come about.

body.text: (AVParis_2,6.1) guruṇā paippalādena vedamantravipaścitā | vardhate dhanadhānyena rāṣṭram evaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: With a preceptor of the <s>Paippalāda</s> [school], learned in the <s>mantra</s>s of the <s>Veda</s>, the kingdom prospers with wealth and grain — of this there is no doubt.

body.text: (AVParis_2,6.2) stabdhaṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ pramattaṃ śraddhāhīnam aśāstragam | bhūmikāmo na yāceta dātāram api pārthivam ||
body.translated_text: One desirous of land should not petition even a generous king who is stubborn, cruel, heedless, lacking in faith, and unversed in the scriptures.

body.text: (AVParis_2,6.3) sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ japtvā gāyatryāyājyayājakaḥ | pūyate bhrūṇahāpy evaṃ cāṇḍālānnāda eva ca ||
body.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Gāyatrī</s> a hundred thousand times, the sacrificer with clarified butter is purified — even a slayer of an embryo, and even one who eats the food of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_2,6.4) sarvadravyaparityāgāc chuddhir anyair udāhṛtā | anyaiś caturṇāṃ vedānām adhītyādyottamā ṛcaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Purification through the renunciation of all possessions has been declared by others; by yet others, [purification comes] through studying the first and last verses of the four <s>Veda</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_2,6.5) yajanād abhicārād vā kva cid vā mantrakarmaṇi | pūtān eva dvijān prāhur agnikāñcanavarcasa iti ||
body.translated_text: Whether through sacrifice, through <s>abhicāra</s> (sorcery), or in any <s>mantra</s>-rite, they declare the twice-born to be purified, having the radiance of fire and gold — thus.

body.text: iti rāṣṭrasaṃvargaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Rāṣṭrasaṃvarga</s> (Acquisition of the Kingdom) is completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_3. rājaprathamābhiṣekaḥ)
(AVParis_3,1.1) om atha rājaprathamābhiṣeke prakṛtidravyāṇi parīkṣeta ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 3. The First Royal Consecration) Oṃ. Now, at the first royal consecration (<s>rāja-prathamābhiṣeka</s>), one should examine the natural substances.

body.text: (AVParis_3,1.2) tad yathā ||
body.translated_text: Namely, as follows:

body.text:
(AVParis_3,1.3) rathasiṃhāsanāsichattracāmaradhvajagajavājivastrālaṃkārasāṃvatsaracikitsakapurohitādīny
(AVParis_3,1.4) upayuktāni nopayojayet ||
body.translated_text: Chariot, lion-throne, sword, parasol, fly-whisk, banner, elephant, horse, garments, ornaments, the royal astrologer (<s>sāṃvatsara</s>), physician, <s>purohita</s> (chaplain), and the like — those that have been [previously] used should not be employed.

body.text:
(AVParis_3,1.5) śmaśānānaladevatāni nihitāni dravyāṇīty
(AVParis_3,1.6) ācāryapurohitavajramukhata ity āha durmatiḥ sa bhāradvājo
(AVParis_3,1.7) na hy agner ivopayuktasyopayogo vidyata iti parāśaro
(AVParis_3,1.8) brahmā brahmāṇḍāgnir ivāprameyo
(AVParis_3,1.9) nānyakulopayukto
(AVParis_3,1.10) yasyānyakulopayuktaḥ purodhāḥ śāntikapauṣṭikaprāyaścittīyābhicārikanaimittikordhvadehikāny atharvavihitāni karmāṇi kuryāt sa tasya pratyaṅgiro bhūtvā hastyaśvarathapadātikaṃ prakṛtimukhebhyo ...
(AVParis_3,1.11) variṣyan na punaḥ kuryād anyaṃ rājā purohitam | nirmālyam iva taṃ rājā nānyo bhūyaḥ samācaret ||
body.translated_text: Objects deposited at cremation-grounds, fire-shrines, or temples — thus says <s>Durmati</s>, that <s>Bhāradvāja</s>: 'The re-employment of used items, the teacher-chaplain as the chief authority.' But <s>Parāśara</s> says: 'Just as there is no reuse of fire once employed, [so too here].' '<s>Brahmā</s> is immeasurable, like the fire of the cosmic egg.' [Items] used by another lineage should not [be employed]. He whose <s>purohita</s> has been employed by another lineage — should he perform the rites prescribed by the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, namely <s>śāntika</s> (pacification), <s>pauṣṭika</s> (prosperity), <s>prāyaścittīya</s> (expiation), <s>ābhicārika</s> (sorcery), <s>naimittica</s> (occasional), and <s>ūrdhvadehika</s> (post-mortem) rites — he, having become a counter-<s>Aṅgiras</s> to him, [will cause loss of] elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry from the chief constituents of the state... One who will bestow [gifts] should not again appoint another as <s>purohita</s>; the king should not employ him again, like discarded ritual offerings.

body.text: (AVParis_3,1.12) svajasraṃ hy agnau hetur bhagavato vyādhitapatitonmattābhiśastaprahīṇapradhvastasaṃprasāraṇam ṛtvik ||
body.translated_text: For the perpetual fire is the cause; the priest of the blessed one [serves] in cases of the afflicted, the fallen, the insane, the accused, the expelled, the ruined, and the one to be restored.

body.text: (AVParis_3,1.13) tasmāt kulīnaṃ śrotriyaṃ bhṛgvaṅgirovidaṃ vinayākṛtiśaucācārayuktam alolupaṃ vrataniyamacāritravṛttalakṣanaguṇasaṃpannaṃ saṃdhivigrahacintakaṃ māhendrajālaprabhṛtikarmādiṣv abhividakaṃ jitasthānāsanaṃ himātapavarṣasahaṃ hrīdhṛtikam ārjavaṃ śamadamadayādānaśaktisaṃpannaṃ bṛhaspatyuśanasoḥ sthānākṛtipramāṇaṃ varṇāśrutavapuṣā cānumeyaṃ tejasvinaṃ gambhīraṃ sattvayuktaṃ guruṃ vṛṇīyād bhūpatir iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the king should choose as preceptor one who is of good family, learned in the <s>Veda</s>s (<s>śrotriya</s>), versed in the <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> traditions, endowed with discipline, proper form, purity, and good conduct, free from greed, possessed of vows, observances, character, conduct, marks, and virtues, a thinker on alliance and hostility, skilled in the rites beginning with the <s>Māhendrājāla</s> and others, who has conquered his seat and posture, who endures cold, heat, and rain, who has modesty and fortitude, who is upright, endowed with tranquility, self-control, compassion, generosity, and power, whose station, form, and authority are modeled on <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Uśanas</s> (<s>Śukra</s>), who is to be recognized by his complexion, learning, and appearance, who is brilliant, profound, endowed with courage — thus.

body.text:
(AVParis_3,1.14) madhuparkādyena vidhinā yathārthaṃ saṃpādya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāt
(AVParis_3,1.15) koṭimadhyāt tṛtīyaṃ bhāgam

children.text: (AVParis_3,1.16) yathābhūmipramāṇena vā
children.translated_text: Or according to the measure of the land,

children.text: (AVParis_3,1.17) hastyaśvaṃ narayānaṃ divyam ābharaṇam ātapatraṃ hiraṇyaṃ kṣitigodhanadhānyaratnādikaṃ ca gurave dadyād
children.translated_text: He should give to the preceptor an elephant and horse, a man-borne palanquin, divine ornaments, a parasol, gold, land, cattle, grain, jewels, and the like,

children.text: (AVParis_3,1.18) yena vā parituṣyeta ||
children.translated_text: Or whatever would satisfy him.

body.translated_text: Having duly accomplished [the appointment] with the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-offering) and other rites, he should give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee): a third from the middle of a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million),

body.text: (AVParis_3,1.19) abhiṣekaḥ saṃhitāvidhau vyākhyātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The consecration is explained in the ritual of the <s>Saṃhitā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_3,2.1) hastyaśvaṃ gurave dadyān narayānaṃ tathaiva ca | divyam ābharaṇaṃ caiva ātapatrādim eva ca ||
body.translated_text: One should give to the preceptor an elephant and horse, a palanquin likewise, divine ornaments, and a parasol and the rest.

body.text: (AVParis_3,2.2) ucchiṣṭārthaṃ na gṛhṇīyān maṅgalārthaṃ mahīpatiḥ | mantrauṣadhyo na sidhyanti rājā tatra vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: The king should not accept for auspicious purposes what has been used as leftovers; <s>mantra</s>s and medicines do not succeed [with such items], and the king perishes thereby.

body.text: (AVParis_3,2.3) nātidīrghaṃ nātihrasvaṃ nātisthūlaṃ kṛśaṃ tathā | na ca hīnātiriktāṅgaṃ kva cit kuryāt purohitam ||
body.translated_text: One should not make as <s>purohita</s> one who is too tall, too short, too stout, or too thin, nor one with deficient or excessive limbs in any way.

body.text: (AVParis_3,2.4) hīnādhikāṅgaṃ patitaṃ vivarṇaṃ stenaṃ jaḍaṃ klībam aśaktiyuktam | bhinnasvaraṃ kāṇaṃ virūpanetraṃ dveṣyaṃ ca rājā guruṃ naiva kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: One with deficient or excessive limbs, one who is fallen, discolored, a thief, dull, impotent, powerless, with a broken voice, one-eyed, or with deformed eyes, and one who is hateful — the king should never make such a one his preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_3,2.5) hīnādhikāṅge purarāṣṭrahāniḥ kāṇe jaḍe vāhanakośanāśaḥ | stene tv aśakte ca samastadoṣāḥ klībe vivarṇe nṛpatir vinaśyet ||
body.translated_text: With one of deficient or excessive limbs, there is loss of city and kingdom; with one who is one-eyed or dull, loss of vehicles and treasury; with a thief or powerless one, all faults [arise]; with an impotent or discolored one, the king perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.1) bhinnasvare jāyate gātrabhedo dveṣye gurau vipratipattim āhuḥ | vivarṇanetre patite tu putrān adhvaryuṇā ca nihanti pautrān ||
body.translated_text: With one of broken voice, bodily harm arises; with a hateful preceptor, they declare opposition; with one of discolored eyes or one who is fallen, [he destroys] sons; and with an <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he destroys grandsons.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.2) kṛṣṇe kośakṣayaṃ vidyād rakte vāhanasaṃkṣayaḥ | piṅgalaḥ pārthivaṃ hanyād rāṣṭraṃ hanyāt tu kekaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: With a dark one, one should know treasury-loss; with a red one, loss of vehicles; a tawny one destroys the king; a squint-eyed one destroys the kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.3) bahvṛcaṃ hi niyuñjyād yaḥ paurohitye tu pārthivaḥ | sa tārapaṅke hastīva saha tenaiva majjati ||
body.translated_text: A king who appoints a <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgvedic priest) to the office of <s>purohita</s> sinks together with him, like an elephant in a quagmire of palm-leaves.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.4) adhvaryuṃ hi niyuñjyād yaḥ paurohitye tu pārthivaḥ | uttitīrṣur ivāśmānam ādatte svavadhāya saḥ ||
body.translated_text: A king who appoints an <s>Adhvaryu</s> to the office of <s>purohita</s> — desiring to cross over, he picks up a stone for his own destruction.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.5) vadhabandhaparikleśaṃ kośavāhanasaṃkṣayaḥ | karoty etānvaye 'vasthās tapoyukto 'pi sāmagaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Slaughter, imprisonment, distress, loss of treasury and vehicles — a <s>Sāmaga</s> (Sāmavedic priest), even if endowed with austerity, brings these conditions upon the lineage.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.6) anvayākṛtisaṃpannaṃ tasmād bhṛgvaṅgirovidam | gotrāṅgirasavāsiṣṭhaṃ rājā kuryāt purohitam ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the king should make as <s>purohita</s> one endowed with lineage and proper form, versed in the <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> traditions, of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> or <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> <s>gotra</s> (lineage).

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.7) makheṣu rāṣṭreṣu pureṣu caiva senāsu rājñāṃ svaniveśaneṣu | ya utpātās trividhā ghorarūpās tān sarvān śamayed brahmavedavit ||
body.translated_text: In sacrifices, kingdoms, cities, armies, and in the king's own encampments — whatever terrible three-fold portents of dreadful form [arise], he who knows the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (Atharvaveda) should pacify them all.

body.text: (AVParis_3,3.8) tasmād guruṃ vedarahasyayuktaṃ caturvidhe karmaṇi cāpramattam | śāntaṃ ca dāntaṃ ca jitendriyaṃ ca kuryān narendraḥ priyadarśanaṃ ca || priyadarśanaṃ ceti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the king should appoint as preceptor one who is endowed with the secrets of the <s>Veda</s>, alert in the four-fold rites, peaceful, self-controlled, with conquered senses, and of pleasing appearance — of pleasing appearance indeed.

body.text: iti rājaprathamābhiṣekaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the First Royal Consecration (<s>Rāja-prathamābhiṣeka</s>) is completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_4. purohitakarmāṇi)
(AVParis_4,1.1) om atha purohitakarmāṇi || rājñaḥ prātar utthitasya kṛtasvastyayanasya
(AVParis_4,1.2) atha purohitaḥ snātānuliptaḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ soṣṇīṣaḥ savitā prasavānām iti vyākhyātam ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 4. Duties of the Royal Chaplain) Oṃ. Now the duties of the <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain): When the king has risen in the morning and the <s>svastyayana</s> (benediction) has been performed — then the <s>purohita</s>, bathed, anointed, pure, wearing white garments, with a turban — [recites] '<s>Savitā</s>, impeller of impulses' — thus it is explained.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.3) imam indra vardhayety uktam ||
body.translated_text: 'This one, O <s>Indra</s>, increase!' — thus it is declared.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.4) pari dhatteti dvābhyāṃ rājño vastram abhimantrya prayacchet ||
body.translated_text: With the two [verses beginning] '<s>pari dhatta</s>' (surround), having consecrated the king's garment with <s>mantra</s>s, he should present it.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.5) yad ābadhnann ity alaṃkārān ||
body.translated_text: 'That which you bind on' — [refers to] the ornaments.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.6) siṃhe vyāghra iti siṃhāsanam ||
body.translated_text: 'In the lion, in the tiger' — [refers to] the lion-throne.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.7) yas te gandha iti gandhān ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever fragrance is yours' — [refers to] the fragrances.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.8) ehi jīvaṃ trāyamāṇam ity akṣiṇī aṅkte ||
body.translated_text: 'Come, protecting the living one' — with this, he anoints the eyes.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.9) vātaraṃhā ity aśvam ||
body.translated_text: 'With the speed of the wind' — [refers to] the horse.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.10) hastivarcasam iti hastinam ||
body.translated_text: 'With the vigor of the elephant' — [refers to] the elephant.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.11) yat te mātā yat te piteti narayānam ||
body.translated_text: 'What your mother, what your father' — [refers to] the man-borne palanquin.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.12) khaḍgaṃ cābhimantrayāmīti khaḍgam ||
body.translated_text: 'And I consecrate the sword' — [refers to] the sword.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.13) khaḍgaṃ cābhimantrayāmi yaḥ śatrūn mardayiṣyati | marditāḥ śatravo 'nena vaśam āyāntu te sadeti ||
body.translated_text: 'And I consecrate the sword which shall crush the enemies; crushed by this, may the enemies always come under your control' — thus.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.14) paryaṅkam āsanaṃ khaḍgaṃ dhvajaṃ chattraṃ sacāmaram | ratham aśvagajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanur varma śareṣudhim ||
body.translated_text: The couch, seat, sword, banner, parasol with fly-whisk, chariot, the best horse and elephant, bow, armor, and quiver,

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.15) āñjanaṃ gandhamālyāni vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca | sarvān śāntyudakenaitān abhyukṣyec cābhimantrayet ||
body.translated_text: Collyrium, fragrances, garlands, garments, and ornaments — all these he should sprinkle with <s>śāntyudaka</s> (peace-water) and consecrate with <s>mantra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.16) dūrvādīn mūrdhni nikṣipya svastyayanair abhimantrayet | abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīty abhimantrito brāhmaṇān praṇipatya prāk ||
body.translated_text: Having placed <s>dūrvā</s> grass and the like on the head, he should consecrate with <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictions): 'Fearlessness from heaven and earth' — thus consecrated, he should bow to the Brahmins, facing east.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.17) yuṣmatprasādāc chāntim adhigacchāmīti ||
body.translated_text: 'By your grace, I attain peace' — thus.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.18) tathāstv ity ukto nirgacched iti ||
body.translated_text: Having been told 'So be it,' he should depart — thus.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.19) evaṃkṛtyasvastyayano yad evāvalokayati ta sidhyati ||
body.translated_text: Having performed the <s>svastyayana</s> rite in this manner, whatever he then looks upon succeeds.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.20) tad api ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: On this, there are also verses:

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.21) asuraiḥ pīḍyamānas tu purā śakro jagatprabhuḥ | kārayām āsa vidhivat purodhastve bṛhaspatim ||
body.translated_text: Long ago, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the lord of the world, being oppressed by the <s>Asura</s>s, had <s>Bṛhaspati</s> duly installed in the office of <s>purohita</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.22) sa vṛto bhayabhītena śamanārthaṃ bubhūṣatā | maṅgalāni sasarjāṣṭāv abhayārthaṃ śatakratoḥ ||
body.translated_text: He, chosen by the fear-stricken one who desired pacification, created eight auspicious [things] for the protection of <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.23) proktāni maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ | bhūmiḥ siddhārthakāḥ sarpiḥ śamī vrīhiyavau tathā ||
body.translated_text: The eight auspicious things proclaimed are: a Brahmin, a cow, fire, earth, mustard seeds, ghee, a <s>śamī</s> tree, and rice and barley.

body.text: (AVParis_4,1.24) etāni satataṃ puṇyāni saṃpaśyann arcayann api | na prāpnoty āpadaṃ rājā śriyaṃ prāpnoty anuttamām ||
body.translated_text: A king who constantly beholds and worships these auspicious things does not encounter calamity and attains supreme prosperity.

body.text:
(AVParis_4,2.1) atha rājakarmāṇi
(AVParis_4,2.2) viśvāvasau muhūrte snāto abhiṣekamantrair abhimantritaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, the royal rites: At the <s>muhūrta</s> (auspicious moment) of <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, having bathed, he is consecrated with <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) <s>mantra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.3) anulepanair anuliptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He is anointed with unguents.

body.text:
(AVParis_4,2.4) pūrvoktena vidhinā vastrālaṃkārādibhiḥ
(AVParis_4,2.5) suvarṇaniṣkaṃ kṛṣṇalaṃ vā vāmahastena saṃgṛhya ||
body.translated_text: According to the previously stated procedure, with garments, ornaments, and the like — grasping a gold coin or a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (black seed-weight) in the left hand,

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.6) yad duḥkṛtaṃ yac chabalaṃ sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ dahatv ity

children.text: (AVParis_4,2.7) anena mantreṇa suvarṇaṃ śarīre nighṛṣya dakṣiṇena hastena viprāya dadyād
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, having rubbed gold on the body, he should give [it] to a Brahmin with the right hand,

children.text: (AVParis_4,2.8) dhenuṃ cārogām
children.translated_text: And a milch cow in good health.

children.text: (AVParis_4,2.9) aparimitaguṇān tilān sauvarṇamaye tāmramaye vā pātre sthāpayitvā yad ajñānād ity abhimantrya viprāya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having placed sesame seeds of immeasurable quality in a golden or copper vessel, having consecrated with 'What through ignorance,' he should give [them] to a Brahmin.

body.translated_text: 'Whatever ill done, whatever impure — may it burn all sin' — thus,

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.10) yad ajñānāt tathā jñānād yan mayā śabalaṃ kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ tiladānena dahyatām iti hi prabho ||
body.translated_text: 'What through ignorance and likewise through knowledge has been done impure by me — may all that be burned through the gift of sesame' — thus, O lord.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.11) bhūmiś ca sasyasaṃpannā brāhmaṇe vedapārage | yathāśakti pradeyā hi bṛhaspativaco yathā ||
body.translated_text: And land rich with crops should be given to a Brahmin versed in the <s>Veda</s>s, according to one's ability, as per the word of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.12) sa bhuktvā vividhān bhogān saptasāgaramekhalām | pṛthivīṃ prāpya modeta candravat pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having enjoyed various pleasures, obtaining the earth girdled by the seven oceans, the lord of the earth would rejoice like the moon.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.13) annaṃ tu vividhaṃ nityaṃ pradadyāt dvijātaye | tūryaghoṣeṇa saṃyuktaḥ kṛtasvastyayanas tathā ||
body.translated_text: He should always give various foods to a twice-born; accompanied by the sound of musical instruments, having performed the <s>svastyayana</s> (benediction) likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.14) gṛhadevāṃs tu saṃpūjya kāryaś cāpy utsavo gṛhe | chattrādīni ca yānāni pūjayed vidhivat svayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,2.14) Having worshipped the household deities, a festival should also be held in the house. One should worship umbrellas and other conveyances ritually and by oneself.

body.text: (AVParis_4,2.15) [puṣpaiś ca vividhaiḥ śubhraiḥ phalaiś cāpy arcayed budhaḥ] tasmāt sarvāṇi satataṃ dānāni tu mahīpatiḥ | dattvā śraddhānvito viprair vṛto bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,2.15) [The wise one should worship with various bright flowers and fruits.] Therefore the king, endowed with faith, having given all manner of gifts constantly, surrounded by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, should eat in silence.

body.text: (AVParis_4,3.1) atha piṣṭamayīṃ rātriṃ caturbhir dīpakaiḥ saha | arcitāṃ gandhamālyena sthāpayet tasya cāgrataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.1) Then, one should place an image of Night made of flour, together with four lamps, honored with perfume and garlands, before him.

body.text: (AVParis_4,3.2) namas kṛtvā tato rātrim arcayitvā yathāvidhi | dhūpena cānnapānena stotreṇa ca samarcayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.2) Having bowed to Night and worshipped her according to rule, one should honor her with incense, food, drink, and a hymn of praise.

body.text: (AVParis_4,3.3) pāhi māṃ satataṃ devi sarāṣṭraṃ sasuhṛjjanam | uṣase naḥ prayacchasva śāntiṃ ca kṛṇu me sadā | ye tvāṃ prapadyante devi na teṣāṃ vidyate bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.3) "Protect me always, O Goddess, together with my kingdom and my friends and kinsmen. Grant us peace at dawn, and always bring me tranquility. Those who take refuge in you, O Goddess — for them there is no fear."

body.text: (AVParis_4.3.4) rātriṃ prapadye jananīṃ sarvabhūtaniveśanīm | bhadrāṃ bhagavatīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ viśvasya jagato niśām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.4) "I take refuge in Night, the mother, the resting-place of all beings — the auspicious, divine, dark Night of the entire world."

body.text: (AVParis_4,3.5) saṃveśanīṃ saṃyamanīṃ grahanakṣatramālinīm | prapanno 'haṃ śivāṃ rātriṃ bhadre pāram aśīmahi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.5) "She who brings rest, who brings restraint, who is garlanded with planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> — I have taken refuge in the auspicious Night; O blessed one, may we reach the far shore."

body.text: (AVParis_4,3.6) yāṃ sadā sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca | sāyaṃ prātar namasyanti sā māṃ rātry abhirakṣatv iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,3.6) "She whom all beings, both stationary and moving, honor at evening and at dawn — may that Night protect me."

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.1) ā rātri pārthivam iṣirā yoṣā trāyamāna ity rātryāṇi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.1) 'O Night,' 'the earthly,' 'the vigorous woman,' 'the protecting' — these are the night [hymns].

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.2) mamobhā mahyam āpa iti sūktābhyām anvālabhya japet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.2) Having touched [the king] with the two hymns beginning 'mine' and 'for me the waters,' one should mutter.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.3) yo na[[ḥ]] sva iti pañcabhiḥ sarṣapāñ juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.3) With the five [verses beginning] 'he who for us,' one should offer mustard seeds.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.4) yo 'smin yas tvā mātur iti dīpena nṛpasyopari triṣ parihṛtya praiṣakṛte prayacchet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.4) With 'he who is here' and 'you whose mother,' having carried a lamp over the king three times, one should give it to the appointed [person].

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.5) abhayam ity ṛcā catasraḥ śarkarāḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.5) With the verse 'fearlessness,' one should throw four pebbles clockwise in each direction.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.6) ehy aśmānam ā tiṣṭheti pañcamīm adhiṣṭhāpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.6) With the fifth [verse] 'come, stand upon this stone,' one should cause [him] to stand upon it.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.7) na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulukuṣṭhadūpaṃ dadyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.7) With 'may no disease approach him, O god,' one should offer incense of <s>guggulu</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.8) yas te gandhas tryāyuṣam iti bhūtiṃ prayacchet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.8) With 'your fragrance' and '<s>tryāyuṣa</s>' (triple-life), one should bestow prosperity.

body.text:
(AVParis_4,4.9) dūṣyā dūṣir asīti pratisaram ābadhya
(AVParis_4,4.10) agnir mā pātu vasubhiḥ purastād iti śarkarān pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.9) With 'you are the averter of harm, O averter,' one should tie on an amulet-cord. (AVParis_4,4.10) With 'may <s>Agni</s> protect me with the <s>Vasus</s> from the east,' one should throw pebbles clockwise in each direction.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.11) bahir niḥsṛtyottareṇa gatvā bāhyenopaniṣkramya suhṛde kuryāc chraddadhate kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.11) Having gone outside to the north, having departed by the outer [gate], one should perform [this rite] for a well-wisher, one who has faith.

body.text: (AVParis_4,4.12) naiśam abhayaṃ karma mausalīputraḥ paiṭhīnasiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,4.12) This is the nighttime fearlessness rite — [taught by] <s>Mausalīputra Paiṭhīnasi</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.1) athāto rātrisūktānāṃ vidhim anukramiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.1) Now then, we shall explain the procedure of the Night-hymns.

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.2) śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ purohitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.2) The <s>purohita</s> (royal priest), pure and wearing white garments —

body.text:
(AVParis_4,5.3) pārthivasya paścimāṃ saṃdhyām upāsya darbhaiḥ pavitrapāṇī rājānam abhigamya
(AVParis_4,5.4) piṣṭamayīṃ rātriṃ kṛtvā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.3) having performed the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) for the king, with <s>darbha</s> grass and purifying implements in hand, approaching the king — (AVParis_4,5.4) having made the flour-image of Night —

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.5) annapānadhūpadīpair arcayitvā mālyaiś ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.5) having worshipped with food, drink, incense, and lamps, and with garlands —

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.6) prajvalitaiś caturbhir dīpakair arcayitvā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.6) having worshipped with four blazing lamps —

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.7) ā rātri pārthivam iṣirā yoṣeti sūktadvayena rātrim upasthāya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.7) having attended upon Night with the two hymns 'O Night,' 'the earthly,' 'the vigorous woman' —

body.text:
(AVParis_4,5.8) trāyamāṇe viśvajite ahne ca tveti rājānaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ triḥ kṛtvā
(AVParis_4,5.9) rājaveśmani dvāre visarjayitvā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.8) with 'the protecting,' 'all-conquering,' and 'for the day also,' having circumambulated the king three times clockwise — (AVParis_4,5.9) having dismissed [the image] at the door of the royal residence —

children.text: (AVParis_4,5.10) na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulukuṣṭhadhūpaṃ dadyād
children.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.10) with 'may no disease approach him, O god,' one should offer incense of <s>guggulu</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>;

children.text: (AVParis_4,5.11) yas te gandha iti bhūtim abhimantrya
children.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.11) with 'your fragrance,' having consecrated the prosperity [offering];

children.text: (AVParis_4,5.12) tryāyuṣam iti rājñe rakṣāṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.12) with '<s>tryāyuṣa</s>' (triple-life), having made a protection for the king;

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.13) asapatnam iti śarkarām abhimantryāṅguṣṭhāt pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.13) with 'without rival,' having consecrated a pebble, one should throw it clockwise from the thumb in each direction.

body.text: (AVParis_4,5.14) śāntā dyaur iti japitvā rājānaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ nayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.14) Having muttered 'peaceful is the sky,' one should lead the king to the sleeping chamber.

body.text:
(AVParis_4,5.15) bhūtinā rakṣāṃ kṛtvā niṣkramya
(AVParis_4,5.16) evamevam aharahaḥ kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,5.15) Having made a protection with the prosperity [charm] and departed — (AVParis_4,5.16) thus one should perform day after day.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.1) yasya rājño janapade atharvā śāntipāragaḥ | nivasaty api tad rāṣṭraṃ vardhate nirupadravam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.1) In whose kingdom dwells an <s>Atharvan</s> priest who has mastered the peace-rites, that kingdom flourishes, free from calamity.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.2) yasya rājño janapade sa nāsti vividhair bhayaiḥ | pīḍyate tasya tad rāṣṭraṃ paṅke gaur iva majjati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.2) In whose kingdom he is absent, that kingdom, oppressed by various fears, sinks like a cow in the mire.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.3) tasmād rājā viśeṣeṇa atharvāṇaṃ jitendriyam | dānasaṃmānasatkārair nityaṃ samabhipūjayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.3) Therefore the king should especially honor with gifts, respect, and hospitality the <s>Atharvan</s> priest who has conquered his senses.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.4) nityaṃ ca kārayec chāntiṃ grahaṛkṣāṇi pūjayet | bhūmidohān prakurvīta devatāyataneṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.4) He should constantly have peace-rites performed, should worship the planets and <s>nakṣatras</s>, and should perform earth-milking rites at the temples of the deities.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.5) catuspatheṣu goṣṭheṣu tīrtheṣv apsu ca kārayet | gotarpaṇaṃ ca vidhivat sarvadoṣavināśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.5) At crossroads, in cowpens, at sacred fords, and in waters, he should have the cow-satisfaction rite performed according to rule — [it is] the destroyer of all evils.

body.text: (AVParis_4,6.6) ya evaṃ kārayed rājā sarvakālaṃ jitendriyaḥ | anantaṃ sukham āpanoti kṛtsnāṃ bhuṅkte vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_4,6.6) A king who has his senses conquered and who has [these rites] performed at all times attains infinite happiness and enjoys the entire earth.

body.text: iti purohitakarmāṇi samāptāni ||
body.translated_text: Thus the duties of the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) are completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_5. puṣyābhiṣekaḥ)
(AVParis_5,1.1) om atha puṣyābhiṣekasya vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpadam | dharmārthakāmasaṃyuktaṃ rājā kuryāt purohitam ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 5: The <s>Puṣyābhiṣeka</s> — Consecration under Puṣya) (AVParis_5,1.1) Oṃ. Now I shall declare the procedure of the <s>Puṣyābhiṣeka</s> (consecration under the Puṣya nakṣatra), yielding prosperity. The king should appoint a <s>purohita</s> endowed with <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_5,1.2) sauvarṇarājatais tāmraiḥ kalaśaiḥ pārthivair api | sahasreṇa śatenātha toyagrahaṇam iṣyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,1.2) With golden, silver, copper, and earthen vessels — a thousand or a hundred — the collection of water is prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_5,1.3) caturṇāṃ sāgarāṇāṃ tu nadīnāṃ ca śatasya tu | abhiṣekāya rājñas tu toyam āhṛtya yatnataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,1.3) For the consecration of the king, one should carefully bring water from the four oceans and from a hundred rivers.

body.text: (AVParis_5,1.4) ekadvitricaturṇāṃ vā sāgarasya tu pañcamam | oṣadhīs teṣu sarveṣu kalaśeṣūpakalpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,1.4) From one, two, three, or four [oceans], and the fifth from the sea. In all those vessels, one should prepare herbs.

body.text: (AVParis_5,1.5) sahā ca dahadevī ca balā cātibalā tathā | madayantī vacā śvetā vyāghradantī sumaṅgalā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,1.5) <s>Sahā</s>, <s>Dahadevī</s>, <s>Balā</s>, and <s>Atibalā</s> likewise, <s>Madayantī</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, <s>Vyāghradantī</s>, and <s>Sumaṅgalā</s> —

body.text: (AVParis_5,2.1) śatāvarī jayantī ca śatapuṣpā sacandanā | priyaṅgū rocano aśīram amṛtā ca sasārikā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,2.1) <s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Śatapuṣpā</s> with sandalwood, <s>Priyaṅgu</s>, <s>Rocana</s>, <s>Aśīra</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Sārikā</s> —

body.text: (AVParis_5,2.2) aśvatthaplakṣabilvānāṃ nyagrodhapanasasya ca | śirīṣāmrakapitthānāṃ pallavaiḥ samalaṃkṛtān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,2.2) adorned with the young shoots of <s>Aśvattha</s>, <s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, <s>Nyagrodha</s>, <s>Panasa</s>, <s>Śirīṣa</s>, <s>Āmra</s>, and <s>Kapittha</s> trees;

body.text: (AVParis_5,2.3) hemaratnauṣadhībilvapuṣpagandhādhivāsitān | ācchāditān sitair vastrair abhimantrya purohitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,2.3) perfumed with gold, gems, herbs, <s>bilva</s> flowers, and fragrance; covered with white cloths — the <s>purohita</s> having consecrated [them with mantras];

body.text: (AVParis_5,2.4) sāvitry ubhayataḥ kuryāc chaṃ no devī tathaiva ca | hiraṇyavarṇāḥ sūktaṃ ca anuvākādyam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,2.4) he should perform [the rite] with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> on both sides, and likewise with 'Auspicious to us, O Goddess,' and the <s>Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ</s> hymn, and the opening <s>anuvāka</s> also.

body.text: (AVParis_5,2.5) dharaṇī pādapīṭhaṃ syād dūrvāmūlāṅkurān śubhān | tasyopari nyaset pīṭhaṃ haimaṃ raupyam athāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,2.5) The earth should serve as the footstool; auspicious <s>dūrvā</s> grass-roots and sprouts [should be placed]; upon that one should place a seat of gold or silver.

body.text: (AVParis_5,3.1) anaḍudvyāghrasiṃhānāṃ mṛgasya ca yathākramam | catvāri carmāṇy etāni pūrvād ārabhya vinyaset ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,3.1) The four hides — of a bull, tiger, lion, and deer, in order — should be placed beginning from the east.

body.text: (AVParis_5,3.2) cāturhotravidhānena juhuyāc ca purohitaḥ | caturdikṣu sthitair viprair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,3.2) The <s>purohita</s> should offer oblations according to the <s>cāturhotra</s> (four-priest) procedure, with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> versed in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s> stationed in the four directions.

body.text: (AVParis_5,3.3) bilvāhāraḥ phalāhāraḥ payasā vāpi vartayet | saptarātraṃ ghṛtāśī va tato homaṃ prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,3.3) One should subsist on <s>bilva</s> fruits, or on fruits, or on milk; for seven nights one should eat ghee, and then perform the oblation.

body.text: (AVParis_5,3.4) gavyena payasā kuryāt sauvarṇena sruveṇa tu | vedānām ādibhir mantrair mahāvyāhṛtipūrvakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,3.4) One should perform [the oblation] with cow's milk, with a golden ladle, with the opening mantras of the <s>Vedas</s>, preceded by the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances).

body.text: (AVParis_5,3.5) śarmavarmā gaṇaś caiva tathā syād aparājitaḥ | āyuṣyaś cābhayaś caiva tathā svastyayano gaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,3.5) The groups [of mantras] are: <s>Śarman</s> (shelter), <s>Varman</s> (armor), <s>Gaṇa</s> (group), and likewise <s>Aparājita</s> (unconquered); <s>Āyuṣya</s> (life-giving), <s>Abhaya</s> (fearlessness), and likewise the <s>Svastyayana</s> (well-being) group.

body.text: (AVParis_5,4.1) etān pañca gaṇān hutvā vācayeta dvijottamān | hiraṇyenākṣatārgheṇa phalaiś ca madhusarpiṣā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,4.1) Having offered these five groups [of mantras], one should have the best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> recite, with gold, unbroken rice, water-offering, fruits, honey, and ghee.

body.text: (AVParis_5,4.2) puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvāsya ārambhaṃ kārayed budhaḥ | tiṣyanakṣatrasaṃyukte mahūrte karaṇe śubhe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,4.2) Having had the auspicious declaration pronounced, the wise one should commence the ritual at a <s>muhūrta</s> (auspicious moment) conjoined with the <s>Puṣya</s> (Tiṣya) <s>nakṣatra</s>, at an auspicious <s>karaṇa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_5,4.3) uccairghoṣa iti tūryāṇy abhimantrya purohitaḥ | sarvatūryaninādena abhiṣikto hy alaṃkṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,4.3) The <s>purohita</s>, having consecrated the musical instruments with 'Loud-sounding' [mantra], [the king] consecrated and adorned with the sound of all instruments,

body.text: (AVParis_5,4.4) siṃhāsanaṃ samāruhya pīṭhikāṃ vā yathākramam | cāmarachattrasaṃyuktaṃ pratihāravibhūṣitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,4.4) mounting a lion-throne or a seat in due order, equipped with a <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) and umbrella, adorned with attendants,

body.text: (AVParis_5,4.5) mattadvipacatuṣkaṃ ca caturdikṣu prakalpayet | upaviṣṭas tato rājā prajānāṃ kārayed dhitam | akarā brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ strībālajaḍarogiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,4.5) should arrange four elephants in rut in the four directions. Then the king, seated, should promote the welfare of his subjects. Exempt from taxation [should be]: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cows, women, children, the disabled, and the sick.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.1) tatas tu darśanaṃ deyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ nṛpeṇa tu | śreṇīprakṛtimukhyānāṃ strījanaṃ ca namaskaret ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.1) Then the king should grant audience to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, to the chiefs of the guilds and principal subjects, and should salute the womenfolk.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.2) āśiṣas te hi dāsyanti tuṣṭā janapadā bhuvi | evaṃ prajānurajyeta pṛthivī ca vaśā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.2) Being pleased, the people of the realm will give him blessings. Thus the subjects will be devoted, and the earth will be under his control.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.3) purohitaṃ mantriṇaṃ ca senādhyakṣaṃ tathaiva ca | aśvādhyakṣaṃ gajādhyakṣaṃ koṣṭhāgārapatiṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.3) The <s>purohita</s>, the minister, and the army-commander likewise, the superintendent of horses, the superintendent of elephants, and the keeper of the granary,

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.4) bhāṇḍāgārapatiṃ vaidyaṃ daivajñaṃ ca yathākramam | yathārheṇa ca yogena sarvān saṃpūjayen nṛpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.4) the keeper of the treasury, the physician, and the astrologer, in order — the king should honor all of them with appropriate means.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.5) rājyaṃ purohite nyasya śeṣāṇāṃ ca yathākramam | sthānāntarāṇi cānyāni dattvā sukham avāpnuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.5) Having entrusted the kingdom to the <s>purohita</s>, and the other [duties] in order, and having assigned other positions, he shall obtain happiness.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.6) dūrvāsiddhārthakān sarpiḥ śamīr vrīhiyavau tathā śuklāni caiva puṣpāṇi mūrdhni dadyāt purohitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.6) The <s>purohita</s> should place on the [king's] head <s>dūrvā</s> grass, mustard seeds, ghee, <s>śamī</s> leaves, rice and barley, and white flowers.

body.text: (AVParis_5,5.7) atharvavihito hy eṣa vidhiḥ puṣyābhiṣecane | rājā snāto mahīṃ bhuṅkte śakralokaṃ sa gacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_5,5.7) This procedure for the <s>Puṣyābhiṣeka</s> is enjoined by the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. A king who is bathed [in this consecration] enjoys the earth and goes to the world of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>).

body.text: iti puṣyābhiṣekaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Puṣyābhiṣeka</s>.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_6. piṣṭarātryāḥ kalpaḥ)
(AVParis_6,1.1) om athātaḥ piṣṭarātryāḥ kalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 6: The Ritual of the Flour-Night) (AVParis_6,1.1) Oṃ. Now then, we shall explain the ritual of the <s>Piṣṭarātrī</s> (flour-night image).

body.text:
(AVParis_6,1.2) ahatavāsāḥ purastāt talpasya gomayena sthaṇḍilam upalipya
(AVParis_6,1.3) ahatavastreṇa siṃhāsanam avachādya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.2) Wearing unworn garments, in front of the bed, having smeared a level surface with cow-dung — (AVParis_6,1.3) having covered the throne with an unworn cloth —

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.4) yāṃ devāḥ prati nandantīti rātrim āvāhayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.4) with 'She in whom the gods rejoice,' one should invoke Night.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.5) saṃvatsarasya pratimām iti piṣṭamayīṃ pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvodanmukhīm upaveśayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.5) With 'the likeness of the year,' having made a flour image, one should seat it facing east.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.6) chattraṃ hiraṇmayaṃ dadyād āsanaṃ ca hiraṇmayam | dadyāc chubhrāṇi vāsāṃsi śubhraṃ caivānulepanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.6) One should give a golden umbrella and a golden seat; one should give white garments and white ointment.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.7) śubhram annam atathā dadyāt prabhūtāṃś caiva modakān | dhūpaṃ ca vividhaṃ nityaṃ pradīpāṃś ca prakalpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.7) One should give white food and abundant sweetmeats; one should arrange various incense always and lamps.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.8) ā mā puṣṭe ca poṣe cety etābhir upasthāya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.8) Having attended upon [the image] with [the mantras] 'Come to me in nourishment and prosperity' —

children.text: (AVParis_6,1.9) rakṣoghnair mantraiḥ sarṣapān abhimantrya
children.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.9) having consecrated mustard seeds with <s>Rākṣasa</s>-destroying mantras —

children.text: (AVParis_6,1.10) āvatas ta iti japan samantāt talpasyāvakīrya
children.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.10) muttering 'from you,' having scattered [them] all around the bed —

children.text: (AVParis_6,1.11) ayaṃ pratisara iti pratisaram ābadhya śarkarān pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.11) with 'this is the amulet-cord,' having tied on the amulet-cord, one should throw pebbles in each direction.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.12) dhūpaśeṣaṃ rājñe dadyād ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.12) The remainder of the incense should be given to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.13) abhayapradaṃ karma ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.13) [This is] the rite that bestows fearlessness.

body.text: (AVParis_6,1.14) paścāt sarveṣu koneṣu dvimukhīm ekamukhīṃ vā | sarvato vijayāṃ rakṣām ekāṃ vā teṣu caturmukhīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.14) Afterward, in all corners, [one should place] a two-faced or one-faced [image]; or an all-conquering protective [image], or a single four-faced one among them.

body.text:
(AVParis_6,1.15) ekamukhīṃ vā sarvatrāpratirathajapa ity eke
(AVParis_6,1.16) sarvatra śarkarākṣepaś ceti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,1.15) Or a one-faced one everywhere — with the 'irresistible' muttering, according to some. (AVParis_6,1.16) And the throwing of pebbles [should be done] everywhere.

body.text:
(AVParis_6,2.1) gṛhītvā piṣṭarātriṃ tu veśmadvāre visarjayet
(AVParis_6.2.2) vanaspatir aso madhya iti guggulukuṣṭhadhūpaṃ dadyād

children.text: (AVParis_6,2.3) yas te gandha iti bhūtim abhimantrya
children.translated_text: Having consecrated the prosperity-offering with 'Whatever your fragrance,'

children.text: (AVParis_6,2.4) tryāyuṣam iti rājñe rakṣāṃ kṛtvā
children.translated_text: Having made a protective [amulet] for the king with 'Triple life-span,'

children.text: (AVParis_6,2.5) asapatnam iti śarkarān abhimantryāṅguṣṭhād [abhi]pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated the pebbles with 'Without rival,' one should throw [them] with the thumb, clockwise, in each direction.

body.translated_text: (AVParis_6,2.1) Having taken the flour-night [image], one should dismiss it at the door of the house. (AVParis_6,2.2) With 'O lord of the forest, in the middle,' one should offer incense of <s>guggulu</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_6,2.6) śāntā dyaur iti japitvā rājānaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ nayet ||
body.translated_text: Having recited 'The sky is pacified,' one should lead the king to the residence.

body.text:
(AVParis_6,2.7) bhūtinā rakṣāṃ kṛtvā niṣkramya
(AVParis_6,2.8) evamevam ahar ahaḥ kuryād iti || piṣṭarātryāḥ kalpaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having made the protective [rite] with the prosperity-offering, going out — thus one should do day after day. The procedure of the Flour-Night is completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_7. ārātrikam)
(AVParis_7,1.1) oṃ na suṣvāpa purā śakro dānavānāṃ purodhasā | prayuktair auṣadhair yogair mantrāṇāṃ japahomataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 7: The <s>Ārātrika</s> [Evening Lamp-Waving Rite]) Oṃ. Formerly, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) could not sleep, [being afflicted] by the <s>purohita</s> of the <s>Dānava</s>s, who employed herbs, yogic [spells], and the chanting and oblation of mantras.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.2) praṇipatya bṛhaspatim atharvāṇaṃ puraṃdaraḥ | dānavaiḥ paribhūto 'haṃ trāhi mām ity uvāca ha ||
body.translated_text: Having prostrated before <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) said: 'I am overcome by the <s>Dānava</s>s — save me!'

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.3) tato 'sāv evam uktas tu prabhūtabalavardhanam | ārogyadaṃ bhūtikaraṃ kṣudropadravanāśanam ||
body.translated_text: Then he (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>), thus addressed, [prescribed] that which increases abundant strength, grants health, produces prosperity, and destroys petty afflictions:

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.4) ārātrikaṃ hi kartavyaṃ tasya trātum idaṃ tadā | kṛtvā piṣṭamayaṃ dīpaṃ suvartisnehasaṃyutam ||
body.translated_text: The <s>ārātrika</s> (lamp-waving rite) must be performed to protect him at that time. Having made a lamp of flour, furnished with a good wick and oil,

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.5) ati nihaḥ prānyān iti dvābhyām enaṃ pradīpayet | pātre sapuṣpe saṃsthāpya sarṣapāṃś ca sahākṣataiḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should light it with the two [verses beginning] 'Beyond all others'; having placed it in a vessel with flowers, along with mustard seeds and unbroken rice,

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.6) priyaṅguṃ śatapuṣpāṃ ca dūrvāṃ caiva śatāvarīm | sapāpahāriṇīṃ bhūtiṃ tatraiva ca baliṃ nyaset ||
