body.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (millet), <s>śatapuṣpā</s> (dill), <s>dūrvā</s> (grass), and <s>śatāvarī</s> — one should place a <s>bali</s> (offering) there together with the sin-removing prosperity-offering.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.7) apsarobhiḥ parivṛto gurur gatvā puraṃdaram | prāptasattvaṃ sumanasam āsane prānmukhaṃ sthitam ||
body.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> (preceptor), surrounded by <s>Apsaras</s>es, having gone to <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who was of restored spirit, cheerful, seated facing east on his throne,

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.8) preto yantv ekaśataṃ ca dīpaṃ samabhimantrayet | triḥ paribhrāmayed rājño mantreṇātha sumaṅgalam ||
body.translated_text: Should consecrate the lamp with 'May the departed go, one hundred' [and similar mantras]; one should wave it thrice around the king with the auspicious mantra.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.9) śāmyanty asya tato rogā grahā vighnavināyakāḥ | svasty astu nrparāṣṭrāya svasti gobrāhmaṇāya ca ||
body.translated_text: Thereby his diseases, planetary afflictions, and obstacle-creators are pacified. May there be well-being for the king's kingdom, well-being for cows and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.10) tatas tu śaṅkhadhvaninā dīpaṃ gṛhītvā satoyadhārāṃ prayato 'pi nirharet | purohito jyotiṣiko 'pi vā svayaṃ hitaiṣinī dhātry atharvo (pakāritā ||
body.translated_text: Then, with the sound of a conch-shell, the <s>purohita</s> or the astrologer himself, holding the lamp with a continuous stream of water, should carry it out devotedly; or a well-wishing nurse versed in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.11) ācāmyātha ha rājānam ācamyādau purohitaḥ | brāhmaṇāya yathāśakti rukmaṃ prātaḥ pradāpayet ||
body.translated_text: Having sipped water, the <s>purohita</s> first [sipping], then the king sipping — one should have gold given to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the morning, according to one's ability.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.12) mūlakarmādikaṃ tasya pañcaguhyakakāritam | bhayaṃ rājño na bhavati tejo vīryaṃ ca vardhate ||
body.translated_text: The root-rites and the like, performed by the five <s>Guhyaka</s>s (secret beings) on his behalf — fear does not arise for the king, and his splendor and valor increase.

body.text: (AVParis_7,1.13) evaṃ vidhānam akhilaṃ vihitaṃ yathāvad etat samastaśubhadaṃ gaditaṃ nrpāṇām | naivāpadaḥ samupayānti nṛpaṃ kadā cid ārātrikaṃ pratiniśaṃ kriyate tu yasya || ity ārātrikaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: Thus the entire procedure, properly ordained, bestowing all auspiciousness, has been declared for kings. Calamities never approach a king for whom the <s>ārātrika</s> is performed every night. Thus the <s>ārātrika</s> is completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_8. ghṛtāvekṣaṇam)
(AVParis_8,1.1) om atha ghrtāvekṣaṇaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 8: Ghee-Gazing [<s>Ghṛtāvekṣaṇa</s>]) Oṃ. Now we shall describe the ghee-gazing [rite].

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.2) prātaḥprātaḥ śaṅkhadundubhinādena brahmaghoṣeṇa vā prabodhito rājā śayanagṛhād utthāyāparājitāṃ diśam abhiniṣkramyopādhyāyaṃ pratīkṣeta ||
body.translated_text: Morning after morning, awakened by the sound of conch and drum, or by the chanting of <s>Brahman</s>, the king should rise from the sleeping-chamber, go forth toward the invincible (northeast) direction, and await the preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.3) atha purohitaḥ snātānuliptaḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ krtamaṅgalaviracitoṣṇīṣī śāntigṛhaṃ praviśya devānāṃ namaskāraṃ kṛtvā svastivācanam anujñāpya vinītavad upaviśet ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>purohita</s>, having bathed, anointed, pure, wearing white garments, with auspicious preparations and turban arranged, should enter the pacification-chamber, pay homage to the gods, pronounce the benediction, and sit down humbly.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.4) yamasya lokād yathā kalāṃ yo na jīvo 'sīti svastyayanaṃ kṛtvollikhyābhyukṣya paristīrya śantātīyena tilān ghṛtāktān juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: With 'From <s>Yama</s>'s world' and 'As a digit' and 'He who is not alive' — having performed the auspicious rite, having drawn [the lines], having sprinkled, having strewn [the grass], one should offer sesame anointed with clarified butter using the <s>Śāntātīya</s> [hymn].

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.5) tān hutvā sauvarṇarājatam audumbaraṃ vā pātraṃ ghṛtapūrṇaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ ghṛtasya jūtiḥ sahasraśṛṅgo yamasya lokād uru viṣṇo vi kramasvety abhimantryājyaṃ teja iti tadālabhate ||
body.translated_text: Having offered those, [taking] a golden, silver, or <s>Udumbara</s> (fig-wood) vessel filled with clarified butter, together with gold, having consecrated it with 'The impetus of clarified butter,' 'The thousand-horned,' 'From <s>Yama</s>'s world,' and 'Widely stride, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — 'Clarified butter is splendor' — thus one touches it.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.6) ājyaṃ tejaḥ samuddiṣṭam ājyaṃ pāpaharaṃ param | ājyena devās trpyanti ājye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Clarified butter is declared to be splendor; clarified butter is the supreme remover of sin; the gods are satisfied by clarified butter; the worlds are established in clarified butter.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.7) bhaumāntarikṣadivyaṃ vā yat te kalmaṣam āgatam | sarvaṃ tad ājyasaṃsparśāt praṇāśam upagacchatv iti ||
body.translated_text: Whatever impurity has come upon you — terrestrial, atmospheric, or celestial — may all that, by contact with clarified butter, be utterly destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.8) tasmin ghṛtapātrasthaṃ hi sarvam ātmānaṃ ca paśyet ||
body.translated_text: In that ghee-vessel, one should see everything — including one's own self.

body.text: (AVParis_8,1.9) dadhnā śiro hṛdayam anvālabhya japet ||
body.translated_text: Having touched the head and heart with curds, one should recite:

children.text: (AVParis_8,1.10) uccā patantam iti dvābhyām
children.translated_text: With the two [verses beginning] 'Flying up high,'

children.text: (AVParis_8,1.11) sūryasyāvṛtam iti pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya śeṣaṃ kārayed ity
children.translated_text: With 'Enveloped by the sun' — having circumambulated clockwise, one should have the remainder performed.

children.text: (AVParis_8,1.12) atra ślokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On this, [here are the] verses:

body.text: (AVParis_8,2.1) ayaṃ ghṛtāvekṣaṇasya prokto vidhir atharvaṇā | upāsyo nityakālaṃ tu rājñā vijayakāṅkṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: This procedure of ghee-gazing has been declared by the <s>Atharvaveda</s>; it should be practiced at all times by a king who desires victory.

body.text: (AVParis_8,2.2) etat samāharet sarvaṃ prayatas tu samāhitaḥ | rājā vijayate rāṣṭraṃ naśyante tasya śatravaḥ ||
body.translated_text: One who performs all this, devoted and concentrated — the king conquers the kingdom, and his enemies are destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_8,2.3) dvijottamāya kapilāṃ rājā dadyāt tu gāṃ śubhām | āśīrvādaṃ tatas tena śrutvā tanmukhaniḥsṛtam ||
body.translated_text: The king should give a tawny auspicious cow to a foremost <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; then, having heard the blessing uttered from his mouth,

body.text: (AVParis_8,2.4) guruṇā vācito yasmād dīrgham āyur avāpnuyāt | putrān pautrāṃś ca maitrāṃś ca labhate nātrasaṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Because he is instructed by the <s>guru</s>, he obtains long life; he obtains sons, grandsons, and friends — there is no doubt in this.

body.text: (AVParis_8,2.5) āyuṣyam atha varcasyaṃ saubhāgyaṃ śatrutāpanam | duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ puṇyaṃ ghṛtāsyāvekṣaṇaṃ smṛtam iti || iti ghṛtāvekṣaṇaṃ samāptam || śrīsāmba | yamasya lokād adhy ābabhūvitha iti ṛcaḥ 6, yathā kalāṃ yathā śapham iti ṛcaḥ 6, ghṛtasya jūtir iti ṛcaḥ 4 ghṛtāvekṣaṇamadhye paippalādā mantrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: It is said to bestow long life, radiance, good fortune, and the tormenting of enemies; it destroys bad dreams; the gazing into the ghee-face is holy. Thus the ghee-gazing is completed. [Reference notes to <s>Paippalāda</s> mantras used in the ghee-gazing.]

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_9. tiladhenuvidhiḥ)
(AVParis_9,1.1) om atha tiladhenuṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśanīm | tilāḥ śvetās tilāḥ kṛṣṇās tilā gomūtravarṇakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 9: Procedure for the Sesame-Cow [<s>Tiladhenu</s>]) Oṃ. Now I shall declare the sesame-cow, which destroys all sins. [There are] white sesame, black sesame, and sesame of cow-urine color.

body.text: (AVParis_9,1.2) tilānāṃ tu vicitrāṇāṃ dhenuṃ vatsaṃ ca kārayet | droṇasya vatsakaṃ kuryāc caturdroṇā tu gauḥ smṛtā ||
body.translated_text: From sesame of various kinds, one should fashion a cow and a calf. The calf should be made of one <s>droṇa</s> (measure); the cow is said to be of four <s>droṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_9,1.3) suvāsāyāṃ śucau bhūmau dhūpapuṣpair alaṃkrtā | kṛṣṇājine tu kartavyā bahūnāṃ vāpi kārayet ||
body.translated_text: On well-scented, pure ground, adorned with incense and flowers, it should be made upon a black antelope skin; or one may make many.

body.text: (AVParis_9,1.4) karṇau ratnamayau kuryāc cakṣuṣī dīpakau tathā | ghrāṇe tu sarvagndhāṃs tu jihvāyāṃ śāradaṃ ghṛtam ||
body.translated_text: One should make the ears of gems, the eyes of lamps likewise, in the nostrils all fragrances, on the tongue fresh clarified butter,

body.text: (AVParis_9,1.5) danteṣu mauktikaṃ dadyāl lalāṭe tāmrabhājanam | ūdhasi tu madhūśīram apāne ca ghṛtaṃ madhu ||
body.translated_text: On the teeth pearls, on the forehead a copper vessel, on the udder honey and <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), and in the rear part clarified butter and honey.

body.text: (AVParis_9,2.1) hṛdaye candanaṃ dadyāj jaṅghayor ikṣukāṇḍakam | suvarṇaśṛṅgī raupyakhurī raupyalāṅgūladakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: On the heart one should place sandalwood, on the shanks sugarcane stalks; with golden horns, silver hooves, and a silver tail as the gift,

children.text: (AVParis_9,2.2) vastrachannā tu dātavyā kāṃsyapātraṃ tu dohanī |
children.translated_text: Covered with cloth it should be given; a bronze vessel serves as the milking pail.

children.text: (AVParis_9,2.3) prajāpatiś cety abhimantrya viprāya dadyāt
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it with '<s>Prajāpati</s>,' one should give it to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: (AVParis_9,2.4) tatra ślokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On this, [here are the] verses:

body.text: (AVParis_9,2.5) dhenuṃ vatsaṃ ca yo dadyād vinātharvābhimantritām | vinānena vidhānena devatvaṃ nopajāyate ||
body.translated_text: He who would give a cow and calf without Atharvan consecration, without this procedure — divinity does not arise.

body.text: (AVParis_9,2.6) viśvarūpāḥ sthitāḥ sarvā dhenavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ | dhenutvaṃ na sa prayāti vinā sūktābhimantritām | niṣphalaṃ naśyate sarvaṃ vinābhimantritaṃ satām ||
body.translated_text: All cows have been declared as established in the Universal Form; cow-hood does not occur without consecration by the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn). Everything without consecration by the righteous becomes fruitless and perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_9,2.7) bālatve yac ca kaumāre yat pāpaṃ yauvane kṛtam | vayaḥpariṇatau yac ca yac ca janmāntareṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was committed in childhood, in youth, in adolescence, and in the fullness of age, and in other births,

body.text: (AVParis_9,2.8) yan niśāyāṃ tathā prātar yan madhyāhnāparāhṇayoḥ | saṃdhyayor yat kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ karmaṇā manasā girā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever was done at night, likewise in the morning, at noon and in the afternoon, whatever sin was committed at the two twilights — by deed, mind, or speech —

body.text: (AVParis_9,3.1) prasūyamānāṃ yo dhenuṃ dadyād brāhmaṇapuṃgave | kṛṣṇājinaṃ guḍadhenuṃ ghṛtadhenuṃ tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: He who gives a cow at the time of birth to a foremost <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a black antelope skin, a jaggery-cow, a clarified-butter-cow likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_9,3.2) suvarṇaratnadhenuṃ ca jaladhenuṃ tathā parām | kṣīradhenuṃ madhudhenuṃ śarkarālavaṇaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: A gold-and-gem-cow, a water-cow, and the supreme milk-cow, a honey-cow, a sugar-cow, and a salt-cow likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_9,3.3) rasādidhenūḥ sarvānyā anena vidhinā smṛtāḥ | yat tu bālye kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yauvane caiva yat kṛtam ||
body.translated_text: Essence-cows and all others — all are prescribed according to this procedure. Whatever sin was committed in childhood and whatever in youth,

body.text: (AVParis_9,3.4) mānakūṭaṃ tulākūṭaṃ kanyānṛtagavānṛtam | udake ṣṭhīvitaṃ caiva musalaṃ cāpi laṅghitam ||
body.translated_text: Fraud in weights, fraud in scales, false oath about a maiden, false oath about cattle, spitting in water, and stepping over a mortar,

body.text: (AVParis_9,3.5) vṛṣalīgamanaṃ caiva gurudārāniṣevaṇam | surāpānasya yat pāpaṃ tiladhenuḥ praśāmyati ||
body.translated_text: Intercourse with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, and attendance upon the teacher's wife, the sin of liquor-drinking — the sesame-cow pacifies [all these].

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.1) yā sa yamapure ghore nadī vaitaraṇī smṛtā | yatra lohamukhāḥ kākāḥ śvānaś caiva bhayāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: That river in the terrible city of <s>Yama</s> known as <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, where there are iron-mouthed crows and terrifying dogs,

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.2) vālukāntāḥ sthalāś caiva pacyante yatra duṣkṛtaḥ | asipattravanaṃ yatra śālūkāḥ śālmalī tathā ||
body.translated_text: Where sinners are boiled in sandy wastelands, where there is the sword-leaf forest, and the <s>Śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) trees likewise —

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.3) tān sukhena vyatikramya dharmarājāśramaṃ vrajet | svāgataṃ te mahābhāga svasti te 'stu mahāmate ||
body.translated_text: Having crossed all these with ease, one should go to the hermitage of the King of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yama</s>). 'Welcome, O greatly fortunate one! May there be well-being for you, O greatly wise one!'

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.4) vimānam etad yogyaṃ te maṇiratnavibhūṣitam | atrāruhya naraśreṣṭha gaccha tvaṃ paramāṃ gatim ||
body.translated_text: 'This celestial car is fit for you, adorned with jewels and gems. Mount it, O best of men, and go to the supreme destination.'

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.5) mā ca cārabhaṭe dadyān mā ca dadyāt purohite | mā ca kāṇe virūpe ca kuṣṭhivyaṅge tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: One should not give [the sesame-cow] to a soldier, nor to a <s>purohita</s>, nor to one who is one-eyed, deformed, leprous, or having bodily marks,

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.6) vedāntagāya dātavyā vedāntagasutāya vā | ekaikasmai ca dātavyā māghamāse tu pūrṇimām ||
body.translated_text: It should be given to one who has studied the <s>Vedānta</s>, or to the son of such a one; it should be given to each one on the full moon of the month of <s>Māgha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_9,4.7) ya imāṃ paṭhate nityaṃ yaś cemāṃ śṛṇuyād api | devalokam atikramya sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati || sūryalokaṃ sa gacchatīti || iti tiladhenuvidhiḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He who reads this always, and he who hears it too — having transcended the world of the gods, he goes to the world of the Sun. He goes to the world of the Sun. Thus the procedure for the sesame-cow is completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_10. bhūmidānam)
(AVParis_10,1.1) om atha rohiṇyāṃ sakalāyām upoṣito brahmā sarvabījarasaratnagandhāvakīrṇaṃ tīrthodakapūrṇakalaśam ādāyātisṛṣṭo apām ity abhiṣekamantrair yathoktair dātāram abhiṣiñcati ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 10: Gift of Land [<s>Bhūmidāna</s>]) Oṃ. Now, on an entire [day under] <s>Rohiṇī</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], having fasted, the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], taking a vessel filled with <s>tīrtha</s>-water (sacred water) strewn with all seeds, juices, gems, and fragrances, with 'Released of the waters' — anoints the donor with the consecration-mantras as prescribed.

body.text:
(AVParis_10,1.2) vratena tvaṃ vratapata iti vratam upaiti
(AVParis_10,1.3) yācitāradātārāv ayācitāśināv adhahśāyinau bhavato

children.text: (AVParis_10,1.4) vratopacāram
children.translated_text: The observance of the vow [continues].

children.text: (AVParis_10,1.5) yathāśaktyaikarātraṃ pañcarātraṃ dvādaśarātraṃ vā vrataṃ caritvā
children.translated_text: Having practiced the vow for one night, five nights, or twelve nights, according to one's ability,

children.text: (AVParis_10,1.6) śvo bhūte tantram ājyabhāgāntaṃ kṛtvānvārabhyātha juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: On the next day, having performed the <s>tantra</s> (ritual procedure) up to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions), having touched [the fire], one should then offer oblations.

body.translated_text: With 'By the vow, O lord of vows' — he undertakes the vow. The supplicant and the donor should sleep on the ground and eat without being asked.

body.text:
(AVParis_10,1.7) kāmasūktaṃ kālasūktaṃ puruṣasūktaṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ saṃkhyāpūrvikābhiḥ sarva ṛtvijo juhvaty
(AVParis_10,1.8) atha suvarṇamayīṃ bhūmiṃ bhūmeḥ pratikṛtiṃ gocarmamātrāṃ kṛtvā
(AVParis_10,1.9) maṇḍapavedyāṃ samānīya vedyuttarato yasyāṃ vedim ity upasthāpya
(AVParis_10,1.10) girayas te parvatā iti parvatān avasthāpya
(AVParis_10,1.11) hiraṇyarajatamaṇimuktāpravālādibhir upaśobhayed yad adaḥ saṃprayatīr iti
(AVParis_10,1.12) sā mandasāneti nadīḥ kalpayitvā rasaiś ca paripūrayed
(AVParis_10,1.13) apām agram asi samudraṃ vo 'bhyavasṛjāmīti samudrān
(AVParis_10,1.14) vanaspatiḥ saha devair na āgann iti bṛhaspatineti vanaspatīn anyāṃś ca
(AVParis_10,1.15) yajñe tvā manasā saṃkalpayen manasā saṃkalpayatītha bhavatīha bhavatīha bhavati
(AVParis_10,1.16) nidhiṃ bibhratī bahudheti namaskārayitvā
(AVParis_10,1.17) satyaṃ bṛhad ity anuvāko ye devā divy ekādaśa stheti puṇyāhaṃ vācayet
(AVParis_10,1.18) saṃsthāpayen
(AVParis_10,1.19) nava divo devajanenety abhimantrya brāhmaṇebhyo dadyād
(AVParis_10,1.20) dātur esāsmai rohiṇī kāmaṃ nikāmaṃ vā dugdha iti
(AVParis_10,1.21) yathā rohanti bījāni phālakṛṣṭe mahītale evaṃ kāmāḥ prarohante pretyeha manasaḥ sadā
(AVParis_10,1.22) sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam | tattat prāpnoti viprebhyo dattvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhi || dattvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhīti || iti bhūmidānaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 10.1.7-22) All the priests offer with the <s>Kāmasūkta</s> (Hymn of Desire), the <s>Kālasūkta</s> (Hymn of Time), the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> (Hymn of the Cosmic Man), and the <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>s (Great Ritual Exclamations) preceded by their numbers. (10.1.8) Then, having made a golden earth, a replica of the earth, the size of a cow-hide, (10.1.9) having brought it to the altar of the pavilion, one should set it up north of the altar [reciting] 'yasyāṃ vedim' (upon which the altar...). (10.1.10) One should set up mountains [reciting] 'girayas te parvatāḥ' (your hills and mountains). (10.1.11) One should adorn it with gold, silver, gems, pearls, coral, and the like [reciting] 'yad adaḥ saṃprayatīḥ' (those that flow together). (10.1.12) Having fashioned rivers [reciting] 'sā mandasānā' and should fill them with liquids. (10.1.13) [Reciting] 'apām agram asi' (You are the foremost of waters) and 'samudraṃ vo 'bhyavasṛjāmi' (I release you into the ocean) — the oceans. (10.1.14) [Reciting] 'vanaspatiḥ saha devair na āgan' (The lord of the forest came to us with the gods) and 'bṛhaspatinā' — the trees and others. (10.1.15) [Reciting] 'yajñe tvā manasā saṃkalpayet' (In the sacrifice, one should resolve you with the mind) — one resolves with the mind: 'Here it exists, here it exists, here it exists.' (10.1.16) Having made obeisance [reciting] 'nidhiṃ bibhratī bahudhā' (bearing treasure in many ways). (10.1.17) One should have the auspicious declaration recited with the <s>anuvāka</s> 'satyaṃ bṛhat' (Truth is great) [and] 'ye devā divy ekādaśa stha' (You eleven gods in heaven). (10.1.18) One should consecrate [the model earth]. (10.1.19) Having consecrated it [reciting] 'nava divo devajanenā' (By the divine race of the nine heavens), one should give it to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s. (10.1.20) [Reciting] 'dātur esā rohiṇī kāmaṃ nikāmaṃ vā dugdhā' (For the giver, this <s>Rohiṇī</s> has milked desire or supreme desire). (10.1.21) 'Just as seeds sprout in soil ploughed by the ploughshare, so desires always sprout here and hereafter from the mind.' (10.1.22) 'Whatever fruit is proclaimed for all gifts — all that one obtains by giving earth to the learned according to the proper rite.' Having given earth according to the proper rite. Thus the <s>bhūmidāna</s> (earth-gift) is complete.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_11. tulāpuruṣavidhiḥ)
(AVParis_11,1.1) om athātas tulāpuruṣavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmas
(AVParis_11,1.2) tad udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre śraddhāpreritau grahaṇakāle vā
(AVParis_11,1.3) ṛtvigyajamānau kḷptakeśaśmaśrū romanakhāni vāpayitvā
(AVParis_11,1.4) saṃbhārān upakalpya prāktantram ājyabhāgāntaṃ kṛtvā
(AVParis_11,1.5) mahāvyāhṛtisāvitrīśāntiṃ brahma jajñānam iti hutvā
(AVParis_11,1.6) agne gobhir agne 'bhyāvartinn agneḥ prajātam iti saṃpātān udapātrānīyābhiṣekakalaśeṣu ninayed
(AVParis_11,1.7) athāsyendro grāvabhyām ity abhiṣecayed
(AVParis_11,1.8) idam āpo yathendro bāhubhyām ity abhiṣecayitvā
(AVParis_11,1.9) yathoktam añjanābhyañjanānulepanaṃ kārayitvā vāso gandhasrajaś cābadhnīyāt
(AVParis_11,1.10) tulāṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca pavitrair abhyukṣya puruṣasaṃmito 'rtha iti saptabhis tadārohayed
(AVParis_11,1.11) acyutā dyaur iti catasṛbhir avarohayet
(AVParis_11,1.12) sūryasyāvṛtam iti pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayitvātmālaṃkārān kartre dadyāt
(AVParis_11,1.13) sahasradakṣiṇaṃ grāmavaram
(AVParis_11,1.14) dvijān annena tarpayet
(AVParis_11,1.15) atha cen niḥsvapakṣeṇa yathā saṃpadyate dhanam | dhātubhiḥ saha taulyam atu vāsobhiś ca rasais tathā | vrīhyādisaptadhānyair vā yathāsaṃpadyate gṛhe ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 11: The <s>Tulāpuruṣa</s> Rite) (AVParis 11.1.1) Oṃ. Now we shall expound the procedure of the <s>tulāpuruṣa</s> (weighing a man [in gold]). (11.1.2) That [should be performed] during the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, when impelled by faith, or at the time of an eclipse. (11.1.3) The priest and the sacrificer, having had their hair, beard, body-hair, and nails trimmed. (11.1.4) Having prepared the ritual materials and performed the preliminary ritual up to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions). (11.1.5) Having offered with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>s, the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the peace [formula], and 'brahma jajñānam' (Brahman was born). (11.1.6) [Reciting] 'agne gobhiḥ,' 'agne 'bhyāvartin,' 'agneḥ prajātam' — having brought the residual waters in water-vessels, one should pour them into the consecration pots. (11.1.7) Then one should consecrate him [reciting] 'asyendro grāvabhyām' (For him <s>Indra</s>, with the pressing-stones). (11.1.8) Having consecrated [reciting] 'idam āpo yathendro bāhubhyām' (These waters, as <s>Indra</s> with his arms). (11.1.9) Having had the prescribed anointing, oiling, and smearing performed, one should bind garments, fragrances, and garlands. (11.1.10) Having sprinkled the balance and the gold with purifying [waters], one should make him ascend it with seven [<s>mantra</s>s beginning] 'puruṣasaṃmitaḥ arthaḥ' (the wealth measured against a man). (11.1.11) One should make him descend with four [<s>mantra</s>s beginning] 'acyutā dyauḥ' (Unshaken is heaven). (11.1.12) Having circumambulated [reciting] 'sūryasyāvṛtam' (the course of the sun), and having announced to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, one should give his own ornaments to the officiant. (11.1.13) [The fee is] a thousand, [along with] the best village. (11.1.14) One should satisfy the twice-born with food. (11.1.15) But if one lacks the means, [one may use] whatever wealth is available — with metals, garments, and liquids together, or with rice and the seven kinds of grain, whatever is available in the house.

body.text: (AVParis_11,2.1) sakhaḍgaḥ saśirastrāṇaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ | tapanīyam agare kṛtvā paścāt tolyo narādhipaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 11.2.1) Wearing a sword, wearing a helmet, adorned with all ornaments, having placed refined gold in a vessel — afterward the king is to be weighed.

body.text: (AVParis_11,2.2) indreṇedaṃ purā dattam adhirājyāptaye varam | sarvapāpapraṇāśāya sarvapuṇyavivṛddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 11.2.2) This was formerly given by <s>Indra</s> as the best [means] for attaining sovereignty — for the destruction of all sins and for the increase of all merit.

body.text: (AVParis_11,2.3) mahādānātidānānām idaṃ dānam anuttamam | akṣayyaphaladaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dātṝṇāṃ śreyavardhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 11.2.3) Among great gifts and superlative gifts, this gift is unsurpassed — bestowing imperishable fruit, the best, increasing the welfare of givers.

body.text: (AVParis_11,2.4) yat pāpaṃ sve kule jātais triḥ sapta puruṣaiḥ kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ naśyate kṣipram agnau tūlaṃ yathā tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 11.2.4) Whatever sin has been committed by those born in one's own family for three times seven generations — all that is quickly destroyed, like cotton in fire.

body.text: (AVParis_11,2.5) anāmayaṃ sthānam avāpya daivair alaṅghanīyaṃ sukṛtair hiraṇmayaiḥ | suvarṇatejāḥ pravimuktapāpo divīndravad rājati sūryaloke || divīndravad rājati sūryaleketi || iti tulāpuruṣavidhiḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 11.2.5) Having attained a healthy station through divine golden meritorious deeds, insurmountable — with the radiance of gold, freed from sin, he shines in the world of the sun like <s>Indra</s> in heaven. Like <s>Indra</s> in heaven, he shines in the world of the sun. Thus the <s>tulāpuruṣa</s> rite is complete.

body.text:

body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 12: The <s>Ādityamaṇḍaka</s> [Sun-cake]) (AVParis 12.1.1) Oṃ. Now, he who desires 'May I be the foremost among all men' — he should give a cake to <s>Bhāskara</s> (the Sun). (12.1.2) Its procedure: (12.1.3) Having baked a disk-shaped [cake] from flour of barley or wheat, (12.1.4) having placed it in a vessel and covered it, (12.1.5) having placed a piece of jaggery, ghee, and gold on top, one should worship with red flowers. (12.1.6) Having consecrated with [the <s>mantra</s>] 'viṣāsahim' (the conqueror of poison), one should present it to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (12.1.7) On that, these verses: (12.1.8) He who by this procedure should give a cake to a twice-born — the wise one should give constantly; hear the meritorious fruit thereof:

body.text: (AVParis_12,1.9) ārogyavān varcasvī ca prajāvān paśumāṃs tathā | dhanavān annavān śrīmāṃs tathā sarvajanapriyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 12.1.9) Healthy, brilliant, blessed with progeny and cattle, wealthy, abundant in food, prosperous, and beloved of all people.

body.text: (AVParis_12,1.10) apamṛtyuśataṃ sāgraṃ nāśayaty avicārataḥ | pradattaṃ sūryalokaṃ ca prāpayet paramaṃ padam || prāpayet paramaṃ padam iti || ity ādityamaṇḍakaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 12.1.10) It destroys more than a hundred untimely deaths without doubt; having given, it leads to the world of the Sun and the supreme station. It leads to the supreme station. Thus the <s>Ādityamaṇḍaka</s> is complete.

(AVParis_13,2.2) tair eva namaskāraṃ kārayitvā

(AVParis_13,2.8) rājā hiraṇyagarbhatvam abhīpsaty asmin bhavanto 'numanyantām iti
(AVParis_13,2.9) tair anuṣṭhitaḥ
(AVParis_13,3.1) ud ehi vājinn iti dvābhyāṃ praveśayet

children.translated_text: (AVParis 13.4.9-10, 13.5.1) He should serve the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s with food as desired. On that, these verses: (13.5.1) He whose <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the foremost knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, who have crossed beyond the four <s>Veda</s>s, being pleased, would pronounce blessings — for him there shall be the fruit of sacrifice.

body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 13: The <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> Rite) (AVParis 13.1.1) Oṃ. Now we shall describe the <s>hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Golden Embryo) rite, which removes all sin. (13.1.2) During the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, when impelled by faith, or at the time of an eclipse. (13.1.3) The priest and the sacrificer should have their hair, beard, body-hair, and nails trimmed. (13.1.4) Then the priest, before sunset, having placed the fire-sticks from an <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree, recites over the one being churned with two [<s>mantra</s>s beginning] 'agne jāyasva' (O <s>Agni</s>, be born). (13.1.5) With the third [<s>mantra</s>] the born [fire is acknowledged], with the fourth it is placed upon [the altar]. (13.1.6) Having set it in a clean place and having had the prescribed anointing, oiling, and smearing performed, (13.1.7) [reciting] 'agneḥ prajātaṃ pari yad dhiraṇyam' (The gold born from <s>Agni</s>) and 'yad ābadhnann' — having tied a golden garland, and having made protection [reciting] 'rakṣantu tvā' (May they protect you), (13.1.8) having spread <s>darbha</s> grass, the two should sleep on the ground. (13.1.9) On the following day, at the <s>abhijit</s> (midday) moment, having placed a golden vessel, disk-shaped, navel-sized, with a lid, (13.1.10) and the ladle, spoon, ghee-pot, water-vessel, and ornaments, (13.1.11) having swept, sprinkled, spread the sacrificial grass, placed the water-vessel near, prepared the ghee with the preparation-ritual, and having offered the regular preliminary oblations and the <s>ājyabhāga</s>s, then one offers: (13.2.1) 'To <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Golden Embryo), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered, (13.2.2) having made obeisance with those same [<s>mantra</s>s], (13.2.3) having worshipped with those same, [one gives] the ladle, spoon, ghee-pot, water-vessel, and ornaments. (13.2.4) Having bathed the king in the golden [vessel] with [<s>mantra</s>s containing] 'hiraṇyavatī' (golden), (13.2.5) having poured <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow-products) and water into that [vessel] with golden pitchers, (13.2.6) having brought the residual waters with the <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> hymn, the <s>Aṃhomuca</s> (sin-releasing) [hymn], the <s>Śāntātīya</s> [hymn], and five names, (13.2.7) one should likewise inform the assembly-members, non-assembly-members, and priests: (13.2.8) 'The king desires the state of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — may the honorable ones consent.' (13.2.9) Authorized by them, (13.3.1) one should make him enter [the vessel] with two [<s>mantra</s>s beginning] 'ud ehi vājin' (Rise, O vigorous one). (13.3.2) Having resolved upon the thirty-three deities, one instructs him: (13.3.3) 'Having restrained speech and withdrawn the senses from their objects, meditate with the mind upon the glorious golden <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme), the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person).' (13.3.4) He agrees: 'So be it.' (13.3.5) The interval is seventeen measures. (13.3.6) <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the seventeenth. (13.3.7) One should announce: 'He has returned from <s>Prajāpati</s>.' (13.3.8) Having likewise informed the assembly-members and non-assembly-members, one should raise him up. (13.3.9) The one who has risen should be covered over with a golden disc. (13.3.10) [Reciting] 'mā te prāṇaḥ' (May your breath not [depart]), one should lift him out. (13.3.11) Having freed the lifted one from the golden [vessel reciting] 'hiraṇyanāmnaḥ' and [reciting] 'yas tvā mṛtyuḥ' (Who, O Death...), one should dismiss [the vessel]. (13.3.12) [Reciting] 'saṃpaśyamānāḥ' (Looking at each other), having been looked upon, having bowed to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, paying homage [reciting] 'namo hiraṇyagarbhāya' (Homage to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>). (13.3.13) Then indeed [they recite] 'of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>' — [this] is said to the most beloved. (13.3.14) The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s should say: 'Arise, O one favored by <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>!' (13.3.15) Having offered with the <s>Apratiratha</s> [hymn], one should consecrate. (13.3.16) Having praised <s>Varuṇa</s> [reciting] 'apsu te rājan varuṇa' (In the waters, O King <s>Varuṇa</s>), having bathed, having returned with purifying [waters], they worship the Sun. (13.4.1) 'Gold is your embryo, and born from gold's embryo — you are <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; therefore protect me, great one from the great.' (13.4.2) Having circumambulated [reciting] 'sūryasyāvṛtam' (the course of the sun), (13.4.3) having entered the house [reciting] 'gṛhān aimī' (I come to the house), (13.4.4) having installed the fire [reciting] 'tvam agne pramatiḥ' (You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the providence), one should release [the fire]. (13.4.5) Then one should give ten thousand as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) to the twice-born,

body.text: (AVParis_13,5.2) brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena sūryo divi virājati | indro 'py eṣāṃ prasādena devān ativirājati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 13.5.2) By the grace of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the sun shines in the sky; by their grace, <s>Indra</s> too outshines the gods.

body.text: (AVParis_13,5.3) hiraṇyadānasya phalam amṛtatvam iti śrutiḥ | śrūyate hy asya dātā yaḥ so 'mṛtatvaṃ samaśnute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 13.5.3) The fruit of giving gold is immortality — so says the <s>Śruti</s> (sacred tradition); for it is heard that he who gives it attains immortality.

body.text: (AVParis_13,5.4) rājekṣuvākuprabhrtayaḥ purā rājarṣayo 'malāḥ | dattvā hiraṇyaṃ viprebhyo jyotir bhūtvā divi sthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 13.5.4) Kings of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty and others, the pure royal sages of old — having given gold to the learned, they became luminous beings established in heaven.

body.text: (AVParis_13,5.5) ya evaṃ saṃskṛto rājā vidhinā brahmavādinā | prajānām iha sāmrājyaṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ ca gacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 13.5.5) A king thus consecrated by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> versed in the ritual procedure attains sovereignty over subjects here, primacy, and supreme excellence.

body.text: (AVParis_13,5.6) amuṣmin brahmaṇā sārdham ānandam anubhūya vai | jyotirmayaṃ satyalokaṃ nacaivāvartate punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In that [world], having experienced bliss together with <s>Brahman</s>, he [reaches] the world of truth, made of light, and does not return again.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_14. hastirathadānavidhiḥ)
(AVParis_14,1.1) om atha hastirathadānānām anukramaṃ vakṣye
(AVParis_14,1.2) jātarūpamayaṃ krtvā ekacakraṃ suśobhanam | hastibhiḥ saptabhir yuktam arcayitvā yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 14: Procedure for the gift of elephant-chariots) Oṃ. Now I shall describe the sequence of elephant-chariot gifts. Having made a single-wheeled [chariot] of gold, splendidly beautiful, yoked with seven elephants, and having worshipped it according to the prescribed rite,

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.3) atha vā caturbhir yuktaṃ haimaṃ rājatam eva vā | aspṛṣṭaṃ dārujaṃ vāpi sarvasaṃbhārapūritam ||
body.translated_text: Or yoked with four [elephants], made of gold or silver, or even of untouched wood, filled with all requisite materials,

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.4) hastiyugmena saṃyuktaṃ saurabheyayutena vā | bhuṅkte saptaiva janmāni saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: Yoked with a pair of elephants, or joined with a cow — one enjoys the earth of seven continents for seven births.

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.5) hastena yukte candramasi paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā puṇye vā ṛkṣe śuciḥ śucau deśe tantram ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: When [the chariot is] yoked with an elephant, on a full-moon or new-moon day, or under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), being pure, in a pure place — thus has the procedure been stated.

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.6) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvārabhyātha juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having arranged the kindling wood facing east, and having touched [the fire], one should then offer oblations.

body.text:
(AVParis_14,1.7) savitre svāhā || pataṃgāya svāhā || pāvakāya svāhā || sahasraraśmaye svāhā || mārtaṇḍāya svāhā || viṣṇave svāhā || prajāpataye svāhā || parameṣṭhine svāhā iti hutvā.
(AVParis_14,1.8) kanakāś ca tilā gāvo dāsī gṛhamahīrathāḥ | kanyā hastī ca vidyā ca mahādāni vai daśa ||
body.translated_text: "<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Savitṛ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Pataṃga</s> (the flying sun)! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Pāvaka</s> (the Purifier)! <s>Svāhā</s> to the thousand-rayed one! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme)!" — having offered thus: "Gold, sesame, cows, a female servant, a house, land, chariots, a maiden, an elephant, and knowledge — these are the ten great gifts."

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.9) tasmāt sarveṣu dāneṣu anuktavidhikeṣu ca | agniṃ brūma iti sūktam ājyatantreṇa homayet ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, in all gifts and those for which no procedure has been stated, one should offer the hymn 'We address <s>Agni</s>' with the clarified-butter procedure.

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.10) aśvadātā vrajet svargam aśvārūḍhaś ca mānavaḥ | pūjyate devagandharvair apsarokiṃnarais tathā ||
body.translated_text: The giver of a horse goes to heaven; and a man mounted on a horse is honored by gods, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Apsaras</s>es, and <s>Kiṃnara</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.11) hastivarcasaṃ prathatām iti kalaśe saṃpātān ānīya yugaṃ yoktraṃ ratham iti sarvaṃ saṃprokṣya ||
body.translated_text: "May the splendor of the elephant spread forth" — having collected the residual offerings in a vessel, and having sprinkled the yoke, the yoke-strap, and the entire chariot,

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.12) aśrāntasya tvā manasā yunajmīti yojayet ||
body.translated_text: "With unwearied mind I yoke you" — thus one should yoke [the chariot].

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.13) aśrāntasya tvā manasā yunajmi prathamasya ca | utkūlam udvaho bhavo uduhya prati dhāvatāt ||
body.translated_text: "With unwearied mind I yoke you, the first one; may you be an uphill carrier, and having carried [the load] up, run back."

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.14) yuktāyārthaṃ dadyāt ||
body.translated_text: One should give the offering to the yoked [chariot].

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.15) śyāvair yuktaḥ śitipadbhir hiraṇyayo yasya rathaḥ pathibhir vartate sukhaiḥ | sa no hastena savitā hiraṇyabhug ghiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
body.translated_text: "The golden chariot, yoked with dark, white-footed [horses], whose chariot moves on comfortable paths — may <s>Savitṛ</s>, the gold-enjoyer, the golden-handed, protect us with that elephant."

body.text: (AVParis_14,1.16) bṛhaddhastirathaṃ yuktaṃ hastena tu dadan naraḥ | savituḥ sthānam āpnoti divyāṃ kāmajavāṃ sabhām ||
body.translated_text: A man who gives a great elephant-chariot, yoked, along with an elephant, attains the station of <s>Savitṛ</s>, the divine assembly swift as desire.

children.text: (Pariśiṣṭa_15. aśvarathadānavidhiḥ)
children.translated_text: (Supplement 15: Procedure for the gift of horse-chariots)

children.text: (AVParis_15,1.1) om athāśvarathadānavidhiḥ.
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Now [follows] the procedure for the gift of horse-chariots.

children.text: (AVParis_15,1.2) goṣṭha udakānte śucau vā deśe prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvārabhyātha juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: At a cow-pen or the water's edge, or in a pure place, having arranged the kindling wood facing east and having touched [the fire], one should then offer oblations.

body.text:
(AVParis_15,1.3) vataraṃhā bhava vājin yujyamāna ity etenāśveṣu saṃpātān ānīyāśrāntasya tveti samānam
(AVParis_15,1.4) tvam indras tvaṃ mahendra iti savitre arghaṃ dattvā
(AVParis_15,1.5) punantu mety ātmānam ālabhya japed
(AVParis_15,1.6) rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti yajamānam abhimantrya samṛddhihomānte
(AVParis_15,1.7) varāṃ dhenuṃ kartre dadyād aśvarathaṃ grāmavaraṃ ceti
(AVParis_15,1.8) ya evaṃ vidhinā dadyād viduṣe aśvarathaṃ sudhīḥ | jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ ca sāmrājyaṃ prajānām iha gacchati ||
body.translated_text: "Be swift as wind, O horse, when yoked" — with this [verse], having collected the residual offerings upon the horses, [proceed as before with] 'With unwearied mind [I yoke you]' — the procedure is the same. "You are <s>Indra</s>, you are great <s>Indra</s>" — having given the <s>argha</s> (honorific offering) to <s>Savitṛ</s>, "May they purify me" — having touched oneself, one should recite. "May the fires protect you" — having consecrated the sacrificer with a mantra, at the end of the prosperity-oblation, one should give to the officiant a choice cow, a horse-chariot, and an excellent village.

body.text: (AVParis_15,1.9) saptānāṃ lokānām ante jyotirlokam anāmayam | gatvā sa paramānandaṃ bhuṅkte yāvad vibhāvasuḥ ||
body.translated_text: He who would give a horse-chariot wisely, according to this procedure, to a learned one — he attains pre-eminence, supremacy, and sovereignty over his subjects here. At the end of the seven worlds, having gone to the world of light, free from disease, he enjoys supreme bliss as long as the sun [shines].

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_16. gosahasravidhiḥ)
(AVParis_16,1.1) om athāto gosahasravidhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 16: Procedure for the gift of a thousand cows) Oṃ. Now [follows] the procedure for [the gift of] a thousand cows.

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.2) goṣṭha udakānte śucau vā deśe prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: At a cow-pen or the water's edge, or in a pure place, having arranged the kindling wood facing east and having touched [the fire], one should then offer oblations.

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.3) ā gāva iti sūktenājyaṃ juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: One should offer clarified butter with the hymn 'Come, O cows.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.4) mahāvrīhīṇām aindraṃ caruṃ saumyaṃ ca sahasratamyāḥ payasi śrapayitvā gāva eva surabhava ity etena juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having cooked a <s>caru</s> (oblation-rice) of great rice — one for <s>Indra</s> and one for <s>Soma</s> — from the thousandth [cow's] milk, one should offer with [the verse] 'Cows indeed are fragrant.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.5) pañcānāṃ nadīnāṃ tīrthodakam ||
body.translated_text: Sacred water from the <s>tīrtha</s>s (pilgrimage fords) of five rivers.

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.6) paścād agnes tīrthodakena pūrṇaṃ kalaśam avasthāpya hiraṇyavarṇā ity abhimantrya saṃ vo goṣṭheneti daśa gāḥ snāpayet ||
body.translated_text: Having placed behind the fire a full vessel with <s>tīrtha</s>-water, having consecrated it with 'Of golden color,' one should bathe ten cows with 'Together in the cow-pen.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.7) tvaramānanayāḥ samabhyukṣya sahasratamyāḥ sānodanekemam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ ma iti rājānam abhiṣicya ||
body.translated_text: Having sprinkled [them] hurriedly, and having anointed the king from the thousandth [cow], with rice, with 'Increase this <s>Kṣatriya</s> for me, O <s>Indra</s>,'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.8) imā āpa iti ṣaḍbhir yothoktam añjanābhyañjanānulepanaṃ kṛtvā ||
body.translated_text: Having performed the anointing, applying collyrium and unguents with the six [verses beginning with] 'These waters,'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.9) sahasratamīṃ prathamām alaṃkṛtya ||
body.translated_text: Having adorned the thousandth cow first,

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.10) ā gāvo mām upatiṣṭhantām ity upatiṣṭhet ||
body.translated_text: One should stand [reciting] 'May the cows attend upon me.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.11) prajāvatīḥ sūyavasād iti ca sarvāḥ pāyayet ||
body.translated_text: And one should let all [cows] drink with 'Rich in offspring, [feeding on] good grass.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.12) priyam aśanaṃ dattvāddhi tṛṇam aghnya iti sahasratamīm ālabhya japet ||
body.translated_text: Having given pleasant food [to the cow] and having touched the thousandth cow, one should recite 'Eat grass, O inviolable one.'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.13) mayā gāvo gopatinā sacadhvam iti mantrānetnārghaṃ dattvā ||
body.translated_text: Having given the <s>argha</s> with the mantras 'With me, the lord of cattle, be together, O cows,'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.14) sahasratamyāḥ pucham aupasaṃgṛhya bhūmiṣ ṭvā pratigṛhṇātv iti japan ||
body.translated_text: Having grasped the tail of the thousandth cow, reciting 'May the earth receive you,'

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.15) sahasratamyāḥ pṛṣṭhato vrajan ||
body.translated_text: Walking behind the thousandth cow,

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.16) sarvāḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya namaskṛtya svastivācya brāhmaṇebhyo nivedya daśa gā dakṣiṇāṃ kartre dadyāt sahasratamīṃ vastrayugmam aca ||
body.translated_text: Having circumambulated all [the cows], having bowed, having pronounced benedictions, having announced to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, one should give ten cows as the officiant's fee, along with the thousandth cow and a pair of garments.

body.text: (AVParis_16,1.17) tad api ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And on this, [here are the] verses:

body.text: (AVParis_16,2.1) saptājanmānugaṃ pāpaṃ puruṣaiḥ saptabhiḥ krtam | tatkṣaṇād vidhinānena nāśayed goprado naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: The sin following through seven births, committed by seven men — a man who gives cows destroys it instantly by this procedure.

body.text: (AVParis_16,2.2) sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ phalaṃ yat parikīrtitam | tad avāpnoti virebhyo gosahasraprado naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Whatever fruit has been proclaimed for all gifts — that a man who gives a thousand cows obtains from the heroes.

body.text: (AVParis_16,2.3) aśvamedhaṃ vṛṣotsargaṃ gosahasraṃ ca yaḥ sutaḥ | dadyān madīya ity āhuḥ pitaras tarpayanti hi ||
body.translated_text: A son who would give the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice), the <s>Vṛṣotsarga</s> (releasing of a bull), and a thousand cows — 'He is mine,' say the ancestors; indeed, he satisfies [them].

body.text: (AVParis_16,2.4) tasmād anena vidhinā gosahasraṃ daden naraḥ | sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti tat paramaṃ padam iti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, a man should give a thousand cows according to this procedure; with his soul purified of all sins, he goes to that supreme abode.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_17. rājakarmasāṃvatsarīyam)
(AVParis_17,1.1) om atha pratisaṃvatsaraṃ rājakarmāṇi krameṇa vakṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 17: Annual royal rites) Oṃ. Now we shall describe the annual royal rites in sequence.

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.2) athāśvayuje māse śuklapakṣasya tṛtīye 'hani ||
body.translated_text: On the third day of the bright fortnight in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s> (September-October),

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.3) haridrāyavānām ||
body.translated_text: With turmeric and barley,

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.4) rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti catasṛbhī rakṣām aśvānāṃ baddhvā hastyaśvānāṃ nīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: Having tied the protective [amulet] with the four [verses beginning with] 'May the fires protect you,' one should perform the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration ceremony) of horses and elephants.

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.5) aśvo 'si kṣiprajanmāsi ....pradadyāt sa viśuddhātmā saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: "You are a horse, swift-born..." one should give, and he, of purified soul, [enjoys] the seven-continented earth.

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.6) hastena yukte candramasi paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā puṇye nakṣatre śucau deśe || tantram ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: When [the chariot is] yoked with an elephant, on a full-moon or new-moon day, or under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, in a pure place — thus the procedure has been stated.

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.7) prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvārabhāthajuhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having arranged the kindling wood facing east and having touched [the fire], one should then offer oblations.

body.text: (AVParis_17,1.8) savitre svāhā || pataṃgāya svāhā || pāvakāya svāhā || sahasraraśmaye svāhā || mārtaṇḍāya svāhā || viṣṇave svāhā || prajāpataye svāhā || parameṣṭhine svāheti hutvā kanakānāṃ baddhvā hastyaśvānāṃ pūrvavan nīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: "<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Savitṛ</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Pataṃga</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Pāvaka</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to the thousand-rayed one! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>!" — having offered thus, having tied the golden [amulets], one should perform the <s>nīrājana</s> of horses and elephants as before.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.1) atha navamyām aparāhṇe vāhanāni snāpayitvā ahatavāsā brahmā dvādaśamitāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā || tantram ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: Then on the ninth day, in the afternoon, having bathed the vehicles, the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] wearing unworn garments, having constructed a <s>vedi</s> (altar) of twelve measures — thus the procedure has been stated.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.2) śāntikṛtyādūṣaṇena vāhanaṃ triḥ prokṣya parīyān ||
body.translated_text: Having thrice sprinkled the vehicle with the pacification-rite purification formula, one should circumambulate.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.3) niḥsālām iti sūktaṃ japan pratyetyābhiṣiñcayed enam ||
body.translated_text: Reciting the hymn 'Without a shed,' having returned, one should anoint him [the king].

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.4) aśvam alaṃkṛtaṃ śabalakaṇṭhaṃ kṛtvopasthāpya dadhyād ||
body.translated_text: Having prepared and presented the adorned horse with a spotted neck, one should offer it.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.5) evam eva maiśradhānyāny udapātrāṇy antarāsu dikṣu ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, mixed grains and water-vessels in the intermediate directions.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.6) tatraiva devatā yajet || agniṃ vāyuṃ varuṇam aśvināv iti ||
body.translated_text: There one should worship the deities — <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the <s>Aśvin</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.7) payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā ||
body.translated_text: Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked oblation) in milk,

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.8) samās tvāgne tvaṃ no agne mā no vidann abhayair aparājitair āyuṣyaiḥ svastyayanair apratiratheneti ca hutvā saṃsthāpya ||
body.translated_text: Having offered with 'Together with you, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'May they not find us' — with fearless, unconquered, life-giving, auspicious, undefeatable [verses], and having concluded [the rite],

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.9) agner ado 'sīty ahatavāsobhiḥ prachādya rasaiḥ kumbhān audumbarān pūrayitvā pratidiśam avasthāpya mamāgne varco abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ud uttamaṃ varuṇāśvinā brahmaṇā yātam iti juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: "You are of <s>Agni</s>'s domain" — having covered with unworn garments, having filled <s>Udumbara</s> (fig-wood) pots with juices and placed them in each direction, one should offer with 'O <s>Agni</s>, [grant me] splendor, fearlessness; O Heaven-and-Earth, [grant] the highest; O <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aśvin</s>s, come with <s>Brahman</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.10) paurṇamāsī prathameti ca juhuyād dundubhim āhanyād ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: And one should offer with 'The full-moon is the first,' and strike the drum — thus it has been stated.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.11) upa śvāsaya pṛthivīm iti tatraivānumantraṇaṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: "Breathe upon the earth" — and at that same [place], the consecrating mantra.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.12) sarvāṇi ca vāditrāṇi vāhanāni ca ||
body.translated_text: And all musical instruments and vehicles [should be present].

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.13) janasyān praharṣaya pañcamīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet ||
body.translated_text: "Bring joy to the people" — one should install [the deity] on the fifth [day].

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.14) na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulakṣṭhadūpaṃ dadyāt ||
body.translated_text: "May disease not reach him, O god" — one should offer incense of <s>guggulu</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.15) yas te gandhas tryāyuṣam iti bhūtiṃ prayacchet ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever your fragrance, [giving] triple life-span" — one should present the prosperity [offering].

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.16) dūṣyā dūṣir asīti pratisaram ābadhya ye purastād iti pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
body.translated_text: "You are the destroyer of the destroyer" — having tied the protective thread, one should throw [amulets] in each direction with 'Those who are in front.'

body.text: (AVParis_17,2.17) bahir niḥsṛtyottareṇa gatvā bāhyenopaniṣkramya suhṛde kuryāc chraddadhate kuryād vāhanānām abhayaṃ karma ||
body.translated_text: Having gone outside, proceeding northward, going around on the outer side, one should perform for a trusting friend the rite of fearlessness for the vehicles.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_18. rājakarmasāṃvatsarīyam)
(AVParis_18,1.1) athāśvayuje māse paurṇamāsyām aparāhṇe hastinīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 18: Annual royal rites [continued]) Now, on the full-moon day of the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, in the afternoon, one should perform the elephant-lustration (<s>nīrājana</s>) ceremony.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.2) prāgudakpravaṇe deśe yatra vā mano ramate ||
body.translated_text: In a place sloping to the east and north, or wherever the mind finds delight.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.3) girayas te parvatā ity etayā hastaśatam ardhaṃ vā maṇḍalaṃ parigṛhya yābhir yajñam iti saṃprokṣet ||
body.translated_text: With [the verse] 'Your mountains, your hills' — having enclosed an area of a hundred <s>hasta</s>s (cubits) or half, and having sprinkled it with 'With which [waters] the sacrifice [is performed],'

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.4) tatra ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: On this, [here are the] verses:

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.5) daśahastasamutsedhaṃ pañcahastaṃ tu vistṛtam | śāntavrkṣamayaṃ kuryāt toraṇaṃ puṣṭivardhanama ||
body.translated_text: One should make an arch (<s>toraṇa</s>) of peaceful wood, ten <s>hasta</s>s in height, five <s>hasta</s>s in breadth, for the increase of prosperity.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.6) śuklaiḥ śuklāmbaradhvajair mālyaiś ca paribhūṣitam | kārayeta bile śubhre rasaiś ca paripūrite ||
body.translated_text: Adorned with white [decorations], white garments, banners, and garlands — one should have it made in an auspicious hole filled with juices.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.7) rasais tvām abhiṣiñcāmi bhūme mahyaṃ śivā bhava | asapatnā sapatnaghnī mama yajñavivardhanī ||
body.translated_text: "I anoint you with juices, O Earth! Be auspicious to me; without rivals, destroyer of rivals, increaser of my sacrifices."

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.8) imau stambhau ghṛtānvaktāv ubhau mā yaśasāvatāt | yo mā kaś cabhidāsati tam imau stambhau nirdahatām iti ||
body.translated_text: "These two pillars, anointed with clarified butter — may both of them [bring] me glory! Whoever may attack me — may these two pillars burn him up."

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.9) uc chrayasva imā yā brahmaṇaspata ity etābhyāṃ suvarṇamālā patākaiḥ stambhau saṃyojya ||
body.translated_text: With the two [verses] 'Rise up' and 'These which, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — having joined the pillars with golden garlands and banners,

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.10) tasyādhastāc caturhastāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā darbhapavitrapāṇir baliṃ puṣpāṇi ca dattvā ||
body.translated_text: Having made a <s>vedi</s> (altar) of four <s>hasta</s>s beneath that, with hands [holding] <s>darbha</s>-grass purifiers, having offered <s>bali</s> (food-offerings) and flowers,

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.11) madhulājāmaśraiḥ svastikasaṃyāvakadadhikṛsarāpūpakāpāyasaghṛtavividhapānabhakṣaphalair agniṃ paristīrya ||
body.translated_text: Having strewn around the fire [offerings of] honey, parched grains, goat's milk, <s>svastika</s>-shaped cakes, <s>saṃyāvaka</s> (fried cake), curd, <s>kṛsara</s> (grain-dish), cakes, rice-pudding, clarified butter, various drinks, delicacies, and fruits,

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.12) āpo asmān mātaraḥ sūdayantv iti caturaudumbarān kumbhān hradodakena pūrayitvā ||
body.translated_text: 'May the Waters, our mothers, purify us' — thus, having filled four <s>audumbara</s> (fig-wood) jars with lake water,

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.13) pratidiśam avasthāpya dadhyād raudrāgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ vāruṇā mantrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having placed [them] in each direction, he should offer: the <s>Raudra</s> (of <s>Rudra</s>), <s>Āgneya</s> (of <s>Agni</s>), <s>Vāyavya</s> (of <s>Vāyu</s>), and <s>Vāruṇa</s> (of <s>Varuṇa</s>) <s>mantra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.14) rakṣoghnaṃ krtyādūśaṇaṃ yaśasyavarcasyāni ca hutvauṣadhīḥ samādāya dvihastaṃ maṇḍalam ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: Having offered the <s>Rākṣoghna</s> (demon-destroying), <s>Kṛtyādūṣaṇa</s> (sorcery-removing), glory-giving, and radiance-giving [hymns], having gathered the herbs — 'a circle of two <s>hasta</s>s (cubits)' — thus it is stated.

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.15) tatra ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: On this, there are verses:

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.16) bṛhatkaṇṭārīkaṇṭakā lāghukaṇṭārikā smṛtāḥ | suvarṇapuṣpī śvetagiri karṇikā hy udisatrā ||
body.translated_text: The great <s>kaṇṭārī</s> thorn-plant, the small <s>kaṇṭārikā</s> are recorded; the golden-flowered one, the white-mountain <s>karṇikā</s>, and <s>udisatrā</s>,

body.text: (AVParis_18,1.17) siṃhī vyāghrī ca hariṇī hy amṛtā cāparājitā | pṛśniparṇī ca dūrvā ca padmam utpalamālinī ||
body.translated_text: <s>Siṃhī</s>, <s>Vyāghrī</s>, and <s>Hariṇī</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s> and <s>Aparājitā</s>; <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Dūrvā</s> grass, lotus, water-lily, and <s>Mālinī</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18,2.1) tām anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: He consecrates that [preparation] with <s>mantra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_18,2.2) vaiṇavaṃ kaṭakam avasthāpyādadhyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having placed a bamboo ring, he should apply [the preparation].

body.text: (AVParis_18,2.3) dvaipavaiyāghrānaḍuccarma paristīrya ||
body.translated_text: Having spread out the hide of a leopard, tiger, or bull,

body.text: (AVParis_18,2.4) tato yā syād adhidevatā tasyai baliṃ dattvā piṇḍāni ca dadyāt ||
body.translated_text: Then, having given an offering (<s>bali</s>) and rice-balls (<s>piṇḍa</s>) to whichever presiding deity [is relevant],

body.text: (AVParis_18,2.5) hastinam ācāmayet ||
body.translated_text: He should have the elephant sip [the consecrated water].

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.1) yasyāṃ diśi sa ripur bhavati tāṃ diśaṃ gatvā hastinam ānayed dhiraṇyena rajatena vajramaṇimuktādibhiḥ śaṅkhena candanena bhadradāruṇayā kuṣṭhena naladena rocanenāñjanena manahśilayā padmakumudotpalair ||
body.translated_text: Having gone to the direction in which that enemy is located, he should bring the elephant, [adorned] with gold, silver, diamond, jewels, pearls, and the like, with conch, sandalwood, <s>bhadradāru</s> (cedar), <s>kuṣṭha</s> plant, <s>nalada</s> (spikenard), <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), collyrium, <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), lotus, white water-lily, and blue lotus.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.2) mamāgne varca iti sūktaṃ dakṣinottaramakhaṃ pratijapet ||
body.translated_text: 'My radiance, O <s>Agni</s>' — this <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) he should recite, turning from south to north.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.3) śeṣeṇa gātrāṇy abhyañjayet ||
body.translated_text: With the remainder, he should anoint the limbs.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.4) tatra slokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: On this, there are verses:

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.5) hastināṃ rakṣaṇe daṇḍaḥ kartavyo vaiṇavo navaḥ | ṣoḍaśāratnimātras tu cāruparvamanaoramaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For the protection of elephants, a new bamboo goad should be fashioned, sixteen cubits in measure, with beautiful joints, pleasing to the mind.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.6) tena vāraṇān vārayet ||
body.translated_text: With that, he should ward off the elephants.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.7) dantāgreṣu tṛṇāni kṛtvā yathā havyaṃ vahasi grasati ||
body.translated_text: Having placed grasses on the tips of the tusks — 'As you carry and consume the oblation' —

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.8) sujātaṃ jātavedasam ity agniṃ prajvālayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Well-born, O <s>Jātavedas</s> (Knower of Births)' — with this he should kindle the fire.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.9) sujātaṃ jātavedasam iti vācayed yathā havyam iti nīrājayitvā ||
body.translated_text: Having recited 'Well-born, O <s>Jātavedas</s>' and performed the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration) with 'As the oblation,'

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.10) nidhiṃ bibhratīti śālāṃ praveśayed ||
body.translated_text: 'Bearing treasure' — with this he should lead [the elephant] into the stable.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.11) anapekṣamānāḥ svāni sthānāni vrajanti dīrghāyuṣo balavantaś ca bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: Without looking back, they go to their own stations; they become long-lived and powerful.

body.text: (AVParis_18,3.12) gosahasraṃ kartre dakṣiṇā grāmavaraṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: A thousand cows and an excellent village are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) for the performer.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_18b. rājakarmasāṃvatsarīyam)
(AVParis_18b,1.1) atha varṣaśataṃ pravardhamāno rājānam abhivardhayiṣyan saṃvatsare janmadine kuryāt || tantram ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 18b. The Annual Royal Rites) Now, wishing to increase the king who prospers for a hundred years, one should perform [the rite] on the birthday in each year. 'The <s>tantra</s> (ritual procedure)' — thus it is stated.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.2) punantu mā vāyoḥ pūto vaiśvānaro raśmibhir iti pavitraiḥ puṇyāhādīni ca maṅgalair yajamānaṃ ca saṃprokṣya yad ābadhnann iti puṣpādyalaṃkāraṃ varjayitvā māhendraṃ caruṃ śrapayet ||
body.translated_text: 'May they purify me; purified by <s>Vāyu</s>, by <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire) with rays' — with the purificatory [verses], the <s>puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day) and other benedictions, having sprinkled the sacrificer, excepting the flower-ornaments [consecrated with] 'That which you bind on,' he should cook a <s>caru</s> (oblation porridge) for <s>Mahendra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.3) lokapālebhyaś ca dvitīyaṃ caruṃ śrapayet ||
body.translated_text: And he should cook a second <s>caru</s> for the <s>Lokapāla</s>s (World-Guardians).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.4) mahām indro ya ojaseti sūktena tṛtīyāyāṃ hy agnau hutvā indrāya svāhetyādi lokapālāṃś ceṣṭvā rājānam anvālabhya ādivaj juhuyād arvāñcam indram indraḥ sutrāmā imam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ me śataṃ jīvataḥ sarada iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Great is <s>Indra</s> who by his might' — with this <s>sūkta</s>, having offered into the fire at the third [oblation], '<s>svāhā</s> to <s>Indra</s>' and the rest, having worshipped the <s>Lokapāla</s>s, having touched the king, he should offer: 'As in the beginning,' 'Hither <s>Indra</s>,' '<s>Indra</s> the protector,' 'This <s>Indra</s>, increase,' 'The <s>Kṣatriya</s> to me,' 'May he live a hundred autumns.'

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.5) rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti catasṛbhī rakṣāṃ kṛtvā rocanayālaṃkuryāt | triguṇena sūtreṇa baddhvā ||
body.translated_text: 'May the fires protect you' — with these four [verses], having made the protective [rite], he should adorn with <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), having bound with a triple-stranded thread.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.6) manāyai tantum iti sūktena rakṣāsūtre saṃpātaṃ ca kṛtvā ||
body.translated_text: 'The thread for the mind' — with this <s>sūkta</s>, having made the <s>saṃpāta</s> (conjunction offering) on the protective thread,

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.7) dhātā te granthim iti badhnāti ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator) your knot' — with this he ties [it].

body.text: (AVParis_18b,1.8) uttaratantraṃ hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: Gold is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) for the subsequent <s>tantra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.1) mahānavamyāṃ hastyaśvadīkṣā pratipatprabhṛti navarātram ||
body.translated_text: On the great ninth (<s>Mahānavamī</s>), the consecration of elephants and horses [begins]; from the first day of the fortnight for nine nights.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.2) śastrasasvasaṃpātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>saṃpāta</s> (junction offering) with weapons and their accessories.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.3) trtīyāyāṃ hastyaśvavāhagrāmyāśvānāṃ karma saptamyāṃ hastyaśvānāṃ darśanam ||
body.translated_text: On the third, the rite for elephants, horses, vehicles, and village horses; on the seventh, the review of elephants and horses.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.4) aṣṭamyām atha piṣṭamayīm ityādi navamyāṃ durgāpūjanam ||
body.translated_text: On the eighth, 'the one made of flour' and the rest; on the ninth, the worship of <s>Durgā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.5) atha vā vanamyām ityādi navamyām ||
body.translated_text: Or, 'on the forest-day' and the rest, on the ninth.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.6) athāparājitadaśamyām ||
body.translated_text: Then, on the invincible tenth (<s>Aparājita-daśamī</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.7) pūrvāhṇe vijayamahūrte uktaṃ prāsthānikam ||
body.translated_text: In the forenoon, at the auspicious moment of victory, the departure rite (<s>prāsthānika</s>) is prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,2.8) etāni khalu prāgdvārāṇītyādi ||
body.translated_text: 'These indeed are the eastern gates' — and so forth.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,3.1) atha śravaṇe nakṣatre rājñām indramahasyeti vyākhyātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, under the <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Śravaṇa</s>, the <s>Indramahas</s> (Great Festival of <s>Indra</s>) for kings — thus it is explained.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,4.1) atha paurṇamāsyām aparāhṇe paurṇamāsikaṃ karma ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full-moon day, in the afternoon, the full-moon rite.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,5.1) athāpāmārgatrayodaśyāṃ śvete muhūrte snānaṃ kṛtvāpāmārgaṃ triḥ paribhrāmayed rājña upari mantreṇa ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the thirteenth of the <s>Apāmārga</s> (waning fortnight), having bathed at the white (auspicious) <s>muhūrta</s>, he should make the <s>apāmārga</s> plant revolve three times above the king with the <s>mantra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,5.2) iśānāṃ tvā bheṣajānām iti tribhiḥ sūktaiḥ pratīcīnaphala iti sūktena vā punaḥ snānam ||
body.translated_text: 'Lord of medicines art thou' — with these three <s>sūkta</s>s, or with the <s>sūkta</s> 'Westward-fruiting,' bathing again.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,5.3) tata ārātrikaṃ paridhatteti dvābhyām iti samānam ||
body.translated_text: Then the evening rite (<s>ārātrika</s>) — with the two [verses beginning] '<s>paridhatta</s>' — [the procedure] is the same.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,6.1) atha dīpotsavaṃ pratipadi hastyaśvādikdīkṣāsamānam ||
body.translated_text: Now, the lamp-festival (<s>dīpotsava</s>) on the first day — the same as the consecration of elephants, horses, and the like.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,6.2) abhyātānāntaṃ kṛtvā ye 'syāṃ prācī dig iti ||
body.translated_text: Having performed up to the concluding offering, 'Those who are in this eastern direction' — thus.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,6.3) mā no devā yas te sarpa ity etaiḥ sūktais tṛṇāni yugatardmanā saṃpātavanti gaṇaṃ ca prātitamitadhānāśane hastyaśvādiyugapat tantraṃ samānam || dhenur dakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: 'May the gods not [harm us],' 'That serpent of yours' — with these <s>sūkta</s>s, having made the <s>saṃpāta</s> (conjunction offering) with grasses by pairs, and the troop [offering], [and the rites] at the distribution of food and grain, the <s>tantra</s> for elephants, horses, and the like simultaneously — [the procedure] is the same. A milch cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,7.1) athākṣayyanavamyāṃ rātrau hastyaśvādīnām anīkānāṃ rathasya parahomaś ca ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the ninth of <s>Akṣayya</s> (the inexhaustible), at night, the <s>parahoma</s> (special oblation) for the troops of elephants, horses, and the like, and for the chariot.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,8.1) atha viṣṇudvādaśyāṃ purohitaḥ paścimāṃ saṃdhyām upāsya gṛhītadarbho yatra rājānam abhigamya pauṣṭikahomaś ca rātrau nīrājanaṃ kṛtvā hastyaśvebhyaś ca ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the twelfth of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu-dvādaśī</s>), the <s>purohita</s>, having performed the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), holding <s>darbha</s> grass, wherever he approaches the king — [he performs] the <s>pauṣṭika-homa</s> (prosperity oblation); and at night, having performed <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration), also for the elephants and horses.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,9.1) atha kārttikyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ raivatyām aśvayujyāṃ vṛṣotsargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Kārttikī</s>, or on [the day] of <s>Revatī</s> [or] <s>Aśvayujī</s>, the release of the bull (<s>vṛṣotsarga</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,10.1) athāgrayaṇīpaurṇamāsyāṃ tantraṃ kṛtvāpād agreti dvābhyāṃ rasaṃ saṃpātyābhimantrya rājānaṃ prāśayet || dhenur dakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Āgrayaṇī</s>, having performed the <s>tantra</s> (ritual procedure), with the two [verses] 'From the foot forward,' having mixed and consecrated the juice, he should have the king partake of it. A milch cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,11.1) atha pauṣyāṃ paurṇamāsyām uktaḥ puṣyābhiṣekaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Pauṣya</s>, the <s>Puṣyābhiṣeka</s> (consecration under <s>Puṣya</s>) is prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,12.1) atha phālgunyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau holākā ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Phālgunī</s>, at night, the <s>Holākā</s> (Holi festival).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,12.2) mahānavamyām uktaprajvalanaṃ nīrājaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: On the great ninth (<s>Mahānavamī</s>), the prescribed kindling and <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,13.1) atha grīṣmapratipady āyuṣyam iti snānaṃ kṛtvāpāṃ sūktair āplutya prakṣiṇam āvrtyāpa upaspṛśyety uktam ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the first day of summer, having performed the bathing with [the hymn] 'For long life,' having immersed [oneself] with the Water hymns, having circumambulated clockwise, 'Touch the waters' — thus it is stated.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,14.1) atha caitryāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tejovrataṃ trirātram aśnātīty uktam ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Caitra</s>, the <s>Tejovrata</s> (vow of radiance), a three-night fast — 'He eats' — thus it is stated.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,15.1) atha madanatrayodaśyāṃ vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ ca madhyāhne garte vā vāpyāṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ ghate vā sarvagandhān prakṣipya prāktantram abhyātānāntaṃ kṛtvā siṃhe vyāghre yaśo haviḥ prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divas pṛthivyā ity etaiḥ sūktair udakaṃ saṃpātyābhimantrya rājānaṃ snāpayet || praviśya saṃprokṣyeti ca tantraṃ saṃsthāpayet || dhenur dakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the thirteenth of <s>Madana</s> and on the full moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, at midday, in a pit, pool, lotus-pond, or jar, having thrown in all fragrances, having performed the <s>tantra</s> up to the concluding offering — 'In the lion, in the tiger,' 'Glory,' 'The oblation,' 'In the morning,' '<s>Agni</s>,' 'On the mountain,' 'In the <s>Aragarāṭa</s>s,' 'Of heaven and earth' — with these <s>sūkta</s>s, having mixed and consecrated the water, he should bathe the king. Having entered and sprinkled, he should conclude the <s>tantra</s>. A milch cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,16.1) atha śrāvaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vijaye muhūrte rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti catasṛbhī rakṣābandhanaṃ kṛtvā nīrājanaṃ ca bāhyenopaniṣkramyeti paiṭhīnasiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the full moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, at the auspicious moment of victory, 'May the fires protect you' — with these four [verses], having performed the tying of the protective [thread] and the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration), 'Going forth outside' — thus [says] <s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,17.1) athādityadina ādityamaṇḍalako vyākhyātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, on the day of the Sun (<s>Ādityadina</s>), the <s>Ādityamaṇḍala</s> (solar disc rite) is explained.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,18.1) atha janmanakṣatre janmanakṣatrayāgahomo vyākhyātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, under the birth-<s>nakṣatra</s>, the birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> sacrifice and <s>homa</s> (oblation) is explained.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,19.1) atha rājakarmāṇi pratinakṣatraṃ kartavyānīty āyudhāni khaḍgaprabhṛtīni bibhṛyād iti kṛttikārohiṇyādīni vyākhyātāni ||
body.translated_text: Now, the royal rites are to be performed for each <s>nakṣatra</s> — 'One should bear weapons, beginning with the sword' — the [rites for] <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and the rest are explained.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,19.2) indrotsava indramahotsavo vyākhyātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Indra</s> festival, the great <s>Indra</s> festival — is explained.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,19.3) pratidinaṃ grahayāgaḥ || pratidinaṃ nakṣatrayāgaḥ || pratidinaṃ daśagaṇī mahāśāntiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Daily the planetary sacrifice (<s>grahayāga</s>); daily the <s>nakṣatra</s> sacrifice; daily the ten-fold great pacification (<s>Daśagaṇī Mahāśānti</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_18b,19.4) pratisthānaṃ kṛttikārohiṇīvyākhyātā nakṣatrasnānāni nakṣatrakṣiṇāś ca ||
body.translated_text: For each station, the [rites of] <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s> are explained, as well as the <s>nakṣatra</s> baths and the <s>nakṣatra</s> penances.

body.text: (AVParis_18b,20.1) rājakarma sāṃvatsarīyaṃ hastyaśvādidīkṣā samāptā ||
body.translated_text: The annual royal rites and the consecration of elephants, horses, and the like — are completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_18c. vṛṣotsargaḥ)
(AVParis_18c,1.1) atha vṛṣotsargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 18c. The Release of the Bull) Now, the <s>vṛṣotsarga</s> (release of the bull).

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.2) kārttikeyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ raivatyām āśvayujyāṃ vā gavāṃ goṣṭhe paurṇamāsatantram ājyabhāgāntaṃ kṛtvā rudraraudrābhyām ājyaṃ juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: On the full moon of <s>Kārttikī</s>, or on [the day of] <s>Revatī</s> or <s>Āśvayujī</s>, in the cattle-pen, having performed the full-moon <s>tantra</s> up to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions), he should offer ghee with the two [verses] of <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Raudrī</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.3) pūṣā gā anu etu na iti catasṛbhiḥ pauṣṇasya juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> follow our cattle' — with these four [verses], he should offer the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (oblation to <s>Pūṣan</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.4) pūṣā gā anu etu naḥ pūṣā rakṣātu sarvataḥ | pūṣā vājaṃ sanotu naḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> follow our cattle; may <s>Pūṣan</s> protect from all sides; may <s>Pūṣan</s> grant us sustenance.'

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.5) pūṣann anu pra gā ihi(iti) yajamānasya sunvataḥ | asmākaṃ stuvatām uta ||
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Pūṣan</s>, go forth after the cattle' — of the worshipper who presses <s>Soma</s>, and of us who praise.

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.6) pūṣan tava vrate vayaṃ pari pūṣā purastād iti ||
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Pūṣan</s>, in your dominion, we [are]' — '<s>Pūṣan</s> from the east' — thus.

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.7) indrasya kukṣiḥ sāhasras tveṣa iti ṛṣabhaṃ saṃpātavantaṃ kṛtvā ya indra iva deveṣu iti ṛṣabhasya dakṣiṇe karṇe japet ||
body.translated_text: 'The belly of <s>Indra</s>, the thousandfold, the fierce one' — having made the bull the recipient of the <s>saṃpāta</s> (conjunction offering), 'He who among the gods is like <s>Indra</s>' — this he should whisper in the right ear of the bull.

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.8) lohitena svadhitina iti vatsatarīm anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: 'With a red axe' — with this he consecrates the heifer.

body.text: (AVParis_18c,1.9) ayaṃ prajānāṃ janitā prajāpatir gavāṃ goṣṭha iha madhyato vasaḥ | vatsatarīṣu apasadane gavām adhi tiṣṭha paśūn bhavanasya gopāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'This <s>Prajāpati</s>, the begetter of creatures, dwelling here in the midst of the cattle-pen — among the heifers, in the resting-place of the cows, stand firm, O guardian of the dwelling, over the cattle.'

body.text:
(AVParis_18c,1.10) iti maṇḍalāni bhrāmayati
(AVParis_18c,1.11) retodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi vayodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi yūthatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi gaṇatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi sahasrapoṣāyai tva7atisṛjāmi aparimitapoṣāyai tvātisṛjāmīti paryukṣyaikarūpaṃ dvirūpaṃ bahurūpaṃ vā yo vā yūthaṃ chādayati yūthena tejasvinālaṃkṛtenālaṃkṛtam aparājitāṃ diśaṃ niṣkrāmayeyuḥ saha vatsatarībhis tantraṃ saṃsthāpayeyur
(AVParis_18c,1.12) atha brahmaṇe gāṃ payasvinīṃ dadyāt pāyasena brāhmaṇān bhojayitvotsṛjya sarvān kāmān āpnoti akṣayāṇ ca lokān āpnotīti
body.translated_text: Thus he makes the circles revolve. 'I release you for the depositing of seed; I release you for the depositing of vitality; I release you for herd-formation; I release you for troop-formation; I release you for the prosperity of a thousand; I release you for unlimited prosperity' — thus, having sprinkled, [the bull] of one color, two colors, or many colors, or one that covers the herd — adorned with an adorned herd possessed of vigor — they should lead [them] out toward the invincible (northeast) direction together with the heifers; they should conclude the <s>tantra</s>. Then he should give a milch cow to the Brahmin; having fed the Brahmins with rice-pudding and having released [the bull], he obtains all desires and attains imperishable worlds — thus.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_19. indramahotsavaḥ)
(AVParis_19,1.1) atha rājñam indramahotsavasya upacārakalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 19. The Great Festival of <s>Indra</s>) Now we shall expound the ritual procedure of the great festival of <s>Indra</s> for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_19,1.2) prauṣṭhapade śuklapakṣe ||
body.translated_text: In [the month of] <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s> (Bhādrapada), in the bright fortnight.

children.text: (AVParis_19,1.3) saṃbhṛteṣu saṃbhāreṣu brahmā rājā ca ubhau snātau ahatavasanau surabhisujātānulepanau karmaṇyau vratavantau upavasataḥ
children.translated_text: When the materials have been gathered, the Brahmin (<s>purohita</s>) and the king, both bathed, wearing unworn garments, with fragrant and fine unguents, ritually fit, observing vows, keep the preparatory fast.

children.text: (AVParis_19,1.4) [vratavantau] śvo bhūte śamnodevyāḥ pādair ardharcābhyām ṛcā ṣakṛtvodakaṃ pari vācam ācānto
children.translated_text: Observing vows, on the morrow, with the <s>pāda</s>s (quarters) of '<s>Śaṃ no Devī</s>' — with the half-verses and the full verse, having sipped water once,

children.text: (AVParis_19,1.5) barhir upakalpayitvā rājānam anvālabhya juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having prepared the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), having touched the king, he should offer.

body.text:
(AVParis_19,1.6) arvāñcam indraṃ trātāram indram indraḥ sutrāmā imam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ me hantāya vṛṣa indrasya indro jayāti iti ca hutvā rāṣṭrasaṃvargaiś cā
(AVParis_19,1.7) atha indram utthāpayanti ā tvā ahārṣam antar dhruvādyaur viśas tvā sarvā vāñchantu iti sarvato 'pramattā dhārayerann
(AVParis_19,1.8) adbhutaṃ hi savanānayet samutthitaṃ bhavati || yadi prācyām agnibhayam || yadi dakṣiṇasyāṃ yamabhayam || yadi pratīcyāṃ varuṇabhayam || yadi udīcyāṃ kṣudbhayam || yadi antardeśebhyobhayato vidyād
(AVParis_19,1.9) agnir mā pātu agniṃ te vasumantam ṛcchantv iti || yathāsvaliṅgaṃ dvābhyāṃ-dvābhyāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśam upasthāpayet ||
body.translated_text: Having offered 'Hither <s>Indra</s>,' '<s>Indra</s> the protector,' '<s>Indra</s>, the good guardian,' 'This <s>Indra</s>, increase,' 'The <s>Kṣatriya</s> to me,' 'The slayer, the bull of <s>Indra</s>,' '<s>Indra</s> conquers,' and with the <s>Rāṣṭrasaṃvarga</s> (kingdom-acquisition) [hymns] — then they raise up [the image of] <s>Indra</s>: 'I have brought you hither,' 'From the steadfast,' 'May heaven and all the people desire you' — they should hold [it] without negligence from all sides. For it is a marvelous thing if the raised [image] should fall: if [it falls] toward the east, there is danger of fire; if toward the south, danger from <s>Yama</s> (death); if toward the west, danger from <s>Varuṇa</s> (waters); if toward the north, danger of famine; if between the regions, one should know danger from both sides.
