'May <s>Agni</s> protect me,' 'May <s>Agni</s>, the rich in <s>Vasu</s>s, come to you' — with two [verses] each according to their respective characteristic, he should install [offerings] clockwise in each direction.

body.text:
(AVParis_19,1.10) gṛdhraś ced asmin nipatati mṛtyor bhayaṃ bhavati || yad vā kṛṣṇaśakunir antarikṣrṇa patati iti japed yas tvā gṛdhraḥ kapota iti antato japet
(AVParis_19,1.11) sarvatra anājñāteṣu trirātraṃ ghṛtakambalam ||
body.translated_text: If a vulture alights upon it, there is danger of death. Or if a black bird falls from the sky — one should recite 'That vulture of yours, the pigeon' — and at the end one should recite. In all unrecognized [cases], a three-night [offering of] ghee-and-blanket [should be performed].

body.text: (AVParis_19,1.12) śirobhaṅge tu rājānaṃ madhyabhaṅge tu mantriṇam | ādibhaṅge janapadaṃ mūlabhaṅge tu nāgarān ||
body.translated_text: If the head breaks, [it portends doom for] the king; if the middle breaks, for the minister; if the beginning breaks, for the province; if the base breaks, for the citizens.

body.text: (AVParis_19,1.13) indrāṭako yadā bhidyād rājakośo vilupyate | rajjuchede parijāte nṛpatis tu vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>Indrāṭaka</s> (image of <s>Indra</s>) is split, the royal treasury is plundered; if the rope is cut or the festoon falls, the king perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_19,2.1) sāvitryā abhimantritaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam āvartayed rājānam abhibhūr yajña iti etais tribhiḥ sūktair anvārabdhe rājani pūrṇahomaṃ juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: Having consecrated with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra], he should circumambulate the king clockwise; 'The overpowering sacrifice' — with these three <s>sūkta</s>s, while the king is being attended upon, he should offer the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_19,3.1) atha paśūnām upācāram ||
body.translated_text: Now, the ritual treatment of the animals.

body.text:
(AVParis_19,3.2) indradevatāḥ syur ye rājño bhṛtyāḥ syuḥ sarve dīkṣitā brahmacāriṇaḥ syur
(AVParis_19,3.3) indraṃ copasadya yajeran || trirātraṃ saptarātraṃ vā
(AVParis_19,3.4) trir ayanam ahnām upatiṣṭhante havisā ca yajante ||
body.translated_text: All who are the king's servants should be devoted to <s>Indra</s>, all should be consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>) and celibate (<s>brahmacārin</s>); and having approached <s>Indra</s>, they should worship. For three nights or seven nights, three times daily they observe the rites and worship with oblations.

children.text: (AVParis_19,3.5) āvṛta indram aham iti indra kṣatram iti haviṣo hutvā
children.translated_text: 'I have chosen <s>Indra</s>,' '<s>Indra</s>, the sovereign power' — having offered the oblation,

children.text: (AVParis_19,3.6) brāhmaṇān svastivācya indram avabhṛthāya vrajanti
children.translated_text: Having pronounced the blessing on the Brahmins, they proceed to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: (AVParis_19,3.7) apāṃ sūktair āplutya pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya apa upaspṛśya anapekṣamāṇāḥ pratyetya brāhmaṇān bhaktyā yad īpsitaṃ varapradānaiḥ paritoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Having immersed [themselves] with the Water hymns, having circumambulated clockwise, having touched the waters, without looking back, having returned, he should gratify the Brahmins with devotion, with the granting of desired boons.

body.text: (AVParis_19,3.8) atha haiṣamitikam iti ||
body.translated_text: Now, thus is the saying regarding this matter.

body.text: (AVParis_19,3.9) śvaḥśvo 'sya rāṣṭraṃ jyāyo bhavati eko 'syāṃ pṛthivyāṃ rājā bhavati na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān indramaheṇa carati iti brāhmaṇam ||
body.translated_text: 'Day by day his kingdom becomes greater; he becomes the sole king on this earth; he does not perish before old age — he who knows thus, and he who, knowing thus, observes the great <s>Indra</s> festival' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (scriptural commentary).

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_19b. brahmayāgaḥ)
(AVParis_19b,1.1) oṃ bhārgavaṃ praṇipatyātha bhagavāñ śaunako 'vadat | brahmayāgavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ vistareṇa vadasva me ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 19b. The <s>Brahmayāga</s>) Oṃ. Having bowed to the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, the blessed <s>Śaunaka</s> said: 'Tell me in full detail the complete procedure of the <s>Brahmayāga</s> (sacrifice to <s>Brahman</s>).'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,1.2) paripṛṣṭaḥ sa tena atha atharvā yajatāṃ varaḥ | vidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ pratiṣṭhāya ākhyātum upacakrame ||
body.translated_text: Being thus questioned by him, <s>Atharvā</s>, the best of sacrificers, having established the complete procedure, began to expound it.

body.text: (AVParis_19b,1.3) sarveṣām eva yāgānāṃ paramo 'yam udāhṛtaḥ | brahmayāgaṃ prayatnena śṛṇu etaṃ tad yathākramam ||
body.translated_text: 'This is declared the supreme of all sacrifices; listen to this <s>Brahmayāga</s> with care, in proper sequence.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,1.4) hṛdye manohare śubhre sarvābādhāvivarjite | śleṣmāntakākṣagṛdhrādiparityakte same śubhe ||
body.translated_text: 'In a spot that is pleasing to the heart, charming, pure, free from all afflictions, abandoned by phlegm-[producing], inauspicious, owl-like, and vulture-like [presences], level and auspicious —'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,1.5) maṇḍapaṃ kārayet tatra yathoktavidhinā guruḥ | patākātoraṇir yuktaṃ dvāraiś ca api pṛthagvidhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'There the preceptor should have a pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>) constructed according to the prescribed procedure, equipped with banners, arches, and with various types of doorways.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,2.1) abhyukṣya śāntitoyena pañcagavyena vā sakṛt | gomayena pralipya ādau pūjayed varṇakiḥ pṛthak ||
body.translated_text: 'Having sprinkled with <s>śānti</s>-water (peace-water) or with <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow) once, having first smeared with cow-dung, he should worship separately with colored [powders].'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,2.2) puṣpaiś ca vividhaiḥ śubhraiḥ phalaiś ca api arcayed budhaḥ | tato baliṃ hared rātrau caturdikṣu vidhānavit ||
body.translated_text: 'The wise one should honor with various beautiful flowers and fruits; then, at night, the ritual-knower should offer <s>bali</s> (food-offering) in the four directions.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,2.3) pradīpān ghṛtapūrṇāṃś ca pradadyād vividhān tathā | ttato maṇḍapamadhye tu vartayed divyamaṇḍalam || [caturaśraṃ caturdvāraṃ vṛttākāram atha api vā] ||
body.translated_text: 'He should offer various lamps filled with ghee; then, in the middle of the pavilion, he should draw a divine <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) — [either] square with four doors, or of circular form.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,2.4) sitacūrṇena tanmadhye likhet padmaṃ suśobhanam | bahiś ca varṇaiḥ śubhrair nānā śobhāṃ prakalpayet ||
body.translated_text: 'In the middle of that, with white powder, he should draw a beautiful lotus; and outside, with bright colors, he should arrange various splendors.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,2.5) madhye padmaṃ tu saṃsthāpya brahmāṇaṃ parameśvaram | brahmajajñānasūktena yathoktam upakalpayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Having established in the center of the lotus <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme lord, he should set up [the image] as prescribed, with the <s>Brahmajajñāna-sūkta</s> (hymn of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>).'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,3.1) tatha imā āpa ityā dyair yathāvad adhivāsayet | rocanācandanādyaiś ca puṣpair dhūpaiś ca pūjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Likewise, with the [hymn beginning] "These waters" and similar ones, he should properly install; and he should worship with <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), sandalwood, and the like, with flowers and incense.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,3.2) ghṛtapradīpamālyaiś ca vastrair bhakṣaiś ca śobhanaiḥ | sitacandanakarpūraṃ dadyād vā api hi guggulam ||
body.translated_text: 'With ghee-lamps, garlands, garments, and fine food-offerings; he should offer white sandalwood, camphor, or indeed <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium).'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,3.3) pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā namet sarvāṅgakair naraḥ | dakṣiṇe paścime vā api bhāge vediḥ praśasyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, having circumambulated, a man should bow with all his limbs; on the southern or western side, the altar (<s>vedi</s>) is commended.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,3.4) kṛtvājyabhāgaparyantaṃ tataḥ śāntyudakaṃ punaḥ | brahmajajñānasūktena kuryāc caivātra pūjanam | tathaiva raudramantraiś ca abhiṣekāya kalpayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Having performed [the rites] up to the ghee-portions, then again the <s>śāntyudaka</s> (peace-water); with the <s>Brahmajajñāna-sūkta</s> he should perform the worship there; likewise, with the <s>Raudra</s> (of <s>Rudra</s>) <s>mantra</s>s, he should arrange for the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration).'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,3.5) hutvābhyātānamantrāṃś ca tato rudragaṇena ca | nīlarudraiś caruṃ vidvān vidhinā śrapayed budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Having offered the concluding <s>mantra</s>s, and then with the <s>Rudragaṇa</s> (troop of <s>Rudra</s>), the wise, learned one should cook the <s>caru</s> (oblation porridge) with the <s>Nīlarudra</s> [hymns] according to the proper method.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,4.1) homayet kutsasūktena ucchuṣmaiś ca yathāvidhi | japen mantrān tathāyuṣyān maṅgalyāṃś cāpi yatnataḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He should offer oblations with the <s>Kutsa-sūkta</s> and with the <s>Ucchuṣma</s> [hymns] as prescribed; he should recite the <s>mantra</s>s for longevity and also the auspicious ones with care.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,4.2) hutvā ca cātanaṃ tatra mātṛnāmagaṇena ca | snāpayet pañcagavyena tathā śāntyudakena ca ||
body.translated_text: 'Having offered the <s>cātana</s> (expulsion rite) there, with the names of the <s>Mātṛ</s> (Mother) troop, he should bathe [the king] with <s>pañcagavya</s> and also with <s>śāntyudaka</s> (peace-water).'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,4.3) phalasnānaṃ ca kurvīta yukto maṅgalavādibhiḥ | bandibhir vedavidbhiś ca strīsaṇgītair manoramaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'He should also perform the fruit-bath, accompanied by reciters of auspicious words, bards, <s>Veda</s>-knowers, and delightful songs of women.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,4.4) cārucāmarahastābhiś citradaṇḍaiḥ sadarpaṇaiḥ | snāpayed brahmasūktena raudreṇāpi tathārcayet ||
body.translated_text: 'With beautiful fly-whisk-bearing [attendants], with variegated staffs and mirrors, he should bathe [the king] with the <s>Brahma-sūkta</s> and also worship with the <s>Raudra</s> [hymn].'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,4.5) tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gataḥ | āśāsyeṣṭaphalaṃ tatra yukto maṅgalapāṭhakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, having circumambulated, having touched the ground with both knees, praying for the desired fruit there, accompanied by reciters of auspicious texts —'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.1) tūryaghoṣeṇa saṃyuktaḥ kṛtasvastyayanas tathā | kuryād dundubhinādaṃ tu śaṅkhabheriprapūritam ||
body.translated_text: 'Accompanied by the sound of musical instruments, having performed the <s>svastyayana</s> (benediction) likewise, he should make the sound of <s>dundubhi</s> drums, filled with the sound of conches and <s>bherī</s> drums.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.2) kuryād uttaratantraṃ ca sadasyān vācayet tataḥ | bhojayec chaktitas tatra brāhmaṇān vedapāragān ||
body.translated_text: 'He should perform the concluding <s>tantra</s> and then have the assembly recite; he should feed there, according to his ability, Brahmins who have mastered the <s>Veda</s>s.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.3) dīnānāthāndhakṛpaṇān bhakṣabhojyair anekadhā | annapānavihīnāṃś ca viśeṣeṇa prapūjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'The destitute, the lordless, the blind, and the wretched, with various foods and eatables; and those deprived of food and drink he should honor especially.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.4) dattvā ca dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā dadyād gaṇabaliṃ niśi | gṛhadevās tu saṃpūjyāḥ kāryaś cāpy utsavo gṛhe ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) according to ability, he should offer the group-offering (<s>gaṇabali</s>) at night; the household deities should be worshipped, and a celebration should be held in the house.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.5) yogino bhojayet paścād gṛhesu gṛhamedhinaḥ | achedyās taravaḥ kāryāḥ prāṇihiṃsāṃ ca varjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Afterward, he should feed the <s>yogin</s>s and the householders in their homes; trees should not be cut, and harm to living beings should be avoided.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.6) bandhanasthāś ca moktavyā baddhāḥ krodhāc ca śatravaḥ | abhayaṃ ghoṣayed deśe guruṃ ca paripūjayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Those in prison should be released, and even enemies bound in anger; he should proclaim safety (<s>abhaya</s>) throughout the land and worship the preceptor.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.7) abhayaṃ sarvato dattvā iṣṭe ca parameśvare | dīrgham āyur avāpnoti kṛtsnāṃ bhuṅkte vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: 'Having given safety to all and [having worshipped] the supreme lord who is desired, he obtains long life and enjoys the entire earth.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.8) brahmayāgavidhiḥ kṛtsno bhaktānāṃ tu mayoditaḥ | atharvaṇā surendrāya praṇatāya śubhecchayā ||
body.translated_text: 'The complete procedure of the <s>Brahmayāga</s> has been declared by me for the devotees; [it was taught] by <s>Atharvā</s> to the lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>) who bowed with auspicious intent.'

body.text: (AVParis_19b,5.9) kṛtābhiṣekaḥ kṛtayāga eṣa kṛtāhhnikaḥ kṛtarakṣaḥ sureśaḥ | atharvaṇo 'nugraham āśu labdhvā triviṣṭapaṃ virarājāsapatnam || iti ||
body.translated_text: 'He who has performed the consecration, who has performed the sacrifice, who has completed the daily rites, who has performed the protective [rites] — the lord of the gods, having quickly obtained the grace of <s>Atharvā</s>, shone resplendent in <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven), without rival.' Thus.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_20. skandayāgaḥ or dhūrtakalpaḥ)
(AVParis_20,1.1) athāto dhūrtakalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 20. The <s>Skandayāga</s> or <s>Dhūrtakalpa</s>) Now we shall expound the <s>Dhūrtakalpa</s> (ritual of <s>Dhūrta</s>, i.e., <s>Skanda</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_20,1.2) caturṣucaturṣu māseṣu phālguṇāṣāḍhakārttikapūrvapakṣeṣu nityaṃ kurvīta ||
body.translated_text: In every group of four months — in the bright fortnights of <s>Phālguna</s>, <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, and <s>Kārttika</s> — one should regularly perform [this rite].

body.text: (AVParis_20,1.3) śvo bhūte ṣaṣṭhyām upavāsaṃ kṛtvā prāgudīcīṃ diśaṃ niṣkramya śucau deśe manohare noṣare maṇḍalaṃ trayodaśaratniṃ kṛtvā madhye maṇḍapasya sarvavānaspatyāṃ mālāṃ kṛtvā ghaṇṭāpatākāsrajaḥ pratisaraṃ ca mālāpṛṣṭhe kṛtvā madhye darpaṇāṃś copakalpayitvā tatra yaṃ vahanti hayāḥ śvetā ity āvāhayet ||
body.translated_text: On the morrow, having observed a fast on the sixth, going forth in the northeast direction to a pure, charming, non-barren place, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle) of thirteen cubits, in the middle of the pavilion having made a garland of all forest-[products], having placed bells, banners, garlands, and protective threads on the back of the garland, and having arranged mirrors in the center — there he should invoke with 'Him whom white horses carry.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.1) yaṃ vahanti hayāḥ śvetā nityayuktā manojavāḥ | tam ahaṃ śvetasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'Him whom white horses carry, ever-yoked, swift as thought — him with white armor, <s>Dhūrta</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.2) yaṃ vahanti gajāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāś cāpi viṣāṇinaḥ | tam ahaṃ siṃhasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'Him whom elephants, lions, and horned tigers carry — him with lion-armor, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.3) yaṃ vahanti mayūrāś ca citrapakṣā vihaṃgamāḥ | tam ahaṃ citrasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'Him whom peacocks carry, bright-winged birds — him with variegated armor, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.4) yaṃ vahanti sarvavārṇāḥ sadāyuktā manojavāḥ | tam ahaṃ sarvasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'Him whom [steeds] of all colors carry, ever-yoked, swift as thought — him with universal armor, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.5) yasyāmoghā sadā śaktir nityaṃ ghaṇtāpatākinī | tam ahaṃ śaktisaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'He whose unfailing spear is ever adorned with bells and banners — him with spear-armor, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.6) yaś ca mātṛgaṇair nityaṃ sadā parivṛto yuvā | tam ahaṃ mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'He who is ever surrounded by the troop of <s>Mātṛ</s>s (Mothers), youthful always — him together with the <s>Mātṛ</s>s, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.7) yaś ca kanyāsahasreṇa sadā parivṛto mahān | tam ahaṃ siṃhasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: 'He who is ever surrounded by a thousand maidens, the great one — him with lion-armor, <s>Dhūrta</s>, I invoke.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.8) āyātu devaḥ sagaṇaḥ sasainyaḥ savāhanaḥ sānucaraḥ pratītaḥ | ṣaḍānano 'ṣṭādaśalocanaś ca suvarṇavarṇo laghupūrṇabhāsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'May the god come with his troop, with his army, with his vehicle, with his retinue, glorious — six-faced, eighteen-eyed, golden-hued, of swift and perfect splendor.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.9) āyātu devo mama kārttikeyo brahmaṇyapitraiḥ saha mātṛbhiś ca | bhrātrā viśākhena ca viśvarūpa imaṃ baliṃ sānucara juṣasva ||
body.translated_text: 'May the god <s>Kārtikeya</s> come to me, with the <s>Brahmanya</s>-ancestors, with the <s>Mātṛ</s>s (Mothers), with his brother <s>Viśākha</s>, of universal form — accept this offering, O attended one.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,2.10) saṃviśasveti saṃveśayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Enter' — thus he should make [the deity] enter.

body.text: (AVParis_20,3.1) saṃviśasva varaghaṇṭāpsaraḥstave yatra subhujo hi nirmitāḥ | saṃviṣṭo me dhehi dīrgham āyuḥ prajāṃ paśūṃś caiva vināyakasena ||
body.translated_text: 'Enter into the excellent bell, the praise of the <s>Apsaras</s>es, where the beautiful-armed ones have been fashioned; having entered, grant me long life, offspring, and cattle, O <s>Vināyakasena</s> (<s>Skanda</s>).'

body.text: (AVParis_20,3.2) imā āpa iti gandhodakaṃ pādyaṃ dadyāt || pratigṛhṇātu bhagavān devo dhūrta iti || ṣat caiva hiraṇyavarṇā itīme divyo gandharva iti gandhān yas te gandha iti cemāḥ sumanasa iti sumanasaḥ || priyaṃ dhātur iti... ||
body.translated_text: 'These waters' — he should offer fragrant water as a foot-washing (<s>pādya</s>). 'May the blessed lord, the god <s>Dhūrta</s>, accept' — thus. 'The golden-colored six [hymns],' 'This divine <s>Gandharva</s>' — [for] fragrances; 'Whatever fragrance is yours' — and 'These lovely flowers' — [for] flowers. 'Dear to <s>Dhātṛ</s>' — [and so forth].

body.text: (AVParis_20,3.3) vanaspatir aso medhya iti dhūpam || yakṣyeṇa te divā agniḥ śukraś ceti dīpam || yo viśvataḥ supratīka iti parṇāni ||
body.translated_text: 'The lord of the forest, the pure sacrificial [one]' — [for] incense. 'I shall worship you; by day <s>Agni</s>, the bright one' — [for] the lamp. 'He who is beautiful-faced from all sides' — [for] the leaves.

body.text:
(AVParis_20,3.4) prakṣālya haviṣy upasādayed dadhyodanaṃ kṣīrodanaṃ guḍodanaṃ mudgapayasamiśradhānyamodakāni sarvagandhān sarvarsān udakapūrṇaṃ mūlapurṇaṃ puṣpapūrṇaṃ phalapūrṇaṃ rasapūrṇaṃ copakalpayitvā
(AVParis_20,3.5) indraḥ sītam ity ullikhya agne prety agniṃ praṇīya prajvalya prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya bhaga etam idhmam iti tisṛbhir etam idhmaṃ sugārhaspatya ity upasamādhāya samiddho agnir iti samiddham anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,3.4) Having washed, one should place near the oblation materials: rice with yogurt, rice with milk, rice with jaggery, green-gram pudding, mixed-grain sweetmeats, all fragrances, all juices; and having prepared [vessels] filled with water, filled with roots, filled with flowers, filled with fruits, and filled with juices — (AVParis_20,3.5) with '<s>Indra</s> the furrow,' having drawn [the lines], with '<s>Agni</s>, go forth,' having led the fire forward, having kindled [it], having placed fuel facing east, with the three [verses] 'O <s>Bhaga</s>, this fuel,' having placed this fuel with 'O prosperous householder,' he consecrates the kindled [fire] with 'The fire is kindled.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,4.1) bhadram icchanto hiraṇyagarbho mamāgne varcas tvayā manyo yas te manyo yad devā devaheḍanam iti ṣat kāmasūktādayo daśa mahīpataye svāhā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,4.1) 'Desiring blessedness,' '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>,' 'O <s>Agni</s>, my splendor,' 'By you, O <s>Manyu</s>,' 'O <s>Manyu</s>, you who,' 'What, O gods, [if there be] offense to the gods' — these six; the ten beginning with the desire-hymns — '<s>svāhā</s> to the lord of the earth!'

body.text: (AVParis_20,4.2) dhūrtāya skandāya viśākhāya pinākasenāya bhrātṛstrīkāmāya svacchandāya varaghaṇtāya nirmilāya lohitagātrāya śalakaṭaṅkaṭāya svāheti hutvā agnaye prajāpataye ye devā divy ekādaśa stheti anumataye agnaye sviṣṭakṛta iti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,4.2) Having offered with '<s>svāhā</s> to <s>Dhūrta</s> (the Cunning One), to <s>Skanda</s>, to <s>Viśākha</s>, to <s>Pinākasenā</s>, to the Desirer-of-Brothers'-Wives, to the Self-Willed, to <s>Varaghaṇṭa</s>, to <s>Nirmila</s>, to the Red-Limbed, to <s>Śalakaṭaṅkaṭa</s>' — and 'to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>,' 'Those gods who stand eleven in heaven,' 'to <s>Anumati</s>,' and 'to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.1) śivāgnikṛttikānāṃ tu stoṣyāmi varadaṃ śubham | sa me stuto viśvarūpaj sarvān arthān prayacchatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.1) I shall praise the auspicious boon-granter of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the <s>Kṛttikās</s>. May he, praised, being of universal form, grant me all desires.

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.2) dhanadhānyakulān bhogān sa me vacanavedanam | dāsīdāsaṃ tathā sthānaṃ maṇiratnaṃ surāñjanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.2) Wealth, grain, lineages, enjoyments — may he [give] at my word and knowledge; maidservants and manservants, likewise a dwelling, gems, jewels, and divine collyrium.

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.3) ye bhaktyā bhajante dhūrtaṃ brahmaṇyaṃ ca yaśasvinam | sarve te dhanavantaḥ syuḥ prajāvanto yaśasvinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.3) Those who with devotion worship <s>Dhūrta</s> (the Cunning One), the devoted one, the illustrious one — they shall all become wealthy, endowed with offspring, and famous.

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.4) yathendras tu varān labdhvā prītas tu bhagavān purā | dehi me vipulān bhogān bhaktānāṃ ca viśeṣata iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.4) Just as <s>Indra</s>, having obtained boons, was pleased, O Lord, in ancient times — so grant me abundant enjoyments, and especially to the devoted.

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.5) kāmasūktenopahāram upaharet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.5) With the Desire-hymn, one should make the offering.

body.text: (AVParis_20,5.6) upahāram imaṃ deva mayā bhaktyā niveditam | pratigṛhya yathānyāyam akruddhaḥ sumanā bhava ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,5.6) "This offering, O God, presented by me with devotion — accepting it duly, be without anger and of gracious mind."

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.1) sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi sadyojātāya vai namaḥ | bhavebhave nādibhave bhajasva māṃ bhavodbhaveti bhavāya namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.1) I take refuge in <s>Sadyojāta</s>; salutation to <s>Sadyojāta</s> indeed. In existence after existence, not in non-existence, favor me — salutation to <s>Bhava</s>, born from existence.

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.2) devaṃ prapadye varadaṃ prapadye skandaṃ prapadye ca kumāram ugram | ṣaṇṇāṃ sutaṃ kṛttikānāṃ ṣaḍāsyam agneḥ putraṃ sādhanaṃ gopathoktaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.2) I take refuge in the god, I take refuge in the boon-granter, I take refuge in <s>Skanda</s>, in the fierce <s>Kumāra</s>; the son of the six <s>Kṛttikās</s>, the six-faced, the son of <s>Agni</s> — [I worship] with the means taught in the <s>Gopatha</s> [Brāhmaṇa].

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.3) raktāni yasya puṣpāṇi raktaṃ yasya vilepanam | kukkuṭā yasya raktākṣāḥ sa me skandaḥ prasīdatu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.3) He whose flowers are red, whose unguent is red, whose roosters have red eyes — may that <s>Skanda</s> be gracious to me.

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.4) āgneyaṃ kṛttikāputram aindraṃ ke cid adhīyate | ke cit pāśupataṃ raudraṃ yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu ta iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.4) Some study him as belonging to <s>Agni</s>, the son of the <s>Kṛttikās</s>; some as belonging to <s>Indra</s>; some as <s>Pāśupata</s> and <s>Raudra</s> (belonging to <s>Rudra</s>) — whoever you are, you are that; salutation to you.

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.5) svāmine namaḥ śaṅkarāyāgniputrāya kṛttikāputrāya namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.5) Salutation to the Lord, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, to the son of <s>Agni</s>, to the son of the <s>Kṛttikās</s> — salutation!

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.6) bhagavān kva cid apratirūpaḥ svāhā bhagavān kva cid apratirūpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.6) The Lord is somewhere incomparable — <s>svāhā</s>! The Lord is somewhere incomparable.

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.7) maṇiratnavarapratirūpaḥ || kāñcanaratnavarapratirūpa iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.7) Incomparable with the finest gems and jewels! Incomparable with the finest gold and jewels!

body.text: (AVParis_20,6.8) ete [te] deva gandhā etāni puṣpāṇy eṣa dhūpa etāṃ mālāṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā ādityakartitaṃ sūtram iti pratisaram ābadhnīyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,6.8) "These are your fragrances, O God; these are [your] flowers; this is incense; this garland" — having circumambulated three times clockwise, with 'the thread fashioned by the sun,' one should tie on the protective cord.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.1) ādityakartitaṃ sūtram indreṇa trivṛtīkṛtam | aśvibhyāṃ grathito granthir brahmaṇā pratisaraḥ kṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.1) The thread fashioned by the sun, made triple by <s>Indra</s>, its knot tied by the two <s>Aśvins</s>, made a protective cord by <s>Brahman</s> —

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.2) dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam aśubhasya ca ghātanam | badhnāmi pratisaram imaṃ sarvaśatrunibarhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.2) auspicious, fame-giving, life-bestowing, and the destroyer of inauspiciousness — I tie on this protective cord, the annihilator of all enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.3) rakṣobhyaś ca piśācebhyo gandharvebhyas tathaiva ca | manuṣyebhyo bhayaṃ nāsti yac ca syād duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.3) From <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Piśācas</s>, from <s>Gandharvas</s> likewise, from humans — there is no fear; and whatever evil deed has been done —

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.4) svakṛtāt parakṛtāc ca duṣkṛtāt pratimucyate | sarvasmāt pātakān mukto bhaved vīras tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.4) from self-caused and other-caused evil, one is released. Freed from all sin, one becomes indeed a hero.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.5) abhicārāc ca kṛtyātaḥ strīkṛtād aśubhaṃ ca yat | tāvat tasya bhataṃ nāsti yāvat sūtraṃ sa dhārayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.5) From sorcery and black magic, and whatever inauspiciousness is wrought by women — so long as he wears the thread, no harm [comes] to him.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.6) yāvad āpaś ca gāvaś ca yāvat sthāsyanti parvatāḥ | tāvat tasya bhayaṃ nāsti yaḥ sūtraṃ dhārayiṣyatīti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.6) As long as waters and cows [exist], as long as mountains shall stand — so long there is no fear for him who will wear the thread.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.7) anvāyaṃ bhuktvā devaṃ visarjayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.7) Having eaten the ritual meal, one should dismiss the deity.

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.8) pramodo nāma gandharvaḥ pradoṣo paridhāvati | muñca śailamayāt pāpan muñcamuñca pramuñca ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.8) "The <s>Gandharva</s> named <s>Pramoda</s> (Delight) runs about at twilight; release from the mountain-born sin — release, release, fully release!"

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.9) [yāvat] imā āpaḥ pavanena pūtā hiraṇyavarṇā anavadyarūpāḥ | tāvad imaṃ dhūrtaṃ pravāhayāmi pravāhito me dehi varān yathoktān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.9) "These waters, purified by the wind, golden-hued, of faultless form — with them I send forth <s>Dhūrta</s> (the Cunning One); being sent forth, grant me the boons as stated."

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.10) uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu gṛhān praviṣṭo gṛhiṇīṃ paśyet dhanavati dhanaṃ me dehīti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.10) When the <s>nakṣatras</s> have risen, having entered the house, one should look at the housewife [and say]: 'O wealthy one, give me wealth!'

body.text: (AVParis_20,7.11) yad bhoktuṃ kāmajātaṃ jagatyāṃ manasā saṃhīhate tattad dvijanmā pinākasenayajamānāt kāmam upabhukto bhuktvāmṛtatvaṃ tadvad evābhyupaiti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_20,7.11) Whatever desire-born food one conceives in one's mind in this world — all that the twice-born one enjoys from the sacrificer of <s>Pinākasenā</s>; having enjoyed, he attains immortality just so.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_21. saṃbhāralakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_21,1.1) oṃ saṃbhārān kīrtayiṣyāmo yathālakṣaṇasaṃyutān | yaiḥ karma kriyamāṇaṃ hi phalavat syād dvijanmanām ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 21: Characteristics of Ritual Materials) (AVParis_21,1.1) Oṃ. We shall enumerate the ritual materials together with their proper characteristics, with which the rite being performed becomes fruitful for the twice-born.

body.text: (AVParis_21,1.2) achinnāgrān kuśān ārdrān indranīlasamaprabhān | śuṣkān api śvetavarṇān āhuḥ śāntikarān budhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.2) <s>Kuśa</s> grasses, with uncut tips, moist, shining like sapphires; even dry ones of white color are declared by the wise to be peace-bringing.

body.text: (AVParis_21,1.3) surabhīṇi ca puṣpāṇi susvādūni phalāni ca manoharāṇi vāsāṃsi saṃbhāreṣūpakalpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.3) Fragrant flowers, sweet-tasting fruits, and pleasing garments — these one should prepare among the ritual materials.

body.text: (AVParis_21,1.4) surabhīṇy eva bījāni anyavastūni yāni ca | arghacandanadhūpādi hemaratnādi cottamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.4) Fragrant seeds and whatever other substances; <s>arghya</s> (guest-water), sandalwood, incense and the rest; gold, gems, and the rest — of the finest quality.

children.text: (AVParis_21,1.7cd) gāvaś ca dakṣiṇārthaṃ hi payasvinyaḥ sulakṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.7cd) And cows for the purpose of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee), milch cows of good marks.

children.text: (AVParis_21,1.8ab) ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca catvāraś caturṇāṃ vedavittamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.8ab) Sixteen, or eight, or four — those most learned in the four <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_21,1.5) ṛtvijas tu samākhyātā vayaḥśīlaguṇānvitāḥ | dvātriṃśat ṣoḍaśāṣṭau vā śāntikārye tathādbhute ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.5) The <s>ṛtvij</s>s (priests) are declared to be endowed with age, conduct, and virtues: thirty-two, sixteen, or eight for the peace-rite and for extraordinary [rites].

body.text: (AVParis_21,1.6) sahiraṇyāḥ savastrāś ca sālaṃkārāḥ savatsakāḥ | te sadasyā iti proktā vācane yajñakarmaṇi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.6) [The cows should be] with gold, with garments, with ornaments, and with calves. Those are called the assembly-members — for the recitation in the sacrificial ritual.

children.text: (AVParis_21,1.7ab) sarve te 'pi hy atharvāṇa ṛtvijaḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.7ab) All those <s>Atharvan</s> priests are remembered as sixteen officiants;

children.text: (AVParis_21,1.8cd) śuddhātmāno japair homair vaidikair vītamatsarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis_21,1.8cd) pure-souled through <s>japa</s> (prayer) and Vedic <s>homas</s> (oblations), free from jealousy.

body.text: (AVParis_21,2.1) tāmrarājatahaimānāṃ mṛnmayānām athāpi vā | achidrāṇāṃ savarṇānāṃ kalaśānāṃ ca saṃgrahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,2.1) The collection of vessels — of copper, silver, gold, or of clay — unbroken and of uniform color.

body.text: (AVParis_21,2.2) carūṇām atha pātrāṇām indhanānāṃ viśeṣataḥ | yavavrīhitila''ādīnām ājyasyāharaṇaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,2.2) Of cooking pots, of ritual vessels, and especially of fuel-wood; the bringing of barley, rice, sesame, and the rest, and of ghee likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_21,2.3) achidrāsphātitāvakrā dīrghaparvāḥ sumadhyamāḥ | śamīdūrvātarūṇāṃ tu jñeyāḥ śāntau śabhāvāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,2.3) Unbroken, unsplit, unbent, with long internodes, of good middle portions — the characteristics of <s>śamī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, and trees for the peace-rite should be known.

body.text: (AVParis_21,2.4) puṣkaratantugovālatruṭisarṣapayavasya tu | ṣaḍguṇitaḥṣaḍguṇito [bhavati] narasyāṅgulamāne ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,2.4) [The measurement of] lotus-fiber, cow-tail-hair, <s>truṭi</s>, mustard-seed, and barley — each multiplied six-fold gives the finger-measure of a man.

body.text: (AVParis_21,2.5) gopucchasadṛśo daṇḍaḥ samaḥ ślakṣṇo manoharaḥ | sruvaś ca śāntuke jñeyaḥ srug uktā yajñalakṣaṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,2.5) The ladle-stick should be like a cow's tail — smooth, even, pleasing. The <s>sruva</s> (small ladle) for peace-rites should be known; the <s>sruk</s> (large ladle) is described with the characteristics of the sacrifice.

body.text: (AVParis_21,3.1) sauvarṇaḥ śāntike proktaḥ pālaśo vātha khādiraḥ | abhicāre viśeṣeṇa kuryāt sruvam ayomayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,3.1) For peace-rites, a golden [ladle] is prescribed, or one of <s>Palāśa</s> or <s>Khadira</s> wood. For sorcery especially, one should make an iron ladle.

body.text: (AVParis_21,3.2) kāṃsyaṃ yccāṭane kuryād āśvatthaṃ vaśyakarmaṇi | viśeṣeṇa tu vidveṣe sruvo nimbamayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,3.2) For expulsion rites, one should make one of bronze; for subjugation rites, one of <s>Aśvattha</s> wood. Especially for rites of enmity, the ladle is remembered to be of <s>Nimba</s> (neem) wood.

body.text: (AVParis_21,3.3) pauṣṭike rājataṃ vidyāt tāmraṃ ca vijayāvaham | amṛtādau tu vijñeyaś cāndanaḥ siddhidaḥ sruvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,3.3) For nourishment rites, one should know it to be of silver; copper brings victory. For the <s>Amṛta</s> (nectar) rite and others, a sandalwood ladle is known to grant success.

body.text: (AVParis_21,3.4) sruvāṇāṃ viṣayaṃ jñātvā kīlakānāṃ vidhiṃ tathā | gṛhasyāśmavidhiṃ dikṣu karmasiddhim avāpnuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,3.4) Having learned the domain of ladles, and the procedure for stakes likewise, and the stone-ritual for the house in the directions, one obtains the success of the rite.

body.text: (AVParis_21,3.5) śleṣmātakārkakaṇṭakikaṭutiktādivarjite | ariṣṭagṛdhrakauśikavihaṃgaiś ca vivarjite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,3.5) [The ground should be] free from <s>Śleṣmātaka</s>, <s>Arka</s>, thorny plants, and bitter and pungent [trees]; and free from <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, vultures, owls, and [other] birds.

body.text: (AVParis_21,4.1) gulmavallīlatāyukte hṛdyaiś ca madhurair drumaiḥ | taruṇaiḥ phalavadbhiś ca śmaśānāsthivivarjite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,4.1) [But] endowed with shrubs, creepers, and vines, with pleasant and sweet-bearing trees, with young fruit-bearing ones, and free from cremation grounds and bones.

body.text: (AVParis_21,4.2) mayūracakravākādihaṃsakāraṇḍavādibhiḥ | susvarair nādite deśe hṛdyāṅkurasamanvite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,4.2) In a place resounding with the sweet voices of peacocks, <s>Cakravāka</s>s, swans, <s>Kāraṇḍava</s>s, and the like — endowed with pleasing sprouts.

body.text: (AVParis_21,4.3) nadītaṭe samudrasya saṃgame vā viśeṣataḥ | anindye digvibhāge ca uttare vāparājite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,4.3) On a riverbank, or especially at the confluence of the ocean; in a blameless quarter of the directions — on the northern or invincible [side].

body.text: (AVParis_21,4.4) bhūmiṃ saṃśodhayet kartā prāgudakppravaṇe śubhe | prācīṃ saṃśodhya yatnena maṇḍapaṃ tatra kārayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,4.4) The performer should purify the ground on auspicious [terrain] sloping to the east and north. Having carefully purified the eastern [part], one should construct the ritual pavilion there.

body.text: (AVParis_21,4.5) navakoṣṭhaṃ samaṃ vāpi hastaiḥ ṣoṣaśabhir mitam | caturaśraṃ caturdvāram ekordhvadvāram eva vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,4.5) With nine compartments, or level, measured by sixteen <s>hastas</s> (cubits); four-sided, with four doors, or with a single upward opening.

body.text: (AVParis_21,5.1) tata īśānakoṇe tu snānavediṃ samācaret | daśadvādaśahastaṃ vā yathāvitānam eva vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,5.1) Then, in the <s>Īśāna</s> (northeast) corner, one should prepare the bathing-altar — ten or twelve <s>hastas</s>, or matching the canopy.

body.text: (AVParis_21,5.2) caturguṇocchrayāś caiva mūlastambhās tu ye tataḥ | upastambhās tu ye pārśve tadardhena prakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,5.2) The main pillars should be four times the height [of a man]; the side-pillars are declared to be half that.

body.text: (AVParis_21,5.3) kumbhāḥ stambhais tathā deyāḥ kāmair dvāraṃ diśāṃ smṛtam | yajamānocchrayaṃ vāpi tadardhena prakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,5.3) Vessels should be given with the pillars; the door is remembered as the direction's desire. [The height may be] that of the sacrificer, and [the side pillars] declared to be half that.

body.text: (AVParis_21,5.4) kuṇḍākṛti gṛhaṃ kuryād dviguṇaṃ pariveṣtitam | sarvadikṣu plavaṃ caiva kuṇḍasyordhvaṃ na chādayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,5.4) One should make a fire-pit-shaped enclosure, surrounded double; with a channel on all sides; and above the fire-pit, one should not cover [it].

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.1) parito dvādaśasthūnaṃ catu[ḥ]stambhaṃ tu madhyataḥ | arcitaṃ pūjitaṃ nityaṃ śāntau śāntigṛhaṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.1) With twelve pillars all around, and four pillars in the middle; always honored and worshipped — this is known as the peace-house for the peace-rite.

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.2) netrādyullocaśobhiṣṭhaṃ nānāvarṇadhvajākulam | raktā pītā ca dhūmrā ca kṛṣṇā nīlātha pāṇḍurā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.2) Adorned with beautiful strings and decorations on top, crowded with banners of various colors — red, yellow, smoky, black, blue, and white;

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.3) vicitrā hīndranīlābhā patākāḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ | [aindrāyudhadhūmrakṛṣṇanīlapāṇḍuravarṇakāḥ] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.3) variegated, sapphire-colored — sixteen banners are prescribed; [of rainbow-hued, smoky, black, blue, and white colors;]

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.4) [pītaraktasitāḥ śyāmā patākāḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ |] kalaśān ṣoḍaśān tatra upariṣṭān mahādhvajaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.4) [yellow, red, white, and dark — sixteen banners are prescribed.] Sixteen vessels there, and above them a great banner.

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.5) vastreṇāchāditān kuryāt sahiraṇyān pṛthakpṛthak | maṇimuktāphalaiḥ puṣpair hṛdyaiś ca madhuraiḥ phalaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.5) One should make [them] covered with cloth, each with gold separately; with gems, pearls, flowers, and with pleasing, sweet fruits.

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.6) samantād dikṣu vinyastaiḥ pradīpaiś cāpy alaṃkṛtam | dhūpair balyupahāraiś ca jayaghoṣaiś ca bandinām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.6) Adorned on all sides with lamps placed in the directions; with incense, <s>bali</s>-offerings, and victory-cries of the bards.

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.7) śaṅkhatūryaninādais tu vīṇādundubhisasmitaiḥ | pūjyamāno hi nṛpatiḥ praviśet sapurohitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.7) With the sounds of conches and instruments, with <s>vīṇās</s> and drums accompanied by laughter — the king, being honored, should enter together with his <s>purohita</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_21,6.8) tataḥ śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā cātanenānuyojitam | saṃprokṣya vidhivan mantrair ānayed araṇī tataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,6.8) Then, having prepared the peace-water, applied with a strainer, having sprinkled duly with mantras, one should then bring the fire-churning sticks.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.1) mathite 'gnau vidhānena śāntyudakena samantrakam | homaṃ kṛtvā yathoktaṃ tu nimittāny upalakṣayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,7.1) When fire has been produced by churning according to procedure, with the peace-water accompanied by mantras, having performed the oblation as prescribed, one should observe the omens.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.2) meghadundubhinirghoṣaiḥ prajvalan sarvatas tathā | avyavachinnadīrghārciḥ susnigdhaḥ siddhikārakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,7.2) [If it sounds] with thunder-like rumbling of drums, blazing on all sides, with unbroken, long flames, well-oiled — [this is] productive of success.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.3) kiṃśukāśokapadmābho nīlotpalanibhas tathā | vahniḥ siddhikaro jñeyaḥ saptarātrān na saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_21,7.3) [If it has] the appearance of <s>Kiṃśuka</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, or lotus, or if it resembles the blue lotus — the fire is known to be productive of success within seven nights, without doubt.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.4) hutamātre prajvalati vihasann iva dṛśyate | taṃ vidyāt siddhidaṃ vahniṃ padmavarṇanibhaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: As soon as the oblation is offered, it blazes up and appears as if laughing — one should know that fire, of lotus-like color, to be a granter of success.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.5) asnigdhārciḥ sadhūmo yaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇo 'pradakṣiṇaḥ | yathoktaviparītas tu na vahniḥ syāt prayaṃkaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: That which has a non-oily flame, is smoky, of black color, and moves counter-clockwise — a fire with characteristics opposite to those stated will not be productive.

body.text: (AVParis_21,7.6) yasmin prasannatām eti hūyamāne hutāśane | tatra nityaṃ mahāsiddhir asamāpte vinirdiśet || asamāpte vinirdiśet || iti saṃbhāralakṣaṇaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: Whenever the sacrificial fire becomes serene while being offered into, one should always declare great success there, even when [the rite is] incomplete. Thus the characteristics of the ritual materials are completed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_22. araṇilakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_22,1.1) om athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi araṇyoś caiva lakṣaṇam | rūpam athā pramāṇaṃ ca guṇadoṣān tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 22: Characteristics of the Fire-Churning Sticks [<s>Araṇi-lakṣaṇa</s>]) Oṃ. Now I shall declare the characteristics of the two fire-churning sticks (<s>araṇi</s>s) — their form, measurement, and their merits and defects likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_22,1.2) coditān śabdaśāstreṇa ācāryeṇa tu dhīmatā | purā kalpe ca yad dṛṣṭam ṛṣibhiś caiva lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: As prompted by the science of grammar, by the wise teacher, and the characteristics seen by the <s>Ṛṣi</s>s in ancient times.

body.text: (AVParis_22,1.3) gṛhyāgniṃ parisaṃgṛhya dharmapatnyā sahaiva tu | vaitānikās tataḥ kuryād ādhānādyā yathoditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having collected the household fire together with the lawful wife, one should then perform the <s>Vaitānika</s> (solemn) rites, beginning with the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>), as prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_22,1.4) tithau śubhāyāṃ nakṣatre diśaṃ gatvā tv aninditām | aśvatthāt tu śamīgarbhād uktam āharaṇaṃ śruteḥ ||
body.translated_text: On an auspicious <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) and <s>nakṣatra</s>, having gone in an unblemished direction, the fetching [of the fire-churning wood] from the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) growing within a <s>Śamī</s> tree is prescribed by the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic scripture).

body.text: (AVParis_22,1.5) śamīvṛkṣe tu yo 'śvattho nānyavṛkṣeṇa saṃyutaḥ | madhye mūlaṃ na bāhye tu sa garbhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Aśvattha</s> that [grows] in a <s>Śamī</s> tree, not joined with any other tree, [rooted] in the middle [of the trunk], not on the outside — that is declared to be the 'embryo' (<s>garbha</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_22,2.1) abhāve tu śamīgarbhe aśvatthād eva vāharet | prāpte caiva śamīgarbhe samāropya visarjayet ||
body.translated_text: In the absence of a <s>Śamī</s>-embryo, one should fetch [wood] from an <s>Aśvattha</s> alone; when a <s>Śamī</s>-embryo is obtained, having placed [the other] upon it, one should release [the old one].

body.text: (AVParis_22,2.2) caturviṃśāṅgulā dīrghā vistareṇa ṣaḍaṅgulā | caturaṅgulocchrayā ca araṇiś cottarāraṇiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Twenty-four <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths) in length, six <s>aṅgula</s>s in breadth, four <s>aṅgula</s>s in height — [this is] the <s>araṇi</s> (lower churning stick) and the <s>uttarāraṇi</s> (upper churning stick).

body.text: (AVParis_22,2.3) ā skandhād uraso vāpi iti staudāyanaiḥ smṛtā | bāhumātrā devadarśair jājalair ūrumātrikā ||
body.translated_text: Up to the shoulder or up to the chest — thus it is remembered by the <s>Staudāyana</s>s; an arm's length by the <s>Devadarśa</s>s; thigh-length by the <s>Jājala</s>s;

body.text: (AVParis_22,2.4) cāraṇavaidyair jaṅghe ca maudenāṣṭāṅgulāni ca | jaladāyanair vitastir vā ṣoḍaśeti tu bhārgavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Shank-length by the <s>Cāraṇavaidya</s>s; eight <s>aṅgula</s>s by <s>Mauda</s>; a span (twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s) by the <s>Jaladāyana</s>s; or sixteen — thus says the <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_22,2.5) śiraḥpramāṇe nābhau tu caturviṃśatikaiva hi | śaunakādibhir ācāryair etan mānaṃ prakīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: Head-measure [is used] for the navel [portion]; indeed, it is twenty-four. This measurement is declared by the teachers beginning with <s>Śaunaka</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_22,3.1) tasyās tu piṇḍaḥ ṣaḍbhāge caturbhāge tu vistare | caturaśrā ca ślakṣṇā ca chidragranthivivarjitā ||
body.translated_text: Its cylindrical projection (<s>piṇḍa</s>) is one-sixth [of the length] and one-fourth in width; it should be four-sided and smooth, free from holes and knots.

body.text: (AVParis_22,3.2) klinnā bhinnāgnisaṃspṛṣṭā sphuṭitā vidyutā hatā | anyaiś ca doṣaiḥ saṃyuktā varjanīyā prayatnataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Wet, cracked, touched by fire, split, struck by lightning, or combined with other defects — [such wood] should be carefully avoided.

body.text: (AVParis_22,3.3) śirogranthir harec cakṣuś chidrā patnīvināśinī | klinnā vināśayet putrān sphuṭitā śokam āvahet ||
body.translated_text: A knot at the head destroys eyesight; a hole [in it] destroys the wife; wetness destroys sons; a crack brings grief.

body.text: (AVParis_22,3.4) ūrdhvaśuṣke na kartavyā kṛṣṇe rūkṣe tathaiva ca | ubhe apy ekavṛkṣe ca araṇiś cottarāraṇiḥ ||
body.translated_text: It should not be made from [wood] dried from above, nor from black or rough [wood]; both the <s>araṇi</s> and the <s>uttarāraṇi</s> should be from the same tree.

body.text: (AVParis_22,3.5) tatpramāṇā tadardhā vā bhūyasī vā yathecchayā | anenaiva tu manthavyo na kuryād yonisaṃkaram ||
body.translated_text: Of that same measure, or half, or more, as one wishes — one should churn with this same [stick]; one should not cause mixing of the <s>yoni</s> (receptacle).

body.text: (AVParis_22,4.1) yonisaṃkarasaṃkīrṇe mahān doṣaḥ prapadyate | sa yajñas tāmaso nāma phalaṃ tatra na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: When there is mixing of the <s>yoni</s>, a great defect occurs; that sacrifice is called <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) — no fruit is found therein.

body.text: (AVParis_22,4.2) piṇḍe tv ayanaviṣuvau pṛthutve ṛtavaḥ sthitāḥ | ardhamāsāś ca dīrghatve kālaś cātra pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the cylindrical part are the two <s>ayana</s>s (solstices) and the equinox; in the breadth the seasons are established; the fortnights in the length; and Time is established therein.

body.text: (AVParis_22,4.3) yajamāno 'raṇir iti vadanty eke vipaścitaḥ | tatpradhānāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yajñaś cāpi tathaiva hi ||
body.translated_text: Some learned ones say the sacrificer is the <s>araṇi</s>; all rites are centered on it, and the sacrifice likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_22,4.4) prathame mūlaṣaḍbhāge pādau jaṅgheti kīrtyate | dvitīye jānunī ūrū tṛtīye śroṇir ucyate ||
body.translated_text: In the first sixth from the base: the feet and shanks are declared; in the second: the knees and thighs; in the third: the hip is said;

body.text: (AVParis_22,4.5) caturthe jaṭharaṃ sāṅgaṃ grīvā caiva tu pañcame | ṣaṣthe śiraḥ samākhyātam aṅgāny etāni nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: In the fourth: the belly with its limbs; in the fifth: the neck; in the sixth: the head is named — these limbs should be designated.

body.text: (AVParis_22,5.1) mathite pādajaṅghe ca piśācaḥ saṃprajāyate | jānunoś ca tathā corvo rākṣastvaṃ prayāti hi ||
body.translated_text: If churned at the feet and shanks, a <s>Piśāca</s> (demon) is produced; at the knees and thighs, it leads to <s>Rākṣasa</s>-hood;

body.text: (AVParis_22,5.2) śroṇyāṃ ca sarvakāmā[ḥ] syur jaṭhare kṣut tathā smṛtā | urasy amitrā grīvāyāṃ mṛtyuḥ śirasi vedanā ||
body.translated_text: At the hip, all desires are fulfilled; at the belly, hunger is said [to result]; at the chest, enemies; at the neck, death; at the head, pain.

body.text: (AVParis_22,5.3) śroṇyām evāta aicchanti nirdoṣā kīrtitā yataḥ | tathā vittapaśūn putrān svargam āyuḥ priyaṃ sukham ||
body.translated_text: Therefore they desire [churning] at the hip alone, since that is declared faultless; likewise [one obtains] wealth, cattle, sons, heaven, long life, delight, and happiness.

body.text: (AVParis_22,5.4) prathamaṃ manthanaṃ śroṇyām ādhāne ca viśeṣataḥ | itarāṇi yatheṣtaṃ hi grīvāṃ sarvatra varjayet ||
body.translated_text: The first churning at the hip, and especially at the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>); the others as desired — but one should always avoid the neck.

body.text: (AVParis_22,5.5) trīṇy aṅgulāni tyaktvādau tathā catvāri cāntataḥ | madhye devāḥ sthitās tasmād vahniṃ tatraiva manthayet ||
body.translated_text: Having left three <s>aṅgula</s>s at the beginning and four at the end — in the middle the gods are established; therefore one should churn the fire there.

body.text: (AVParis_22,6.1) anulomā bhaved yoniḥ pārśvabhedo na vidyate | ānulomyena mathitaḥ sarvān kāmān prayacchati ||
body.translated_text: The <s>yoni</s> (receptacle) should be in the natural direction; there should be no side-perforation. Churned in the natural direction, it grants all desires.

body.text: (AVParis_22,6.2) mūlād aṅgulam utsṛjya trīṇitrīṇi ca pārśvayoḥ | devayonis tu vijñeyā tatra mathyo hutāśanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having left one <s>aṅgula</s> from the base and three on each side — that is to be known as the <s>devayoni</s> (divine receptacle); there the sacred fire should be churned.

body.text: (AVParis_22,6.3) [mūlāt tyaktvāṅgulāny aṣṭau agrāt tu dvādaśaiva hi | antare devayoniḥ syāt tatra mathyo hutāśanaḥ] ||
body.translated_text: [Having left eight <s>aṅgula</s>s from the base and twelve from the top — the <s>devayoni</s> should be in between; there the sacred fire should be churned.]

body.text: (AVParis_22,6.4) vedā yajñāya saṃbhūtā yajñā agnau pratiṣṭhitāḥ | araṇyor jāyate cāgnis tayos tasmāt pradhānatā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s>s arose for sacrifice; the sacrifices are established in fire; and fire is born from the <s>araṇi</s>s — therefore their primacy.

body.text: (AVParis_22,6.5) araṇyardhena caiva syuḥ khādirau cātrapīḍakau | netraṃ tu ṣaḍguṇaṃ cātrād uttaro 'ṣṭāṅgulaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: With half of the <s>araṇi</s> [wood], the two <s>Khadira</s> (acacia) pressers should be [made]; the cord (<s>netra</s>) should be six times [the length]; the upper [stick] is remembered as eight <s>aṅgula</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_22,7.1) aṣṭāṅgulaḥ pramanthaḥ syāc cātraṃ syād dvādaśāṅgulam | ovīlī dvādaśāṅgulā eṣa yajñavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The churning stick (<s>pramantha</s>) should be eight <s>aṅgula</s>s; the plate (<s>cātra</s>) should be twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s; the spindle-whorl (<s>ovīlī</s>) twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s — this is the remembered sacrificial procedure.

body.text: (AVParis_22,7.2) vyāmamantraṃ vadanty eke anye hastatrayaṃ viduḥ | trivṛtaṃ muṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ yajñavṛkṣajavalkalaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Some say the cord is a fathom in length; others know it as three hands [long]; triple-twisted, held in the fist, [made] from the bark of sacrificial trees.

body.text: (AVParis_22,7.3) cātre ca bhāskarāḥ proktā uttare vasavas tathā | netre devagaṇāḥ sarve viṣṇuś caiva tu pīḍake ||
body.translated_text: In the plate, the <s>Bhāskara</s>s (solar deities) are declared; in the upper [stick], the <s>Vasu</s>s; in the cord, all the divine hosts; and <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the presser.

body.text: (AVParis_22,7.4) araṇir yā dvitīyā tu uttarā sā prakīrtitā | tatraikadeśaṃ saṃgṛhya uttaraḥ sa ca kīrtitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The second <s>araṇi</s> is declared to be the upper one (<s>uttarā</s>); grasping one portion of it, that is also called the 'upper' [piece].

body.text: (AVParis_22,7.5) prāṅmukhodaṅmukho vāpi bhrāmakaḥ paścimāmukhaḥ | pāṇibhyāṃ pīḍanaṃ śubhram uttarāgraṃ pragṛhya tu ||
body.translated_text: Facing east or north, the turner faces west; with two hands, the pressing is auspicious, grasping the upper tip.

body.text: (AVParis_22,8.1) mūle mūlaṃ tu saṃyojya cātrasyaivottarasya ca | araṇyupari saṃsthāpya pīḍakena tu pīḍayed ||
body.translated_text: Joining base to base of the plate and the upper [stick], having placed [them] upon the <s>araṇi</s>, one should press with the presser.

body.text: (AVParis_22,8.2) netreṇa bhrāmayec cātraṃ yāvad vahniḥ prajāyate | sarvair hi devaiḥ saṃpannas tena sarvasukhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should rotate the plate with the cord until fire is produced; [the fire] is endowed with all the gods, and is therefore considered the source of all happiness.

body.text: (AVParis_22,8.3) brahmādyair daivataiś caiva vidvadbhiś ca tapodhanaiḥ | eṣa yantraprayogas tu dṛṣṭo yajñārthahetubhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: By <s>Brahmā</s> and the other deities, and by the wise ones rich in austerity — this mechanism of the instrument has been seen for the purpose of sacrifice.

body.text: (AVParis_22,8.4) yajamānena manthavyaḥ svaśākhāśrotriyeṇa vā | tanmantrena dvijāgryair vā smṛtam etad dhi manthanam ||
body.translated_text: It should be churned by the sacrificer, or by a <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) of his own branch, or by foremost twice-born with the [appropriate] mantra — this churning is thus remembered.

body.text: (AVParis_22.9.1) (atha) yady araṇī jīrṇe syātāṃ jantubhir manthanena vā || samānīte nave araṇī āhṛtya śve bhūte darśenāṣṭvā tasmin pūrve śakalīkṛtya gārhapatye prakṣipyopary agnau dhārayan japati ||
body.translated_text: Now, if the <s>araṇi</s>s become worn out, by insects or by churning — having brought new <s>araṇi</s>s, on the next day, having [performed] the <s>Darśa</s> (new-moon) [rite], having splintered the old ones, having thrown them into the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, and holding [them] above the fire, one recites:

body.text:
(AVParis_22,9.2) ud budhyasvāgne pra viśasya yonyāṃ devayajyāyai voḍhave jātavedaḥ | araṇyor araṇī saṃ carasva jīrṇāṃ tvacam ajīrṇayā nir ṇudasvety
(AVParis_22,9.3) ājyaṃ saṃskṛtyāhavanīye manasvatīṃ juhoti || [putrārthī śrāvayet] ||
body.translated_text: 'Awake, O <s>Agni</s>! Enter your <s>yoni</s> (receptacle), O <s>Jātavedas</s>, to carry the divine worship; move together among the <s>araṇi</s>s; push out the worn-out skin with the unworn one.' Having prepared the clarified butter, one offers the <s>Manasvatī</s> [oblation] in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire. [One desiring sons should have it recited.]

body.text: (AVParis_22,9.4) mano jyotir juṣatām ājyasya vichinnaṃ yajñaṃ sam imaṃ dadhātu | yā iṣṭā uṣaso yā aniṣṭās tāḥ saṃ cinomi haviṣā ghṛtena svāheti agnaye 'gnimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ puroḍāśaṃ nirvapati || śarāv odanaṃ sadakṣiṇaṃ dadāti || sā prakṛteṣtiḥ saṃgṛhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'May the mind, the light, delight in the clarified butter; may it restore this severed sacrifice. Whatever desired dawns and undesired ones — I gather them with this oblation of clarified butter, <s>svāhā</s>.' One offers to <s>Agni Agnimān</s> a cake on eight potsherds. One gives a rice dish with a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee). This is the <s>prakṛti-iṣṭi</s> (archetypal offering) to be employed.

body.text: (AVParis_22,10.1) prasaṅgenaiva kathitam agnimanthanam atra vai | araṇyoś cāṅgasaṃbhūtaṃ netraṃ cātraṃ ca pīḍakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: By way of connection, the fire-churning has been described here; along with the limbs of the <s>araṇi</s>s — the cord, the plate, and the presser.

body.text: (AVParis_22,10.2) ya idaṃ dhārayiṣyati araṇyor iha lakṣaṇam | na tasya durlabhaṃ kiṃ cid loke paratra ca ||
body.translated_text: He who will uphold this teaching of the characteristics of the <s>araṇi</s>s — nothing will be difficult to obtain for him, either in this world or the next.

body.text: (AVParis_22,10.3) putrārthī śrāvayen nityam acirāl labhate sutam | śrutaśīlaṃ vṛttavantaṃ dīrghāyur vipulāṃ prajām ||
body.translated_text: One desiring a son should always have it recited; in a short time he obtains a son — one of learning and character, virtuous, long-lived, and abundant progeny.

body.text: (AVParis_22,10.4) etad evaṃ samākhyātaṃ pippalādena dhīmatā | dvijānāṃ bālavṛddhānāṃ puraścaraṇam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: This has been thus declared by the wise <s>Pippalāda</s> — the supreme preliminary practice for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, both young and old.

body.text: (AVParis_22,10.5) adhītyaitac ca dehānte paraṃ brahmādhigacchati | na tasya mṛtyur na jarā nidrā vyādhir na caiva hi | kṣutpipāsābhayaṃ nāsti brahmabhūtaḥ sa tiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: Having studied this, at the end of the body [i.e., at death], one attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. For him there is no death, no old age, no sleep, no disease; there is no [fear of] hunger, thirst, or danger — he stands having become <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_23. yajñapātralakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_23,1.1) om athāto yajñapātrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yonir eva ca | rūpaṃ tathā pramāṇaṃ ca kramenaiva prakathyate ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 23: Characteristics of Sacrificial Vessels [<s>Yajñapātra-lakṣaṇa</s>]) Oṃ. Now the characteristics of sacrificial vessels — their origin, form, and measurement — are described in sequence.

body.text: (AVParis_23,1.2) camasagrahapātrāṇi homapātrāṇi yāni ca | yajñavṛkṣās tathā śākhā brahmavede pradarśitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Cups (<s>camasa</s>), receiving vessels, and oblation vessels — sacrificial trees and branches — are shown in the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (Atharvaveda).

body.text: (AVParis_23,1.3) pitṛpiṇḍeṣu darvyādyam agniṣvāttaṃ ca yājñikam | sāyaṃhomeṣu nityāni tathā naimittikāni ca ||
body.translated_text: In ancestral <s>piṇḍa</s>-offerings, the ladle (<s>darvī</s>) and the rest; the fire-eaten (<s>agniṣvātta</s>) [offering] and sacrificial [items]; the regular evening oblations, and likewise the occasional ones.

body.text: (AVParis_23,1.4) bilvākṛtiś caruḥ proktas tāmro vā mṛnmayo 'pi vā | grīvāyāṃ mukhavistīrṇaś carusthālīti kīrttitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>caru</s> (oblation-pot) is said to be <s>bilva</s>-shaped (bael-fruit shaped), made of copper or even of clay; at the neck, wide-mouthed — it is called the <s>carusthālī</s> (oblation-vessel).

body.text: (AVParis_23,1.5) kuśasyāmrasya vā parṇair veṇor vā balbajasya vā | catuṣkoṇārdhavītaṃ ca loke śūrpaṃ tad ucyate ||
body.translated_text: Of leaves of <s>kuśa</s> grass, mango, bamboo, or <s>balbaja</s> grass — four-cornered, half-woven — that is called in common parlance a winnowing fan (<s>śūrpa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,2.1) asiḥ khaḍgaṃ ca nistriṃśaḥ paryāyāḥ parikīrttitāḥ | tadākṛṭy eva yad rūpaṃ yajñe sphyaṃ ca vadanti tam ||
body.translated_text: Sword, blade, and scimitar are declared as synonyms; that which has a form of that very shape — in the sacrifice they call it the <s>sphya</s> (wooden sword).

body.text: (AVParis_23,2.2) idhmocchrayam ardhakhātaṃ khātenaiva tu vistaraḥ | madhye hīnaṃ tathordhvāgraṃ vāraṇaṃ tad ulūkhalam ||
body.translated_text: The height of the kindling [log], half-dug [into the ground], the breadth equal to the depth; hollowed in the middle with an upward opening — that barrier is the mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,2.3) sthūlatvān muṣṭimātraṃ ca skandhamātraṃ pramāṇataḥ | vāraṇaṃ musalaṃ caiva adhastāl lohaveṣṭitam ||
body.translated_text: Of thick [dimension], fist-measure, shoulder-length in measurement — the barrier, the pestle (<s>musala</s>), with iron-binding below.

body.text: (AVParis_23,2.4) sruvas tu mūladaṇḍaś ca bilaṃ cāṅguṣṭhaparvaṇaḥ | samavete pṛthagbhūte bilārdhe daṇḍavṛttatā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>sruva</s> (ladle) consists of a root-handle and a bowl of thumb-joint [size]; when joined or separate, half the bowl [determines] the handle's roundness.

body.text: (AVParis_23,2.5) vaikaṅkatī dhruvā proktā sarvayajñeṣu yā smṛtā | tathāgnihotrahavaṇī sruvaś cāpi tathā smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The permanent [ladle] made of <s>Vaikaṅkata</s> wood is declared for all sacrifices; likewise the <s>Agnihotra</s> offering-ladle and the <s>sruva</s> are thus remembered.

body.text: (AVParis_23,3.1) mūladaṇḍā tvagbilā ca puṣkaraṃ caturaṅgulam | puṣkarād dviguṇaṃ cāgraṃ gajoṣṭhaṃ paripaṭhyate ||
body.translated_text: With a root-handle and a bark-bowl, the cup (<s>puṣkara</s>) is four <s>aṅgula</s>s; the tip from the cup is twice [that] — it is read as 'elephant-lip' [shaped].

body.text: (AVParis_23,3.2) [netrādikaraṇair hīnaṃ nāsikābhyāṃ dvijais tathā | dvyaṅgulaḥ khātā ca bilād aṅgulaṃ caiva piṇḍikā | vṛttā vā caturaśrā vā sādhastāc chobhanā smṛtā] ||
body.translated_text: [Without eye-like and nose-like features, by twice-born [authorities]; two <s>aṅgula</s>s dug from the bowl and one <s>aṅgula</s> is the knob; round or four-sided, below it is considered auspicious.]

body.text: (AVParis_23,3.3) ardhāṅgulaṃ pṛthutvena bilabāhyaṃ samantataḥ | bilaṃ vṛttaṃ sruco madhye daṇḍasthaulyaṃ bilārdhataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Half an <s>aṅgula</s> in thickness, outside the bowl all around; the bowl is round, in the middle of the offering-ladle (<s>sruc</s>); the handle's thickness is half the bowl.

body.text: (AVParis_23,3.4) caturviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ daṇḍaṃ vadanty eke manīṣiṇaḥ | saptatriṃśad aṅgulāni sā sruk caiva prakīrtitā ||
body.translated_text: Some wise ones declare the handle to be twenty-four <s>aṅgula</s>s; thirty-seven <s>aṅgula</s>s — that is declared to be the offering-ladle (<s>sruk</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,3.5) bhinnā viśīrṇā vakrā ca klinnā ca sphuṭitā tathā | suṣirā granthibhir yuktā cakṣurādivināśinī ||
body.translated_text: Broken, crumbling, crooked, wet, split, hollow, having knots — [such ladles are] destroyers of eyesight and the rest.

body.text: (AVParis_23,4.1) dagdhaśeṣe 'rdhaśuṣke ca vidyutā caiva pātite | unmūlye patite bhagne manasāpi na cintayet ||
body.translated_text: One should not even think of [using wood from a tree that is] burnt to a remnant, half-dried, struck by lightning, uprooted, fallen, or broken.

body.text: (AVParis_23,4.2) śubhanakṣatrātithiṣu śubhāṃ gatvā diśaṃ budhaḥ | sruvārthaṃ pātayed vṛkṣaṃ prātaḥ prāgraṃ ca saumyavāk ||
body.translated_text: On auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>s and <s>tithi</s>s (lunar days), having gone in an auspicious direction, the wise one should fell a tree for the purpose of the <s>sruva</s> (ladle), in the morning, with its top facing east, speaking pleasant words.

body.text: (AVParis_23,4.3) mṛgo hariṇaruruś ca kṛṣṇapṛṣṭhaśiras tathā | yat tasya carma tvak caiva tat kṛṣṇājinam ucyate ||
body.translated_text: A deer, an <s>hariṇa</s> (antelope), a <s>ruru</s> (spotted deer), or one with a black back and head — its skin and bark is called <s>kṛṣṇājina</s> (black deerskin).

body.text: (AVParis_23,4.4) vāmamuṣṭigṛhītās tu prachidyante sakṛt kuśāḥ | paraśunāsinā vā tat sakṛdāchinnam ucyate ||
body.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s> grasses, grasped in the left fist, should be cut once — with an axe or a sword; that is called 'cut once.'

body.text: (AVParis_23,4.5) aṅguṣṭhaparvāgramukhaṃ darvyākṛti tu mekṣaṇam. vaikaṅkate pālāśe vā prādeśas tu pramāṇataḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>mekṣaṇa</s> (stirring stick), shaped like a ladle, with its opening the size of a thumb-joint — made of <s>vikaṅkata</s> or <s>palāśa</s> wood, a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) in measure.

body.text: (AVParis_23,5.1) alābu vaiṇavaṃ vāpi dārvyaṃ vaiṇavam eva vā | akṣāv amaṇḍalau proktau yathā dṛṣṭaṃ pura rṣibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: A gourd, or one of bamboo, or a wooden one, or bamboo indeed — the axles are said to be without wheels, as was seen by the <s>ṛṣi</s>s of old.

body.text: (AVParis_23,5.2) cakrābhyāṃ kāṣṭhasaṃghātaiḥ śilpibhiś caiva yat kṛtam | loke prasiddhaṃ śakaṭam agniṣṭhaṃ yājñike vidhau ||
body.translated_text: A cart made by craftsmen from assemblages of wood with two wheels — well-known in the world as a cart, is called <s>agniṣṭha</s> (fire-bearing) in the sacrificial procedure.

body.text: (AVParis_23,5.3) ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ vijānīyān navanītaṃ susaṃskṛtam | sauvīrādy añjanaṃ caiva atha vā daivikaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ājya</s> (clarified butter) one should understand as <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee), well-prepared fresh butter; <s>sauvīra</s> and other collyria, or else the divine kind likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_23,5.4) abhyañjanaṃ ca tat praktaṃ tilatailaṃ ca yad viduḥ | āsanaṃ kaśipu proktaṃ kāyasthaṃ copabarhaṇam ||
body.translated_text: That is said to be unguent, and the sesame oil that is known; a seat is called <s>kaśipu</s> (cushion), and a body-covering is called <s>upabarhaṇa</s> (bolster).

body.text: (AVParis_23,5.5) yavodarair aṣṭabhis tu aṅgulaṃ paripaṭhyate | carutviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ tu yājñikair hasta ākṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Eight barley-bellied [measures] are reckoned as one <s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth); a <s>hasta</s> (cubit) is determined by the sacrificial priests as twenty <s>aṅgula</s>s of the <s>caru</s> (oblation vessel).

body.text: (AVParis_23,6.1) hastamātraṃ sruvaḥ khaḍgaṃ sakṛdāchinnam eva ca | bāhumātrā juhūḥ proktā dhruvā barhis tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: The <s>sruva</s> (ladle) is one <s>hasta</s> in measure, and the <s>khaḍga</s> (knife) is cut once; the <s>juhū</s> (offering spoon) is declared to be one arm's length, and likewise the <s>dhruvā</s> (steady spoon) and the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass).

body.text: (AVParis_23,6.2) tāmraś caiva sruvaḥ proktaḥ khaḍgaṃ khādiram eva ca | pālāśī ca juhūḥ kāryā idhmāś caiva viśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>sruva</s> is said to be of copper; the <s>khaḍga</s> of <s>khādira</s> (catechu) wood; the <s>juhū</s> should be made of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) wood, and especially the fuel-sticks (<s>idhma</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,6.3) grahāḥ pātrāṇi camasā daṇḍayūpāsanāni ca | vṛkṣeṣu yājñikeṣu syur yathālābheṣu nānyataḥ ||
body.translated_text: The cups (<s>graha</s>), vessels (<s>pātra</s>), goblets (<s>camasa</s>), staffs, sacrificial posts (<s>yūpa</s>), and seats — these should be of sacrificial trees, as available, and not otherwise.

body.text: (AVParis_23,6.4) samidhaḥ prādeśamātryo nityahome prakīrtitāḥ | samillakṣaṇadṛṣṭāni pramāṇāni yathākramam ||
body.translated_text: Fuel-sticks of one <s>prādeśa</s> (span) in measure are prescribed for the daily oblation; the dimensions as observed in the characteristics of fuel-sticks are in proper order.

body.text: (AVParis_23,6.5) śamy aśvattha[ḥ] palāśaś ca khādiro 'tha vikaṅkataḥ | kāśmaryodumbaro bilvo yajñavṛkṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śamī</s>, <s>aśvattha</s> (fig), <s>palāśa</s> (butea), <s>khādira</s> (catechu), <s>vikaṅkata</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), and <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) — these are proclaimed as the sacrificial trees.

body.text: (AVParis_23,7.1) eṣām alābhe vṛkṣāṇām anye grāhyās tu yājñikaiḥ | yajñāṅgakārye draṣṭavyāḥ samidarthaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: When these trees are unavailable, other [trees] may be taken by the sacrificial priests; they should be considered for sacrificial purposes, especially for fuel-sticks.

body.text: (AVParis_23,7.2) yavavrīhimahāvrīhiprayaṅgūṇāṃ hi taṇḍulāḥ | śyāmākataṇḍulatilā āsādyāḥ śruticoditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The grains of barley, rice, great rice, and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet); <s>śyāmāka</s> (panic grain) grains, sesame — these are to be procured as enjoined by scripture.

body.text: (AVParis_23,7.3) sāyaṃhomeṣu yad dravyaṃ prātarhomeṣu tad bhavet | bhinnadravyahutaṃ yat tu na hutaṃ tasya tad bhavet ||
body.translated_text: Whatever substance [is used] in the evening oblations, the same should be [used] in the morning oblations; what is offered with different substances — that is as if not offered at all.

body.text: (AVParis_23,7.4) udite 'nudite caiva samayādhyuṣite tathā | kṣudhākāle tathāpy keke pakṣahomaṃ tu kārayet ||
body.translated_text: Whether the sun has risen or not, whether the time has merely dawned, at the time of hunger, and also at certain [other times] — one should have the half-month oblation (<s>pakṣahoma</s>) performed.

body.text: (AVParis_23,7.5) yāyāvarāṇāṃ munibhiḥ pakṣahomas tu taiḥ smṛtaḥ | yathā kathaṃ cid vacanaṃ śrutyuktaṃ dvija ācāret ||
body.translated_text: The half-month oblation is recorded by the sages for the wandering ascetics (<s>yāyāvara</s>s); a twice-born should observe whatever statement is declared in scripture, in whatever manner.

body.text: (AVParis_23,8.1) āturaḥ pathikaś caiva rājopadravapīḍitaḥ | pakṣahomaṃ tadā kuryān nistīrya satataṃ caret ||
body.translated_text: One who is sick, a traveler, or one afflicted by royal calamity — he should then perform the half-month oblation; having completed it, he should always continue [the regular daily rite].

body.text: (AVParis_23,8.2) caturdaśagṛhītaṃ tu sakṛd unnayate haviḥ | ekā samit sakṛd dhomaḥ so 'rdhamāsāya kalpate ||
body.translated_text: An oblation raised once, taken up [in quantity for] fourteen [days] — a single fuel-stick, a single oblation — that suffices for a half-month.

body.text: (AVParis_23,8.3) caturdaśaguṇaṃ kṛtvā srucā pātreṇa pūrvavat | evaṃ gārhapatye ca dakṣiṇāgnau ca juhvati ||
body.translated_text: Having made it fourteen-fold, [offered] with the ladle or vessel as before — thus they offer into both the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire) and the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire).

body.text: (AVParis_23,8.4) pūrvā hutvāhutīḥ sāyaṃ vyuṣṭāyām apare 'hni | etenaiva vidhānena juhvati prātarāhutīḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having offered the earlier oblations in the evening, then on the next day at dawn — by this same procedure they offer the morning oblations.

body.text: (AVParis_23,8.5) ṛṣibhiś ca purā dṛṣṭam āpatkāleṣu sarvataḥ | araṇyoś ca samāropya śrutidṛṣṭena karmaṇā ||
body.translated_text: This was seen by the <s>ṛṣi</s>s of old, in times of emergency, everywhere; and having kindled the fire from the fire-sticks (<s>araṇi</s>), by the rite observed in scripture —

body.text: (AVParis_23,9.1) homārtheṣv etad draṣṭavyam āhitāgnigṛheṣv api | tatprayojanamātraṃ tu na doṣaḥ sūtakeṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: This should be observed for oblation purposes, even in the houses of fire-maintainers (<s>āhitāgni</s>); its use alone [is required], and there is no fault during birth-impurity (<s>sūtaka</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,9.2) sadyaḥśaucādikaṃ proktaṃ sūtakaṃ ca dvijātibhiḥ | svayaṃhomīti vacanān na doṣaḥ śruticodanāt ||
body.translated_text: Immediate purification and the like, and birth-impurity — these are declared by the twice-born; because of the statement 'one who offers by himself,' there is no fault, by the injunction of scripture.

body.text: (AVParis_23,9.3) vratināṃ sattriṇāṃ caiva mahārājāhitāgnayaḥ | eṣāṃ doṣo na vidyeta sāyamprātaḥ kriye sthite ||
body.translated_text: For those observing vows, for those engaged in long sacrificial sessions (<s>sattra</s>), and for great kings who maintain the sacred fires — there is no fault for them when the evening and morning rites are maintained.

body.text: (AVParis_23,9.4) pālāśyaḥ samidho 'doṣā nityaṃ home prakīrtitāḥ | atha vā kauśikoktānāṃ yajñiyānāṃ mahīruhām ||
body.translated_text: <s>Palāśa</s> (butea) fuel-sticks are declared faultless for the daily oblation always; or [fuel-sticks] from the sacrificial trees declared by <s>Kauśika</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_23,9.5) aṅgulatrayam āvartya ucchraye 'py aṅgulatrayam | puroḍāśapramāṇaṃ tu sarvatra kathitaṃ nṛṇām ||
body.translated_text: Wrapping three <s>aṅgula</s>s around, and three <s>aṅgula</s>s in height also — the measure of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) is declared as universal for all people.

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.1) ṣoḍaśāṅgulam āvartya tribhāgaṃ cottaram ṛju | dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi sthānaṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ prakīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: Wrapping sixteen <s>aṅgula</s>s around, and the upper third upright — the place of the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) is declared to be in the southern direction.

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.2) aṣṭāviṃśaty aṅgulāni gārhapatyaṃ prakīrtitam | āhavanīyam [catur]viṃśatiś caturaśraṃ tu kārayet ||
body.translated_text: Twenty-eight <s>aṅgula</s>s are declared for the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire); the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (oblation fire), of twenty-four, should be made square.

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.3) aṅgulāni tu ṣaṭtriṃśad dhnvākṛtyā tu kārayet | dakṣiṇāgnes tu vai kuṇḍaṃ vidvadbhij parikathyate ||
body.translated_text: Thirty-six <s>aṅgula</s>s, to be made in a bow-shape — this is declared by the learned as the fire-pit of the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.4) īśānyāṃ diśi sabhyasya gārhapatyavidhānataḥ | sabhyaṃ necchanti śālāgnau māhakiḥ kauśikas tathā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Sabhya</s> (assembly fire) [is placed] in the northeast direction, according to the procedure of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>; <s>Māhaki</s> and <s>Kauśika</s> do not desire the <s>Sabhya</s> in the hall fire.

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.5) maudāyanās tathecchanti śaunakeyās tathaiva ca | mantād eva tathā proktaṃ dravyaṃ yatra na dṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Maudāyana</s>s desire it, and the <s>Śaunakeya</s>s likewise; from the <s>mantra</s> alone it is declared [that] where the substance is not seen,

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.6) ājyaṃ tatra vijānīiyād dhomas tatra sruveṇa ca | abhyukṣaṇaṃ haviḥkarma kartavyaṃ vajrapāṇinā ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ājya</s> (ghee) should be understood there, and the oblation there with the <s>sruva</s> (ladle); the sprinkling and the oblation-rite should be performed by the wielder of the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt, i.e., <s>Indra</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_23,10.7) kuśahastena kartavyā japahomapitṛkriyāḥ | yajñe caiva aṅgabhūtāś ca pātramantrahavirdvijāḥ | carutbhiś ca kriyāḥ sarvāś cāturhotraṃ tad ucyate ||
body.translated_text: Recitation, oblation, and ancestral rites should be performed with <s>kuśa</s> grass in hand; and in the sacrifice, the constituent parts are: vessels, <s>mantra</s>s, oblation-materials, and Brahmins; all rites with the <s>caru</s> (oblation vessels) — that is called <s>cāturhotra</s> (the fourfold priestly function).

body.text: (AVParis_23,11.1) yājñikās tu vadanty anye caturbhir yac ca hūyate | brahmaṇādhvaryuhotṛbhyāṃ tribhir agnicaturthakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: But other ritualists say that which is offered by four — by the <s>Brahmā</s> (superintendent), the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiant), and the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker), these three with fire as the fourth.

body.text: (AVParis_23,11.2) durbhikṣe cākule bhaṅge ṛtvijāṃ cāpy asaṃbhave | ekaś cāturhotraṃ kuryād āpastambe prapaṭhyate ||
body.translated_text: In famine, in confusion, in emergency, and when priests are unavailable — a single person may perform the <s>cāturhotra</s>; this is recited in [the school of] <s>Āpastamba</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_23,11.3) ṛtvijāṃ ca7apy asāmnidhye adhvaryus tat paṭhet svayam | asthānapaṭhite kuryur ṛtvig ityādi coditam ||
body.translated_text: When the priests are not present, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> himself should recite that; they should perform [the rite] when recited out of [proper] place — thus 'the priest' and the like is enjoined.

body.text: (AVParis_23,11.4) khāte lūne tu yac coktaṃ saṃskāraśrutihetubhiḥ | dravyāṇāṃ yajñakLptyarthaṃ kuryāt pūrveṇa saṃgraham ||
body.translated_text: What is declared regarding digging and cutting, with reasons of <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) and scripture — for the purpose of preparing sacrificial materials, one should gather them according to the earlier [method].

body.text: (AVParis_23,11.5) pātrāsādaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca prokṣaṇena vivarjitam | ubhayoś caiva kurvīta pākayajñeṣṭikarmavat ||
body.translated_text: The second placement of vessels, exempt from sprinkling — one should perform both, as in the <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) and <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) rites.

body.text: (AVParis_23,12.1) kṛṣṇājinaṃ tilā darbhā mantrā ājyaṃ dvijottamāḥ | doṣo na vidyate hy eṣāṃ yathārthaṃ saṃniyojayet ||
body.translated_text: Black deerskin, sesame, <s>darbha</s> grass, <s>mantra</s>s, <s>ājya</s> (ghee), and excellent Brahmins — there is no fault in these; one should employ them as appropriate.

body.text: (AVParis_23,12.2) ājyaṃ dhūmahavir jvālā paripākaḥ sphuliṅgakaiḥ | dāvāgnikāṣṭhasaṃsparśe agner doṣo na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: Ghee, smoke-offering, flame, complete cooking, and sparks — in contact with forest-fire or firewood, there is no fault of the fire.

body.text: (AVParis_23,12.3) japādhyāyatapodānaiḥ sopavāsaiḥ sahomakaiḥ | śrāddhādipitṛkāryais ca na doṣaḥ parivedane ||
body.translated_text: Through recitation, study, austerity, and giving, together with fasting and oblation, and ancestral rites such as <s>śrāddha</s> — there is no fault in [a younger brother] marrying before [the elder].

body.text: (AVParis_23,12.4) pitṛbhrātṛsapatnaiś ca patitonmattaṣaṇḍhakaiḥ | jātyandhamūkabadhirair na doṣaḥ parivedane ||
body.translated_text: If the father, brother, or rival is fallen, insane, or a eunuch, or if [the elder is] blind from birth, mute, or deaf — there is no fault in [a younger brother] marrying before [the elder].

body.text: (AVParis_23,12.5) atyantakāminā caiva patnīhīnena caiva hi | eṣām anujñām ādāya kuryād vaitānikī[ḥ] kriyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Or for one who is excessively desirous or without a wife — having obtained their permission, one should perform the ritual (<s>vaitānikī</s>) rites.

body.text: (AVParis_23,13.1) raudrarākṣasapaiśācān āsurāṃś cābhicārikān | mantāṃś ca pitṛkarmaivaṃ kṛtvālabhyodakaṃ spṛśet ||
body.translated_text: After performing <s>Raudra</s> (of <s>Rudra</s>), <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Paiśāca</s>, <s>Āsura</s>, and <s>ābhicārika</s> (sorcery) <s>mantra</s>s, as well as ancestral rites — one should touch water that has been obtained.

body.text: (AVParis_23,13.2) sruk sruvaś ca dhruvā khaḍgaṃ musalolūkhalaṃ caruḥ | udakenaiva soṣṇena saṃprakṣālya viśudhyati ||
