body.translated_text: The <s>sruk</s> (large ladle), <s>sruva</s> (small ladle), <s>dhruvā</s> (steady spoon), <s>khaḍga</s> (knife), mortar and pestle, and <s>caru</s> (oblation vessel) — these are purified by washing with warm water alone.

body.text: (AVParis_23,13.3) pātraṃ grahāś ca camasā haviḥ śūrpaṃ kuśāsanam | somaspṛṣṭaṃ ca yad bhāṇḍaṃ vāriśaucena śudhyati ||
body.translated_text: Vessels, cups, goblets, oblation-material, winnowing basket, <s>kuśa</s>-seat, and any utensil touched by <s>Soma</s> — these are purified by water-purification.

body.text: (AVParis_23,13.4) vedoktaṃ sarvamantoktaṃ śaunakena mahātmanā | avaśyaṃ tad dvijaiḥ kāryaṃ śreyaskāmais tu nityaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is declared in the <s>Veda</s> and in all <s>mantra</s>s by the great-souled <s>Śaunaka</s> — that must necessarily be performed by twice-born who always desire welfare.

body.text: (AVParis_23,13.5) pātrānāṃ tu prasāṅgena yad anyat parikīrtitam | sāyaṃ prātas tu homāṅgaṃ purā dṛṣṭaṃ maharṣibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: What else has been proclaimed incidentally regarding vessels — that which is an auxiliary to the evening and morning oblation was seen of old by the great <s>ṛṣi</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.1) guruṇā bhāṣitenaiva yājñikānumatena ca | sadāpadiṣṭadravyāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ parikīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: By the preceptor's word alone and by the approval of the ritualists — the characteristics of the prescribed substances have been proclaimed.

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.2) nityaṃ ye 'nusmariṣyanti yajñapātreṣu lakṣaṇam | rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpsyanti te dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: Those who will always remember the characteristics regarding sacrificial vessels — they will surely obtain the fruit of the <s>Rājasūya</s> and <s>Aśvamedha</s> [sacrifices].

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.3) pippalādena mahatā samākhyātam idaṃ śubham | brāhmaṇānāṃ hitārthāya putraśiṣyahitāya ca ||
body.translated_text: This auspicious [teaching] was fully expounded by the great <s>Pippalāda</s>, for the benefit of Brahmins and for the welfare of sons and disciples.

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.4) niṣkāmo vā sakāmo vā vedoktaṃ yaḥ samācaret | niṣkāmasya tu muktiḥ syāt sakāmaḥ phalam aśnute ||
body.translated_text: Whether desireless or with desires, one who observes what is declared in the <s>Veda</s> — for the desireless there shall be liberation; the one with desires enjoys the fruit.

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.5) niṣkāmeṇa tu yat kiṃ cit kartavyam iti vaidikam | tat sarvaṃ muktidaṃ jñeyaṃ parāparaparaṃ sukham ||
body.translated_text: Whatever is to be done according to the <s>Veda</s> by one who is desireless — all that is to be known as granting liberation, the supreme bliss beyond the beyond.

body.text: (AVParis_23,14.6) na śokas tasya no vyādhir na mṛtyur na jarā tathā | na kṣudhā na pipāsā ca amṛtātmā sa tiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: For him there is no grief, no disease, no death, no old age, no hunger, no thirst — he abides as the immortal Self.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_24. vedilakṣaṇam [+ agnivarṇalakṣaṇam])
(AVParis_24,1.1) om atha rṣiputrikāyāṃ tu sphutaṃ sarveṣu karmasu | lakṣaṇaṃ hy agnivarṇānāṃ pravakṣyāmi yathākramam ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 24. Characteristics of the Altar [and Fire-Color Characteristics]) Oṃ. Now, in the daughter of the <s>ṛṣi</s>s [i.e., the <s>Paippalāda</s> tradition], clearly, in all rites, I shall declare the characteristics of fire-colors in proper order.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.2) vāstukarmaṇy athotpāte pater nīrājane vidhau | sarvanakṣatrahomeṣu grahātithyavidhau tathā ||
body.translated_text: In house-building rites, in portent [rites], in the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration) procedure of the lord, in all <s>nakṣatra</s>-oblations, in planetary and guest rites likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.3) yātrodyāne vivāheṣu cūḍopanayaneṣu ca | sarveṣu cāgnihomeṣu vahnivarṇān nibodhata ||
body.translated_text: In departure ceremonies, in marriage celebrations, in <s>cūḍā</s> (tonsure) and <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) rites — in all fire-oblation rites, learn the fire-colors.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.4) mānenādhyardhaśīrsaṇyā trimadhyā ṣaṇmukhā smṛtā | caturaśrā cakartavyā vediḥ śāntīṣṭikarmasu ||
body.translated_text: In measure, one and a half [units at] the head, three in the middle, with six faces (hexagonal) it is declared; the altar for <s>śānti</s> (pacification) and <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) rites should be made square.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.5) eṣā vai viparītā ca kāryā ghoreṣu karmasu | karmaṇām anurūpāṃ tu vediṃ vakṣyāmy ataḥ param ||
body.translated_text: The same reversed should be made for terrible rites; I shall now declare the altar appropriate to [each type of] rite.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.6) yathāvartanagocarmacakratalpeṣu saṃmitā | saṃmṛjya prokṣya saṃstīrya vidhivac copaśobhayet ||
body.translated_text: Measured [the same as] a turning-circle, a hide, a wheel, or a bed; having swept, sprinkled, and strewn [grass], one should adorn it properly.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.7) ślakṣṇāḥ samāhitāḥ sarvāḥ prāgudakpravaṇāḥ śubhāḥ | saṃmṛjya prokṣya saṃstīrya vidhivac copaśobhayet ||
body.translated_text: All [altars] should be smooth, level, sloping toward the east and north, auspicious; having swept, sprinkled, and strewn, one should adorn them properly.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.8) dakṣiṇena tu yā vakrā yājñikaṃ sā vināśayet | yā ca vakrottareṇa syād yajamānaṃ vināśayet ||
body.translated_text: One that is curved to the south would destroy the ritualist; one that is curved to the north would destroy the sacrificer.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.9) purastāt pṛṣṭhato vāpi madhyato viṣamā ca yā | puram antaḥpuraṃ cāpi nāyakaṃ ca hinasti sā ||
body.translated_text: One that is uneven in front, behind, or in the middle — it destroys the city, the inner quarters, and the leader.

body.text: (AVParis_24,1.10) eṣā saṃkṣepataḥ proktā vediḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇā | viśeṣatas tu teṣv eva karmasv evābhidhāsyate ||
body.translated_text: This has been declared in brief — the altar with its general characteristics; specifically, in those very rites, it shall be described.

body.text: (AVParis_24,2.1) prācīṃ saṃśodhayed bhūmiṃ yajñavāstu yathoditam | samitkuśāgnivarṇānāṃ lakṣaṇajño bhaved guruḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should purify the ground toward the east — the sacrificial site as prescribed; the preceptor should be a knower of the characteristics of fuel-sticks, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and fire-colors.

body.text: (AVParis_24,2.2) tatas tu yatnavān samyag agnāv upasamāhite | agnivarṇān parīkṣeta yathovācośanāḥ kaviḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,2.2) Then, with careful effort, when the fire has been properly established, one should examine the colors of the fire, as the sage <s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra) declared.

body.text: (AVParis_24,2.3) śabdaṃ varṇaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca rūpaṃ snehaṃ prabhāṃ gatim | sparśaṃ cāpi parīkṣeta agnāv iti viniścayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,2.3) One should examine the sound, color, smell, form, oiliness, radiance, movement, and touch of the fire — this is the firm conclusion.

body.text: (AVParis_24,2.4) svāhākārāvasāne tu svayam utthāya pāvakaḥ | havir yātrābhilaṣati tad vidyād arthasiddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,2.4) When, at the conclusion of the '<s>svāhā</s>' utterance, the fire rises of its own accord and desires the offering — one should know that [this portends] the accomplishment of the purpose.

body.text: (AVParis_24,2.5) vṛṣavāraṇameghaughanemidundubhiniḥsvanaḥ | mṛṇālapadmadūrvābhakumudotpalagandhamuk ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,2.5) [If the fire has] the sound of a bull, elephant, thundercloud, wheel-rim, or drum; [if it has] the scent of lotus-stalk, lotus, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, white water-lily, or blue lotus —

body.text: (AVParis_24,3.1) tathā mahātmā stanayan vāhakumbhanibhadyutiḥ | saṃhitajvālanikaraḥ pāvakaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,3.1) likewise, [if] the noble [fire], thundering, has the radiance of a rain-cloud or a water-pot; with a compact mass of flames — such a fire destroys sin.

body.text: (AVParis_24,3.2) kuraṇṭākṛtigokṣīrahemāruṇataḍitprabhaḥ | protphullotpalakundendukumudābhotpaladyutiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,3.2) [If it has] the form of a <s>Kuraṇṭa</s> flower, the radiance of cow's milk, gold, dawn, or lightning; the splendor of a fully-opened blue lotus, jasmine, moon, white water-lily, or lotus —

body.text: (AVParis_24,3.3) huto 'pi saṃjvalaty eva snigdho viprasya dakṣiṇaḥ | lelihānaḥ pramuditaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇo 'rthasidhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,3.3) even when offered into, it continues blazing; oily, turning to the right for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; licking, joyful, of dark color — [this portends] the accomplishment of the purpose.

body.text: (AVParis_24,3.4) viśālamūlo hy amalo nīlaḥ pṛthulamadhyamaḥ | pradīptāgro 'malatato jvālāmālākulo 'nalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,3.4) With a broad base, pure, blue, with a broad middle, with a blazing tip, with spotless sides, crowded with garlands of flames — such is the fire.

body.text: (AVParis_24,3.5) pradakṣiṇaḥ prasannārcir arciṣmān arcitadyutiḥ | arcanīyaś ca nṛpater arcito havyavāhanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,3.5) Moving clockwise, with a serene flame, radiant, of worshipped splendor — this fire, worthy of worship, is the oblation-bearer honored for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_24,4.1) paristaraṇayogāc ca yajñakāṇḍaparicchadam | śāntiveśmārdhvadīptārcir ṛtvijaś cānulimpati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,4.1) And by the arrangement of the sacred grass, the paraphernalia of the sacrificial section; with flames blazing upward in the peace-pavilion, it anoints the priests.

body.text: (AVParis_24,4.2) prahasann iva śabdena dyotayann iva tejasā | kṛtapuṇyasya nṛpater hūyamāno hutāśanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,4.2) As if laughing with sound, as if illuminating with radiance — the fire being offered into, [it signals] a king of accumulated merit.

body.text: (AVParis_24,4.3) karmaṇo 'vabhṛthe yasya haviṣo 'nte ca pārthivam | sugandhābhir adhūmābhiḥ śikhābhiḥ saṃspṛśann iva ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,4.3) At whose concluding bath of the rite, and at the end of the oblation, [the fire] for the king, as if touching [him] with fragrant, smokeless flames —

body.text: (AVParis_24,4.4) arcibhir jvālabhāraiś ca pradahan dviṣatāṃ diśaḥ | vidhūmaḥ kuṇḍalī yaḥ syād anulomaś ca siddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,4.4) with rays and masses of flames, burning the directions of the enemies; [if the fire is] smokeless, coiled, and moving clockwise — [this is] for success.

body.text: (AVParis_24,5.1) kuraṇṭahemāruṇaśaṅkhakundamuktāvalīndupratime hutāśe | samasvane siṃhavṛṣair gajendrabalāhakaughasvanadundubhīnām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,5.1) When the fire [has the appearance of] <s>Kuraṇṭa</s> flower, gold, dawn, conch, jasmine, or a string of pearls, resembling the moon; with the sound of lions, bulls, great elephants, masses of thunderclouds, or drums;

body.text: (AVParis_24,5.2) viśālamūle pṛthule ca madhye jñeyānale saṃprati pīḍitāgre | mṛṇālapadmānilatulyagandhe trisāgarāntā vasudhā nṛpasya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,5.2) with a broad base and wide in the middle, known as a fire with a pressed-down tip; with a scent like lotus-stalk, lotus, and wind — [then] the earth up to three oceans [belongs to] the king.

body.text: (AVParis_24,5.3) ātaptapadmānilatulyagandhe trisāgarāntā vasudhā nṛpasya | tasyārthabāndhavavatī sakalā mahīyaṃ vīryāṃśujālavivarāhatarājaśabdā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,5.3) With a scent like heated lotus and wind — the earth up to three oceans [belongs to] the king. His entire earth, with wealth and kinsmen, [resounds] with the word 'king' destroying the openings of the net of rays of valor.

body.text: (AVParis_24,5.4) vibhrājate tv akhilarāgayuto hutāśo hastāvṛtaṃ kathayatīva jayaṃ nṛpasya | sūryāṃśubhiḥ kṛtavighaṭṭanahemapadmakiṃjalkacūrṇanikarāruṇatāmalāṃśuḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,5.4) When the fire blazes with all colors complete, it declares, as it were, the victory of the king as if enclosed by a hand; [with] rays as tawny-dark as the heap of pollen of golden lotuses struck by the rays of the sun.

body.text: (AVParis_24,5.5) kṣīrodaśuktipuṭagarbhavikīrṇamuktāsaṃghātapāṇḍurarajo rathanemighoṣaḥ | dātā nṛpāya vasudhāṃ tu himāṃśumaulijyotsnāvikāśitasamudrajalāṃ hutāśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,5.5) [If it has] the sound of a chariot-wheel, white with dust like scattered pearls from within the oyster-shell of the ocean of milk — [such] a fire bestows upon the king the earth whose ocean-waters are illuminated by the moonlight of the crescent-crowned one.

body.text: (AVParis_24,6.1) lakṣmīpradoharamṛṇālakapālaśubhrasnigdhānuvṛttaśikharaprakṛtiś ca yatra | vaiśvānaro jvalati yasya viśuddhamūrtiḥ sa prāpnuyān nṛpaśatādhipatāṃ narendraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,6.1) Where the fire blazes with a naturally smooth, rounded tip, white as the bowl of a lotus-stalk, bestowing <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) — that king shall attain sovereignty over a hundred kings.

body.text: (AVParis_24,6.2) bālārkabodhitasaroruhagarbhagandhas toyāvalambijaladastanitābhirāmaḥ | rājño dadāti vasudhāṃ hutabhug gajendradantāgrakampitamahārṇavavīcivṛkṣām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,6.2) [If the fire has] the scent of a lotus-bud awakened by the young sun, delightful as the rumble of a water-bearing cloud — the fire bestows upon the king an earth whose trees are like the waves of the great ocean shaken by the tip of a great elephant's tusk.

body.text: (AVParis_24,6.3) yasyāṃ vasantaravimaṇḍalatulyabimbo vedyāṃ nṛpasya paripūrṇamarīcijālaḥ | tasyānalākalitasāgaratoyavastrā mrāgaikṣavenir avanir vaśam abhyupaiti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,6.3) On whose altar the fire-disc resembles the orb of the spring sun, full of a net of rays — his earth, clothed in ocean-waters gathered by the fire, with braids of sugarcane and deer, comes under his dominion.

body.text: (AVParis_24,6.4) yasyānalo jvalati kāñcanatulyagauro prajvālyamānavapur utpalakośagandhaḥ | āyāti tasya bhavanaṃ hy alidīptimālā savrīḍasūryakiraṇā kṣitipālalakṣmīr iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_24,6.4) For him whose fire blazes golden-bright, with the fragrance of a blue lotus bud, its body shining as if kindled — <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the royal Fortune), whose garland is the radiance of bees, whose sunbeams are bashful, comes to his abode.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_25. kuṇḍalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_25,1.1) oṃ śaunakaṃ tu sukhāsīnaṃ bhārgavaḥ paripṛcchati | kuṇḍaṃ kasmin bhavet kīdṛk kasyāṃ vā diśi kiṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 25: Characteristics of the Fire-pit) (AVParis_25,1.1) Oṃ. <s>Bhārgava</s> asks <s>Śaunaka</s>, comfortably seated: "In what [direction] should the fire-pit be? Of what shape? In which direction? What is the result?"

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.2) sa tasmā upasannāya ācaṣṭe bhārgavāya tu | kuṇḍaṃ yasmin bhaved yādṛg yasyāṃ vā diśi yat phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.2) He, having approached, explains to the <s>Bhārgava</s>: "In what the fire-pit should be, of what shape, in which direction, and what result —"

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.3) caturaśraṃ śaphākṛtyā ardhacandraṃ trikoṇakam | vartulaṃ pañcakoṇaṃ ca padmābhaṃ saptakoṇakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.3) Four-sided, hoof-shaped, half-moon, triangular, circular, five-cornered, lotus-shaped, and seven-cornered —

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.4) kuṇḍāny etāni pūrvādidikṣu aṣṭasu vinirdiśet | digdevatānāṃ cāṣṭānāṃ karmaṇi svamsvam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.4) these fire-pits should be assigned in the eight directions beginning with the east; and for the rites of the eight directional deities, each its own should be prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.5) caturaśraṃ tu pūrvasyām aindreṣv api ca karmasu | śaphākṛti tadāgneyyām āgneyeṣv api karmasu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.5) The four-sided one in the east, and also for rites of <s>Indra</s>; the hoof-shaped one in the southeast, and also for rites of <s>Agni</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.6) ardhacandraṃ tu yāmyāyāṃ yāmyeṣv api ca karmasu | nairṛtyāṃ ca trikoṇaṃ syād abhicāravidhau śubham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.6) The half-moon in the south, and also for rites of <s>Yama</s>; in the southwest, the triangular one — auspicious in the procedure of sorcery.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.7) vāruṇyāṃ vartulaṃ jñeyaṃ vāruṇyeṣv api karmasu | vāyavyāṃ pañcakoṇaṃ tu vāyavyeṣv api karman ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.7) In the west, the circular one is to be known, and also for rites of <s>Varuṇa</s>; in the northwest, the five-cornered one, and also for rites of <s>Vāyu</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.8) uttarasyāṃ tu padmābhaṃ saumyeṣv api ca karmasu | aiśānyāṃ saptakoṇaṃ tu raudreṣv api yathoditam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.8) In the north, the lotus-shaped one, and also for rites of <s>Soma</s>; in the northeast, the seven-cornered one, and also for rites of <s>Rudra</s>, as stated.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.9) sarvakarmasu vijñeyaṃ kuṇḍaṃ padmanibhaṃ tu yat | caturaśraṃ tu sarvatra samaṃ syād vijayāvaham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.9) For all rites, the lotus-shaped fire-pit should be known; and the four-sided one is everywhere suitable, bestowing victory.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.10) sarvaśāntikaraṃ kuṇḍaṃ padmākāraṃ viśeṣataḥ | śāntike caturaśraṃ ca pauṣṭike vartulaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.10) The lotus-shaped fire-pit is especially conducive to all peace-rites; the four-sided one for peace, the circular one for nourishment,

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.11) abhicāre trikoṇaṃ ca vaśyādau cārdhacandrakam | ṣaṭkoṇaṃ māraṇādau ca vidveṣe cāṣṭakoṇakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.11) the triangular one for sorcery, the half-moon for subjugation and the rest; the six-cornered one for killing rites and such, and the eight-cornered one for rites of enmity.

body.text: (AVParis_25,1.12) mekhalā sarvakuṇḍeṣu dvādaśāṅgulam iṣyate | caturaṅgulamānena pūrvāpūrvasamucchritā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,1.12) The raised rim in all fire-pits is prescribed to be twelve finger-widths; with a four-finger-width measure, each successively raised above the preceding one.

body.text: (AVParis_25,2.1) na cet purastād dhīnaṃ syāt sukhaṃ yajñaḥ samāpyate | yat tu dakṣiṇato 'hīnaṃ tad rājñas tv abhayapradam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,2.1) If [the fire-pit/pavilion] is not deficient on the east side, the sacrifice is completed with ease. If it is deficient on the south side, that bestows fearlessness upon the king.

body.text: (AVParis_25,2.2) yathāhīnaṃ paścimena bhavet tat siddhidaṃ śubham | uttareṇa samamyat syāt tad rājño rājyavardhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,2.2) If it is deficient on the west side, that is auspicious and grants success. If it is level on the north side, that increases the king's sovereignty.

body.text: (AVParis_25,2.3) madhye samaṃ ca sukhadaṃ digvidikṣu samaṃ tu yat | tad rājajanasaṃpatkṛt sarvāṃś cārīn vināśayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,2.3) If level in the middle — [that is] bliss-giving; if level in all directions and intermediate quarters, that creates prosperity for the king and his people, and destroys all enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_25,2.4) na cet purastād ityādi ya eṣa kathito vidhiḥ | maṇḍapānāṃ gṛhāṇāṃ ca māne śāntikaraḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,2.4) 'If not deficient on the east' and so forth — this procedure that has been stated is remembered as peace-bringing in the measurement of pavilions and houses.

body.text: (AVParis_25,2.5) hastakuṇḍaṃ sadāhome ayute dvikaraṃ smṛtam | lakṣahome catuṣpāṇi koṭyām aṣṭakaraṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_25,2.5) A one-<s>hasta</s> (cubit) fire-pit for the daily oblation; for ten thousand [oblations], one of two <s>hastas</s> is prescribed; for a hundred thousand, four <s>hastas</s>; for a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), eight <s>hastas</s> is prescribed.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_26. samillakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_26,1.1) oṃ samidhāṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi pramāṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ śubham | tathāśubhaṃ ca tattvena yathāphalavibhāgataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 26: Characteristics of Fuel-sticks) (AVParis_26,1.1) Oṃ. I shall declare the measure, auspicious and inauspicious characteristics of fuel-sticks, truly, according to the division of results.

body.text: (AVParis_26,1.2) yajñakarmaṇi kartavyā[ḥ] śāntike pauṣṭike tathā | prādeśamātrīḥ samidhaḥ proktāḥ sarveṣu karmasu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,1.2) In the sacrificial rite, for peace and nourishment rites — fuel-sticks of one <s>prādeśa</s> (span) in length are prescribed for all rites.

body.text: (AVParis_26,1.3) tiryag yavodarāṇy aṣṭāv ūrdhvā vā vrīhayas trayaḥ | aṅgulasya pramāṇena prādeśo dvādaśāṅgulaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,1.3) Eight barley-grains placed crosswise, or three rice-grains upright — by the measure of a finger; a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) is twelve finger-widths.

body.text: (AVParis_26,1.4) ata ūrdhvaṃ na kartavyā nāpi hrasvā na cordhvataḥ | na vakrā caiva kartavyā nāpi granthisamanvitā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,1.4) Beyond this they should not be made, nor shorter, nor above [the measure]; they should not be made crooked, nor possessed of knots.

body.text: (AVParis_26,1.5) ūrdhvatas tu yato vakrā citradadruvicarcikāḥ | karoti yāge kṣipraṃ tu tasmāt tāṃ parivarjayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,1.5) One that is crooked from above, spotted, bent, or having scabs — it quickly causes [harm] in the sacrifice; therefore one should avoid it.

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.1) dviphalā piṇḍavarjāpi triphalā vāpi yā bhavet | ṣaṭphalā saptaphalā yā caturaṅgaṃ vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.1) One with two splits, or free from lumps, or with three splits; one with six or seven splits — destroys the four-fold [army].

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.2) sapattrapuṣpasamidhaḥ kalpayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ | pauṣṭikaṃ karma kurvīta sidhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.2) The discerning one, having prepared fuel-sticks with leaves and flowers, should perform the nourishment rite — it succeeds, without doubt.

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.3) pattrapuṣpayutā yās tu śāntadrumasamudbhavāḥ | samidho goṣṭhamadhye tu praśastāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.3) Those with leaves and flowers, born from peaceful trees, are declared and praised as fuel-sticks in the midst of the cattle-pen.

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.4) [athāparaṃ pravakṣyāmi samidhāṃ caiva lakṣaṇam] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.4) [Now I shall declare another characteristic of fuel-sticks.]

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.5) viśīrṇā dvidalā hrasvā vakrā caiva dvidhāgrataḥ | kṛśā ca dīrghā sthūlā ca karmasiddhivināśinī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.5) Crumbling, split in two, short, crooked, or double-tipped, thin, long, or thick — [these are] destroyers of ritual success.

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.6) [yad yatra lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ yasmin kāle yathāvidhi | tatra tenaiva siddhiḥ syād viparīte tathā bhayam] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.6) [Whatever characteristic is stated for whichever [time], in which rite and by which rule — thereby comes success; in the opposite, fear.]

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.7) samāhṛtānāṃ samidhāṃ tāsāṃ caiva phalaṃ śṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.7) Now hear the results of the collected fuel-sticks.

body.text: (AVParis_26,2.8) viśīrṇāyuḥkṣayaṃ kuryād dvidalā rogadā bhavet | abhimukhagatamātrā sadyo hrasvā nivartayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,2.8) A crumbling one causes the loss of life; a split one brings disease. One that has come only face-forward — a short one quickly turns back [the rite].

body.text: (AVParis_26,3.1) durbhagaṃ kurute vakrā sthānabhraṃśaṃ dvidhāgrataḥ | kṛśā sarvavināśāya dīrghā nāśayate śriyam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,3.1) A crooked one creates misfortune; a double-tipped one, loss of position. A thin one [leads to] total destruction; a long one destroys prosperity.

body.text: (AVParis_26,3.2) sthūlā tu kurute vighnaṃ sarvakārye dvijasya tu | ataḥ pramāṇaṃ vividhaṃ phalaṃ cāpi tathā śṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,3.2) A thick one creates obstacles in all affairs of the twice-born. Now hear the various measures and results likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_26,3.3) latāpallavasaṃjātā dvādaśāṅgulakalpitā | kṣīrāktā śāntike home hotavyā tu viśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,3.3) [A fuel-stick] born from creepers and shoots, measuring twelve finger-widths, moistened with milk — should be offered especially in the peace-oblation.

body.text: (AVParis_26,3.4) kevalaṃ muktisiddhyarthaṃ ghṛtāktā[m] homayeddvijaḥ | daśāṅgulapramāṇāṃ hi homayen mantrakarmaṇi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,3.4) Solely for the attainment of liberation, the twice-born should offer [one] smeared with ghee. One measuring ten finger-widths he should offer in mantra-rites.

body.text: (AVParis_26,3.5) navāṅgulā tu kartavyā tailābhyaktābhicārike | aṣṭāṅgulā vibhūtyarthe ghṛtadadhnā tu homayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,3.5) One of nine finger-widths, smeared with oil, should be made for sorcery. One of eight finger-widths for prosperity — he should offer with ghee and yogurt.

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.1) kevalaṃ madhusaṃyuktā saptāṅguladalīkṛtā | uccāṭane praśastā sā dvidalā ca na śāntaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.1) Solely mixed with honey, of seven finger-widths, split in two — this is praised for expulsion rites; but split in two is not for peace.

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.2) vidveṣe kaṭutailāktā dvidalā tu ṣaḍaṅgulā | sarvato granthihīnā tu viprāṇāṃ syāt samic chubhā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.2) For enmity rites, [one] smeared with pungent oil, split in two, of six finger-widths. Free from knots everywhere — that is the auspicious fuel-stick for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.3) avakrāgranthisaṃyuktā kṣatriyāṇāṃ jayāvahā | madhye tu granthisaṃyuktā vaiśyānāṃ bhūtisādhanī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.3) Uncrooked, with a knot — [this] brings victory for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. With a knot in the middle — [this] bestows prosperity for <s>Vaiśyas</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.4) trayāṇām api vakṣyante yā grāhyāḥ samidhaḥ smṛtaḥ | nātyārdrā nātiśuṣkā vā naiva coṣarasaṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.4) For all three [classes], the fuel-sticks to be taken are now declared: neither too moist nor too dry, nor born from barren soil,

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.5) na dagdhā na kṛmidaṣṭāḥ sarvadoṣavivarjitāḥ | samidhām indhanānāṃ ca tulyān vṛkṣān bravīmy ataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.5) not burnt, not worm-eaten, free from all defects. I shall now declare the trees for fuel-sticks and firewood that are equivalent.

body.text: (AVParis_26,4.6) śuṣukair yā indhanaiḥ pūrvaṃ yajñavṛkṣamayaiḥ śubhaiḥ | ārdrāṇi homayec caiva śuṣkaiḥ kalahakarmaṇi | śuṣkāṇi hīndhanāni syuḥ samidhas tu yathoditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,4.6) First, with dry fuel-woods of auspicious sacrificial trees; moist [fuel-sticks] should also be offered; dry ones in rites of quarrel. Dry ones should be the firewood; fuel-sticks are as stated.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.1) puṣṭikāmaḥ palāśasya gṛhṇīyāc chāntikarmaṇi udumbarasya vittārthī vaṭāśvatthasya rājyadhīḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,5.1) One desiring nourishment should take [fuel-sticks] of <s>Palāśa</s> in the peace-rite; one desiring wealth, of <s>Udumbara</s>; one aspiring to kingship, of <s>Vaṭa</s> (banyan) or <s>Aśvattha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.2) śrīkāmo bilvavṛkṣasya kadambasya tathaiva ca | vidveṣaṃ kaṭukaiḥ kuryāt kaṇṭakair maraṇaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,5.2) One desiring prosperity, of <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple) or <s>Kadamba</s> tree likewise. One should perform enmity [rites] with pungent [woods]; with thorny ones, killing [rites] result.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.3) kakubhaṃ kaṭabhaṃ vṛkṣaṃ kauvirālaṃ tu kauhakam | vaṃśaṃ vibhītakaṃ śigruṃ vidyād uccāṭane hitān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,5.3) <s>Kakubha</s>, <s>Kaṭabha</s>, <s>Kauvirāla</s>, and <s>Kauhaka</s> trees, bamboo, <s>Vibhītaka</s>, and <s>Śigru</s> — one should know these as beneficial for expulsion rites.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.4) stambhane sarvasainyānāṃ vijayārthe jayaṃ diśet | apāmārgeṇa saubhāgyam āyuṣkāmo hi dūrvayā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_26,5.4) For the paralysis of all armies, for the purpose of victory, [these] grant victory. With <s>Apāmārga</s> [one obtains] good fortune; one desiring long life [should use] <s>Dūrvā</s> grass.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.5) punnāgacampakau vṛkṣā ye cānye kṣīriṇaḥ śubhāḥ | yad yatra lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ yasmin kāle yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.5) <s>Punnāga</s> and <s>campaka</s> trees, and whatever other auspicious milky trees — whatever characteristic is stated for whichever, at what time, and according to which rule —

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.6) tatra tenaiva siddhiḥ syād viparīte tathā bhayam | arkaḥ palāśo madhuko nyagrodhodumbaras tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.6) in that, success is achieved by that very [method]; in the opposite case, there is fear. <s>Arka</s> (sun-plant), <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest), <s>madhūka</s> (mahua), <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan), and <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig) likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.7) plakṣo 'śvattho gomayānikuśāś ca samidhaḥ kramāt | yathākrameṇa samidha ādityādigraheṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.7) <s>plakṣa</s> (fig), <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), cow-dung, <s>kuśa</s> grass — these are the fire-sticks, in order. In order for the planets beginning with the Sun,

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.8) śataṃ sahasraṃ lakṣaṃ vā gāyatryā paramāhutiḥ | hūyamānaṃ tu yat kiṃ cit kṛtānnaṃ yadi vā tilāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.8) a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand — with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the supreme oblation. Whatever is offered — whether cooked food or sesame seeds —

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.9) grahanakṣatrapīḍāyāṃ sāvitryāpi hutaṃ hutam | eṣabhedo mayākhyātaḥ śubhasya tv aśubhasya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.9) when there is affliction from planets and <s>nakṣatra</s>s, what is offered with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> is [well] offered. This distinction between the auspicious and the inauspicious has been declared by me.

body.text: (AVParis_26,5.10) yathoktam etad yaḥ kuryāt sa sarvaphalam āpnuyād iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 26.5.10) He who performs this as prescribed obtains the fruit of everything.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_27. sruvalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_27,1.1) oṃ sauvarṇarājatais tāmraiḥ kāṃsyair draumais tathāyasaiḥ | sruvaiḥ sarvaguṇopetaiḥ karma kuryād yathākramam ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 27: Characteristics of the <s>Sruva</s> [Ladle]) (AVParis 27.1.1) Oṃ. With ladles of gold, silver, copper, bronze, wood, and iron — endowed with all qualities — one should perform the rite in order.

body.text: (AVParis_27,1.2) sauvarṇai rājatair yajñe tāmraiḥ śāntikapauṣṭike | kāṃsyena rudhiraṃ māṃsaṃ nānyaj juhuvīta kiṃ cana ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.1.2) With golden and silver [ladles] in sacrifice, with copper ones in peace-rites and prosperity-rites; with bronze, one should offer blood and flesh — nothing else whatsoever.

body.text: (AVParis_27,1.3) sarve yajñe prayoktavyā varjayitvāyasaṃ sruvam | āyasaṃ khādiraṃ caiva abhicāre prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.1.3) All [ladles] are to be used in sacrifice, excepting the iron ladle; the iron one and the <s>khadira</s>-wood one should be employed in sorcery.

body.text: (AVParis_27,1.4) adhunvaṃś caiva juhuyāt sruveṇāsphuṭitāhutim | dhunvan hi hanti putrān tu rākṣasā sphuṭitāhutiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.1.4) Without shaking, one should offer with the ladle an unspattered oblation; for shaking destroys sons, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s [seize] a spattered oblation.

body.text: (AVParis_27,1.5) nānyat kiṃ cid abhidhyāyed uddhṛtyānyata āhutim | tad daivatam abhidhyāyed āhutir yasya hūyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.1.5) One should not contemplate anything else while lifting the oblation from another [vessel]; one should contemplate only that deity for whom the oblation is being offered.

body.text: (AVParis_27,2.1) sruve pūrṇe japen mantram uttānaṃ śāntike karam | śāntike pauṣṭike caiva varjayet tu kanīnikām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.2.1) When the ladle is full, one should recite the <s>mantra</s> with the hand turned upward in peace-rites; in peace-rites and prosperity-rites, one should avoid the little finger.

body.text: (AVParis_27,2.2) nātidīrgho nātihrasvo nātisthūlaḥ kṛśas tathā | aṣṭāviṃśatyaṅgulaḥ syāt kaniṣṭhāgrapramāṇataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.2.2) Neither too long nor too short, neither too thick nor too thin — it should be twenty-eight <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-widths), measured from the tip of the little finger.

body.text: (AVParis_27,2.3) dīrgho hinasti rājānaṃ hrasva rtvijaṃ vināśayet | sthūlaḥ sasyopaghātāya kṛśaḥ kṣayakaraḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.2.3) A long [ladle] harms the king; a short one destroys the priest; a thick one is for the damage of crops; a thin one is said to cause decline.

body.text: (AVParis_27,2.4) gopucchāgrākṛtir daṇḍo maṇḍalāgra[m] śiro viduḥ | aṅguṣṭhāgrapramāṇena nimnaṃ śirasi khānayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.2.4) The handle is shaped like a cow's tail-tip; the head they know to be round at the tip; to the measure of a thumb-tip, one should make a depression in the head.

body.text: (AVParis_27,2.5) etal lakṣaṇam uddiṣṭaṃ sruvasya phalabhedataḥ | gopathena yathāśāstram uddhṛtaṃ śruticodanāt | sruveṇa kurute karma hastenāpi tathā śṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 27.2.5) This characteristic has been declared for the <s>sruva</s> according to the distinction of results. It has been extracted from the <s>Gopatha</s> [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] according to scripture, from the injunction of <s>Śruti</s>. When one performs the rite with a ladle, or by hand as well — hear thus:

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_28. hastalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_28,1.1) oṃ yadā juhoti hastena dakṣiṇenetareṇa vā | tadā vakṣye vidhiṃ tasya śreyasī syād yathāhutiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 28: Characteristics of Hand-Offering) (AVParis 28.1.1) Oṃ. When one offers by hand, with the right or with the other — then I shall declare the procedure for that, so that the oblation may be most excellent.

body.text: (AVParis_28,1.2) yathā naśyati caivāsya karma guhyam ajānataḥ | tathāhaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi gopathaḥ pāṭham icchatām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.1.2) How the rite of one who does not know [the rules] is indeed destroyed, secret as it is — that I shall fully declare, [as taught by] <s>Gopatha</s> for those who desire the recitation.

body.text: (AVParis_28,1.3) kuśabalbajamauñjāṃ vā kṛtvā veṣṭim anāmikām | homakarma tataḥ kuryāt spṛṣṭvā vāmena dakṣiṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.1.3) Having made a band of <s>kuśa</s> grass, <s>balbaja</s> grass, or <s>muñja</s> grass around the ring finger, then one should perform the oblation-rite, touching the right [hand] with the left.

body.text: (AVParis_28,1.4) na riktapāṇir juhuyān nānipātitajānukaḥ | anipātitajānoś ca haranty āhutī rākṣasāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.1.4) One should not offer with an empty hand, nor without having lowered the knee; for <s>Rākṣasa</s>s seize the oblations of one whose knee is not lowered.

body.text: (AVParis_28,1.5) uddhṛtya samidho 'nnaṃ vā pañcabhir juhuyād budhaḥ | śanaiś ca nirvaped annaṃ madhye 'gnau susamāhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.1.5) Having lifted up fire-sticks or food, the wise one should offer with five [fingers]; and one should gently pour the food in the middle of the fire, well-concentrated.

body.text: (AVParis_28,2.1) gṛhakarmaṇi yajñe vā tathā pañcabhir eva tu | śāntike pauṣṭike vaiva varjayet tu kanīnikām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.2.1) In domestic rites and in sacrifice, likewise with five [fingers] only; in peace-rites and prosperity-rites, one should avoid the little finger.

body.text: (AVParis_28,2.2) tisṛbhir juhuyād annaṃ na tilān naiva taṇḍulān | yadābhicārikaṃ kiṃ cit tasmin kāle prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.2.2) One should offer food with three [fingers] — not sesame seeds and not rice grains; whenever any sorcery-rite [is to be performed], one should employ [three fingers] at that time.

body.text: (AVParis_28,2.3) vāmenābhicāran nityaṃ tribhir aṅgulibhiḥ samaiḥ | nirdiṣṭaṃ tisṛbhiḥ śūlaṃ tena śatruṃ nipātayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.2.3) For sorcery, always with the left [hand], with three even fingers; the trident is prescribed with three [fingers] — with it one should strike down the enemy.

body.text: (AVParis_28,2.4) apasavyena hastena savyaṃ yadi juhoti tat | savyena cāpasavyaṃ tu [savyaṃ yadi juhoti tat] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.2.4) If one offers the right-hand [oblation] with the left hand, and the left with the right hand —

body.text: (AVParis_28,2.5) abhicāras tu tat proktaḥ....ṣarvaśāntiṃ gamiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 28.2.5) that is declared to be sorcery... it will lead to complete destruction.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_29. jvālālakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_29,1.1) oṃ bṛhaspatiṃ sukhāsīnam ātmavidyāparāyaṇam | praṇipatya mahartvijaṃ nāradaḥ paripṛcchati ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 29: Characteristics of Fire-Flames) (AVParis 29.1.1) Oṃ. <s>Nārada</s>, having bowed to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, seated comfortably, devoted to self-knowledge, the great officiating priest, asks:

body.text: (AVParis_29,1.2) kathayasva mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada | aśubhaṃ yac chubhaṃ vāpi lakṣaṇaṃ pāvakasya tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.1.2) 'Tell [me], O greatly wise one, versed in all sciences — the inauspicious and auspicious characteristics of fire.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,1.3) sa pṛṣṭas tena tat sarvam ācacakṣe mahāmatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.1.3) Asked by him, the great-minded one declared all of that:

body.text: (AVParis_29,1.4) hūyamānoyadā vahnir ṛjujvālaḥ pradṛśyate | snigdhaś ca kiṃśukābhaś ca siddhis tatra vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.1.4) 'When the fire being offered into shows straight flames, is oily and resembles the <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest) — success should be declared there.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,1.5) yatra bālārkavarṇābhaḥ karmaṇy agniḥ pradṛśyate | śāntiṃ labhete tatrāśu yajamānapurohitau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.1.5) 'Where the fire appears in the rite with the color of the young sun — there peace is quickly obtained by the sacrificer and the <s>purohita</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,1.6) aśokakusumābho 'pi kāñcanābhas tathaiva ca | śāntiṃ karoty ākālena hūyamāno hutāśanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.1.6) 'Even with the hue of <s>aśoka</s> blossoms, or likewise with a golden hue — the fire, when offered into, brings peace in due time.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,2.1) adhūmo jvalate kṣipraṃ kṛtvāvartaṃ pradakṣiṇam | tadā śāntiṃ vijānīyād viparīte tathā bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.2.1) 'When it blazes quickly without smoke, making a clockwise spiral — then one should know there is peace; in the opposite case, there is fear.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,2.2) śvasate garjate caiva visphuliṅgāḥ samantataḥ | prāyaścittiṃ tadākuryād yad uktaṃ kauśikena tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.2.2) 'When it hisses and roars, and sparks [fly] in all directions — then one should perform an expiation, as stated by <s>Kauśika</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,2.3) athāpy āliṅgate bhūmiṃ bhramate ca samantataḥ | aśubhaṃ kathayet tatra hotre 'sau pāvakaḥ svayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.2.3) 'And when it embraces the ground and whirls about on all sides — one should declare inauspiciousness there; the fire itself [speaks] to the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,2.4) kapilaḥ piṅgalas tāmro raktaḥ kāñcanasaprabhaḥ | śubhakṛt pāvako jñeyo viparīto bhayāvahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.2.4) 'Tawny, reddish-brown, coppery, red, with the radiance of gold — the fire should be known as auspicious; the opposite is fear-bringing.'

body.text: (AVParis_29,2.5) yadāgnau lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ cid aśubhaṃ tu pradṛśyate | hotā kleśam avāpnoti śāntiṃ tatra prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 29.2.5) 'Whenever any inauspicious characteristic appears in the fire — the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest suffers affliction; one should employ a peace-rite there.'

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_30. laghulakṣahomaḥ)
(AVParis_30,1.1) oṃ śaunakaṃ tu sukhāsīnaṃ gautamaḥ paripṛcchati | lakṣahomasya yat puṇyam āhutīnāṃ ca devatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 30: The Short <s>Lakṣahoma</s> [Hundred-Thousand Oblation]) (AVParis 30.1.1) Oṃ. <s>Gautama</s> asks <s>Śaunaka</s>, seated comfortably: 'What is the merit of the <s>lakṣahoma</s>, and what are the deities of the oblations?'

body.text: (AVParis_30,1.2) tasmai yathāvad ācaṣṭe śaunako jñānalocanaḥ | śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā lakṣahomaṃ yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.1.2) <s>Śaunaka</s>, whose eye is knowledge, duly declared to him: 'Listen attentively — the <s>lakṣahoma</s> according to proper procedure.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,1.3) agnyāgārasya yā bhūmis tāṃ pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ | śuddhākṣārā samā snigdhā yā ca pūrvottaraplavā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.1.3) 'The ground for the fire-house I shall describe completely: it should be pure, free from alkali, level, smooth, and sloping to the east and north.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,1.4) abhasmāsthyaṅgāratūṣā praśastā parikīrtitā | pramāṇaṃ bāhumātraṃ tu jaṅghāmātraṃ dviratnikam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.1.4) 'Free from ash, bones, charcoal, and chaff — that is declared praiseworthy. The measure is one arm's length, or a leg's length, or two cubits.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,1.5) caturaśraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ tulyaṃ sūtreṇa dhārayet | brāhmaṇā vedasaṃpannā brahmakarmasamādhayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.1.5) 'Four-sided, four-cornered, held level by a string. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, endowed with Vedic knowledge, accomplished in <s>Brahman</s>-rites,'

body.text: (AVParis_30,1.6) upoṣya caikarātraṃ ca gāyatryā ayutaṃ japet | upoṣya caiva gāyatryā japeyur ayutaṃ budhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.1.6) 'having fasted for one night, should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> ten thousand times; having fasted, the wise ones should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> ten thousand times.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,2.1) te śuklavāsasaḥ snātāḥ sragbhir gandhair alaṃkṛtāḥ | nirāhārās tathā dāntāḥ saṃtuṣṭāḥ sajitendriyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.2.1) 'They, wearing white garments, bathed, adorned with garlands and fragrances, fasting, self-controlled, content, with senses conquered,'

body.text: (AVParis_30,2.2) kauśam āsanam āsīnāḥ prayuñjyur homam uttamam | ullikhya cādbhir abhyukṣya saṃskṛtya vidhipūrvakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.2.2) 'seated on a silken seat, should perform the supreme oblation. Having scraped [the ground], sprinkled with water, and consecrated according to rule,'

body.text: (AVParis_30,2.3) agne praihy agninā rayim ity upasthāpya pāvakam | kuryād upasamādhāya samās tvāgne samāhitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.2.3) 'having established the fire [reciting] "agne praihi" and "agninā rayim" (O <s>Agni</s>, proceed; by <s>Agni</s>, wealth) — one should perform the preliminary offering, concentrated: "samās tvā agne samāhitaḥ" (O <s>Agni</s>, may we be composed).'

body.text: (AVParis_30,3.1) lakṣahoma@@kute pūrṇe dhenuṃ dadyāt payasvinīm | anaḍvān kāñcanaṃ vastraṃ tuṣyeyur yena vā dvijāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.3.1) 'When the <s>lakṣahoma</s> is complete, one should give a milch cow, a bull, gold, garments — or whatever would please the twice-born.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,3.2) yavais tu vipulān bhogān dhānyair āyuṣyam eva ca | tilair hutvā tu tejasvī āyuḥ kīrtiṃ ca vardhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.3.2) 'By offering with barley, one obtains abundant enjoyments; with grain, long life; by offering with sesame, one becomes brilliant — life and fame increase.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,3.3) ādityaloko 'rkamayī pālāśī soma āpyate | āśvatthī viṣṇulokasya brāhma audumbarī tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.3.3) 'With <s>arka</s>-wood, one attains the world of the Sun; with <s>palāśa</s>-wood, the world of <s>Soma</s>; with <s>aśvattha</s>-wood, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world; and with <s>udumbara</s>-wood, that of <s>Brahman</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,3.4) anenaiva vidhānena hūyate 'tra hutāśanaḥ | hutvaitāṃś caturo lakṣān brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.3.4) 'By this very procedure, the fire is offered into. Having offered these four <s>lakṣa</s>s (hundred-thousands), one goes to the world of <s>Brahman</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_30,3.5) yāvaj jīvati kartāsau tāvat putrān dhanaṃ śriyam | pūrṇe kāle vimānena nīyate paramaṃ padam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30.3.5) 'As long as the performer lives, so long [he enjoys] sons, wealth, and prosperity; at the completion of his time, he is conveyed by a celestial chariot to the supreme station.'

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_30b. bṛhallakṣahomaḥ)
(AVParis_30b,1.1) om atha kāṅkāyano bhagavantam atharvāṇaṃ papraccha || bhagavan kena vidhānena koṭihomaṃ lakṣahomam ayutahomaṃ vā prārambhamāṇaḥ katham ṛtvijo vṛṇīte kathaṃ ca kuryus tasmai sa hovāca ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 30b: The Extended <s>Lakṣahoma</s>) (AVParis 30b.1.1) Oṃ. Then <s>Kāṅkāyana</s> asked the venerable <s>Atharvan</s>: 'Venerable sir, by what procedure, when undertaking a <s>koṭihoma</s> (ten-million oblation), <s>lakṣahoma</s> (hundred-thousand oblation), or <s>ayutahoma</s> (ten-thousand oblation), how does one select the priests, and how should they perform?' To him he said:

body.text:
(AVParis_30b,1.2) brāhmaṇo vā rājā vā vaiśyo vā grāmo vā janapado vā śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmaḥ koṭihomaṃ lakṣahomam ayutahomaṃ vāhaṃ kariṣyāmīti tasyā samāpter bhavadbhir amāṃsāśibhir brahmacāribhir haviṣyabhugbhir bhavitavyam
(AVParis_30b,1.3) tais tatheti uktaḥ kuṇḍam ekahastaṃ dvihastaṃ caturhastam aṣṭahastaṃ vā [samastahastaṃ vā dīrghaṃ vā] daśahastaṃ khānayet tathā ca bādariḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.2-3) 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a king, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a village, or a district — desiring prosperity or desiring peace — [saying] "I shall perform a <s>koṭihoma</s>, <s>lakṣahoma</s>, or <s>ayutahoma</s>" — until its completion, you must be non-meat-eaters, celibate, and subsisting on sacrificial food.' Having been told 'So be it' by them, one should have a fire-pit excavated — one <s>hasta</s> (cubit), two <s>hasta</s>s, four <s>hasta</s>s, eight <s>hasta</s>s, [or equal <s>hasta</s>s, or elongated], or ten <s>hasta</s>s. And thus [says] <s>Bādari</s>:

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.4) lakṣahome tu kartavyam aṣṭahastaṃ na saṃśayaḥ | dvihastaṃ vā prakurvīta caturhastam athāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.4) 'For the <s>lakṣahoma</s>, one should make it eight <s>hasta</s>s, without doubt; or one may make it two <s>hasta</s>s, or four <s>hasta</s>s as well.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.5) kuṇḍaṃ vā daśahastaṃ tu dvivistāraṃ tathottaram | na cet purastād dhīnaṃ syāt sukhaṃ yajñaḥ samāpyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.5) 'Or a fire-pit of ten <s>hasta</s>s, with double the width, and likewise in the northern [dimension]; if the front side is not deficient, the sacrifice is completed with ease.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.6) atha dakṣiṇato hīnaṃ yajamānabhayaṃkaram | paścimena vihīnaṃ syād yajñasyāsiddhidaṃ dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.6) 'But if deficient on the south, it brings fear to the sacrificer; if deficient on the west, it surely prevents the success of the sacrifice.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.7) uttareṇa vinirdiṣṭaṃ rājño rājyaharaṃ bhṛśam | madhye vihīnaṃ yad kuṇḍaṃ prajākṣayakaraṃ viduḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.7) 'If deficient on the north, it is declared to cause severe loss of kingdom for the king; a fire-pit deficient in the middle is known to cause destruction of progeny.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.8) sraktihīnaṃ tu yat kuṇḍaṃ tad apy aśubhadaṃ bhavet | dvādaśāṅgulamānena mekhalākṣetram ucyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.8) 'A fire-pit deficient in the rim is also inauspicious. The girdle-zone is declared to measure twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-widths).'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.9) mekhalātrayam uddhiṣṭam ubhayaṃ caturaṅgulam | caturaṅgulamānena pūrvāpūrvasamucchritā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.9) 'Three girdles are prescribed, both [inner and outer] of four <s>aṅgula</s>s; each successively raised by four <s>aṅgula</s>s.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.10) prathamā sāttvikī proktā dvitīyā rājasī smṛtā | tṛtīyā tāmasī jñeyā mekhalā vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.10) 'The first is declared <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), the second is known as <s>rājasika</s> (passionate), the third girdle, [marked by] the bull-banner, is to be known as <s>tāmasika</s> (dark).'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.11) caturdaśāṅgulāṃ tatra yoniṃ kurvīta sādhakaḥ | aṣṭāṅgulaṃ bhaved vṛttaṃ nirvāhas tu ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.11) 'There, the adept should make the <s>yoni</s> (source-channel) fourteen <s>aṅgula</s>s [long]; the round part should be eight <s>aṅgula</s>s; the outlet-channel, six <s>aṅgula</s>s.'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.12) gajoṣṭhasadṛśākāra prājāpatyā ca sā ciduḥ | evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena kuṇḍaṃ lakṣaṇalakṣitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.12) 'Shaped like an elephant's lip — they call it the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>). Having thus made the fire-pit according to procedure, marked with [all] characteristics,'

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.13) sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ sarvatas tu samāhitaḥ | kuṇḍaṃ siddhikaraṃ jñeyam āyuḥkīrtivivardhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 30b.1.13) 'complete in all characteristics, [the adept] fully concentrated on all sides — the fire-pit should be known as success-producing, increasing life and fame.'

body.text:
(AVParis_30b,1.14) tasmād yatnena kuṇḍaṃ khātvādbhir abhyukṣya purastād agner ādityādīn grahān pratiṣṭhāpyottarataḥ kṛttikādīni nakṣatrāṇi svāsu dikṣu lokapālān sarvāsu kuṇḍasraktiṣv agnyādidevān ratiṣṭhāpya
(AVParis_30b,1.15) teṣāṃ pratimantram āvāhanādikaṃ kṛtvā vilīnapūtam ājyaṃ gṛhītvā sruvaṃ srucaṃ ca saṃmṛjya pratapyedhmam upasamādhāyānvārabdhāya vāstoṣpatyādibhiś caturbhir gaṇaiḥ śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kartāram ācāmayati ca saṃprokṣati ca ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, having dug the fire-pit with effort, having sprinkled it with water, having established the planets beginning with <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) to the east of the fire, the <s>nakṣatra</s>s beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s> to the north, the world-guardians in their own directions, and the deities beginning with <s>Agni</s> at all the corners of the fire-pit — having performed the invocation and the rest for each with its mantra, having taken melted and purified clarified butter, having wiped the <s>sruva</s> and <s>sruc</s> (ladles), having heated and arranged the kindling wood, having touched [the fire], and having made the pacification-water with the four groups [of mantras] beginning with <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> — then he makes the performer sip water and sprinkles him.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.16) atha samidho ghṛtāktās tilān vā svāhākāravatīḥ saṃkhyāvatyo gāyatryā mahāvyāhṛtibhir vā sarva ṛtvijo juhvati ||
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>ṛtvij</s>s (officiating priests) offer fuel-sticks anointed with clarified butter, or sesame, with the <s>svāhā</s> exclamation, in counted numbers, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> or the <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>s (great sacred utterances).

body.text: (AVParis_30b,1.17) śrīparṇamiśrāḥ śrīkāmasya śamīparṇamiśrāḥ śāntikāmasya karīrasaktumiśrā vṛṣṭikāmaysa badarādiphalamiśrāḥ paśukāmasya ||
body.translated_text: Mixed with <s>Śrīparṇa</s> leaves for one desiring prosperity; mixed with <s>Śamī</s> leaves for one desiring peace; mixed with <s>Karīra</s> flour for one desiring rain; mixed with <s>Badara</s> (jujube) and other fruits for one desiring cattle.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.1) aharahaḥ karmaṇo 'pavargād atha pūrṇāyāṃ koṭyāṃ lakṣe vāyute vānvārabdhe yajamāne niśi mahābhiṣEkaṃ kṛtvā vasor dhāraṃ juhvati ||
body.translated_text: Day after day, upon completion of the [daily] ritual — when a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand), or <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) [oblations] are completed, with the sacrificer having touched [the fire], the great consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) is performed at night, and the stream-of-wealth (<s>vasor dhārā</s>) oblation is offered.

body.text:
(AVParis_30b,2.2) audumbarīṃ srucaṃ śuraḥpramāṇāṃ brāhmaṇasya lalātapramāṇāṃ kṣatriyasya skandhapramāṇāṃ vaiṣyasyāpramāṇāṃ janapadasya
(AVParis_30b,2.3) teṣām ante saraṇārthaṃ nimnaṃ khānayitvoṣṇodakena prakṣālyājyam ānīya vasor dhārāṃ vaiśvānaraṃ prāpnoti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Udumbara</s> (fig-wood) offering-ladle: of head-size for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of forehead-size for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, of shoulder-size for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, of unspecified size for the provincial [people]. Having dug a depression at their end for the flow, having washed with warm water, having brought in the clarified butter, the stream-of-wealth (<s>vasor dhārā</s>) [oblation] reaches the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [fire].

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.4) tad yad ājyadhānīṃ ca vaiśvānaraṃ prāpnoti athoccārayati ||
body.translated_text: When the clarified-butter vessel and the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [fire] are reached, then one utters [the following]:

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.5) ojaś ca me kṣatraṃ ca me ye agnayo amo devavadhebhyo bhavāśarvau mṛḍataṃ prāṇāya nama iti hutvā arghaṃ pradāya vastraṃ lodhraṃ mālyaṃ phalādīni bhājane kṛtvā namas te astu paśyata iti svāhākāreṇāgnau prakṣipya yamyaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Vigor is mine, and sovereignty is mine' — 'Those fires which for the slaying of gods' — 'O <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, be merciful' — 'Salutation to <s>Prāṇa</s> (Life-breath)' — having offered thus, having given the <s>argha</s> (honorific offering), having placed cloth, <s>lodhra</s>, garlands, fruits, and the rest in a vessel, 'Salutation to you, behold' — having cast [it] into the fire with the <s>svāhā</s> exclamation, whatever desire one desires, that desire is fulfilled for him.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.6) samṛddhihomādi samānaṃ svastyayanāni japet puṇyāhaṃ vācayed gobhūtilasuvarṇaṃ vāsaś ca rtvigbhyaḥ saṃpradāya praṇipatya visarjayet ||
body.translated_text: The prosperity-oblation and the rest are the same; one should recite the auspicious prayers; one should have the <s>Puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day) pronounced; having given cows, land, sesame, gold, and cloth to the <s>ṛtvij</s>s, one should bow and take leave.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.7) tasminn ahani vyatīte yadi strī mālyahastā śvetacandanāniliptā śvetapuṣpāṇy ādāya prayacched gaurasarṣapān pāṇyādhāre vā gṛhītvā prāsādam ārohayet kuñjaraṃ vā pramattam aśvaṃ śvetaṃ vā parvataṃ govṛṣaṃ vā yānaṃ yuktaṃ vājibhir yady ārohet svapnakāle samastasiddhiṃ vidyān manaso yām abhīṣṭām ||
body.translated_text: On that day having passed, if a woman with garlands in hand, anointed with white sandalwood, taking white flowers, should give [them]; or if, having taken yellow mustard in the palm, she should ascend a palace, an elephant, a spirited white horse, a mountain, a bull, or a vehicle yoked with horses — at the time of dreaming, one should know [this as] the complete success of one's heart's desire.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.8) tasmāt tāṃ rātrīṃ prayataḥ svapet || svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvā rtvigbhyo nivedayet || paro 'pehi yo na jībo 'si vidma te svapna yathā kalāṃ yathā śapham iti rājamukham abhimantrya yathāgataṃ gaccheyus tad api ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore on that night one should sleep devoutly; having seen the dream, one should report it to the <s>ṛtvij</s>s. 'Go away, you who are not alive! We know you, O dream; as a digit, as a hoof-print' — having consecrated the king's face [with these mantras], they should depart as they came. On this too, [here are the] verses:

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.9) divyāntarikṣabhaumeṣu adbhuteṣu na saṃśayaḥ | koṭihomaṃ viduḥ prājñā lakṣaṃ vāyutam eva vā ||
body.translated_text: For celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents — there is no doubt; the wise know the <s>koṭi-homa</s>, or the <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred-thousand) or <s>ayuta</s> (ten-thousand) [oblation].

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.10) avijñātaṃ ca yat pāpaṃ sahasā caiva yat kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ lakṣahomasya karaṇād dhi vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: Whatever sin was unknown, and whatever was committed rashly — all that is destroyed by the performance of the <s>lakṣa-homa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_30b,2.11) tasmāt sarveṣu kāryeṣu śāntikeṣu viśeṣataḥ | yaḥ kuryāt prayato nityaṃ na so 'narthān samaśnute ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, in all affairs, especially in pacification rites — he who always performs them devoutly does not encounter misfortune.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_31. koṭihomaḥ)
(AVParis_31,1.1) oṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaś caiva pīḍyamānā mahāsūraiḥ | mṛtyunā vyādhibhiś caiva brahmāṇam idam abruvan ||
body.translated_text: (Supplement 31: The <s>Koṭi-homa</s> [Ten-Million Oblation]) Oṃ. The gods and <s>Ṛṣi</s>s, tormented by great <s>Asura</s>s, by death and diseases, spoke thus to <s>Brahmā</s>:

body.text: (AVParis_31,1.2) karmaṇā kena deveśa mṛtyur vyādhiś ca jīyate | aiśvaryaṃ prāpyate vāpi sthānaṃ ca paramaṃ prabho ||
body.translated_text: "By what ritual action, O Lord of Gods, are death and disease conquered? And how is sovereignty obtained, and the supreme station, O Lord?"

body.text: (AVParis_31,1.3) evam ukto mahātejā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ | pratyuvāceśvaraḥ sarvān viprān devagaṇaiḥ saha ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds, the Lord, replied to all — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s together with the hosts of gods:

body.text: (AVParis_31,1.4) śṛṇudhvaṃ prayatāḥ sarve prāpyate yena karmaṇā | aiśvaryam āyur ārogyaṃ putrā vijaya eva ca ||
body.translated_text: "Hear, all of you, attentively — by what action are obtained sovereignty, long life, health, sons, and victory:

body.text: (AVParis_31,1.5) savyāhṛtiṃ sapraṇavāṃ gāyatrīṃ śirasā saha | ye japanti sadā tebhyo na bhayaṃ vidyate kva cit ||
body.translated_text: Those who always recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with the <s>Vyāhṛti</s>s, with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), together with the <s>Śiras</s> (head verse) — for them, fear exists nowhere.

body.text: (AVParis_31,2.1) tayā homaś ca kartavyaḥ satataṃ siddhim icchatā | yavais tilaiḥ samidbhiś ca vrīhibhiḥ sarṣapais tathā ||
body.translated_text: With that [<s>Gāyatrī</s>], the oblation should always be performed by one desiring success — with barley, sesame, fuel-sticks, rice, and mustard seeds.

body.text: (AVParis_31,2.2) atha cen mahatīṃ siddhiṃ prārthayedhvaṃ surottamāḥ | purodhasā kārayadhvaṃ koṭihomaṃ mahāphalam ||
body.translated_text: But if you seek great success, O best of gods, have your <s>purohita</s> perform the <s>koṭi-homa</s>, which yields great fruit.

body.text: (AVParis_31,2.3) yādṛśaṃ kṛtavān pūrvam atharvā tryambakasya tu | tādṛśena vidhānena koṭihomaḥ prayujyate ||
body.translated_text: Such as <s>Atharvā</s> formerly performed for <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — by that very procedure, the <s>koṭi-homa</s> is to be employed.

body.text: (AVParis_31,2.4) mahattvaṃ prārthayamānaḥ śarvo 'tharvāṇam abravīt | kuruṣva mama tat karma mahattvaṃ yena labhyate ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), desiring greatness, said to <s>Atharvā</s>: 'Perform for me that ritual by which greatness is obtained —

body.text: (AVParis_31,2.5) aiśvaryam āyur ārogyaṃ sthānaṃ ca paramaṃ prabho | putrā lakṣmīr yaśo medhā balaṃ pauruṣyam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: Sovereignty, long life, health, the supreme station, O Lord — sons, prosperity, fame, intelligence, strength, and manliness.'

body.text: (AVParis_31,3.1) evam ukto mahātejā atharvā mantradarśavit | gāyatrīṃ tapasā yuktām ṛcaḥ padam itīti ha ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant <s>Atharvā</s>, seer of mantras, [took] the <s>Gāyatrī</s> endowed with <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — 'a verse, a <s>pada</s>' — thus indeed.

body.text: (AVParis_31,3.2) [ṛcaḥ padaṃ mātrayeti mantre vijñāyate hi sā |] gāyatrī vai tripād brahma viśvarūpā ca saṃsthitā ||
body.translated_text: [A verse, a <s>pada</s>, and a <s>mātra</s> (unit) — thus is she known in the mantra.] The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed the three-footed <s>Brahman</s>, established in the universal form.

body.text: (AVParis_31,3.3) prāṇadā sarvabhūtānāṃ dhāraṇī yāpi nityaśaḥ | iti niścitya manasā koṭihomaṃ prayojayat ||
body.translated_text: She who gives life-breath to all beings, who sustains [them] always — having thus resolved in his mind, he employed the <s>koṭi-homa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,3.4) samidbhiḥ śāntavṛkṣasya gāyatryā susamāhitaḥ | tato mahattvam agamad aiśaryaṃ paramaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: With fuel-sticks of peaceful trees, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, fully concentrated — then he attained greatness and supreme sovereignty.

body.text: (AVParis_31,3.5) mahādeva iti cāsya nāma lokeṣu viśrutam | upadravāś ca ye ke cid upaghātās tathaiva ca | sarve 'sya praśamaṃ yātāḥ skandaṃ putraṃ ca labdhavān ||
body.translated_text: And the name '<s>Mahādeva</s>' (Great God) became renowned for him in the worlds; and whatever afflictions and calamities there were — all of them were pacified for him, and he obtained <s>Skanda</s> as his son.

body.text: (AVParis_31,4.1) tataḥ prītas tu bhagavāñ śaṃkaraḥ paryapṛcchata | atharvāṇaṃ mahāprājñaṃ koṭihomasya ko vidhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), pleased, asked the greatly wise <s>Atharvā</s>: 'What is the procedure of the <s>koṭi-homa</s>?'

body.text: (AVParis_31,4.2) caturviṃśākṣaraṃ brahma tripādaṃ lokadhāraṇam | sāvitraṃ tena homo 'yaṃ kṛto me koṭisaṃmitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The twenty-four-syllabled <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Gāyatrī</s>), three-footed, sustaining the worlds — the <s>Sāvitra</s> [mantra] — with that, this oblation was performed by me, amounting to a <s>koṭi</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,4.3) vidhiṃ cāsya pravakṣyāmi sarvalokahitāya vai | yatprayogād bhavec chāntir vṛddhiś ca paramā nṛṇām ||
body.translated_text: And I shall declare its procedure for the welfare of all the worlds — by whose employment there comes pacification and supreme growth for men.

body.text: (AVParis_31,4.4) upadraveṣu bhūtānām āpatsu vividhāsu ca | koṭihomaḥ prayoktavyaḥ ketūnāṃ darśane tathā ||
body.translated_text: In afflictions of beings and in various calamities — the <s>koṭi-homa</s> should be employed; likewise when comets are seen.

body.text: (AVParis_31,4.5) upasargabhaye caiva paracakrabhaye tathā | anāvṛṣṭibhaye caiva koṭihomaṃ prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: In fear of natural calamities, in fear of enemy forces, and in fear of drought — one should employ the <s>koṭi-homa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.1) ārambhaṃ tasya kurvīta śukle cāpi tithau śubhe | muhūrte vijaye caiva tithichidrāṇi varjayet ||
body.translated_text: One should commence it in the bright [fortnight], on an auspicious <s>tithi</s>, at the victorious <s>muhūrta</s> (moment); one should avoid the <s>tithi</s>-gaps (inauspicious lunar days).

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.2) rohiṇyāṃ vaiṣṇave tvāṣṭre pauṣṇe maitrottareṣu ca | abhijitpuṣyasaumyeṣu kuryāt puṇyeṣu vā budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (<s>Śravaṇa</s>), <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (<s>Citrā</s>), <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (<s>Revatī</s>), <s>Maitra</s> (<s>Anurādhā</s>), the <s>Uttara</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Saumya</s> (<s>Mṛgaśiras</s>) — the wise one should perform [it] under auspicious [<s>nakṣatra</s>s].

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.3) atha cet tvarate kartuṃ koṭihomaṃ mahāphalam | puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvāsya ārambhaṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: But if one hastens to perform the <s>koṭi-homa</s> of great fruit, the wise one should have the <s>Puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day) pronounced and then commence.

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.4) aṣṭahastaṃ tu nirdiṣṭaṃ koṭihomasya khātakam | tasyaivārdhapramāṇena lakṣahome vidhīyate ||
body.translated_text: The fire-pit for the <s>koṭi-homa</s> is prescribed as eight <s>hasta</s>s (cubits); for the <s>lakṣa-homa</s>, half that measure is ordained.

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.5) trirātropoṣito brahmā kṛtvā śāntiṃ caturgaṇīm | prokṣayet karmasiddhyarthaṃ vāstu śāntyudakena tu ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> [priest], having fasted for three nights, having performed the four-fold pacification, should sprinkle the ritual site with pacification-water for the success of the rite.

body.text: (AVParis_31,5.6) mahāśāntividhānena nirmathyāgniṃ samāhitaḥ | tāvat kuryād budhaḥ sarvaṃ yāvan no nairṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
body.translated_text: Having churned the fire by the great pacification procedure, concentrated — the wise one should perform everything thus until the <s>Nairṛta</s> (southwestern) [oblation] is done.

body.text: (AVParis_31,6.1) tataḥ prabhāte bahuśa uddhṛtyāgniṃ samāhitaḥ | nirmathya hāvayet tatra samidho brāhmaṇān bahūn ||
body.translated_text: Then at dawn, having extracted the fire many times, concentrated, having churned [it], he should have many <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s offer fuel-sticks there.

body.text: (AVParis_31,6.2) śataṃ sahasraṃ koṭiṃ vā viṃśatir daśa vā dvijāḥ | juhuyuḥ śāntavṛkṣasya samidho ghṛtasaṃyutāḥ ||
body.translated_text: A hundred, a thousand, or a <s>koṭi</s> — twenty or ten twice-born should offer fuel-sticks of peaceful trees, combined with clarified butter.

body.text: (AVParis_31,6.3) svayaṃ vāpi yajed brahmā savitāraṃ dinedine | pākayajñavidhānena mantraś cātra viṣāsahim ||
body.translated_text: Or the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] himself may worship <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun) day after day, by the <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) procedure; and here the mantra is 'the poison-conquering one.'

body.text: (AVParis_31,6.4) śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryāt tilaiḥ pāpāpanuttaye | samidbhiḥ sarvakāmas tu bilvaiḥ prāpnoti kāñcanam ||
body.translated_text: One desiring peace should use barley; for the removal of sin, sesame; for all desires, fuel-sticks; with <s>bilva</s> (bael), one obtains gold.

body.text: (AVParis_31,6.5) labhate śriyam agryāṃ tu padmais tejo ghṛtena tu | dadhnā tu labhate putrān payasā brahmavarcasam ||
body.translated_text: One obtains supreme prosperity with lotuses; radiance with clarified butter; sons with curds; and <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual splendor) with milk.

body.text: (AVParis_31,7.1) haviṣyabhojino dāntāḥ śuklāmbaradharās tathā | hāvakā niyatāḥ sarve bhaveyur brahmacāriṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: All the oblation-offerers should be restrained, eating only sacrificial food, wearing white garments, disciplined, and observing <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy).

body.text: (AVParis_31,7.2) āraṇyam upayuñjānaḥ payasā vāpi vartayet | phalāhāro 'pi vā brahmā koṭihomaṃ samācaret ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> [priest], using forest [produce] or subsisting on milk, or eating only fruits, should perform the <s>koṭi-homa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,7.3) pratyekaṃ caiva hotṝṇāṃ dātavyā dakṣiṇā tataḥ | niṣko aśvo gaur vāsaś ca hiraṇyaṃ vāpi śaktitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the ritual fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be given to each of the <s>hotṛ</s>s (offerers): a <s>niṣka</s> (gold coin), a horse, a cow, cloth, or gold — according to one's ability.

body.text: (AVParis_31,7.4) yaś caivāpi bhaved brahmā prayoktā sarvakarmaṇām | sarvasvaṃ tasya deyaṃ syād dhiraṇyaṃ vāpi tatsamam ||
body.translated_text: And whoever is the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], the director of all rites — to him should be given one's entire property, or gold equivalent to it.

body.text: (AVParis_31,7.5) koṭihome samāpte tu yajed grahagaṇān budhaḥ | kārayed amṛtāṃ caiva ghṛtakambalam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>koṭi-homa</s> is completed, the wise one should worship the planetary hosts; he should have the <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortality) [rite] performed, and the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s> (ghee-blanket) [rite] as well.

body.text: (AVParis_31,8.1) kāryāmṛtā mṛtyubhaye ghṛtakambalasaṃyutā | paracakrāgame tv aindrī ghṛtakambala[m] eva ca ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Amṛtā</s> [rite] should be performed when there is fear of death, accompanied by the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s>; the <s>Aindrī</s> [rite] when enemy forces approach, also with the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s>.

body.text:
(AVParis_31,8.2) raudrī sarvādbhutotpattau ghṛtakambalasaṃyutā | [salilā salilakṣaye ghṛtakambala eva ca ||]
(AVParis_31,8.3) ghṛtakambalapṛṣṭhā ca salilā salilakṣaye | yenayena tu kāmena koṭihomaṃ prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Raudrī</s> [rite] at the occurrence of all portents, accompanied by the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s>; [the <s>Salilā</s> (water-rite) when waters diminish, also with the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s>.] The <s>Salilā</s>, backed by the <s>Ghṛtakambala</s>, when waters diminish; for whatever desire one employs the <s>koṭi-homa</s>,

body.text: (AVParis_31,8.4) āmnātaṃ tatra yat karma tad ante kārayed budhaḥ | eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭo abhicāre vidhīyate ||
body.translated_text: Whatever rite is prescribed there — the wise one should have it performed at the end. This same procedure is observed when it is applied for <s>abhicāra</s> (hostile sorcery).

body.text: (AVParis_31,8.5) pratilomayātra homaḥ sāvitryā tilasarṣapaiḥ | ārambhaṃ tasya ghoreṣu nakṣatreṣu dineṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: In hostile [application], the oblation with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (<s>Gāyatrī</s>) is done in reverse order, with sesame and mustard. Its commencement [should be] under terrible <s>nakṣatra</s>s and days.

body.text: (AVParis_31,8.6) kārayet kṛṣṇapakṣasya tithichidreṣu sarvadā | maghāśleṣā tathā mūlaṃ revaty ārdrā ca sarvadā ||
body.translated_text: One should have it performed always during the dark fortnight, at <s>tithi</s>-gaps; [under] <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, and <s>Ārdrā</s> — always.

body.text: (AVParis_31,9.1) darbhārthe tu śarān kuryād ghṛtārthe tailam ucyate | svāhākāre tu phaṭkāro veṇyādyāḥ syuś caturdaśa ||
body.translated_text: Instead of <s>darbha</s> grass, one should use reeds; instead of clarified butter, oil is prescribed; instead of <s>svāhā</s>, the exclamation '<s>phaṭ</s>'; the fourteen [deities] beginning with <s>Veṇī</s> and the rest.

body.text: (AVParis_31,9.2) cāṇḍālāgnau citāgnau vā sūtikāgnāv athāpi vā | hāvayed ghoravṛkṣāṇāṃ samidhas tailasaṃyutāḥ ||
body.translated_text: In a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>'s fire, a cremation fire, or even a fire of childbirth — one should have fuel-sticks of terrible trees offered, mixed with oil.

body.text: (AVParis_31,9.3) raktoṣṇīṣī raktavāsāḥ kṛṣṇāmbaradharo 'pi vā | juhuyād vāmahastena samidho dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Wearing a red turban, red garments, or even black clothing — one should offer fuel-sticks with the left hand, facing south.

body.text: (AVParis_31,9.4) khādirāgnau madhūcchiṣṭe kṛtvā pratikṛtiṃ ripoḥ | tāpayet pratilomāṃ tu sāvitrīṃ manasā japet ||
body.translated_text: In a <s>Khadira</s> (acacia) fire, having made an effigy of the enemy in beeswax, one should heat it while reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> in reverse order mentally.

body.text: (AVParis_31,9.5) kaṇṭhe śūlārpitāṃ kṛtvā tāpayet tu dinedine | yāvac chatrur vaśaṃ yāti vilīnāyāṃ vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: Having impaled it on a trident at the throat, one should heat it day after day; as long as [it takes until] the enemy comes under control — when it melts, he perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_31,10.1) evaṃproktavidhānena koṭihomasya śaṃkaraḥ | prītimān ucyate yena tac chubhaṃ bhautikaṃ dadau ||
body.translated_text: By the procedure thus declared for the <s>koṭi-homa</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) became pleased; by it he gave the auspicious material [gift].

body.text: (AVParis_31,10.2) atharvā bhautikaṃ labdhvā śiṣyebhyas tat punar dadau | śubhaṃ mokṣakaraṃ puṇyaṃ priyaṃ paśupater vratam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_31,10.2) <s>Atharvā</s>, having received the <s>Bhautika</s> [knowledge], gave it again to his disciples — the auspicious, liberation-granting, meritorious, beloved vow of <s>Paśupati</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,10.3) etaj jñātvā tu yaḥ samyak koṭihomaṃ prayojayet | sarvān kāmān avāpnoti brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_31,10.3) He who, knowing this properly, performs the <s>koṭi-homa</s> (ten-million oblations), attains all desires and goes to the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,10.4) yas tv imaṃ śrāvayed vidvān paṭhate caiva sarvadā | koṭihomaphalaṃ labdhvā rudraloke mahīyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_31,10.4) The learned one who causes this to be heard and recites it always — having obtained the fruit of the <s>koṭi-homa</s>, is glorified in the world of <s>Rudra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_31,10.5) gopathāt pāṇineyāya madhye nṝṇāṃ pramodinām | hitārtham uddhṛto granthaḥ koṭihomas tu viśrutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_31,10.5) From the <s>Gopatha</s> [Brāhmaṇa], for the <s>Pāṇineya</s> school, among delighted men — this text, well-known as the <s>Koṭi-homa</s>, was extracted for their benefit.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_32. gaṇamālā)
(AVParis_32,1) oṃ bhūs tat savituḥ śaṃ no devīḥ śāntā dyauḥ śaṃ na indrāgnī śaṃ no vāto vātu uṣā apa svasus tama iti śāntigaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 32: The <s>Gaṇamālā</s> — Garland of Hymn-Groups) (AVParis_32,1) Oṃ. 'Bhūḥ,' 'That of Savitṛ,' 'Auspicious to us, O Goddesses,' 'Peaceful is the sky,' 'Auspicious to us, Indra and Agni,' 'May the wind blow us auspiciousness,' 'Uṣā,' 'Drive away the darkness of the sister' — [this is] the Peace-group (<s>śānti-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,2) kṛtyāpratiharaṇo dūṣyā dūṣir asi īśānāṃ tvā samaṃ jyotir uto asy abandhukṛd ye purastāt suparṇas tvā yāṃ te cakruḥ pratīcīnaphalo yad duṣkṛtam ayaṃ pratisaro yāṃ kalpayantīti kṛtyāpratiharaṇāni || iti kṛtyāgaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,2) [The group] for counteracting sorcery: 'Averter of sorcery,' 'You are the averter of harm, O averter,' 'Equal light of the lords,' 'And you are the kin-maker,' 'Those in front,' 'The eagle you,' 'What they have fashioned,' 'Having fruit turned back,' 'Whatever evil has been done,' 'This is the amulet-cord,' 'What they prepare' — these are the sorcery-counteracting [hymns]. Thus [ends] the Sorcery-group (<s>kṛtyā-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,3) cātanaḥ stuvānam idaṃ havir ye 'māvāsyām upa prāgān niḥsālām arāyakṣayaṇaṃ śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇy ā paśyati tānt satyaujās tvayā pūrvaṃ purastād yukto antardāve juhuta prāgnaye rakṣohaṇam ity anuvākaś cātanāni || iti cātanagaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,3) [The group] for driving away: 'The praiser,' 'This offering,' 'Those at the new-moon,' 'Come forward,' 'Out of the house,' 'Destroyer of demons,' 'Auspicious to us, O goddess Pṛśniparṇī,' 'He who sees those,' 'Truly mighty,' 'By you formerly,' 'United from in front,' 'In a forest-fire,' 'Offer,' 'Forward to Agni,' 'The demon-slaying' hymn-section — [these are] the driving-away [hymns]. Thus [ends] the Driving-away-group (<s>cātana-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,4) mātṛnāmā divyo gandharva ā paśyatīmaṃ me agne yau te māteti mātṛnāmāni || iti mātṛgaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,4) [The group bearing] mother-names: 'The divine Gandharva,' 'He who sees,' 'This [one] to me, O Agni,' 'Who [are] your mother' — these are the mother-name [hymns]. Thus [ends] the Mother-group (<s>mātṛ-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,5) vāstoṣpatīya āśānām āśāpālebhya ihaiva dhruvām ṛdhaṅmantro yonim uta putraḥ pitaram indrasya gṛho 'sīti catasro dive svāhāśamavarma me pṛthivyai śrotrāyeti dhanvānīti dve ūrjaṃ bibhrad iti ṣaṭsatyaṃ bṛhad ity anuvāko vāstoṣpatīyāni || iti vāstugaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,5) [The group] for the Lord of the Dwelling: 'Of the directions,' 'To the guardians of the directions,' 'Here indeed, the firm,' 'The prospering mantra,' 'The womb,' 'And the son [to] the father,' 'This is Indra's house,' the four [beginning] 'To heaven, svāhā,' 'Pacification, armor for me,' 'Of earth,' 'For hearing,' 'Of the bow' — the two; 'Bearing nourishment' — the six; 'Truth, great' — the hymn-section [beginning thus]. These are for the Lord of the Dwelling. Thus [ends] the Dwelling-group (<s>vāstu-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,6) pāpmahā vi devā jarasāvṛtam apa naḥ śośucad agham ava mā pāpmann iti pāpmahā || iti pāpmahā gaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,6) [The group] for destroying sin: 'Apart,' 'O Gods, [remove] the old sin,' 'Remove from us the blazing evil,' 'Remove me, O sin' — [these are] the sin-destroyers. Thus [ends] the Sin-destroying-group (<s>pāpmahā-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,7) takmanāśano jarāyujaḥ prathamo yad agnir ud agātāṃ daśavṛkṣa muñca kṣetriyāt tvā hariṇasya raghuṣyado muñcāmi tvā bhavāśarvau manve vāṃ yo giriṣu dive svāhāgnis takmānam agner ivāsyāva mā pāpmant sṛjāva jyām iva varaṇo vārayātā imaṃ yavaṃ vidradhasya balāsasya namo rūrāyeti dve śīrṣaktiṃ śīrṣāmayam iti takmanāśanāni || iti takmanāśanagaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,7) [The group] for destroying fever: 'Born from the membrane,' 'The first,' 'When Agni rose up,' 'O Ten-Trees,' 'Release,' 'From hereditary [disease],' 'Of the deer's swift one,' 'I release you,' 'Bhava and Śarva,' 'I consider you two,' 'Who is on the mountains,' 'To heaven, svāhā,' 'Agni, the fever,' 'Like Agni's,' 'Remove me, O sin,' 'Release,' 'Like a bowstring from the bow,' 'The Varaṇa repels,' 'This barley,' 'Of abscess,' 'Of phlegmatic disease,' 'Salutation to Rūra' — the two; 'Head-pain,' 'Head-disease' — [these are] the fever-destroyers. Thus [ends] the Fever-destroying-group (<s>takmanāśana-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,8) duḥsvapnanāśanāni dauṣvapnyaṃ daurjīvityaṃ paro 'paihi yo na jīvo 'si pary āvarte duṣvapnyād yat svapne annam aśnami yo na stāyad dipsati yo naḥ suptāṃ jāgrato yan me manso duṣvapnyaṃ kāma svapnaṃ suptvā vidma te svapneti trayaḥ paryāyā duḥsvapnanāśanāni || iti duḥsvapnanāśanagaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,8) [The group] for destroying bad dreams: 'Bad dreams,' 'Evil dream, evil life,' 'Go away!' 'O you who are alive to us,' 'I turn about from bad dreams,' 'Whatever food I eat in a dream,' 'He who [preys on] us sleeping,' 'Of those awake,' 'Whatever bad dream of my mind,' 'O Desire, dream,' 'Having slept, we know your dream' — three sections. [These are] the bad-dream-destroyers. Thus [ends] the Bad-dream-destroying-group (<s>duḥsvapnanāśana-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,9) āyuṣyo yathā dyauḥ prāṇāpānāv ojo 'si tubhyam evākṣībhyāṃ te muñcāmi tvota devā āvatas ta upa priyam antakāya mṛtyava ā rabhasva prāṇāya namo viṣāsahim ity āyuṣyāṇi || iti āyuṣyagaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_32,9) [The group] for long life: 'As the sky,' 'In-breath and out-breath,' 'You are vitality,' 'To you indeed,' 'From your two eyes,' 'I release you,' 'And the gods,' 'Protect you,' 'Toward the beloved,' 'For Death, for Death,' 'Take hold,' 'To life-breath, salutation,' 'O Vanquisher' — [these are] the life-giving [hymns]. Thus [ends] the Long-life-group (<s>āyuṣya-gaṇa</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_32,10) varcasyo ye triṣaptā asmin vasu prātar agniṃ hastivarcasaṃ siṃhe vyāghre yaśo havir yaśasaṃ mendro girāv aragarāṭeṣu yathā somaḥ prātaḥsavane yac ca varco akṣeṣu yena mahānaghnyā jaghanam iti varcasyāni || iti varcasyagaṇaḥ ||
