body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.3.3) Resembling various kinds of smoke, rough, with rays obscured by smoke — one hundred and one, offspring of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), are the <s>Dhūmaketu</s>s (smoke-bannered comets).

body.text: (AVParis_52,3.4) kṛṣṇābhāḥ kṛṣṇaparyantāḥ kaluṣākṛtiraśmayaḥ | rāhoḥ putrās trayas triṃśad grahās tāmasakīlakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.3.4) Dark in appearance, with dark edges, with turbid and dim rays — thirty-three comets, offspring of <s>Rāhu</s>, are the <s>Tāmasakīlaka</s>s (darkness-pegs).

body.text: (AVParis_52,3.5) nānāvarṇāgnisaṃkāśā jvālāmālā visarpiṇaḥ | viśvarūpāḥ sutā agner grahā viṃśaṃ śataṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.3.5) Of various colors, resembling fire, with garlands of flames, spreading — the offspring of <s>Agni</s> (Fire), the <s>Viśvarūpa</s>s (all-formed), are said to be one hundred and twenty comets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,4.1) aruṇās tu sutā vāyor dāruṇāḥ saptasaptatiḥ | vāteritā bhramantīva rūkṣā vikīrṇaraśmayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.4.1) Reddish, offspring of <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), terrible, seventy-seven; driven by the wind, whirling as it were, rough, with scattered rays.

body.text: (AVParis_52,4.2) tārāpuñjapratīkāśās tārāmaṇḍalasaṃvṛtāḥ | prājāpatyā grahās tv aṣṭau gaṇakā nāmanāmataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.4.2) Resembling clusters of stars, surrounded by circles of stars — the <s>Prājāpatya</s> comets (of <s>Prajāpati</s>) are eight, named <s>Gaṇaka</s>s (counters).

body.text: (AVParis_52,4.3) catvāras tārajā yuktāḥ sūkṣmāṇo rūparaśmayaḥ | brahmasaṃtānakā nāma dve śate caturuttare ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.4.3) Four are star-born, joined, minute, with beautiful rays; the <s>Brahmasaṃtānaka</s>s (threads of <s>Brahmā</s>) by name — two hundred and four.

body.text: (AVParis_52,4.4) vaṃśagulmapratīkāśā [vaṃśagulmasaraśmayaḥ] | kākatuṇḍanibhābhiś ca raśmibhiḥ kiṃcid āvṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.4.4) Resembling bamboo thickets, [with rays like bamboo-thicket-rays,] and somewhat covered with rays resembling crow's beaks,

body.text: (AVParis_52,4.5) udakaṃ cotsṛjantīva snigdhatvāt saumyadarśanāḥ | ete nāmnā smṛtāḥ kaṅkās triṃśad dvau vāruṇā grahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.4.5) And releasing water as it were, pleasant to behold from their smoothness — these are known by name as <s>Kaṅka</s>s (herons); thirty-two are <s>Vāruṇa</s> (of <s>Varuṇa</s>) comets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,5.1) muṇḍatārāḥ kabandhābhā rukmakeśāś ca raśmayaḥ | kālaputrāḥ kabandhās te smṛtāḥ ṣaṇṇavatir grahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.5.1) Bald stars, resembling headless trunks, with golden hair-like rays — the offspring of <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the <s>Kabandha</s>s (headless trunks), are known to be ninety-six comets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,5.2) arciṣmāṃś ca prabhāsaś ca romaśo viṣamāṃs tathā | asnigdhāś cātikāyāś ca kiṃśuko rājasāyakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.5.2) <s>Arciṣmān</s> (the Flaming), <s>Prabhāsa</s> (the Luminous), <s>Romaśa</s> (the Hairy), <s>Viṣama</s> (the Uneven) likewise, the Unsmooth, the Enormous, <s>Kiṃśuka</s> (the Parrot-tree), <s>Rājasāyaka</s> (the Royal Arrow),

body.text: (AVParis_52,5.3) ṛṣakaiś caiva rādhātaḥ kumudaḥ phanako ghanaḥ | eṣām aśveti vijñeyā ārās tu parisarpakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.5.3) And <s>Ṛṣaka</s>s, from <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Kumuda</s> (the Lotus), <s>Phanaka</s> (the Hooded one), <s>Ghana</s> (the Dense) — their swift [motion] should be known; the <s>Ārā</s>s are the creeping ones.

body.text: (AVParis_52,5.4) nakṣatracāriṇo hy ete bhṛguputrā mahābalāḥ | pāṇḍurābhiḥ sudīrghābhiḥ śikhābhiḥ śītaraśmayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.5.4) These move through the lunar mansions, offspring of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), of great power, with pale, very long crests, and with cool rays.

body.text: (AVParis_52,5.5) atisaṃtānakāś tv anye ṣaṣṭir vāyoḥ sutā grahāḥ | vikesarāḥ prakāśante kṛṣṇalohitaraśmayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.5.5) The <s>Atisaṃtānaka</s>s (super-threads), others — sixty comets, offspring of <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind); disheveled in appearance, they shine with dark-red rays.

body.text: (AVParis_52,6.1) miśrībhūtās tu te jñeyā guṇṭhitā iva reṇunā | dhūmaketoḥ sutā jñeyāḥ śatam ekādhikaṃ ca tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.6.1) Mixed together, they should be known as covered with dust, as it were; they should be known as offspring of <s>Dhūmaketu</s> (the Smoke-Bannered one) — one hundred and one of them.

body.text: (AVParis_52,6.2) atyarthaṃ kanakās tv anye prataptakanakaprabhāḥ | antakaputrakāḥ ṣaṣṭir asnigdhā madhyacāriṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.6.2) Extremely golden, others, with the radiance of heated gold — the offspring of <s>Antaka</s> (Death), sixty, unsmooth, moving in the middle path.

body.text: (AVParis_52,6.3) ye tu nakṣatravaṃśasya bhāgam uttaram āśritāḥ | ekatārā vapuṣmanto mahākāyāḥ prabhānvitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.6.3) But those that occupy the northern part of the constellation-path, single-starred, beautiful in form, of great size, endowed with radiance,

body.text: (AVParis_52,6.4) vyālakasya tu ye putrāḥ saptaṣaṣṭiḥ samantataḥ | nāmato 'dhikacā nāma tattvajñaiḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.6.4) And those that are offspring of <s>Vyālaka</s> — sixty-seven in all; by name they are called <s>Adhikacā</s>s, as proclaimed by knowers of truth.

body.text: (AVParis_52,6.5) saṃtānakanibhā ye tu dṛśyante sūkṣmaraśmayaḥ | ekatārā dvitārā vā atha vā pañcatārakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.6.5) Those that resemble threads and are seen with faint rays, single-starred or double-starred, or else five-starred,

body.text: (AVParis_52,7.1) brahmarāśes tu te putrā grahāḥ saṃtānasaṃsthitāḥ | saṃcaranti nabhaḥ sarvam utpanne puruṣakṣaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.7.1) Those are offspring of <s>Brahmarāśi</s> (the constellation of <s>Brahmā</s>), comets stationed in continuity; they traverse all of space when the destruction of people arises.

body.text: (AVParis_52,7.2) aṇavo lohitās tv anye prakāśante 'dhikeśakāḥ | pañcaṣaṣṭis tu te jñeyāḥ prājāpatyā grahāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.7.2) Others are minute, reddish, and shine with prominent hair; sixty-five should be known — they are said to be <s>Prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>) comets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,7.3) pariveṣeṣu jāteṣu grahāṇāṃ maṇḍaleṣu ca | dṛśyante kārmukā nāma saptatyekā samāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.7.3) When halos appear around the discs of planets, those seen are named <s>Kārmuka</s>s (bows) — seventy-one, they are said to be of equal [duration].

body.text: (AVParis_52,7.4) adharmasaṃbhavās tv anye caturdaśa parikramāḥ | adhaḥśikhāḥ prakāśante vivarṇā ghoratārakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.7.4) Others born of <s>Adharma</s> (Unrighteousness), fourteen in revolution, with downward-pointing crests, they shine, discolored, with terrible stars.

body.text: (AVParis_52,7.5) karṇachidraprātīkāśāḥ kṛṣṇās te tārakākṛtau | kīlakā rāhuputrās tu candrasūryatalāśrayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.7.5) Resembling perforations in the ear, dark, star-shaped — the <s>Kīlaka</s>s (pegs), offspring of <s>Rāhu</s>, dwelling in the planes of the sun and moon.

body.text: (AVParis_52,8.1) vajraḥ kavandhas triśirāḥ śaṅkhabhedī śikhāvataḥ | daṇḍāś ca rāhuputrāḥ syur nāmabhis tulyavarcasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.8.1) <s>Vajra</s> (Thunderbolt), <s>Kavandha</s> (Headless Trunk), <s>Triśiras</s> (Three-Headed), <s>Śaṅkhabhedin</s> (Conch-Splitter), the crested ones, and <s>Daṇḍa</s>s (Rods) — these are offspring of <s>Rāhu</s>, of brilliance matching their names.

body.text: (AVParis_52,8.2) yathā somārkayor jyoter maṇḍalābhyāśasevinaḥ | rājanyatvāt pradṛśyante prajānāṃ saṃkṣayāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.8.2) Just as those dwelling near the luminous discs of the moon and sun, because of their regal nature, become visible and bring destruction to the people,

body.text: (AVParis_52,8.3) tatra mandaphalā jñeyāḥ śaśāṅkatalasevinaḥ | divākaratalābhyāśaṃ sevino bhṛśadāruṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.8.3) Among them, those dwelling in the plane of the moon should be known as having mild effects; those dwelling near the plane of the sun are exceedingly terrible.

body.text: (AVParis_52,8.4) pannagās tu caturviṃśat kṛṣṇā dvātriṃśatir grahāḥ | dakṣiṇādyāsu vīkṣyante nīcair vibhrāntamaṇḍalāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.8.4) The <s>Pannaga</s>s (serpents) are twenty-four; the dark [comets] are thirty-two; they are seen in the southern and other [paths], moving low with wandering orbits.

body.text: (AVParis_52,8.5) kevalaṃ tārakākārā dṛśyante niḥprabhaprabhāḥ | pītaraktā grahāḥ pañca pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.8.5) Merely star-shaped in appearance, seen with lustreless radiance, five comets, yellowish-red, are recorded in the southeast.

body.text: (AVParis_52,9.1) dakṣiṇāparataś cāpi pītaraktau grahau smṛtau | uttarāparatas tv ekaḥ pītarakto grahaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.9.1) And in the southwest also, two comets are recorded as yellowish-red; in the northwest, one yellowish-red comet is recorded.

body.text: (AVParis_52,9.2) aiśānyāṃ śvetaraktābha ekas tiṣṭhati sūryakaḥ | yaḥ saṃdhivelāsv arkābho dikṣu sarvāsu dṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.9.2) In the northeast, one white-reddish one stands, called <s>Sūryaka</s> (sun-like); it appears sun-like at the twilight junctions in all directions.

body.text: (AVParis_52,9.3) nātidūre raveḥ snigdhaḥ sa varṣāyābhayāya ca | yavakrītoṣaraibhyāś ca nāradaḥ sarvatas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.9.3) Not too far from the sun, smooth, it is [a sign] of rainfall and of safety. <s>Yavakrīta</s>, <s>Uṣaraibhya</s>s, and <s>Nārada</s> everywhere likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_52,9.4) karṇaś ca raibhyasya putrau cārvāvasuparāvasū | saptaite sthāvarā jñeyāḥ saha sūryeṇa sarpiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.9.4) <s>Karṇa</s> and the two sons of <s>Raibhya</s> — <s>Cārvāvasu</s> and <s>Parāvasu</s> — these seven should be known as stationary [comets], moving along with the sun.

body.text: (AVParis_52,9.5) sthāvarāṇāṃ narendrāṇāṃ prācyānāṃ pakṣam āśritāḥ | svastyātreyo mṛgavyādha ṛmucuḥ pramṛcus tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.9.5) Those stationary ones, belonging to the eastern quarter of the lords of men — <s>Svastyātreya</s>, <s>Mṛgavyādha</s> (the Deer-Hunter), <s>Ṛmucu</s>, and <s>Pramṛcu</s> likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_52,10.1) prabhāsaś candrabhāsaś ca tathāgastyaḥ pratāpavān | dṛḍhavratas triśaṅkuś ca ajau vaiśvānare mṛḍaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.10.1) <s>Prabhāsa</s> and <s>Candrabhāsa</s>, and the powerful <s>Agastya</s>; <s>Dṛḍhavrata</s> (Firm-in-Vow) and <s>Triśaṅku</s>, in [the constellations] <s>Aja</s> and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Mṛḍa</s>,

body.text: (AVParis_52,10.2) aruṇaś ca danuś caiva yāmyāyāṃ sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ | gautamo 'trir vasiṣṭhaś ca viśvāmitras tu kaśyapaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.10.2) And <s>Aruṇa</s> and <s>Danu</s> — these are the stationary [comets] in the southern quarter. <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

body.text: (AVParis_52,10.3) ṛcīkaputraś ca tathā bharadvājaś ca vīryavān | ete sapta mahātmāna udīcyāṃ sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.10.3) And the son of <s>Ṛcīka</s>, and the mighty <s>Bharadvāja</s> — these seven great souls are remembered as the fixed [stars] in the northern [sky].

body.text: (AVParis_52,10.4) śiśumāreṇa sahitā dhruveṇa ca mahātmanā | pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ somo bhṛgur aṅgirasā saha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.10.4) Together with the Dolphin constellation (<s>Śiśumāra</s>) and the great-souled Pole Star (<s>Dhruva</s>): <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, together with <s>Aṅgiras</s>,

body.text: (AVParis_52,10.5) hāhāhūhū ca vijñeyau viṣṇoś ca padam uttamam | madhyāntasthāvarāṇāṃ tu niyatāv iti buddhimān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.10.5) and <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s> should be known, as well as the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the wise one [knows] that those fixed [stars] at the center and ends are bound [in their courses].

body.text: (AVParis_52,11.1) kūṭasthānāni sarvāṇi dikṣv etāny upadhārayet | prabhānvitāni śvetāni snigdhāni vimalāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.11.1) One should observe all these summit-positions in the [various] directions — endowed with radiance, white, unctuous, and clear,

body.text: (AVParis_52,11.2) arciṣmanti prasannāni tāni kuryuḥ prajāhitam | niḥprabhāṇi vivarṇāni nirarcīmṣy amalāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.11.2) blazing and serene — those bring welfare to the people. [Those that are] without radiance, discolored, without flames, and dull,

body.text: (AVParis_52,11.3) hrasvāny asnehayuktāni na bhāvāya bhavanti hi | yat kiṃcit sthāvaraṃ loke tat prasanneṣu vardhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.11.3) small and lacking unctuousness — these indeed do not lead to prosperity. Whatever is fixed in the world flourishes when [the summit-stars] are serene;

body.text: (AVParis_52,11.4) kūṭastheṣv aprasanneṣu sthāvaraṃ parihīyate | ādityaś caiva śukraś ca lohitāṅgas tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.11.4) when the summit-stars are disturbed, the fixed [order] declines. The Sun, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars, the Red-Bodied),

body.text: (AVParis_52,11.5) rāhuḥ somaḥ śanaiścaro bṛhaspatibudhau tathā | aindra āgneyo yāmyaś ca nairṛto vāruṇas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.11.5) <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) likewise; [the directional planets:] that of <s>Indra</s> (east), of <s>Agni</s> (southeast), of <s>Yama</s> (south), of <s>Nirṛti</s> (southwest), of <s>Varuṇa</s> (west),

body.text: (AVParis_52,12.1) vāyavyaś caiva saumyaś ca brāhmaś caivāṣṭamo grahaḥ | navamaś caiva vijñeyo dhūmaketur mahāgrahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.12.1) of <s>Vāyu</s> (northwest), of <s>Soma</s> (north), and the eighth is that of <s>Brahmā</s> (zenith); and the ninth should be known as the great planet <s>Dhūmaketu</s> (Comet).

body.text: (AVParis_52,12.2) yugagrahā na cānye te tatrāṣṭau diggrahāḥ smṛtāḥ | sanakṣatreṣu mārgeṣu dṛśyante tu yugagrahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.12.2) The age-planets (<s>yugagraha</s>s) are not others; among them, eight are remembered as directional planets. The age-planets are seen on paths [marked] with <s>nakṣatra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_52,12.3) vibhrāntamaṇḍalāḥ śeṣā dṛśyante khacarā grahaḥ | mṛtyor niśvāsajāś cānye jñeyāḥ ṣoḍaśa ketavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.12.3) The remaining sky-roaming planets are seen with disturbed orbits; and the sixteen <s>ketu</s>s (comets) born from the breath of Death should be known.

body.text: (AVParis_52,12.4) kūṣmāṇḍavad visaṃchannas triṇavā dakṣiṇe pathi | ekādaśaiva vijñeyā dvādaśādityasaṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.12.4) Concealed like <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>s (gourds), three groups of nine on the southern path; eleven should be known, and twelve are born from the Sun.

body.text: (AVParis_52,12.5) sūryavarcanirīkṣās te tejodhātumayā grahāḥ | dakṣayajñe tu rudrasya krodhād anye tu niḥsṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.12.5) They have the appearance of the Sun's splendor — those planets made of the essence of light. Others issued from the wrath of <s>Rudra</s> at <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.

body.text: (AVParis_52,13.1) bhīmarūpā daśaikaś ca jvalāṅkuśadharā grahāḥ | sapta paitāmahās tv anye tiryaggā jarjaragrahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.13.1) Eleven of terrifying form, bearing flaming goads — [these are] planets; seven others, of <s>Pitāmaha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), move obliquely — the tattered (<s>jarjara</s>) planets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,13.2) śikhāḥ sṛjanto vitatās tantuśuklapaṭopamāḥ | śvetaketava ity anye vyākhyātā daśa pañca ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.13.2) Emitting extended crests, resembling white cloth threads — the 'White Comets' (<s>śvetaketu</s>s), fifteen others, are described.

body.text: (AVParis_52,13.3) uddālakarṣiputrās te nīcair vibhrāntamaṇḍalāḥ | te syuḥ śvetaśikhāḥ sarve saumyāḥ kāntās tanuprabhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.13.3) They are the sons of the sage <s>Uddālaka</s>, with low disturbed orbits; they all have white crests, are gentle, beautiful, and of slender radiance.

body.text: (AVParis_52,13.4) aṣṭādaśendunā sārdhaṃ mathyamāne purāmṛte | ketavaḥ kundapuṣpābhāḥ kṣīrodanabhasi smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.13.4) Eighteen, together with the Moon, [appeared] when the <s>Amṛta</s> (nectar) was churned of old — comets resembling <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, remembered [as appearing] in the sky of the Milk Ocean.

body.text: (AVParis_52,13.5) viraśmayaś ca viśikhā mahākāyā nirarciṣaḥ | raupyakumbhanibhāḥ saumyā grahāḥ syuḥ śītatejasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.13.5) Without rays, without crests, of great bodies, without flames, resembling silver pitchers, gentle — [these] planets are of cool splendor.

body.text: (AVParis_52,14.1) brahmakopamayas tv eko viśvātmā sarvato grahaḥ | caturyugānte lokānām udayas tasya vidyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.14.1) But one [comet], born of <s>Brahman</s>'s wrath, is the universal Self, a planet [appearing] everywhere; its rising occurs at the end of a four-age cycle (<s>caturyuga</s>) for the [destruction of] the worlds.

body.text: (AVParis_52,14.2) nakṣatrapatham utsṛjya nabhoaṃśāḥ pārśvacāriṇaḥ | pūrvato 'bhyuditā vā syur nīcair uttaratas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.14.2) Having left the path of the <s>nakṣatra</s>s, [those that are] portions of the sky and side-moving — they may rise from the east or [appear] low from the north;

body.text: (AVParis_52,14.3) bhūmyām abhyuditā vā syur hrasvasnehapariplutāḥ | sarva eva tu vijñeyā grahā mandaphalodayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.14.3) or they may rise from the earth, flooded with scant unctuousness — all such planets should be known as yielding slow results.

body.text: (AVParis_52,14.4) sarveṣāṃ paitṛkaṃ karma prajābhāgyodbhavaṃ mahat | sarve te sarvato hanyur aśubhaṃ yad vadanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.14.4) For all of them, the ancestral rite (<s>paitṛka karma</s>) produces great fortune for progeny; all of them would destroy inauspiciousness on all sides — so they declare.

body.text: (AVParis_52,14.5) tatkarmajanmamāhātmyaṃ śīlābhijanam eva ca | tadrūpāṃs tadguṇāṃś cāpi tanmayāṃs tatparigrahān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.14.5) [One should know] the greatness of the deeds and birth [of each comet], its character, noble lineage, its corresponding forms, qualities, constituents, and associations.

body.text: (AVParis_52,15.1) sarva eva rogapradā mṛtyuśastrāgnitaskaraiḥ | paśusasyopaghātaiś ca hanyur anyaiś ca kāraṇaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.15.1) All are indeed disease-producing — through death, weapons, fire, and thieves, through destruction of cattle and crops, they afflict, and by other causes as well.

body.text: (AVParis_52,15.2) dhūpanāt sparśanāt sthānād udayāstamasaṃbhavāt | hanyuḥ pañcavidhaṃ sarve ketavo nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.15.2) By fumigation, contact, position, and from rising and setting — the comets afflict in five ways; there is no doubt in this.

body.text: (AVParis_52,15.3) mṛdudhruvograkṣipreṣu sādhāraṇacareṣu ca | dāruṇeṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu sādhāraṇacareṣu ca | dāruṇeṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu vidyāt tatsadṛśaṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.15.3) In mild, fixed, fierce, and swift [<s>nakṣatra</s>s], in those of common movement, and in terrible asterisms — one should know the result to be corresponding [to those characteristics].

body.text: (AVParis_52,15.4) yathādiṣṭaṃ yathāvarṇaṃ yathāvargaparigraham | sarva evoditā hanyuḥ sarva eva mahāgrahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.15.4) As indicated, according to color, according to the class-association — all [comets] when risen would afflict; all are indeed great planets.

body.text: (AVParis_52,15.5) mṛtyoḥ kālasya sūryasya brahmaṇas tryambakasya ca | bhaumasya rāhor agneś ca prajātā ye sudāruṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.15.5) Those born from Death, Time, the Sun, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Agni</s> are extremely terrible.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.1) prajāpateś ca dharmasya somasya varuṇasya ca | pītādyāś ca diśāṃ putrā vijñeyā mṛdudāruṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.1) Those [born] from <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, and those yellow and other [colored] sons of the directions — should be known as mild-to-terrible.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.2) kaśyapasya ca marīcer uddālakaṛṣes tathā | putrā mandaphalā jñeyās teṣām amṛtasaṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.2) The sons of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, and the sage <s>Uddālaka</s> — should be known as yielding mild results; [they are] of <s>Amṛta</s> (nectar) origin.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.3) śukrādīnāṃ ca ye putrā grahāṇāṃ parikīrtitāḥ | teṣāṃ vīryāṇi jāniyāt pitṛbhyaḥ sādhikāni tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.3) And those that are declared as the sons of the planets beginning with <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) — one should know their powers to be even greater than those of their fathers.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.4) nāradātreyagargāṇāṃ guror uśanasas tathā | grahāṇāṃ saṃgraho hy evam eṣa kārtsnyena kīrtitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.4) This collection of planets, according to <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Atreya</s>, <s>Garga</s>, the preceptor, and <s>Uśanas</s> (Venus), has thus been proclaimed in its entirety.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.5) anekaśatasāhasra anekaśatalakṣaṇaḥ | devalabdhavarākāśe prāha sarvān pṛthakpṛthak ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.5) [The collection is] of many hundreds of thousands, with many hundreds of characteristics; [the sage], having obtained a boon in the divine sky, declared them all separately.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.6) etadutthe tu sarvasmin bhaye 'tha samupasthite | mahāśāntiṃ prakurvīta rājā rāṣṭrasya rakṣaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.6) When all such danger arises from these [comets], the king should perform the <s>Mahāśānti</s> (Great Pacification) rite for the protection of the kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_52,16.7) tat prayāti śamaṃ sarvaṃ prajānāṃ tu sukhaṃ bhavet | rājāno muditās tatra pālayanti vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 52.16.7) All that disturbance subsides, and there shall be happiness for the people; kings, rejoicing there, protect the earth.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_53. rāhucāraḥ)
(AVParis_53,1.1) om upetya yaś candramasaṃ raviṃ vā gṛhṇāti sūnor asurasya putraḥ | nibodhataitasya śubhāśubhāni grahasya mṛtyoḥ praticeṣṭitāni ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 53: <s>Rāhu</s>'s Course [Eclipse Omens]) (AVParis 53.1.1) Oṃ. The son of the demon's son (<s>Rāhu</s>), having approached the Moon or the Sun, seizes [them]. Learn of this planet of Death — its auspicious and inauspicious activities.

body.text: (AVParis_53,1.2) yadā tu rāhuḥ śaśino raver <vā> [grahe] grahītukāmo bhavati prasahya | tadā karoty adbhutadarśanāni yair jñāyate rāhur upaiṣyatīti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.1.2) When <s>Rāhu</s> desires to seize the Moon or the Sun by force, then it produces marvelous portents by which it is known that <s>Rāhu</s> is approaching.

body.text: (AVParis_53,1.3) udvepate tadā candro yadā rāhuḥ pradṛśyate || pāṇḍur vā jāyate klībaḥ śaśo vāsya vivardhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.1.3) The Moon then trembles when <s>Rāhu</s> is sighted; or [the Moon] becomes pale and weak, or the hare [mark on] it increases.

body.text: (AVParis_53,1.4) rekhāntarāpurārāṇi kalmaṣāṇi divākare | vadanti ca bhaṛśaṃ śvāno vānti vātāś ca bhīṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.1.4) Marks, spots, and blemishes [appear] between the lines on the Sun; dogs bark excessively, and terrifying winds blow.

body.text: (AVParis_53,1.5) saṃdhyayor ubhayoś colkā gavāṃ prakṣīyate payaḥ | kṣīriṇām aiva vṛkṣāṇāṃ tad ahar naśyate payaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.1.5) Meteors [appear] at both twilights; the milk of cows diminishes; even for milk-bearing trees, the sap perishes on that day.

body.text: (AVParis_53,2.1) apsu snigdhāni dṛśyante kākābadhnanti maṇḍalam | ūrdhvaṃ vadati gomāyur yadā rāhuḥ pradṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.2.1) Unctuous [reflections] are seen in the waters; crows form a circle; the jackal howls upward when <s>Rāhu</s> is sighted.

body.text: (AVParis_53,2.2) candragrahanimittāni śuklapakśāṣṭamīparam | ā paurṇamāsyā dṛśyeran sūryasya ca tathobhayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.2.2) The omens of the Moon's eclipse may be seen from the eighth of the bright fortnight up to the full moon, and likewise for the Sun's [eclipse], on both [occasions].

body.text: (AVParis_53,2.3) udito gṛhyamāṇas tu hanti vedavido janān | bālāṃś ca jaṭilān hanti ye ca kāṣāyavāsasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.2.3) When [the luminary] is seized while rising, it slays those who know the <s>Veda</s>s; it also slays the young, the matted-haired [ascetics], and those wearing ochre robes.

body.text: (AVParis_53,2.4) yauvanasthāṃś ca pūrvāhṇe hanti yajñavido janān | audakāni ca sarvāṇi nāgendrāś cātra duḥkhitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.2.4) In the forenoon, it slays those in their prime and those who know the sacrifices; all aquatic [creatures] too [suffer], and the great serpents (<s>Nāgendra</s>s) are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_53,2.5) atha madhyapathaṃ prāptaḥ śūdrān hanti ca taskarān | parivṛkto nṛpaṃ hanti candraś caraṇacāraṇān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.2.5) When [<s>Rāhu</s>] has reached the mid-path, it slays <s>Śūdra</s>s and thieves; when [the Moon is] surrounded, it slays the king; [when] the Moon [is released], wandering performers and bards.

body.text: (AVParis_53,3.1) pralambaḥ pramadān hanti kṣatraṃ rāṣṭraṃ ca sarvaśaḥ | traigartāś cātra pīḍyante ye ca daṇḍabhṛto janāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.3.1) When drooping (<s>pralamba</s>), it slays women, and the warrior class and the kingdom entirely; the <s>Trigarta</s>s are afflicted there, as well as those who bear the rod of punishment.

body.text: (AVParis_53,3.2) uparakto yadodeti yadā vā pratitiṣṭhati | ayogakṣemam ādiśyet triṣu lokeṣu dāruṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.3.2) When [the luminary] rises eclipsed or when it sets [still eclipsed], one should predict terrible insecurity in the three worlds.

body.text: (AVParis_53,3.3) śāradaṃ trīṇi varṣāṇi sasyaṃ jātaṃ na pacyate | naidāghenātra jīvanti prajā mūlaphalena vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.3.3) For three autumnal years, the crop, though sprouted, does not ripen; the people survive by summer [foraging] or on roots and fruits.

body.text: (AVParis_53,3.4) sarvaṃ saṃgrasate jyotiś ciram antardadhāti vā | hanti sphītāni rāṣṭrāṇi pradhānaṃ ca mahīpatim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.3.4) [If <s>Rāhu</s>] swallows all the light or conceals it for a long time, it slays prosperous kingdoms and the chief sovereign.

body.text: (AVParis_53,3.5) yadi <tu> rāhur ubhau śaśibhāskarau grasati pakṣam anantaram antataḥ | puruṣaśoṇitakardamavāhinī bhavati bhūr na ca varṣati mādhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.3.5) If <s>Rāhu</s> swallows both the Moon and the Sun in the very next fortnight, in succession, the earth flows with streams of human blood and mud, and <s>Mādhava</s> (spring) does not rain.

body.text: (AVParis_53,4.1) gṛhītvā bhāskaraṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhṇāti śaśinaṃ yadi | taṃ tu somottaraṃ nāśas tatra rdhyante hi devatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.4.1) If, having first seized the Sun, [<s>Rāhu</s>] then seizes the Moon — that [eclipse] with the Moon following [means] destruction; but thereby the deities prosper.

body.text: (AVParis_53,4.2) vayasāṃ maraṇaṃ chidre prakīrṇe rakṣasāṃ vadhaḥ | nāgānāṃ tu mahānāge chidre devo na varṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.4.2) In a partial [eclipse], there is death of birds; in a scattered [eclipse], slaughter of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s; [if it occurs] in the Great Serpent [<s>nakṣatra</s>], [it portends harm] for <s>Nāga</s>s; in a partial [eclipse], the god does not rain.

body.text: (AVParis_53,4.3) śveto varṇo brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu lohitaḥ | vaiśyānāṃ pītako varṇaḥ śūdrāṇāṃ kṛṣṇa ucyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.4.3) White is the color of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, red is [the color] of <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, yellow is the color of <s>Vaiśya</s>s, and dark is said [to be the color] of <s>Śūdra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_53,4.4) eteṣāṃ yena varṇena rāhuś carati bhāskare | yā jātis tasya varṇasya tāṃ sa pīḍayate grahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.4.4) By whichever color <s>Rāhu</s> moves across the Sun — the caste corresponding to that color is the one that planet afflicts.

body.text: (AVParis_53,4.5) śyāmo bhavati vātāya draukṣo bhavati vṛṣṭaye | haridraḥ sarvadhānyānāṃ kopaṃ sṛjati dāruṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.4.5) [If] dark, it portends wind; [if] coppery, it portends rain; [if] turmeric-colored, it produces a terrible calamity for all grains.

body.text: (AVParis_53,5.1) tāmro bhavati śastrāya śastrāya rūkṣo bhavati mṛtyave | bahvākāras tu bhūtānāṃ ghoraṃ janayate jvaram ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.5.1) [If] copper-colored, it portends weapons; [if] rough, it portends death; [if] of many forms, it generates a terrible fever among beings.

body.text: (AVParis_53,5.2) dhūmavarṇo 'gnivarṇo vā grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā | agnyutpātān gṛhasthānāṃ karotīha mahāgrahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.5.2) [If] smoke-colored or fire-colored, whether in villages or cities — the great planet causes fire-calamities for householders.

body.text: (AVParis_53,5.3) nīlalohitaparyanto rāhuś carati bhāskare | amātyo hanti rājānaṃ rājā vāmātyam ātmaha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.5.3) When <s>Rāhu</s>, with dark-red borders, moves across the Sun — a minister slays the king, or the king [slays] his own minister, self-destructively.

body.text: (AVParis_53,5.4) yasya rājñaś ca nakṣatre svarbhānur uparajyati | rājyabhraṃśaṃ suhṛnnāśaṃ maraṇaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.5.4) In whichever king's <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) causes an eclipse, one should predict loss of kingdom, destruction of allies, and death.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.1) snigdhavarṇo yadārciṣmān parvasthaḥ snehavān grahaḥ | kṣipraṃ vāpy uditaṃ brūhi sarvabhūtabhayāya vai ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.1) When [the eclipsing planet] is of unctuous color, blazing, stationed at the eclipse-point, unctuous — or declare it risen swiftly — indeed, [it bodes] fear for all beings.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.2) pradakṣiṇe tu somasya apasavye tu vigrahaḥ | raśmibhede bhayaṃ ghoram ullekhe mantriṇāṃ vadhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.2) On the right side of <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) [there is prosperity]; on the left, conflict; in the splitting of rays, terrible danger; in a scraping [eclipse], the slaughter of ministers.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.3) darśayitvā tu rūpāṇi yadā rāhur na dṛśyate | śastradurbhikṣasaṃpātair bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.3) When, having displayed its forms, <s>Rāhu</s> becomes invisible, one should predict terrible danger through weapons, famine, and calamities.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.4) gṛhītāstamitayos tu na bhuñjīran dvijātayaḥ | ā punardarśanāt tābhyāṃ japahomau vivartayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.4) While [the luminaries are] seized and set, the twice-born should not eat; until the re-sighting of those two [luminaries], one should continue <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation) and <s>homa</s> (fire oblation).

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.5) candrasūryagrahe nādyād adyāt snātvā tu muktayoḥ | amuktayor astaṃgayor adyāt snātvā pare 'hani ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.5) During a lunar or solar eclipse, one should not eat; one may eat after bathing when they are released. If not released when they set, one should eat after bathing on the following day.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.6) tataḥ ṣaṭsu tataḥ ṣaṭsu tato 'dhyardheṣū vā punaḥ | ardhavarṣeṣu māseṣu ādityasya tato grahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.6) Then after six [months], then after six [more], or then after one and a half [years] again; after half-years and months — thereafter is the Sun's eclipse.

body.text: (AVParis_53,6.7) tataḥ ṣaṭsu tataḥ ṣaṭsu triṣu varṣeṣu vā punaḥ | etāvad eva rāhos tu cāram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 53.6.7) Then after six [months], then after six [more], or after three years again — the wise declare this to be the extent of <s>Rāhu</s>'s course.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_54. ketucārāḥ)
(AVParis_54,1.1) oṃ bhārgavas tu purovāca maharṣīn bhagavān ṛṣiḥ | ketusaṃcāraṃ śṛṇuta utthānaṃ caiva yādṛśam ||
body.translated_text: (Pariśiṣṭa 54: Courses of the Comets [<s>Ketucāra</s>]) (AVParis 54.1.1) Oṃ. The blessed sage <s>Bhārgava</s> (of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s lineage) formerly spoke to the great sages: 'Hear of the course of comets and the manner of their rising.'

body.text: (AVParis_54,1.2) nimittani ca vakṣyāmitasyoktāni hi yāni tu | tāni sarvāṇi jāniyād utpātajñānakovidaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.1.2) 'I shall speak of the omens that have been declared for them; one skilled in the knowledge of portents should know them all.'

body.text: (AVParis_54,1.3) viprāñ śvetākṛtir hanti kṣatriyān hanti lohitaḥ | vaiśyāṃs tu pītako hanti śūdrān hanti tathāsitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.1.3) A white-formed [comet] slays <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; a red one slays <s>Kṣatriya</s>s; a yellow one slays <s>Vaiśya</s>s; a dark one likewise slays <s>Śūdra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_54,1.4) itarān pīḍayet ketur anyavarṇo yadā bhavet | ṣaṇmāsābhyantare rājño maraṇaṃ ca tadādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.1.4) When a comet becomes of a different color, it afflicts the others; and within six months, it should predict the death of a king.

body.text: (AVParis_54,1.5) śvetaḥ śastrākulaṃ kuryāl lohitas tv agnito bhayam. kṣudbhayaṃ pītakaḥ kuryāt kṛṣṇo rogam atholbaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.1.5) A white [comet] causes disturbance by weapons; a red one, fear from fire; a yellow one causes fear of famine; a black one, terrible disease.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.1) yasmin deśe śiras tasya sa deśaḥ pīḍyate bhṛśam | madhye tu madhyamā pīḍā yato pucchaṃ tato jayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.1) In whichever region its head [points], that region is severely afflicted; in the middle [there is] moderate affliction; from wherever the tail [points], there is victory.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.2) śaktyākāro 'tināśāya duḥkhāya musalākṛtiḥ | dīrghaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sukhāyaiva hrasvaḥ sthūlo vināśakṛt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.2) A spear-shaped [comet portends] utter destruction; a pestle-shaped one, suffering; one that is long and thin [portends] happiness indeed; one that is short and thick causes destruction.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.3) utthānaṃ caiva ketūnāṃ vināśāyaiva hi smṛtam | tasmād ātharvaṇair mantraiḥ śamanam ārayed budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.3) The rising of comets is remembered as portending destruction indeed; therefore, the wise one should undertake pacification with <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> mantras.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.4) māhendrūn anṛtān raydrūn vauśvadevīm athāpi vā | utpāteṣu mahāśāntiṃ kārayed bahudakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.4) [One should perform] the <s>Māhendrī</s>, <s>Anṛtā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, or <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> [rites]; in [times of] portents, one should have the great pacification (<s>Mahāśānti</s>) performed with abundant gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.5) ārādhitāḥ śamaṃ yānti tadutpātā na saṃśayaḥ | homair japyaiś ca vividhair dānaiś cabahurūpakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.5) When propitiated, those portents go to peace — there is no doubt; through oblations, various recitations, and gifts of many kinds.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.6) tasya yatra śiro deśe tata utthāya vāvrajet | dhanaṃ vā sarvam utsṛjya mṛtyor mucyetā vā na vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.6) From whichever region its head [points], one should rise up from there and depart; or abandoning all wealth, one may or may not be freed from death.

body.text: (AVParis_54,2.7) dattvā vā pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ rājā śāntiṃ niyacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 54.2.7) Or, having given away the entire earth, a king attains peace.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_55. ṛtuketulakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_55,1.1) om ṛtuketūn pravakṣyāmi yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ | yāvanto yasya putrāḥ syuḥ kuryur yac coditā divi ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 55: Characteristics of Seasonal Comets) (AVParis 55.1.1) Oṃ. I shall declare the seasonal comets (<s>ṛtuketu</s>s) properly and in order — how many sons each has, and what they produce when they rise in the sky.

body.text: (AVParis_55,1.2) sarve te dharaṇījātā māsā ye devanirmitāḥ | ādityaraśmibhir baddhāḥ saure tiṣṭhanti maṇḍale ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.2) All those [comets] born on earth, which are months fashioned by the gods, bound by the rays of the sun, stand in the solar circle.

body.text: (AVParis_55,1.3) daśa vai vāruṇās tatra sūryaputrās tu viṃśatiḥ | caturviṃśatir āgneyā yamaputrā nava smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.3) Ten indeed are of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and twenty are sons of the Sun; twenty-four are of <s>Agni</s> (fire), and nine are remembered as sons of <s>Yama</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,1.4) aṣṭādaśa ca kauberā vāyuputrās tu viṃśatiḥ | eṣā saṃkhyā tu ketūnāṃ śatam ekottaraṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.4) Eighteen are of <s>Kubera</s>, and twenty are sons of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); this count of comets is remembered as one hundred and one.

body.text: (AVParis_55,1.5) śrāvaṇaprauṣṭhapadayor vāruṇāṃs tu vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.5) In [the months of] <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> and <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s> (Bhādrapada), one should specify those of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

body.text:
(AVParis_55,1.6) [ārādhitāḥ śamaṃ yānti tadutpātā na saṃśayaḥ | homair jāpaiś ca vividhair dānaiś ca bahurūpakaiḥ ||]
(AVParis_55,1.7) āvāhayet tato meghān pūrṇāṃ kuryād vasuṃdharām | unmattāḥ sarito yānti jalavegasamāhitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.6-7) [When propitiated, those portents go to peace — there is no doubt; through oblations, various recitations, and gifts of many kinds.] One should then invoke the rain-clouds and make the earth full; the rivers flow wildly, propelled by the force of water.

body.text: (AVParis_55,1.8) dhānyaṃ samarghatāṃ yāti ītayo na bhavanti hi udaye vāruṇānāṃ tu etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.1.8) Grain attains proper price, and calamities do not arise — this is the characteristic at the rising of [comets] of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,2.1) aśvayuji kārttike ca sūryaputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.2.1) In <s>Aśvayuj</s> (Āśvina) and <s>Kārttika</s>, one should specify the sons of the Sun; hear their effects and by what characteristics [they manifest].

body.text: (AVParis_55,2.2) tato dahati dīptāṃśuḥ sarvānnāni divākaraḥ | mriyante ca tathā gāvaḥ śvāpadāś ca viśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.2.2) Then the brilliant-rayed sun burns all foodstuffs; and cows die likewise, and wild beasts especially.

body.text: (AVParis_55,2.3) viṣaṃ ca prabalaṃ tatra sarvadamṣṭriṣu dāruṇam | udaye sūryaputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.2.3) And there the venom is powerful and terrible among all fanged creatures — this is the characteristic at the rising of the sons of the Sun.

body.text: (AVParis_55,3.1) mārgaśīrṣe ca pauṣe ca agniputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.3.1) In <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Pauṣa</s>, one should specify the sons of <s>Agni</s> (fire); hear their effects and by what characteristics [they manifest].

body.text: (AVParis_55,3.2) agnir dahati rāṣṭrāṇi haritāni vanāni ca vidravanti tato deśāḥ samantād bhayapīḍitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.3.2) Fire burns the kingdoms and the green forests; thereupon regions flee on all sides, afflicted by fear.

body.text: (AVParis_55,3.3) kasmiṃś cij jāyate kṣemaṃ kasmiṃś cij jāyate bhayam | udaye hy agniputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.3.3) In some [places] prosperity arises, in some fear arises — this is the characteristic at the rising of the sons of <s>Agni</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,4.1) māghaphālbunayor madhye yamaputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.4.1) Between <s>Māgha</s> and <s>Phālguna</s>, one should specify the sons of <s>Yama</s>; hear their effects and by what characteristics [they manifest].

body.text: (AVParis_55,4.2) śīghraṃ bhavati durbhikṣaṃ hāhābhūtam acetanam | chardijvarātisārāś ca glāniś caivākṣivedanā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.4.2) Swiftly there occurs famine, with [people] crying 'Alas! Alas!', senseless; vomiting, fever, dysentery, and exhaustion, along with eye-disease.

body.text: (AVParis_55,4.3) udaye yamaputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.4.3) This is the characteristic at the rising of the sons of <s>Yama</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,5.1) caitravaiśākhayor madhye kauberāṃs tu vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.5.1) Between <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaiśākha</s>, one should specify those of <s>Kubera</s>; hear their effects and by what characteristics [they manifest].

body.text: (AVParis_55,5.2) ucchritair dhvajavedībhir ucchritair dhvajatoraṇaiḥ | havirdhūmākulā tatra dṛśyate vasudhā tadā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.5.2) With raised banners and altars, with raised banners and arched gateways, the earth is then seen filled with the smoke of oblations.

body.text: (AVParis_55,5.3) triviṣṭapaṃ samāpannas tadā śakro mahīpatiḥ | evaṃ prajñās tu manyante kubere graham āgate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.5.3) <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the lord of the earth, then attains heaven; thus the wise understand when the planet enters [the domain of] <s>Kubera</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,5.4) udaye tu kuberāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.5.4) This is the characteristic at the rising of [comets] of <s>Kubera</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,6.1) jyaiṣṭhe caiva tathāṣāḍhe vāyuputrān vinirdiśet | teṣāṃ caiva tu karmāṇi lakṣaṇaiḥ śṛṇu yādṛśaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.6.1) In <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s> and <s>Āṣāḍha</s> likewise, one should specify the sons of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); hear their effects and by what characteristics [they manifest].

body.text: (AVParis_55,6.2) vāyanti ca mahāvātā mahāyuddhaṃ mahābhayam | bhajyante ca mahāvṛkṣās toraṇāṭṭālakāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.6.2) Great winds blow, [there is] great war and great fear; great trees are broken, and arched gateways and watchtowers likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_55,6.3) gṛhāṇi rāmaṇīyāni kṣayaṃ yānti jalāni ca | udaye vāyuputrāṇām etad bhavati lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.6.3) Beautiful houses are ruined, and waters diminish — this is the characteristic at the rising of the sons of <s>Vāyu</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_55,6.4) ṛtugatam udayanam eṣāṃ mahaujasāṃ vāruṇādiketūnām | jānāti yaḥ phalaṃ ca protkṛṣṭāḥ saṃpadas tasya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 55.6.4) He who knows the seasonal rising and the fruit of these mighty comets of <s>Varuṇa</s> and the rest — excellent prosperity is his.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_56. kūrmavibhāgaḥ)
(AVParis_56,1.1) oṃ kṛttikārohiṇīsaumyaṃ madhyaṃ kūrmasya nirdiśet || śeṣān ṛkṣavibhāge tu trikaṃ prati vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 56: The Tortoise Division [<s>Kūrmavibhāga</s>]) (AVParis 56.1.1) Oṃ. One should designate <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and [the asterism] of <s>Soma</s> as the middle of the tortoise; the remaining [asterisms] should be assigned in groups of three to the [other] divisions of the asterism-chart.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.2) sāketamithile mekalālayāv ahichattranāgapuraṃ kāśipāriyātrakurupāñcālāḥ || atha kosalakauśāmbītīraṃ pāṭaliputraṃ kaliṅgapurapṛthivīmaṇḍalamadhye 'bhihate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.2) <s>Sāketa</s> and <s>Mithilā</s>, <s>Mekalā</s> [and its] region, <s>Ahicchatra</s>, <s>Nāgapura</s>, <s>Kāśī</s>, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>, <s>Kuru-Pāñcāla</s> — also <s>Kosala</s>, <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, the river-banks, <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, <s>Kaliṅgapura</s> — [these are] in the center of the earth-circle; when [the middle is] struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.3) aṅgavaṅgakaliṅgamāgadhamahendragavasam ambaṣṭhāḥ || bhāgāḥ pūrvasamudrāḥ śirasy abhihate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.3) <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Gavasam</s>, and the <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>s — [these] are the portions at the eastern ocean; when the head [of the tortoise] is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.4) khaśabhadrā samataṭasamavardhamānakavaidehā gāndhārāḥ || kosalatosalaveṇātaṭasajjapurā mādreyatāmaliptā dakṣiṇapūrve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.4) <s>Khaśa</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Samataṭa</s>, <s>Samavarddhamāna</s>, the <s>Kavideha</s>s, the <s>Gāndhāra</s>s — <s>Kosala</s>, <s>Tosala</s>, <s>Veṇātaṭa</s>, <s>Sajjapura</s>, <s>Mādreya</s>, <s>Tāmaliptā</s> — when the southeast is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.5) āvantyakā vidarbhā matsyā cakorabhīma[gam]rathā yavanavalayakāntīsiṃhalalaṅkuṇanāsikyakarmaṇoyāmimahi^narmadabhṛgukacchā dakṣiṇapaścād dhate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.5) The <s>Āvantyaka</s>s, the <s>Vidarbha</s>s, the <s>Matsya</s>s, the <s>Cakora</s>s, <s>Bhīma</s>, the <s>Ratha</s>s, the <s>Yavana</s>s, the <s>Valaya</s>s, <s>Kāntī</s>, <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Kuṇa</s>, <s>Nāsikya</s>, <s>Karmaṇo</s>, <s>Yāmi</s>, <s>Mahī</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Bhṛgukaccha</s> — when the south-southwest is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.6) sahyagirivaijayantī kuṇkuṇanāsikyakarmaṇoyāmimahinarmadabhṛgukacchā dakṣiṇapaścād dhate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.6) <s>Sahya</s> mountain, <s>Vaijayantī</s>, <s>Kuṇkuṇa</s>, <s>Nāsikya</s>, <s>Karmaṇo</s>, <s>Yāmi</s>, <s>Mahī</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Bhṛgukaccha</s> — when the south-west is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.7) saurāṣṭrasindhusauvīramālavā rāmarāṣṭrakānvītān || ānartagacchayantrān pucche 'bhihate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.7) <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Sauvīra</s>, the <s>Mālava</s>s, and <s>Rāmarāṣṭraka</s> with its dependencies, <s>Ānarta</s>, <s>Gaccha</s>, and <s>Yantra</s> — when the tail is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.8) sārasvatāṃs trigartān matsyān nānvārabālhikān || mathurāpuraṃgadeśān uttarabhāge hate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.8) The <s>Sārasvata</s>s, the <s>Trigarta</s>s, the <s>Matsya</s>s, the <s>Nānvāra</s>s, the <s>Bālhika</s>s, and those of <s>Mathurā</s> city and region — when the northern portion is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.9) brahmāvartaṃ śatadruhimavantaṃ parvataṃ ca mainākaṃ kāśmīraṃ caiva tathā uttarapārśve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.9) <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, the <s>Śatadru</s> (Sutlej), <s>Himavat</s> mountain and <s>Maināka</s>, and <s>Kāśmīra</s> likewise — when the north-west side is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_56,1.10) nepālakāmarūpaṃ ca videhodumbaraṃ tathā || tathāvantyaḥ kaikayaś ca uttarapūrve hate 'bhihanyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 56.1.10) <s>Nepāla</s> and <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, and <s>Videha</s> and <s>Udumbara</s> likewise; also the <s>Avanti</s>s and the <s>Kekaya</s>s — when the northeast is struck, [these] are afflicted.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_57. maṇḍalāni)
(AVParis_57,1.1) viśākhe kṛttikāḥ puṣyaḥ pūrvau proṣṭhapadau tathā | bharaṇyaś ca maghāś caiva phalgunyau prathame tathā ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 57: The <s>Maṇḍala</s>s [Celestial Divisions]) (AVParis 57.1.1) <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, the two <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>s (Pūrva and Uttara Bhādrapadā), <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and the two <s>Phalgunī</s>s (Pūrva and Uttara) first.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.2) yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.2) If in these [asterisms] the earth trembles, or thunderclaps and meteors occur, and bodiless [voices] roar, and the deities tremble,

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.3) ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | āgneyaṃ tad vijānīyād durbhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.3) or the sun is seized (eclipsed) therein, or the moon is eclipsed — one should know that as belonging to the <s>Āgneya</s> (fire) [division], and should predict famine therein.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.4) alpakṣīrās tathā gāvo agner vyādhiś ca jāyate | purāṇi deśā grāmāś ca pīḍyante hy agninā tadā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.4) Cows yield little milk, and disease from fire arises; cities, regions, and villages are then afflicted by fire.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.5) pīḍyante cāgnikarmāṇo agniveśāś ca ye narāḥ | pittajvaras tathā śvāsaha prajāḥ pīḍayate tadā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.5) Those who perform fire-rituals and men of the <s>Agniveśa</s> [clan] are afflicted; bilious fever and asthma then torment the people.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.6) akṣirogās tathā ghorāḥ puruṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ | āpagāś cātra śuṣyanti na ca sasyavatī mahī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.6) Terrible eye-diseases [affect] men especially; rivers dry up, and the earth is not fruitful with crops.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.7) tapyate ca tadā bhūmir na ca devo 'bhivarṣati | nīlalohitaparyaktā aphalāḥ pādapās tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.7) The earth then burns, and the rain-god does not shower; trees are covered with dark red [hue] and bear no fruit.

body.text: (AVParis_57,1.8) durbhikṣaṃ marako vyādhiḥ paracakrabhayaṃ tathā | etai rūpais tu vijñeyam āgneyaṃ caladarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.1.8) Famine, plague, disease, and fear of invasion [result]; by these signs should one recognize the Āgneya (fire) portent-observation.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.1) hasto 'śvinyau tathā citrā ṛkṣam aryamadaivatam | brāhmaṃ mṛgaśiraḥ svātir vāyavyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.1) <s>Hasta</s>, the two <s>Aśvinī</s>s, <s>Citrā</s>, the asterism of <s>Aryaman</s> (Uttara Phalgunī), the <s>Brāhma</s> [asterism] <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, and <s>Svāti</s> — [this] is known as the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind) <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.2) yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.2) If in these [asterisms] the earth trembles, or thunderclaps and meteors occur, and bodiless [voices] roar, and the deities tremble,

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.3) ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | vāyavyaṃ tad vijānīyād akṣemaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.3) or the sun is seized (eclipsed) therein, or the moon is eclipsed — one should know that as belonging to the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind) [division], and should predict insecurity therein.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.4) pāṃsuvarṣaṃ tadā ghoraṃ kṣīre sarpir na vidyate | prāsādatoraṇādīni prapatanti mahītale ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.4) Then terrible dust-rain [falls], and no butter is found in milk; palaces, arched gateways and such fall to the ground.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.5) madrakā yavanāś caiva śakāḥ kāmbojabālhikāḥ | gandhārāś ca vinaśyanti etaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā kila ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.5) The <s>Madraka</s>s, the <s>Yavana</s>s, the <s>Śaka</s>s, the <s>Kāmboja</s>s, the <s>Bālhika</s>s, and the <s>Gandhāra</s>s perish along with these indeed.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.6) gajā vājina uṣṭrāś ca vṛkā nakulaceṭakāḥ | pīḍyante vyādhinā sarve ye ca śastropajīvinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.6) Elephants, horses, camels, wolves, and mongoose-keepers are all afflicted by disease, as well as those who live by weapons.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.7) pure śreṣṭhā vinaśyanti gaṇeṣu guṇasaṃmitāḥ | gṛhāṇi ramaṇīyāni viśīryante ca sarvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.7) The foremost in cities perish, those endowed with qualities in assemblies; beautiful houses crumble everywhere.

body.text: (AVParis_57,2.8) āyāsaś colbaṇas tatra śastrabhrāmaḥ samantataḥ | etai rūpais tu vijñeyaṃ vāyavyaṃ caladarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.2.8) There is terrible hardship, and the brandishing of weapons on all sides — by these signs should one recognize the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind) portent-observation.

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.1) ārdrāśleṣās tathā mūlan pūrvāṣāḍhās tathaiva ca | vāruṇaṃ revatī caiva sūryadaivatyam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.1) <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> likewise, the <s>Vāruṇa</s> [asterism] (<s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>), <s>Revatī</s>, and the one whose deity is the Sun (<s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.2) yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.2) If in these [asterisms] the earth trembles, or thunderclaps and meteors occur, and bodiless [voices] roar, and the deities tremble,

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.3) ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | vāruṇaṃ tad vijānīyāt subhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.3) or the sun is seized (eclipsed) therein, or the moon is eclipsed — one should know that as belonging to the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water) [division], and should predict abundance therein.

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.4) bahukṣīrās tathā gāvo nāgāś ca phalinas tathā | śāntārayaḥ prajāḥ sarvā gomino jaṅgalaṃ payaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.4) Cows yield much milk, and serpents and trees bear fruit; all people are free from calamity, rich in cattle, with abundant water and provisions.

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.5) jalopajīvinaḥ sarve prāpnuvanty ṛddhim uttamām | khecarāś cātra dṛśyante snigdhavarṇāḥ samantataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.5) All who live by water attain the highest prosperity; sky-dwellers (birds) are seen everywhere, smooth and lustrous in color.

body.text: (AVParis_57,3.6) nyastaśastrāś ca rājāno brahmakṣatraṃ ca vardhate | etai rūpais tu vijñeyaṃ vāruṇaṃ caladarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.3.6) Kings lay down their weapons, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>Kṣatriya</s>s flourish — by these signs should one recognize the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water) portent-observation.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.1) jyeṣṭhānurādhā śravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhāś ca punarvasū | prājāpatyam āṣāḍhāś ca māhendraṃ maṇḍalaṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.1) <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā), the two <s>Punarvasu</s>s, the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [asterism], and <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> — [this] is known as the <s>Māhendra</s> (of <s>Indra</s>) <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.2) yady atra calate bhūmir nirghātolkāsta eva vā | aśarīrāś ca nardante kampante daivatāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.2) If in these [asterisms] the earth trembles, or thunderclaps and meteors occur, and bodiless [voices] roar, and the deities tremble,

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.3) ādityo vātra gṛhyeta somo vāpy uparajyate | māhendraṃ tad vijānīyāt sukṣemaṃ cātra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.3) or the sun is seized (eclipsed) therein, or the moon is eclipsed — one should know that as belonging to the <s>Māhendra</s> [division], and should predict good security therein.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.4) gāvaḥ samagravatsāś ca striyaḥ putrasamanvitāḥ | kīṭā vyālā mriyante ca ye cānye svedajantavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.4) Cows have their calves complete, and women are accompanied by sons; insects and serpents die, as do other creatures born of moisture.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.5) vedādhyayanayajñeṣu brāhmaṇā niratāḥ sadā | viṭkṣatriyāḥ svakarmāṇaḥ śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣakārakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.5) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s are always devoted to Vedic study and sacrificial rites; <s>Vaiśya</s>s and <s>Kṣatriya</s>s attend to their own duties; <s>Śūdra</s>s serve and labor.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.6) viṃśatiśataṃ tv āgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ navatiṃ calet | aśītiṃ calate tv aindraṃ vāruṇaṃ saptatiṃ calet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.6) The <s>Āgneya</s> (fiery) [earthquake] moves one hundred and twenty [yojanas]; the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind-type) moves ninety; the <s>Aindra</s> (Indra-type) moves eighty; the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water-type) moves seventy.

body.text: (AVParis_57,4.7) āgneyo bhūmikampo yaḥ sa dvimāsād vipacyate | vāruṇas tu phalaṃ sadyo vāyavyas tu trimāsikaḥ || māhendrasya phalaṃ vidyān māsam ardhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 57.4.7) The <s>Āgneya</s> earthquake ripens its effects within two months; the <s>Vāruṇa</s> [gives] its result immediately; the <s>Vāyavya</s> within three months; and the effect of the <s>Māhendra</s> (great Indra-type) should be known as [occurring within] one and a half months.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_58. digdāhalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_58,1.1) om ata ūrdhvaṃ ca digdāhān kīrtyamānān nibodhata | yathā diśaḥ pradahyante tāsāṃ dāhaphalaṃ ca yat ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 58: Signs of the Burning of the Directions) (AVParis 58.1.1) Oṃ. Now henceforth, understand the burnings of the directions as they are declared — how the directions are set ablaze and what the result of their burning is.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.2) indro 'gnir marutaś caiva pradahanti diśo daśa | śubhāśubhāya lokānāṃ kṛtāntenābhicoditāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.2) <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the <s>Marut</s>s set ablaze the ten directions, for the good and ill of the worlds, impelled by <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Fate).

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.3) yadāstamita āditye vahner jvālā pradṛśyate. diśāṃ dāhaṃ tu tad vidyād bhārgavasya vaco yathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.3) When, after the sun has set, the flame of fire is seen [at the horizon], one should know it as the burning of a direction — so says <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.4) nānārāgasamutthānāṃ nānāvidhaphalodayāḥ | pāṃśuneva ca saṃchannā digdāhāyogam āśritāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.4) Arising from various colors, yielding various kinds of results, covered as if by dust — [these] depend on the conjunction of directional burning.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.5) diśaḥ sarvāḥ pradahyante akṣemāya phalāya ca | avadāhād ṛte dāhaṃ yadi snigdhāḥ pradarśanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.5) When all directions are ablaze, [it portends] danger and calamity; but if, apart from a partial burning, the appearances are unctuous,

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.6) tamodhūmarajaskā ye dīptadvijamṛgāvṛtāḥ | pradīptalakṣaṇāḥ satyāḥ sarva evāhitāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.6) those that are [accompanied by] darkness, smoke, and dust, surrounded by blazing meteors and animals, and have the characteristics of conflagration — these are truly all harbingers of harm.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.7) tathā kanakakiṃjalkataḍitkalpāḥ śivāś ca ye | rūkṣāḥ kṛṣṇātha māñjiṣṭhā bandhujīvakavac ca ye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.7) Likewise, those that are like golden filaments and lightning are auspicious; but those that are dry, black, or madder-red, or like the <s>bandhujīvaka</s> flower,

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.8) śvetā raktāś ca pītāś ca dāhāḥ kṛṣṇāś ca varṇataḥ | brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdravināśāya prakīrtitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.8) white, red, yellow, and black burnings by color are declared to portend the destruction of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, <s>Vaiśya</s>s, and <s>Śūdra</s>s respectively.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.9) raktāḥ śastrabhayaṃ kuryur pītā vyādhiprakopanāḥ | agnivarṇās tathā kuryur agniśastrabhayaṃ mahat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.9) Red [burnings] would cause fear of weapons; yellow ones provoke disease; fire-colored ones would cause great fear of fire and weapons.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.10) sapītaparuṣaśyāmā ye ca vāruṇasaṃnibhāḥ | sarva eva kṣudhārogamṛtyuśastrāgnikopanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.10) Those that are yellow-rough-dark and those resembling <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [color] — all these provoke famine, disease, death, weapons, and fire.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.11) ṛtau tu varṣaṃ tīvraṃ syāt sainyavidravam eva ca | bhṛśam uddyotanī saṃdhyā kurute vā grahāgamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.11) In the [rainy] season, there would be intense rainfall and also the flight of armies; an exceedingly blazing twilight either [portends these] or the approach of [malefic] planets.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.12) dikṣu dagdhāsu pīḍyante yathādig deśabhaktayaḥ | śakunajñānanirdiṣṭā ye ca tatrādhikārakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.12) When the directions are burned, those dwelling in the corresponding regions suffer, as indicated by the science of omens, and those who are the rulers there.

body.text: (AVParis_58,1.13) yathoktā tu mahāśāntir yathoktavidhinā kṛtā | sarvaṃ digdāhajaṃ ghoraṃ śamayet sā sadakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58.1.13) But the great pacification rite (<s>mahāśānti</s>), performed according to the prescribed procedure, accompanied by proper fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), would quell all the terrible [effects] born of directional burning.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_58b. ulkālakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_58b,1.1) om ulkādayo hi nirdiṣṭā nirghātās tu purātra ye | teṣām idānīṃ vakṣyāmi viśeṣāṃs tu pṛthakpṛthak ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 58b: Signs of Meteors) (AVParis 58b.1.1) Oṃ. The meteors (<s>ulkā</s>) and thunderbolts (<s>nirghāta</s>) that were previously described here — I shall now declare their specific varieties, one by one.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.2) aṅgānām āntarikṣāṇāṃ yad aṅgam abhipūjitam | tad ulkālakṣaṇaṃ śrīmad aṅgaṃ kārtsnyena vakṣyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.2) Among the atmospheric limbs, whichever limb is most honored — that glorious section on the signs of meteors shall be described in full.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.3) apradhṛṣyāṇi yāni syuḥ śarīrāṇīndriyair dṛḍhaiḥ | kṣamāvanti viśuddhāni satyavratarātāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.3) Those bodies that are invincible, with firm sense-organs, endowed with forbearance, pure, and devoted to truth and vows —

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.4) tāny etāni prakāśante bhābhir vitimiraṃ nabhaḥ | samantāj jvalayantīha yasmād asukaraṃ nabhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.4) these shine forth, illuminating the sky free from darkness with their radiance, blazing all around here, since [they make] the sky difficult [to endure].

body.text:
(AVParis_58b,1.5) tāni bhāvakṣayād bhūyaḥ pracyutāni nabhastalāt | kṣitau salakṣaṇāny eva nipatantīha bhārgava
(AVParis_58b,1.6) teṣāṃ nipatatāṃ tatra yatrayatropalakṣyate | tatratatraiva vividhaṃ prajānāṃ jāyate bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.5-6) Those [celestial bodies], having fallen from the vault of heaven due to the exhaustion of their merit, descend to earth with their characteristic signs, O <s>Bhārgava</s>. Wherever those falling ones are observed, there and there alone various fears arise among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.7) rūpavarṇaprabhāsnehapramaṇākṛtisaṃgamaiḥ | teṣāṃ balābalaṃ jñātvā guṇadoṣaḥ pravakṣyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.7) Having ascertained their strength and weakness through [observing] the combination of form, color, radiance, unctuousness, size, and shape, the merits and defects shall be declared.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.8) tārā dhiṣṇyās tatholkāś ca vidyuto 'śanayas tathā | vikalpāḥ pañcadhā caiṣāṃ parasparabalottarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.8) Stars (<s>tārā</s>), fixed luminaries (<s>dhiṣṇya</s>), meteors (<s>ulkā</s>), lightning (<s>vidyut</s>), and thunderbolts (<s>aśani</s>) — these are the five varieties, each successively stronger than the other.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.9) tatra śabdenba mahatā visvareṇa vikarṣiṇā | mahācakram ivāgacchad āyatākṣā nabhastalāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.9) Among these, [the thunderbolt] arrives from the vault of heaven with a great, discordant, dragging sound, like a great wheel, with elongated eyes.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,1.10) manuṣyamṛgahastyaśvavṛkṣāśmapathaveśmasu | patanty aśanayo dīptāḥ sphoṭayantyo dharātalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.1.10) Blazing thunderbolts fall upon humans, deer, elephants, horses, trees, rocks, roads, and houses, shattering the surface of the earth.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.1) sahasaivopapanneṣu bhṛśaṃ tadanuyāyinā | sattvavibhraṃśinātyarthaṃ śabdenodvegakāriṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.1) [They come] with suddenly arisen [phenomena], closely followed by that [thunderbolt], with a sound that causes extreme terror, shattering living beings.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.2) jvālābhāravisarpiṇyaḥ prakṛtyā duḥkhadarśanāḥ | vidyuto nipatanty āśu jīveṣu vanarāśiṣu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.2) Spreading forth masses of flames, dreadful to behold by nature, lightning bolts fall swiftly upon living creatures and forest masses.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.3) tīkṣṇaśūlaviśālāgrā patantī cāpi vardhate | prakṛtyā pauruṣī tūlkā tasyā bhedān nibodhata ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.3) Sharp, with a broad spear-like point, growing as it falls — the meteor (<s>ulkā</s>) is by nature of human size. Learn its varieties:

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.4) kṛśā nārīva dīptā syāc chikhā sāṅgāravarṣiṇī | uddyotayantī gaganaṃ kāñcanenaiva varmaṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.4) It may blaze like a slender woman, with a crest raining embers, illuminating the sky as if with golden armor,

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.5) pītena pāṇḍunā vāpi dhūmadhūmāruṇena vā | viśīryatā mahābhreṇa mahatā cānuṣaṅgiṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.5) with a yellow or pale [hue], or smoke-colored and ruddy like smoke, disintegrating with a great cloud-mass and a large trailing [tail].

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.6) vaṃśagulmanibhāś cāpi kāś cid indradhvajopamāḥ | kāś cid indrāyudhaprakhyāḥ kāś cin maṇḍalasaṃsthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.6) Some resemble bamboo thickets, some are like <s>Indra</s>'s banner; some appear like <s>Indra</s>'s bow (rainbow); some are situated in circles.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.7) chattravac cāpu dṛśyante cakravan nipatanti ca | daṇḍavac cāpi tiṣṭhanti pradhāvanti ca sarpavat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.7) Some are seen like parasols, and some fall like wheels; some stand like staffs, and some rush like serpents.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.8) prakīrṇena kalāpena khe gacchantīva barhiṇaḥ | abhyucchritena pucchena yāti kā cid dharātalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.8) With spread-out plumage, they move through the sky like peacocks; one descends to earth with an upraised tail.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,2.9) tejāṃsi vikiranty anyāḥ pradhāvanti ca golavat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.2.9) Others scatter sparks of radiance and rush like balls.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.1) pranṛttapretamārjātavarāhānugatās tathā | sasvanā niḥsvanāś cāpi patanti dharaṇītale ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.1) And those followed by the paths of dancing ghosts, cats, and boars, both with sound and soundless, fall upon the surface of the earth.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.2) etāsāṃ phalam ulkānāṃ pravakṣyāmi pṛthakpṛthak | tantunaiva hi saṃbaddhā uhyamāneva vāyunā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.2) I shall declare the results of these meteors one by one: some are seen falling as if connected by a thread, carried by the wind;

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.3) patantī dṛśyate kā cit kā cid bhramati cāmbare | ulkāsaṃghaiḥ parivṛtā kā cid yāti dharātalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.3) some are seen falling, some revolve in the sky; some, surrounded by swarms of meteors, descend to earth.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.4) sāmānyaṃ tu phalaṃ tāsāṃ tat samāsena vakṣyate | varāhapretaśārdūlasiṃhamārjāravārāiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.4) The general result of those [meteors] shall be stated in summary: those resembling boars, ghosts, tigers, lions, cats,

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.5) tulyā bhayāvahā ulkā nikṛṣṭāhinibhā ca yā | śūlapaṭṭiśaśaktyṛṣṭimudgarāsiparaśvadhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.5) and serpents are equally fear-inducing meteors, as are those resembling inferior serpents; [those resembling] tridents, battle-axes, lances, spears, clubs, swords, and axes

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.6) vṛṣṭyākāreṇa tulyāś ca vṛkṣābhāś ca vigarhitāḥ | padmaśaṅkhenduvajrāhimatsyadhvajanibhāḥ śubhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.6) and those resembling rainfall are equally condemned; and those resembling trees are [also] condemned. Those resembling lotuses, conches, the moon, thunderbolts, serpents, fish, and banners are auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.7) śrīvṛkṣasvastikāvārtahaṃsadviradavarcasaḥ | jvalitāṅgārasaṃkāśā jihmagā atha śīghragāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.7) Those with the splendor of <s>Śrī</s>-trees, <s>svastika</s>s, whirlpools, swans, and elephants; those resembling blazing embers, moving crookedly or swiftly —

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.8) vinā pucchāvakāśena hrasvenātikṛśena vā | daśāntarāṇi dhanuṣaḥ pucchaṃ cāpi pradṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.8) without a tail-space, or with a short and very thin [tail] — when the tail is visible [spanning] ten intervals of a bow-[length],

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.9) ulkāvikāro boddhavyo dhiṣṇya ity abhisaṃjñitaḥ | yas tu śuklena varṇena vapuṣā pelavena vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.9) one should understand the variant of a meteor designated as <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (a fixed luminary). But that which has a white color or a delicate form,

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.10) padmatantunikāśena dhūmarājīnibhena vā | ulkāvikāraḥ so 'py uktas tārakā nāmanāmataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.10) resembling a lotus-fiber or a streak of smoke — that variant of the meteor is called by the name <s>tārakā</s> (star).

body.text: (AVParis_58b,3.11) evaṃ pañcavidhā hy etāḥ śaunakena prakīrtitāḥ | svargacyutānāṃ patatāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ puṇyakarmaṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.3.11) Thus these five varieties have been declared by <s>Śaunaka</s>: [they are] the signs of those who fall from heaven, [beings] of meritorious deeds.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.1) etāsām indraśirasi patanaṃ nṛpater bhayam | devatārcāsu patane rājarāṣṭrabhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.1) Of these, when [a meteor] falls on the head of <s>Indra</s>'s [image], there is danger to the king; when it falls on images of deities, there will be danger to the king and kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.2) puradvare purakṣobha indrakīle janakṣayaḥ | brahmāyatanaghāteṣu brāhmaṇānām upadravaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.2) At the city gate, [it portends] disturbance of the city; at the <s>Indrakīla</s> (city-pillar), destruction of people; at <s>Brahma</s>'s sanctuaries, calamity for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.3) caityavṛkṣābhighāteṣu satkṛtyānāṃ mahad bhayam | dvāre cāyuḥkṣayaṃ vidyād gṛhe tu svāmino bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.3) At sacred trees, great fear for the virtuous; at a door, one should know it as destruction of life; in a house, danger to the master.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.4) goṣṭheṣu gomināṃ vidyāt karṣakāṇāṃ khaleṣu ca | gṛheṣu rājñāṃ jānīyād bheṣu tadbhaktināṃ bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.4) In cattle-pens, one should know [danger] to cattle-owners; on threshing-floors, to farmers; in the palaces of kings, one should know fear for their subjects.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.5) āśāgrahopaghāteṣu taddeśyānāṃ tapasvinām | adhomukhīnṛpaṃ hanyād brāhmaṇān ūrdhvagāminī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.5) At the hermitages of the direction-planets, [danger] to the ascetics of that region; a downward-facing [meteor] slays a king; an upward-going one [slays] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.6) tiryaggā rājapatnīṃ ca śreṣṭhinaḥ pratilomanī | vaṃśagulmanibhā rāṣṭraṃ nṛpam indradhvajopamā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.6) A sideways-moving one [slays] the queen; a retrograde one [slays] the chief merchant. One resembling a bamboo thicket [destroys] the kingdom; one like <s>Indra</s>'s banner [slays] the king.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.7) gajam indrāyudhaprakhyā puraṃ maṇḍalasaṃsthitā | mantriṇaś cakrasaṃsthānā chattrākārā purodhasam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.7) One resembling <s>Indra</s>'s bow [kills] an elephant; a circular one [destroys] the city; a wheel-shaped one [kills] ministers; a parasol-shaped one [kills] the royal priest.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.8) mayūrapucchānugatā kuryād ulkā jalakṣayam | vilīyamānā nabhasi pibaty ulkā payodharān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.8) A meteor following a peacock's tail would cause destruction of water; one dissolving in the sky drinks up the rain-clouds.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.9) sphuliṅgān visṛjantyo yāḥ pradhāvanti samantataḥ | golavac ca pradhāvanti tāsu rāṣṭrabhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.9) Those that scatter sparks and rush about in all directions, and those that rush like balls — from these, danger to the kingdom arises.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.10) ulkāsaṃghaiḥ parivṛtā yāḥ patanti nabhastalāt | anusāriṇya ulkās tā rājarāṣṭrabhayāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.10) Those that fall from the vault of heaven surrounded by swarms of meteors — those following meteors bring danger to king and kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.11) pretānugatamārgāś ca varāhānugatāś ca yāḥ | kravyāgnivyālarūpāś ca tā janakṣayakārikāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.11) Those following the paths of ghosts and boars, and those in the form of funeral fire and serpents — they cause the destruction of people.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.12) kṣeveḍitāsphoṭitotkruṣṭā gītavāditranisvanāḥ | ulkāpāteṣu boddhavyā rājarāṣṭrabhayāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.12) Hissing, clapping, shouting, [accompanied by] sounds of singing and instruments — these should be understood in the context of meteor-falls as bringing danger to king and kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.13) sasvanā dāruṇāḥ saṃdhyāvāyoś ca pratilomagāḥ | nabho madhyaṃ ca yā yānti yāś ca kuryur gatāgatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.13) Those with sound, those that are terrible, those going against the twilight and the wind, those that go to the middle of the sky, and those that make back-and-forth movements —

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.14) hinasti śuklā śirasā madhyena kṣatajaprabhā | pārśvābhyāṃ pītakā hanti kṛṣṇolkā pucchayoginī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.14) a white [meteor] destroys with its head; a blood-colored one with its middle; yellow ones destroy with their sides; a black meteor [destroys] with its tail-conjunction.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.15) śuklā devanṛpān hanyāt kṣatriyān kṣatajaprabhā | pītā vaiśyopaghātāya śūdrān hanyāt sitetarā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.15) A white one would slay gods and kings; a blood-colored one, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s; a yellow one [portends] harm to <s>Vaiśya</s>s; a non-white one would slay <s>Śūdra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.16) patantyo nopalakṣyante karma tāsāṃ prakāśate | kṣitāv aśanayo yatra tatra nāsti bhayāgamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.16) Those that fall unobserved — their effect becomes manifest [later]. Where thunderbolts [fall] on the ground, there is no arrival of fear.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.17) satārā nipatanty anyā mārutapratilomagāḥ | bhavanti vidyuto neṣṭā iṣṭāś ca syur ato 'nyathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.17) Others fall with stars, going against the wind; lightning bolts are inauspicious, and the opposite would be auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.18) tārā dhiṣṇyāś ca boddhavyāś cirān mṛduphalodayāḥ | tāsām api ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ patanaṃ doṣakārakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.18) Stars and <s>dhiṣṇya</s>s should be understood as having delayed and mild effects; but even for them, excessive falling is productive of harm.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.19) yatoyato vikārāḥ syur nipatanty atimātraśaḥ | tatastato nṛpo yāyād daivo mārgaḥ sa ucyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.19) From whichever direction anomalies arise and [meteors] fall excessively, the king should march in that direction — that is called the divine path.

body.text: (AVParis_58b,4.20) nimitteṣu mahāśāntim ulkāyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ | kṛtvā siddhim avāpnoti ulkādoṣāc ca mucyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 58b.4.20) By performing the great pacification rite (<s>mahāśānti</s>) for [all] portents, and especially for meteors, one attains success and is freed from the defects of meteors.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_59. vidyullakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_59,1.1) ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vidyullakṣaṇam uttamam | varṇarūpavikārāṃś ca deśabhāgāñ śubhāśubhān ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 59: Signs of Lightning) (AVParis 59.1.1) Henceforth I shall declare the excellent signs of lightning — the variations in color and form, and the auspicious and inauspicious regional divisions.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.2) caturthīṃ pañcamīṃ caiva pratīkṣeta sadā śuciḥ | āṣāḍhaśuddhe niyataṃ vidyuddarśanam adbhutam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.2) One should always observe, while pure, the fourth and fifth [days of the lunar fortnight]; in the bright half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the sighting of lightning is indeed portentous.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.3) ativṛṣṭim anāvṛṣṭiṃ bhāvābhāvau tathaiva ca | sarvasasyeṣu niṣpattir vidyuto darśane naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.3) Excessive rain, drought, the existence and non-existence [of things], the fruition of all crops — [all these] a person [can know] from the observation of lightning.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.4) aindryāṃ cet syandate vidyud aindrasthaś cāpi mārutaḥ | subhikṣaṃ kṣemam ārogyaṃ nirītiṃ ca vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.4) If lightning flashes in <s>Indra</s>'s [eastern] direction, and the wind is also stationed in <s>Indra</s>'s quarter, one should predict abundance, security, health, and freedom from calamity.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.5) āgneyyāṃ ced ubhau syātāṃ bhayaṃ śastrāgnivṛṣṭihtaḥ | yāmyāyāṃ viṣamāriś ca vyādhimṛtyubhayaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.5) If both [winds] should be in the southeast, there is danger from weapons, fire, and rain; in the south, there is uneven plague and fear of disease and death likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.6) kanīyasī tu nairṛtyāṃ tathā bahvītikā samā | madhyamā sasyasaṃpattir vāruṇyāṃ vyādhisaṃkulā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.6) The lesser [wind] in the southwest — that is a year of many calamities; moderate grain-harvest; in the west, it is beset with diseases.
