body.text: (AVParis_59,1.7) pataṃgadaṃśamaśakā vāyavyāṃ madhyasapadaḥ | ativāribhayaṃ vidyāt saumyāyāṃ bhūrisaṃpadaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.7) Insects, gadflies, and mosquitoes in the northwest, with moderate crops; one should know fear of excessive rain in the north, with abundant prosperity.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.8) nirītiḥ sasyasaṃpat tu pradhānāiśyāṃ manoramā | pratilomeṣu vāteṣu ītibāhulyam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.8) Freedom from calamity and a delightful grain-harvest, chiefly in the northeast; when winds blow in reverse directions, one should predict abundance of calamities.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.9) anulomeṣu vāteṣu nirītiṃ tu samādiśet | śubhāyāṃ syandamānāyām aniṣṭā syandate yadi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.9) When winds blow in their natural directions, one should predict freedom from calamity; if an inauspicious [stream] flows when the auspicious one is flowing,

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.10) saṃpadyate mahāsasyān mahāṃś cet syād avagrahaḥ | aśubhā syandate pūrvaṃ yadi paścāc ca śobhanā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.10) Great grain crops result; but if there should be a great drought, and the inauspicious one flows first but afterwards the auspicious one [flows],

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.11) suvṛṣṭim eva tatrāhur na ca sasyaṃ samṛdhyati | yadā tu sarvāḥ syandante viṣamāṃ vṛṣṭim ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.11) They declare good rainfall in that case, but the grain does not flourish; when all [streams] flow, one should predict irregular rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.12) bahulāyāṃ vidyuti tu bahuvāribhayaṃ bhavet | savidyutaḥ sastanito darśayanti yadā śubhām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.12) When there is lightning with abundance, there will be fear of excessive water; when clouds with lightning and thunder display an auspicious [form],

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.13) pūrvottarāṃ diśaṃ meghāḥ suvṛṣṭiṃ tāṃ vijānate | pūrvataḥ pūrvavarṣeṣu dṛśyante yadi toyadāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.13) In the northeast direction — that is known as good rainfall; if rain-bearing clouds are seen in the east during the early rains,

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.14) pradakṣiṇāvartaśubhāḥ suvṛṣṭim iti nirdiśet | āgneyeṣv ativṛṣṭiḥ syāt sasyaṃ cāpi vipadyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.14) Moving clockwise auspiciously, one should predict good rainfall; with southeastern [clouds] there would be excessive rain, and the grain crop also fails.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.15) viṣamā vṛṣṭir yāmyeṣu vyādhiṃ mṛtyuṃ ca nirdiśet | bahvītikā nairṛteṣu samūlaphaladāyinī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.15) Irregular rainfall with southern [clouds] — one should predict disease and death; with southwestern [clouds], many calamities, but yielding roots and fruits.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.16) vāruṇeṣu payodeṣu madhyamaṃ sasyam ādiśet | vāyavyāṃ prathamaṃ varṣaṃ yatra varṣati vāsavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.16) With western rain-clouds, one should predict moderate grain; in the northwest, the first rain where <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) rains,

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.17) tatrātivṛṣṭir bhavati svalpabījāni vāpayet | varṇasnebhopapannās tu pūrvavṛṣṭyāṃ payodharāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.17) There excessive rain occurs; one should sow few seeds. Rain-clouds endowed with color and moisture in the early rains,

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.18) saumyāṃ yatra pravarṣeyus tatra sarvavṛṣṭyāṃ payodharāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.18) Where they rain in the north — there rain-clouds [bring] all [types of] rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.19) ity etat pūrvavarṣeṣu lakṣaṇaṃ vidyutāṃ sphuṭam | varṣārāvagataṃ sarvaṃ yathāvat parikīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.19) This is the clear characteristic of lightning in the early rains; everything regarding the rainy season has been properly declared.

body.text: (AVParis_59,1.20) śubheṣv api mahāśāntir avighātāya vocyate | aśubheṣu samarghāya tasmāt sarveṣu śāntikam iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 59.1.20) Even in auspicious [signs], a great pacificatory rite is prescribed for averting obstacles; in inauspicious [signs], for the sake of prosperity — therefore pacificatory rites in all cases.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_60. nirghātalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_60,1.1) aṣṭau bhavanti nirghātās teṣām indraḥ praśasyate | pūrveṇa vṛṣṭiṃ sasyaṃ ca rājavṛddhiṃ ca nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 60: Characteristics of Thunder)
(AVParis 60.1.1) There are eight [types of] thunderclaps; among them, <s>Indra</s>'s is praised. From the east, one should predict rain, grain, and the king's prosperity.

body.text: (AVParis_60,1.2) pūrvottare subhikṣaṃ tu bhūmilābhas tathottare | aparottare caurabhayaṃ vājināṃ cāpy upadravaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 60.1.2) In the northeast, abundance of food; in the north, gain of land; in the northwest, fear of thieves and also calamity for horses.

body.text: (AVParis_60,1.3) paścimāyāṃ bhayaṃ rājño jalajātiś ca pīḍyate | nairṛte sasyagostrīṇāṃ gaṇānāṃ ca mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 60.1.3) In the west, danger to the king, and aquatic creatures are afflicted; in the southwest, great fear for grain, cattle, women, and communities.

body.text: (AVParis_60,1.4) dakṣiṇe rājapīḍā syād āyuś cātra vinirdiśet | ānartasya bhayaṃ vidyād yadi syāt pūrvadakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 60.1.4) In the south, there would be affliction of the king, and one should predict [reduction of] lifespan; one should know fear for <s>Ānarta</s> if [the thunder] is from the southeast.

body.text: (AVParis_60,1.5) sa yojanaparaḥ śabdo nirghātasya viśāmyati | sarvatra ca bhayaṃ vidyāt tatra yatra viśāmyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 60.1.5) The sound of thunder subsides beyond a <s>yojana</s> (league); and one should know fear everywhere, wherever it subsides.

body.text: (AVParis_60,1.6) bhaye raudrīṃ prakurvīta abhayāṃ vābhayapradām | tayā śāmyanti cotpātāḥ sukhaṃ cātyantikaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 60.1.6) In [case of] danger, one should perform the <s>Raudrī</s> [rite] or the <s>Abhayā</s> (Fearlessness) [rite] that grants freedom from fear; by that, portents are pacified, and there is supreme happiness.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_61. pariveṣalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_61,1.1) om athātaḥ pariveṣāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva vakṣyate | vṛddhagargo yathā pūrvam uvāca mama suvrata ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 61: Characteristics of Halos)
(AVParis 61.1.1) Oṃ. Now the characteristics of halos will be described, as <s>Vṛddha-Garga</s> previously spoke to me, O man of good vows.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.2) svāyaṃbhuvaniyogena vikāraṃ kurute 'malaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.2) By the ordinance of <s>Svāyambhuva</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), the pure [sky] produces transformations.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.3) śvetaḥ śyāmo hariḥ kṛṣṇa iti varṇā vyavasthitāḥ | proktā megheṣu catvāro vyaktāḥ snigdhāḥ supūjitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.3) White, dark, yellow, and black — these are the established colors; four are declared in the clouds, distinct, smooth, and well-honored.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.4) snigdheṣu pariveṣeṣu vaturṣv eteṣu nārada | saṃdhyāyām atra varṇeṣu vṛṣṭiṃ teṣv abhinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.4) When halos are smooth, in these four [colors], O <s>Nārada</s>, at twilight, in these colors, one should predict rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.5) kācanīlāñjanāriṣṭāśanisarpanibheṣu ca | raupyadravasamābheṣu meghas triṣv api varṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.5) When [clouds are] resembling gold, blue collyrium, calamity, thunderbolt, and serpent, and resembling molten silver — the cloud rains in all three [seasons].

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.6) nimagnā tu yadā saṃdhyā bhavaty etat suvṛṣṭaye | ebhyaś ca viparītā ye te 'vṛṣṭibhayadā ghanāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.6) When the twilight is submerged, that portends good rainfall; those clouds that are opposite to these are producers of fear of drought.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.7) varāhair makarair uṣṭrair vṛkaiḥ kaṅkais tathā kharaiḥ | śaśakākṛtayaḥ kuryuḥ saṃdhyāyāṃ jaladā bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.7) Rain-clouds with shapes of boars, <s>makara</s>s (sea-monsters), camels, wolves, herons, and donkeys, and with the appearance of hares — at twilight they cause fear.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.8) hemapāvakavarṇāś ca vipulaṃ ca janakṣayam | śabdaṃ śvakharagomāyugṛdhravāyasasaṃsthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.8) Those of gold and fire colors cause extensive destruction of people; those resembling the sounds of dogs, donkeys, jackals, vultures, and crows,

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.9) pūrvāparāsu saṃdhyāsu saṃgrāmaṃ prāhur unmukhāḥ | aśvasthā vāraṇasthāś ca yeṣu yodhā narā iva ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.9) At the evening and morning twilights, the prominent ones predict war; those in which warriors are seen as if standing on horses and elephants,

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.10) megheṣu saṃpradṛśyante ye pāśāṅkuśasaṃnibhāḥ | tathā savāraṇāś caiva vinighnantaḥ parasparam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.10) Those seen in the clouds resembling nooses and elephant-goads, and also with elephants, striking each other,

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.11) kravyādbhir bhakṣyamāṇāś ca gṛdhragomāyuvāyasaiḥ | udyudhyante yadā yuktā rāñjaḥ saṃśayakārakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.11) And being devoured by flesh-eaters — vultures, jackals, and crows — when they fight equipped [for battle], they cause uncertainty for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.12) mayūrāṭṭālapadmendukāśanīlanibhāni tu | saṃdhyāsv abhrāṇi dṛśyante tīvraṃ varṣam upasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.12) Resembling peacocks, watchtowers, lotuses, moons, white [clouds], and blue — when such clouds are seen at twilights, intense rain is imminent.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.13) savidyut sadhanuṣkaś ca saghoṣaḥ śikhisaṃnibhaḥ | saṃdhyāsv abhrāṇi dṛśyante tīvraṃ varṣam upasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.13) With lightning, with rainbows, with thunder, resembling a peacock — when such clouds are seen at twilights, intense rain is imminent.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.14) nīlalohitaparyantaṃ kṛṣṇagrīvaṃ savidyutam | vivarṇaṃ parighaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyād udakavāhakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.14) With blue-red edges, with a dark neck, with lightning, discolored — seeing such a <s>parigha</s> (atmospheric bar), one should know it portends rain.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.15) trivarṇe parighe vāpi trivarṇair vā balāhakaiḥ | udayāstamayam iyād yadi sūryaḥ kadā cana ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.15) With a three-colored atmospheric bar, or with three-colored clouds, if the sun should ever traverse from rising to setting [through them],

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.16) pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśyānāṃ mahad bhayam upasthitam | lokakṣayakaraṃ vidyād yadi devo na varṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.16) A great danger has arisen for the royal dynasties on earth; one should know it causes destruction of the world if the god does not rain.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.17) matsyarūpī sādṛśyena yady uttiṣṭheta bhāskaraḥ | sphuṭaraśmis tadādityaḥ sa nirdahati medinīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.17) If the sun should rise resembling a fish in appearance, with clear rays — then that sun scorches the earth.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.18) etad dṛṣṭvā mahad rūpam āditye samupasthite | vispaṣṭaṃ jyotir vispaṣṭaṃ sadyovarṣasya lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.18) Seeing this great form present in the sun, with a clear and distinct light — that is the sign of immediate rain.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.19) grahasaṃchādanaṃ cāpi garjanaṃ pratigarjanam | paraspareṇa kurvanti meghā vegasamīritāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.19) The obscuring of planets, and thundering and counter-thundering — clouds driven by force do this to each other.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.20) tasmiṃś caturvidhe yuddhe meghānāṃ vyomacārinām | utpadyante trayo bhāvās tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.20) In that fourfold battle of the clouds moving through the sky, three outcomes arise — hear them as I declare.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.21) garjamāneṣu megheṣu vāraṇaḥ pratigarjati | tāṃ diśaṃ yojayet snenāṃ garjanaṃ yatra mīyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.21) When the clouds thunder and the elephant thunders in response, one should direct the army toward that direction where the thunder ceases.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.22) vidyuto 'bhravikāreṣu śakrāyudhanibhāyudhāḥ | sphoṭitāśanighaṇṭāś ca yāṃ diśaṃ meghavāraṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.22) Lightning in the cloud-transformations, weapons resembling <s>Śakra</s>'s (Indra's) weapon, bursting thunderbolts and bells — whichever direction the cloud-elephants

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.23) saṃghaṭṭeṣu samudbhutāḥ parasparajighāṃsavaḥ | tāṃ diśaṃ yojayet senāṃ rājā jayati tāṃ diśam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.23) Arise in collisions, seeking to destroy each other — one should direct the army toward that direction; the king conquers that direction.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.24) grahaṇāchādane caiva garjane pratigarjane | evam eva vidhir jñeyaḥ sarvaś caiva viniścayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.24) In seizure and obscuration, in thundering and counter-thundering, the same rule should be known, and [this is] the complete determination.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.25) parimāṇaṃ na śakyaṃ tat samīritum aśeṣataḥ | aparābhravikārāṇāṃ ratnānām iva sāgare ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.25) The full extent of the other cloud-transformations cannot be exhaustively stated, like gems in the ocean.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.26) saṃdhyā yojanabhāk proktā stanitaṃ tu dviyojanam | parighaḥ pañcayojanyaḥ pratyādityas triyojanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.26) The twilight is said to extend one <s>yojana</s>; thunder, two <s>yojana</s>s; the atmospheric bar, five <s>yojana</s>s; the mock-sun, three <s>yojana</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.27) nirghātaḥ ṣaṭ tathā vidyut pariveṣo dviṣaḍyataḥ | dāhaṃ yojanakaṃ cāpi ulkā tv amitabhāginī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.27) Thunderclap, six; likewise lightning; the halo extends twelve <s>yojana</s>s; a conflagration extends one <s>yojana</s>; and a meteor has unlimited range.

body.text: (AVParis_61,1.28) daśasaṃsthā samāptāni śāyāṅgāni pramāṇataḥ | aṅgāni tv āntarikṣāṇi vijñeyāni samāsataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 61.1.28) The ten configurations of the atmospheric limbs are completed with their measurements; the atmospheric phenomena should be known in summary.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_62. bhūmikampalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_62,1.1) oṃ catvāro bhumikampās tu gargaḥ provāca buddhimān | agnir vāyus tathāpaś ca caturthas tv indra ucyate ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 62: Characteristics of Earthquakes)
(AVParis 62.1.1) Oṃ. The wise <s>Garga</s> spoke of four [types of] earthquakes: [those caused by] <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), then <s>Āpas</s> (Water), and the fourth is said to be [that of] <s>Indra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.2) teṣāṃ rūpaṃ vikārāṃś ca vyākhyāsyāmo 'nupūrvaśaḥ | yaj jñātvā buddhimān dhīro nirdiśed vividhaṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.2) We shall explain their forms and effects in order; knowing which, the wise and discerning one should predict various results.

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.3) prakampitāyāṃ bhūmau cet saptāhābhyantareṇā tu | [bhaveyur atra saṃgrāmā rājñāṃ mṛtyubhayapradāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.3) If the earth is shaken, within seven days [there would be battles among kings causing fear of death,

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.4) rājñāṃ virodho bhavati maraṇāni bhavanti ca |] tāmraḥ sūryaś ca candraś ca pītāś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.4) Conflict arises among kings, and deaths occur;] the sun and moon become coppery, and animals and birds become yellowish.

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.5) diśaḥ sarvā bhaveyuś ca sūryodayasamaprabhāḥ | yad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād agniprakampitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.5) All the directions become equal in radiance to sunrise; that which bears these characteristics should be known as a fire-earthquake.

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.6) tasmin bhavati nirdeśaḥ śaunakasya vaco yathā | hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca yac cānyad vidyate gṛhe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.6) For this, the prediction is as the word of <s>Śaunaka</s> [states]: gold and precious metal and whatever else exists in the house,

body.text:
(AVParis_62,1.7) sarvam etat parityajya kartavyo dhānyasaṃgrahaḥ | rāṣṭrāṇi saṃdahed agnir grāmāṃś ca nagarāṇi ca
(AVParis_62,1.8) saṃgrāmāś cātra vartante māṃsaśoṇitakardamāḥ | rājānaś ca virudhyante devaś cātra na varṣati ||
body.translated_text:
(AVParis 62.1.7) Abandoning all that, one should gather grain stores. Fire burns kingdoms, villages, and cities.
(AVParis 62.1.8) Battles occur there, with mire of flesh and blood; kings become hostile, and the god does not rain.

body.text: (AVParis_62,1.9) evam etatprakampānāṃ garhitam agnikampitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.1.9) Thus among these earthquakes, the fire-earthquake is condemned.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.1) prakampitāyāṃ bhūmau ced iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.1) When the earth is shaken [by wind] —

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.2) atipracaṇḍo bahulo vāyur bhavati dāruṇaḥ | śarkarākarṣaṇaś cāpi dikṣu caiva vidikṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.2) The wind becomes excessively fierce, abundant, and terrible, dragging gravel in the directions and intermediate directions.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.3) tad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād vāyuprakampitam | śastrair āvaraṇaṃkuryāt prākāraṃ parikhāṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.3) That which bears these characteristics should be known as a wind-earthquake. One should make a defense with weapons, a rampart, and a moat.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.4) na tadā pravased grāmaṃ jñātvātmānaṃ tu gopayet | saṃgrāmāś cātra vardhante māṃsaśoṇitakardamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.4) One should not then enter the village; knowing [the danger], one should protect oneself. Battles increase there, with mire of flesh and blood.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.5) virudhyante ca rājāno maraṇāni bhavanti hi | rājaputrasahastrāṇāṃ bhūmiḥ pibati śoṇitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.5) Kings become hostile, and indeed deaths occur; the earth drinks the blood of thousands of princes.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.6) māsaṃ viṃśatirātraṃ vā devas tatra na varṣati | dvābhyāṃ gatābhyāṃ māsābhyāṃ paraṃ syād bahulaṃ jalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.6) For a month or twenty nights, the god does not rain there; after two months have passed, there would then be abundant water.

body.text: (AVParis_62,2.7) daṣṭaṃ dūṣayate cātra kṣatabaddhāni cādhikam | eṣām eva tu kampānāṃ garhitaṃ vāyukampitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.2.7) Bites become infected, and bound wounds [worsen] even more; among these very earthquakes, the wind-earthquake is condemned.

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.1) prakampitāyāṃ bhūmau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.1) When the earth is shaken [by water] —

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.2) varṣantas tu samāyānti mahāmeghāḥ samantataḥ | nakrāś ca śiśumārāś ca kūrmā makarasaṃsthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.2) Great rain-clouds come raining from all sides; crocodiles, dolphins, and turtles stationed on <s>makara</s>s (sea-monsters)

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.3) abhrākṛtiṣu dṛśyante grasantaś candrabhāskarau | tad etallakṣaṇopetaṃ vidyād ambuprakampitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.3) Are seen in the cloud-formations, swallowing the moon and sun; that which bears these characteristics should be known as a water-earthquake.

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.4) parvateṣu vaped bījam ūṣare jāṅgale tathā | tatroptaṃ nandate bījam anyatra bhuvi naśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.4) One should sow seeds on mountains, on saline land, and on dry land likewise; the seed sown there flourishes, but elsewhere on earth it perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.5) udajāni tu puṣpāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca | gacchanti tatra vṛddhiṃ ca sattvāny udakajāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.5) Water-born flowers, roots, and fruits — these increase there, and also water-born creatures.

body.text: (AVParis_62,3.6) [kṣemaṃ subhikṣam ārogyaṃ suvṛṣṭiṃ cātra nirdiśet] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.3.6) [One should predict welfare, abundance of food, health, and good rainfall.]

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.1) prakampitāyāṃ bhūmau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.1) When the earth is shaken [by <s>Indra</s>] —

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.2) gambhīraṃ garjamānas tu megha āyāti pārthivaḥ | snigdho hy añjanasaṃkāśaḥ sumahatparvatopamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.2) A cloud rumbling deeply approaches — royal, unctuous, resembling collyrium, equal to a great mountain.

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.3) vitrāsayan diśaḥ sarvā drutaṃ cāpi pravarṣati | indrāyudhaṃ bhavec cātra vidyut stanitam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.3) Terrifying all directions, it also rains swiftly; and therein a rainbow appears, along with lightning and thunder.

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.4) suvṛṣṭiṃ kṣemam ārogyaṃ subhikṣaṃ paramā mudaḥ | yajñodbhavais tu modante ānandair moditāḥ prajāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.4) Good rain, security, health, abundance, and supreme joy [result]; the people rejoice with sacrificial delights, gladdened by happiness.

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.5) eteṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ praśastaṃ hīndrakampanam | jānīyāl lakṣaṇair etaiḥ sarvam eva śubhāśubham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.5) Of these earthquakes, the <s>Indra</s>-quake is the most auspicious; one should know all auspicious and inauspicious [effects] by these characteristics.

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.6) eteṣu triṣu kampeṣu atharvā śāstrakovidaḥ | māhendrīm amṛtāṃ vāpi kuryāc chāntiṃ sadakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.6) In these three [types of] quakes, the <s>Atharvan</s> priest skilled in the scriptures should perform the <s>Māhendrī</s> or <s>Amṛtā</s> pacification rite with appropriate gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_62,4.7) indrakampe tu vidhivad aindrair mantrair vidhānavit | tatohalasya pradhānārthaṃ juhuyāc ca japet tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 62.4.7) In an <s>Indra</s>-quake, the one knowledgeable of ritual procedures should, according to rule, offer oblations and perform recitations with <s>Aindra</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>) mantras for the chief purpose.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_63. nakṣatragrahotpātalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_63,1.1) om atha paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vakṣatreṣu graheṣu ca | pariveṣān bahuvidhān nānāvidhaphalodayān ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 63: Characteristics of Portents regarding Asterisms and Planets [Halos]) (AVParis 63.1.1) Oṃ. Now I shall declare further concerning asterisms and planets — the halos (<s>pariveṣa</s>s) of many kinds, producing various fruits.

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.2) aindravāruṇakauberān raktapāṇḍuramecakān | pāṇḍūn babhrūṃś ca pītāṃś cānīlānalayamātmanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.2) Those belonging to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Kubera</s> — red, white, and dark; pale, tawny, yellow, and dark-blue — those partaking of Fire and <s>Yama</s>;

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.3) prājāpatyāṃś ca raudrāṃś ca nairṛtyāṃś cāpi bhārgava | hariśabalakāpotān pariveṣān uvāca ha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.3) those of <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s> — O <s>Bhārgava</s>! — green, variegated, and pigeon-colored — thus he spoke of the halos.

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.4) navaite pariveṣāṇāṃ varṇā daivatayonayaḥ | bahutvam ete gacchanti anyonyaguṇasaṃśrayāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.4) These nine are the colors of halos, having their origins in the deities; they attain multiplicity through mutual combination of qualities.

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.5) gṛhītvābhrarajaḥ sūkṣmaṃ varṇayog saṃnipatya ca | pitāmahaniyogena māturo maṇḍalīkṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.5) Having gathered the fine dust of clouds and combining with the color-mixture, by the grandfather's (<s>Pitāmaha</s>'s) ordination, the wind forms it into a circle.

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.6) śubhāśubhārthaṃ lokānāṃ jyotīmṣy avaruṇaddhi saḥ | tasya rūpaṃ guṇaṃ jñātvā guṇadoṣaḥ pracakṣyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.6) For the auspicious and inauspicious [fortune] of the worlds, it obstructs the luminaries; knowing its form and quality, the merits and faults are declared.

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.7) nakṣatratārakāṇāṃ ca parato viṣayasya ca niviṣṭo bhāva āgantuṃ pariveṣa iti smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.7) That which is situated beyond the stars and beyond its domain, with the nature of approaching — that is remembered as a <s>pariveṣa</s> (halo).

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.8) dhṛtatīkṣṇārkakiraṇe prasannā mṛdumaṇḍale | prasnigdhe caikavarṇe ca māṃsale vyaktalakṣaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.8) When the sharp solar rays are steady, when the circle is calm and soft, unctuous, of a single color, fleshy, and of clear characteristics —

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.9) lohitākṣau kṣurakrānte saraśmau pītamaṇḍale | ā pradoṣād vimadhyāhnād ā nakṣatrāntagāmini ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.9) with red extremities, razor-edged, with rays, in a yellow circle, [visible] from the early evening up to midday, reaching to the end of the asterism —

body.text: (AVParis_63,1.10) sahābhrabhārastanite pariveṣe prakāśini | anṛtāv api jānīyān mahad bhayam upasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.1.10) when the halo is luminous together with the weight of clouds and thunder — even out of season, one should know that great danger is at hand.

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.1) kṛṣṇanīhāratimire prakṛtyākrāntamaṇḍale | vikārair nābhasaiḥ kīrṇe sphuliṅgopacite 'śubhe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.1) When [there is] black mist and darkness, when the circle is overrun by its nature, scattered with atmospheric disturbances, filled with sparks, inauspicious,

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.2) viṣame vigatasnehe vidhvastakaluṣābhrake | triṣu saṃdhiṣu bhūyiṣṭhaṃ darśanaṃ copagacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.2) uneven, devoid of unctuousness, with dispersed and murky clouds — it most often appears at the three junctures (dawn, noon, dusk).

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.3) dvitrinakṣatrage vāpi nakṣatrārdhagate 'pi vā | pradīptair vā rasadbhiś ca vīkṣyamāṇe mṛgadvijaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.3) Or when it traverses two or three asterisms, or reaches half an asterism, or when blazing and dripping [halos] are observed by deer and birds —

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.4) pariveṣe vijānīyān nṛpādyānām upasthitam | saptarātrād bhayaṃ ghoraṃ cauraśastrāgnimṛtyubhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.4) in [such] a halo, one should know that [calamity] beginning with the king is at hand; within seven nights, terrible danger from thieves, weapons, fire, and death.

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.5) dhūmakarburamāñjiṣṭharaktapītāsitākṛtiḥ | bhavaty ekatare pārśve rūpeṇāvilamaṇḍalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.5) [A halo that is] smoky, variegated, madder-red, red, yellow, black in form, appearing on one side, with a turbid circle —

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.6) tanunā cātra jālena samantāt pariveṣṭitaḥ | muhurmuhuś ca vilayaṃ saṃsthānaṃ cāpi gacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.6) and therein enclosed on all sides by a thin web-like [formation], and repeatedly dissolving and reforming —

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.7) so 'pi vāyvātmako jñeyo mṛdumandadivākaraḥ | pariveṣo 'lpaphalado vātavṛṣṭiḥ pravṛṃhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.7) that also should be known as belonging to <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), [when] the sun is soft and dim; [such] a halo yields little fruit, [but] wind and rain increase.

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.8) atha ced vātavṛṣṭis tu trirātrān nāpajāyate | jalajvalanacaurāṇāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ prajāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.8) But if wind and rain do not arise within three nights, then the manifestation of [danger from] water, fire, and thieves occurs.

body.text: (AVParis_63,2.9) pariveṣagato 'lkā syād dvimaṇḍalaparigrahe | dvābhyāṃ senāpatibhayaṃ yuvarājabhayaṃ tribhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.2.9) If a meteor enters the halo while two circles encompass [it] — from two [circles], fear from a general; from three, fear from a crown prince.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.1) maṇḍalaiḥ purarodhaḥ syāt tribhir abhyadhikair dhryvan | trāṇi yatrāvarudhyante nakṣatragrahacandramāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.1) With [more than] three circles, there would be siege of the city, firmly; [in the place] where asterisms, planets, and the moon are enclosed —

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.2) tryahād varṣaṃ samācaṣṭe sa māsād vigrahaṃ vadet | senāpatikumārāṇāṃ senāyāś cāpi vidravaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.2) within three days it predicts rain; within a month it foretells conflict — the flight of generals, princes, and the army.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.3) lohitāṅgapariveṣe śastrāgnyutpāta eva ca | sthāvarāḥ karṣakāś cāpi kṣudradhānyaṃ ca pīḍyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.3) When <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars) [has] a halo, there is a portent of weapons and fire; the sedentary [classes], farmers, and minor grains are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.4) vātavṛṣṭiṃ ca janayet pariviṣṭaḥ śanaiścaraḥ | rājyam eva hi garbhāṃś ca rāhuḥ pīḍayate dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.4) When <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is encircled [by a halo], it produces wind and rain; <s>Rāhu</s> certainly afflicts the kingdom and pregnancies.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.5) vyādhīṃś caiva prajanayet pariviṣṭaś ca candramāḥ | kṣucśvāsāgnibhayaṃ ghoraṃ rājato mṛtyutas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.5) When the Moon is encircled [by a halo], it produces diseases; terrible danger from hunger, asthma, fire, the king, and death.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.6) pariviṣṭo 'mbare ketuḥ śikhinaś ca hinasti saha | dvayoḥ saṃgrāmam ācaṣṭe grahayoḥ pariviṣṭayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.6) When a comet in the sky is encircled [by a halo], it destroys the flame-crested ones (peacocks) together [with others]; when two planets are encircled, it predicts war between them.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.7) kṣudbhayaṃ triṣu vijñeyaṃ varṣanigraha eva ca | caturbhir mriyate rājā sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.7) In three [planets encircled], fear of famine should be known, along with cessation of rain; in four, the king dies together with his ministers and priest.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.8) yugānta iva jānīyāt patriviṣṭeṣu pañcasu | brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdrān hanyāt pratipadādiṣu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.8) When five are encircled, one should know [it is] like the end of an age; [the halo] slays <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, <s>Vaiśya</s>s, and <s>Śūdra</s>s from the first [lunar day] onward.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.9) grāmān puraṃ ca kośaṃ ca pañcamyādiṣv atas triṣu | aṣṭamyāṃ yuvarājānāṃ camūpālān hinasti saha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.9) Villages, cities, and the treasury [are afflicted] from the fifth [day] onward for three [days]; on the eighth, it destroys crown princes and army commanders together.

body.text: (AVParis_63,3.10) navamyāṃ ca daśamyāṃ ca ekādaśyāṃ ca pārthivān | trayodaśyāṃ balakṣobho dvādaśyāṃ rudhyate puram ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.3.10) On the ninth, tenth, and eleventh — kings; on the thirteenth, disturbance of the army; on the twelfth, the city is besieged.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.1) rājapatnīṃ caturdaśyāṃ pajcadaśyāṃ nṛpasya ca | purohitāmātyanṛpā hanyur anyonyam eva tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.1) On the fourteenth, the queen; on the fifteenth, the king himself; the priest, ministers, and king slay each other mutually.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.2) purarodhaṃ vijānīyāt pariviṣṭe bṛhaspatau | mantriṇo lekhakāś cāpi rudhyante sthāvarāṇi ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.2) When <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) is encircled, one should know [it portends] siege of the city; ministers, scribes, and the sedentary [classes] are obstructed.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.3) vṛṣṭiṃ cāpi vijānīyāt pariviṣṭe budhe grahe | yāyinaḥ kṣatriyāś cāpi rājapakṣaś ca pīḍyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.3) When the planet <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is encircled, one should know [it portends] rain; travelers, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, and the royal faction are afflicted.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.4) dhānyārghaṃ ca priyaṃ kuryāt pariviṣṭo bhṛgoḥ sutaḥ | tārāgrahapariveṣā nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca kevalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.4) When the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) is encircled, it makes grain prices favorable; halos of stars and planets [affect] the asterisms alone.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.5) mahāgrahodayaṃ kuryān maraṇaṃ vā mahīpateḥ | rakte pīte 'site tāmre kṛṣṇe ca harite 'ruṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.5) [A halo around a great planet] causes the rise of a great planet or the death of a king; in red, yellow, black, copper, dark, green, and tawny [halos] —

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.6) kṣucśastravyādhivarṣāgnimṛtyusasyānilānayoḥ | varṇānāṃ ca bhayaṃ jñeyaṃ yathā varṇaparigrahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.6) fear from famine, weapons, disease, rain, fire, death, crops, wind, and calamity should be known according to the respective colors; as the color encompasses, [so is the effect].

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.7) kāpotaḥ śabalaś cāpi tiryagyonibhayāvahau | mayūragalaśaṅkhendumuktāgokṣīrapāṇḍurāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.7) Pigeon-colored and variegated [halos] bring fear from animal-born [creatures]; those white as peacock-neck, conch, moon, pearl, and cow's milk,

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.8) madhūkaghṛtamaṇḍābhā dūrvāśyāmāś ca vṛṣṭaye | vimuktāriṣṭakākārās tailāmalakasaṃnibhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.8) those resembling <s>Madhūka</s> flowers, ghee-surface, and <s>Dūrvā</s>-grass-dark — [portend] rain; those free from inauspicious signs, resembling sesame-oil and <s>Āmalaka</s> (gooseberry),

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.9) snigdhāmalajalaprakhyā darpaṇābhās ca pūjitāḥ | babhravaḥ paruṣā rukṣā haridrāruṇasaṃnibhāḥ | vichinnā lohitā hrasvā vivarṇāś ca śubhāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.9) unctuous, clear, water-like, mirror-like — [these] are honored; tawny, rough, dry, resembling turmeric and tawny-red, broken, blood-red, short, and discolored — [these] are inauspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_63,4.10) yāyināṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca tathaivākrandasāriṇām | pariveṣān vijānīyād bāhyābhyantaramadhyataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.4.10) One should recognize the halos of travelers, the sedentary, and likewise the mobile and the stationary, from the outer, inner, and middle [portions].

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.1) saṃraktaśyāmakaluṣo yeṣāṃ bhāgo hataprabhaḥ | teṣāṃ parājayaṃ vidyāt snigdhe śvete ca vai jayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.1) Those whose portion is reddish-dark and turbid, of diminished lustre — one should know their defeat; in unctuous white, indeed, [there is] victory.

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.2) yenayenābhravarṇena yoyo bhāgo 'nurajyate | tattat teṣāṃ phalaṃ vidyāt tad bhūtyādiṣu kīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.2) By whatever cloud-color a given portion is tinged, one should know that as its fruit — that has been declared in matters of prosperity and the like.

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.3) chidrāṇy etāny ataś cāhur mahānti vimalāni ca | tair dvāraiḥ pārthivo yāyāt panthānas te vikaṇṭakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.3) These are called great and clear openings; through those gateways a king should march — those paths are free of obstacles.

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.4) kālāmbudaparisrāvair grahodayanimittakam | ityarthaṃ janma sarveṣāṃ śeṣam utpātalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.4) From the outpourings of dark clouds, [portents] occasioned by the rise of planets — thus is the birth of all [portents]; the rest is [covered under] the characteristics of portents.

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.5) raudrī sadakṣiṇā śāntir utpāteṣu prakīrtitā | samuccaye tu vijñeyā vaiśvadevy abhayā tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.5) The <s>Raudrī</s> pacification with gifts is proclaimed for [times of] portents; in [times of] accumulation [of portents], the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> [rite] and the <s>Abhayā</s> (fearlessness rite) should be known.

body.text: (AVParis_63,5.6) atharvotpātahṛdayaṃ jñātvā svayam anāturaḥ | prayuñjīta mahāśāntiṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśinīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 63.5.6) Having understood the heart of <s>Atharvan</s> portent-lore, one who is himself untroubled should employ the great pacification (<s>Mahāśānti</s>) that destroys all impurities.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_64. utpātalakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_64,1.1) oṃ yān provācāṅgirāḥ pūrvaṃ yāṃśca vedo 'śanāḥ kaviḥ | tān ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi utpātāṃs trividhān api ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 64: Characteristics of Portents) (AVParis 64.1.1) Oṃ. Those which <s>Aṅgiras</s> formerly declared, and which the sage <s>Veda</s> spoke along with <s>Aśana</s> (the Thunderbolt) — those portents of three kinds I shall now fully declare.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.2) prakṛter anyathābhavo yatrayatropajāyate | tatratatra vijānīyāt sarvam utpātalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.2) Wherever a change from the natural state occurs — there one should know all the characteristics of portents.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.3) pārthivaṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca divyaṃ cotpātalakṣaṇam | nakṣatropadraveṣūktaṃ yathāvidhi tathaiva tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.3) Earthly, atmospheric, and celestial — [these are] the portent characteristics; [what has been] stated regarding afflictions of asterisms — that [applies] in the same manner according to rule.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.4) teṣūtpātagaṇeṣu āhū rasātalasamudbhavān | nirghātān bhūmikampāṃś ca kīrtyamānān nibodhata ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.4) Among those groups of portents, they speak of those arising from the nether regions — thunderclaps and earthquakes that are now being described — understand [them]!

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.5) vāruṇāgneyavāyavyāḥ kampayanti vasuṃdharām | śubhāśubhārthaṃ lokānāṃ rātrau ahani cakravat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.5) Those belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> cause the earth to tremble; for the auspicious and inauspicious [fortune] of the worlds, by night and day in a cycle.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.6) teṣāṃ vakṣyāmi kampānāṃ lakṣaṇāni phalāni ca | yatrovācāuśanāḥ khyātān nāradāya sma pṛcchate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.6) Of those quakes, I shall declare the characteristics and fruits — those which the renowned <s>Auśanas</s> (descendant of <s>Uśanas</s>) spoke to <s>Nārada</s> when he asked.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.7) saptāhābhyantare kampe bhaved vajradharātmake | sasvanair āptaparyantaṃ svastikābhraghanair nabhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.7) Within seven days of a quake that partakes of <s>Vajradhara</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) nature — with sounds, the sky [is filled] to its limits with clusters of <s>svastika</s>-marked clouds.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.8) saindracāpāyudhā kampād vidyudgaṇagavākṣakaiḥ | pāśorminagarākārair naganāganibhair ghanaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.8) From the quake [come clouds] with rainbow-weapons, with lattice-windows of lightning clusters, resembling cities made of nooses and waves, like mountains and serpent-mountains.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.9) nabhaso 'ntaṃ ca sevinyo vidyutaḥ svārkasaṃnibhāḥ | prānte susaṃvṛtāś cāpi śītāśītāś ca mārutāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.9) Lightning bolts resembling the sun itself attend the edge of the sky; and the winds are well-enclosed at the borders, [alternately] cold and warm.

body.text: (AVParis_64,1.10) dhārāṅkuraparisrāvair nīlotpaladalaprabhaiḥ | svanadbhiś chādyate vyoma kampayed varuṇaḥ svayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.1.10) With outpourings of rain-streams, with the lustre of blue lotus petals, resounding — the sky is covered; <s>Varuṇa</s> himself would cause it to quake.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.1) tārāpātair diśaṃ dāhair ulkāpātaiś ca sasvanaiḥ | hāhākṛtam ivābhūti pradīpitapathaṃ nabhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.1) With falling stars, burning of directions, and sounding meteor-falls — the sky becomes as if crying 'Alas!', its path set ablaze.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.2) saptāhābhyantare vāpi kṣitau vahniḥ prakupyate | sa āgneyo bhavet kampo rājarāṣtrabhayāvahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.2) Within seven days, fire erupts on earth — that is the <s>Āgneya</s> (fire-born) quake, bringing fear to king and kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.3) niḥprakāśam ivākāśe bhāskaro nātibhāskaraḥ | diśas tu na prakāśante duḥkhāṛtā iva yoṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.3) The sky is as if lightless, the sun not very brilliant; the directions do not shine, like women afflicted by sorrow.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.4) saghoṣā mārutā rūkṣā vānti śarkarakarṣiṇaḥ | saptāhābhyantare kampe mārute 'tibhayāvahe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.4) Noisy, dry winds blow, dragging gravel — within seven days of a quake born of <s>Māruta</s> (wind), extremely frightful.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.5) subhikṣakṣemadau kampau vijñeyāv aindravāruṇau | vāyavyāgneyajau kampau rājarāṣtrabhayāvahau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.5) The quakes of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> should be known as bringing abundance and security; those born of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Agni</s> bring fear to king and kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.6) yasyāṃ yasyāṃ diśi dharā virauti vikṛtasvarā | tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśi bhayṃ sārdhaṃ syād adhikāridbhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.6) In whichever direction the earth cries out in a distorted voice, in that direction there shall be danger together with those in authority.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.7) nirghātā bhūmikampāś ca sasamāsam udāhṛtāḥ | ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śeṣam utpātalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.7) Thunderclaps and earthquakes have been described in summary; henceforth I shall declare the remaining characteristics of portents.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.8) prāgyāmyāparasaumyānāṃ gandharvanagaraṃ tathā | raktapītāśitaiś caiva varṇair dikṣu pradṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.8) Of the eastern, southern, western, and northern [directions] — a <s>Gandharva</s>-city (mirage) appears in the directions in red, yellow, and black colors.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.9) rājñaḥ senāpateś cāpi yuvarājapurodhasām | vyasanaṃ maraṇaṃ vāpi vijñeyam anupūrvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.9) [It portends] calamity or death for the king, the general, the crown prince, and the priest — one should know [this] in sequence.

body.text: (AVParis_64,2.10) varuṇāmāṇ ca bhayaṃ jñeyaṃ yathāvarṇaparigrahāt | vidikṣu ca vivarṇāsu pīḍā jñeyā vivarṇinām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.2.10) Danger from <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [direction] should be known according to the color-association; and in the intermediate directions, when discolored, one should know affliction for those of [corresponding] discolored [complexion].

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.1) satataṃ dṛśyamāne ca rājarāṣṭrabhayāvaham | āśādhikārikāṇāṃ ca pīḍā jñeyā yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.1) When [portents are] seen constantly, they bring danger to the king and kingdom; affliction should be known for those responsible for [the respective] directions, according to the rule.

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.2) viruddhayonigamanam anyasattvaprasūtayaḥ | hastapādākṣiśirasām adhikānāṃ pradarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.2) Going to a womb of the wrong kind, births of [offspring of] other species, the appearance of [beings with] extra hands, feet, eyes, or heads,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.3) abhyaṅgatā ca saṃyoge gatihīnaṃ ca ceṣṭitam | viruddhānāṃ ca sattvānām anyonyapratisaṃgamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.3) fusion of bodies in conjunction, movement and action devoid of [normal] gait, the coming together of mutually hostile creatures,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.4) calatvam acalānāṃ ca calānām acalakṛyā | bhāṣitaṃ cāpi abhāṣāṇām aśabdānāṃ ca bhāṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.4) the movement of immovable things and the immobility of moving things, the speech of mute things and the sounding of silent things,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.5) anagnau darśanaṃ cāgneḥ śītoṣṇasya viparyayaḥ | lohādīnāṃ plavaś cāpsu nodake cāmbhasāṃ sravaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.5) the appearance of fire without a [source of] fire, the reversal of cold and heat, the floating of iron and such in water, and the flow of waters without [actual] water,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.6) akālapuṣpaprasavaḥ sasyāḥ pañcacaturguṇāha | saṃyogo lāṅgalānāṃ ca prabhānāṃ ceṣṭitāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.6) the flowering and fruiting of plants out of season, crops [yielding] four or fivefold, the coupling of ploughs, and the movements of radiances,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.7) vicitrair devatāsadbhir vṛkṣaprasravaṇāni ca | diśo dhūmāndhakārāś ca dīptāś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.7) the exudation of trees with various divine manifestations, smoke and darkness in the directions, and blazing deer and birds,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.8) rajastamāśritaṃ vyoma kaluṣau candrabhāskarau | vastramāṃsāmbhasāṃ dīptirāgaprajvalitāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.8) the sky pervaded by dust and darkness, the Moon and Sun turbid, the blazing and flaring up of garments, flesh, and waters in a reddish glow,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.9) akasmād gopurāṭṭālaśailaprasādaveśmanām | daraṇaṃ jvalanaṃ vāpi kampo dhūmapravartanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.9) the sudden cracking, burning, trembling, or emission of smoke from city gates, watchtowers, mountain palaces, and houses,

body.text: (AVParis_64,3.10) abhīkṣṇā mārutāś caṇḍā vānti śarkarakarṣiṇaḥ | saṃhitā maṇḍalānāṃ ca nīlalohitapītakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.3.10) frequent fierce winds blowing, carrying gravel, and the conjunction of circles [halos] in dark-blue, red, and yellow —

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.1) dhvajastambhendrakīlānāṃ śuṣkacaityādibhiḥ saha | chinne bhinne drumāṇāṃ ca skandhaśākhāṅkurodbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.1) from banners, pillars, and <s>Indra</s>-posts together with dry shrines and the like — when trees are cut or split, the sprouting of trunks, branches, and buds,

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.2) gītānāṃ ca mṛdaṅgānāṃ vāditrāṇāṃ nisvanāḥ | bhaveyur ākāśapathe sagandharvapurogamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.2) the sounds of songs, drums, and musical instruments that might resound in the sky-path, led by <s>Gandharva</s>s (celestial musicians),

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.3) chāyādarśanam adravye virātre virutāni ca | divārātricarāṇāṃ ca viparītapracāratā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.3) the seeing of shadows in insubstantial objects, cries in the dead of night, and the reversed behavior of day-roaming and night-roaming [creatures],

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.4) nirabhravṛṣṭayaś caiva nirabhrastanitāni ca | sasvanānām adhūmānām ulkānāṃ patanaṃ divā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.4) rain from a cloudless sky, thunder from cloudless skies, the falling of sounding, smokeless meteors by day,

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.5) indor arkasya vā cāpi pāṃsvaśmādiṣu darśanam | abhīkṣṇapariveṣāśca kaluśā ravisomayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.5) the appearance of dust, stones, and such in the Moon or the Sun, frequent halos, and turbidity around the Sun and Moon,

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.6) mayūrakokilādīnāṃ madāvāptir anārtavā | vanānāṃ ca nagānāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca nirgamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.6) the out-of-season excitement of peacocks, cuckoos, and the like, and the emanations from forests, mountains, and deities,

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.7) āraṇyānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ puragrāmaniveśanam | abhūtānāṃ pravṛtiśca pravṛttānāṃ ca nāśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.7) the settling of wild animals in towns and villages, the occurrence of things that never existed, and the disappearance of things that existed —

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.8) etad utpātajaṃ rājño yasyā deśe abhyudīryate | tasya deśo vinaśyeta kṣīyate ca sapārthivaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.8) this portent-born [omen] — in whichever king's land it manifests — that land perishes, and [the kingdom] declines along with its sovereign.

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.9) tyajanti vāpi yaṃ deśaṃ pāṣaṇḍā dvijadevatāḥ | vidveṣaṃ vāpi gacchanti so 'pi deśo vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.9) That land which heretics and the twice-born and deities abandon, or toward which they develop enmity — that land too is destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_64,4.10) nartanaṃ ca kuśūlānāṃ dhānyarāśeśca kampanam | ulūkhālānāṃ saṃsarpo musalānāṃ praveśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.4.10) The dancing of granaries, the trembling of heaps of grain, the crawling of mortars, the entering of pestles,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.1) ceṣṭitaṃ rājadarvīṇāṃ mṛdbhāṇḍānāṃ tathaiva ca | dahanaṃ caiva śītānām [śabdā hy uttarāṇi ca] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.1) the movement of royal ladles and earthen vessels likewise, and the burning of cold things [and sounds from the north] —

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.2) purīṣabhakṣaṇaṃcaiva dīnānāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām | grāmyāṇāṃ dīnavapuṣāṃ pradhānyastanitāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.2) the eating of excrement by wretched deer and birds, and the thundering of domestic [animals] with emaciated bodies,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.3) vālukāṅgāradhānyānāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ vāpi vṛṣṭayaḥ | puradvāre ca bakavad vāyasānāṃ ca ceṣṭitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.3) showers of sand, embers, and grain, or eating [of the same]; the behavior of crows like herons at the city gate,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.4) biḍālamatsyamajjānāṃ jantūnāṃ kṣudrasaṃjñinām | anyonyabhakṣaṇāni syur ekasaṃsthāśca rātrayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.4) the mutual devouring among cats, fish, marrow-[creatures], and small-named insects; and nights of a single [unbroken] appearance —

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.5) māṃsasasyānnavidveṣaḥ kriyāvyuparamas tathā | yasmin deśe pradṛśyante tasmin kṣudbhayam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.5) aversion to flesh, crops, and food, and likewise the cessation of [normal] activities — in whichever land these are seen, one should predict famine and danger there.

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.6) śastrajvalanasaṃsarpaḥ sthūṇīsaraṇapūraṇam | chattravastradhvajānāṃ ca valmīkeṣu pradarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.6) The crawling of weapons and fire-brands, the filling [up] of pillars and pathways, and the appearance of parasols, garments, and banners on anthills,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.7) arke abhraparighādīnāṃ pariveṣo arkacandrayoḥ | lākṣālohitavarṇatvaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca vicāraṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.7) halos around the sun, [and] cloud-circles and such around the sun, halos around the Sun and Moon, a lac-red coloration of all, and [their] examination,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.8) tvacmāṃsarudhirāsthīnāṃ medomajjāsthivṛṣṭayaḥ | nirabhravṛṣṭayaścāsya rajatakṣatasaprabham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.8) showers of skin, flesh, blood, bones, fat, marrow, and bone-[fragments]; cloudless rain with the appearance of silver-wounded [light],

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.9) praghātākampanirghātāvidyutā cābhrapātanam | bhavecca devatādīnāṃ śiroabhiṣṭhānavarjanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.9) violent strikes, tremors, thunder, lightning, and the falling of clouds; and the abandonment and avoidance of deity-shrines and head-positions,

body.text: (AVParis_64,5.10) strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ ca prasavaṃ tṛṇādīnāṃ ca mānuṣam | amānuṣāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ bhāṣitāni manuṣyavat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.5.10) human-like births from women and men, and from grasses and the like; the speech of non-human beings in human fashion,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.1) vasāśoṇitagandhatvaṃ gajadaivatavājinām | yasmin deśe bhavet tasmin śastrakopabhayaṃ mahat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.1) the smell of fat and blood from elephants, deity-images, and horses — in whichever land this occurs, there is great danger of armed conflict.

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.2) śoṇitāśruparisrāvāḥ prahāsodvīkṣaṇakriyā | nṛtyavāditragītāni sākrośābhāṣitāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.2) Flows of blood and tears, the action of laughing and looking up, dancing, instrumental music, and singing, along with shouting and speaking,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.3) prakampanaṃ devatānāṃ tathaiva jvalanāni ca | apāṃ śoṣavikārāśca ceṣṭitaṃ ca manuṣyavat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.3) the trembling and blazing of deity-images likewise, the drying and alteration of waters, and human-like behavior —

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.4) daraṇaṃ rasanaṃ rājño vaikṛtyodvartanāni ca | kṣiteḥ kampaprahāsāśca rodanotkrośāani ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.4) the cracking and sweating of the king's [throne], distortions and upheavals, trembling and laughing of the earth, and weeping and crying out,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.5) pīṭhikāvyañjanaṃ chattra[m]śasatrakīlakamaṇḍalau | nīlāṅgalohitatalau udye arkaniśāakarau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.5) [the appearance of] pedestals, emblems, parasols, weapons, spikes, and circles; the Moon and Sun, when risen, with dark-blue limbs and red disks,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.6) candrārkolkāprabhedāśca bhāskarendudvayaṃ tathā | pratisrotavahā nadya iṣavaḥ pratikomagāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.6) the splitting of the Moon, Sun, and meteors, and [the appearance of] a double Sun and Moon; rivers flowing upstream, and arrows moving backwards,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.7) dantabhaṅgāḥ sakūrmāśca naravarṇavājinām | chattrabhaṅgāḥ sakūrmāśca naravāraṇavājinām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.7) the breaking of tusks and teeth, along with [pieces of] tortoise-shell, of men's [images], horses, and elephants; the breaking of parasols, along with tortoise-shells, of men, elephants, and horses,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.8) māṃsatailavipākaśca caityatailaparisravāḥ | śakradhvajapatākānāṃ bhaṅgakravyadasvanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.8) the cooking of flesh and oil, and the exuding of oil from shrines; the breaking of <s>Śakra</s>'s banner-flags and the cry of carrion-eaters,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.9) biḍalolūkyor yuddhaṃ nṛpaprāsādasaṃnidhau | pāṃsunā cāvṛtaṃ vyoma rajasā tamasāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.9) the fighting of cats and owls near the royal palace; the sky covered with dust, grime, or darkness,

body.text: (AVParis_64,6.10) lohitāgniprabhākāśaṃ dīptā dvijamṛgas tathā | vātāvartās tusaṃdhyāsu prasphuranto apasavyagāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.6.10) the sky [appearing] blood-red and fire-bright, and blazing birds and animals likewise; whirlwinds at the twilight junctions, sparking and moving leftward,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.1) maṇḍalāni samājāśca sarvato mṛgapakṣiṇām | kravyādair ārasadbhiśca vyākulāḥ sarvato diśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.1) circles and congregations of animals and birds on all sides; all directions disturbed by howling carrion-eaters,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.2) trirātrād aparaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ pranaṣṭendudivākarau | anṛtau cāpi dṛśyeta ghorastanitadīrghatā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.2) rain after three nights with the Moon and Sun having disappeared; and even out of season there is seen terrible prolonged thunder,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.3) vajrādayo rāhuputrā vṛkṣāḥ śakunayas tathā | maṇḍalābhyantarasthāśca bhavanti ravisomayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.3) the sons of <s>Rāhu</s> [such as] thunderbolts, trees, birds likewise, and those stationed within the circles of the Sun and Moon,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.4) ākāśe vā pradṛśyante prakampanti va parvatāḥ | viṣyeta ravisomau ca ābhīkṣaṃ tārakās tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.4) or [they] are seen in the sky, or mountains tremble; the Sun, Moon, and stars appear repeatedly —

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.5) naradanaṃ ca biḍālāṇāṃ kṣīravṛkṣaniṣevaṇam | kharair dīptair ulūkaiśca rasadbhiḥ saha vigrahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.5) the roaring of cats, [their] frequenting of milk-trees; [along with] blazing donkeys and owls, together with howling [jackals], [there is] conflict.

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.6) siṃhāsanāni chattrāṇi bhṛṅgārāḥ śayanās tathā | kampanti akasmād bhajyante saṃsarpanti ārasanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.6) Thrones, parasols, water-pitchers, and beds tremble suddenly, break, crawl, and roar —

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.7) rājñāṃ bhayakaraṃ sarvam etad utpātalakṣaṇam | deśasya ca vijānīyād gargasya vacanaṃ yathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.7) all this is a portent-sign causing fear for kings; one should understand [the effect on] the land, as is the statement of <s>Garga</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.8) saṃdhyādaṇḍapariveṣā rajoarkaparighādayaḥ | maṇḍalānāṃ samūhāśca dikṣu pītāruṇaprabhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.8) Twilight-staffs, halos, dust-[clouds], sun-circles, and the like; clusters of circles in the directions, with yellow and reddish radiance,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.9) kravyādā vānarā dvāri visphūrjanti ārasanti ca | tuṇḍaiśca vāyasā bhūmiṃ kuṭṭayanto ramanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.9) carrion-eaters and monkeys at the gate sparking and howling; crows striking the earth with their beaks and amusing themselves,

body.text: (AVParis_64,7.10) mlāyate mālyam atyarthaṃ gandhāḥ kuṇapagandhinaḥ | vastreṣu bhakṣabhojyeṣu bhavati utpātalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.7.10) garlands wilting excessively, fragrances smelling of corpses; in garments and food-offerings, there appears the mark of a portent.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.1) kṣaudraṃ ghṛtaṃ ca dadhi ca prasravet prathitā drumāḥ | sārameyāḥ śmaśāneṣu rudanti viruvanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.1) Honey, ghee, and curds exude from famous trees; dogs weep and howl in cremation grounds.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.2) etad autpātikaṃ grāme yasmiṃś ca dṛśyate pure | tasmin grāme pure vāpi vidyād atibhayaṃ mahat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.2) This portent-phenomenon — in whatever village or city it is seen — in that village or city, one should know that very great fear [is imminent].

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.3) aśvatthodumbaraplakṣanyagrodhe kusumodbhavaḥ | śvetalohitapītāni kṛṣṇānīndrāyudhāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.3) The flowering of the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>Plakṣa</s> (wavy-leafed fig), and <s>Nyagrodha</s> (banyan) — white, red, yellow, and dark flowers, and [those resembling] rainbows —

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.4) evaṃ varṇaduṇānāṃ ca patanaṃ devaveśmanām | brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdravināśo rājasaṃvṛtām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.4) according to the qualities of such colors, and the falling of deity-temples — destruction of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, <s>Vaiśya</s>s, and <s>Śūdra</s>s, and [the land becomes] enveloped by the king's [enemies].

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.5) rūkṣasrāvā citivṛkṣe tadbhayaṃ sumahad bhavet | ghṛtakṣīraphalāśrāve ghṛtakṣīrāmbhasāṃ kṣayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.5) Rough exudation from a funeral-pyre tree — that danger is very great; when ghee, milk, or fruit exudes, [there is] loss of ghee, milk, and water.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.6) surāśrāve mithobhedo rudhire rāṣṭravidravaḥ | rudhire goviṣāṇācca srute gobrāhmaṇakṣayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.6) When liquor exudes, mutual discord; when blood [exudes], the flight of the kingdom; when blood flows from a cow's horn, destruction of cows and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.7) phale phalaṃ yadā paśyet puṣpe puṣpaṃ samāvṛtam | garbhāḥ sravanti nārīṇāṃ yuddhaṃ rājavadho api vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.7) When one sees fruit within fruit, or a flower enveloped within a flower — women miscarry, and there is war or even the death of a king.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.8) phaṇābhṛto mahatsarpān maṇḍūlā atha vṛścikāḥ | maṇḍūkā grasate yatra tatra rājāvahanyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.8) Where frogs swallow great hooded serpents, scorpions, or toads — there a king is slain.

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.9) himapātānilotpātā vikṛtādbhutadarśanam | kṛṣṇāñjanābhram ākāśaṃ tārolkāpātapiṅgalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.9) Snowfall, wind-calamities, and the appearance of distorted marvels; the sky [like] dark collyrium-clouds, tawny from falling stars and meteors,

body.text: (AVParis_64,8.10) citrā garbhodbhavāḥ strīṣu goajāśvamṛgapakṣiṣu | pattrāṅkuralatānāṃ ca vikārāḥ śiśire śubhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.8.10) marvelous births in women, cows, goats, horses, deer, and birds; and the auspicious anomalies of leaves, shoots, and creepers in winter,

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.1) vajrāśanimahīkampāḥ saṃdhyānirghātanisvanāḥ | pariveṣarajodhūmā raktārkāstamanodayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.1) thunderbolts, lightning, and earthquakes; twilight-thunderclaps; halos, dust, and smoke; red [color at] sunset and sunrise of the sun —

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.2) drumebhyo annarasasnehamadhupuṣpaphalodgamāḥ | gopakṣiśabdavṛddhiśca śivāni madhumādhave ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.2) the emergence of food, sap, oil, honey, flowers, and fruit from trees; the increase of cow and bird sounds — these are auspicious in the spring (<s>Madhu-Mādhava</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.3) tārolkāpātakaluṣaṃ kapilārkendumaṇḍalam | anagnijvalanasphoṭadhūmareṇvanilāhatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.3) [The sky] turbid from falling stars and meteors, tawny disks of Sun and Moon, fireless burning, bursting, smoke, dust, and wind-strikes,

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.4) raktapītāruṇāṃ saṃdhyāṃ nabhaḥ saṃkṣubhītārṇavam | saritāṃ cāmbusaṃśoṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā grīṣme śubhaṃ vadet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.4) red-yellow-ruddy twilight, sky like a churned ocean, and the drying up of river waters — seeing these in summer, one should declare [them] auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.5) śakrāyudhaparīveṣavidyutśuṣkavirohaṇam | akasmād varṇavaikṛtyaṃ rasanaṃ daraṇaṃ kṣiteḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.5) Rainbows, halos, lightning, dry vegetation, sudden color-changes, sweating, and cracking of the earth,

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.6) saronadyudapānānāṃ vṛddhir vā uttaraṇaplavāḥ | taraṇaṃ cārdravegānāṃ varṣāsu na bhayāvaham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.6) the increase of lakes, rivers, and wells, or overflows and floods; the crossing of swift currents — in the rainy season, [these are] not fear-producing.

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.7) divyastrīgītagandharvavimānādbhutanisvanāḥ | grahanakṣatratārāṇāṃ darśanaṃ ca divāmbare ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.7) The sounds of divine women singing, <s>Gandharva</s>s, celestial chariots, and marvelous [beings]; the sighting of planets, <s>nakṣatra</s>s, and stars in the daytime sky,

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.8) gītavāditranirghoṣo vanaparvatasānuṣu | sasyavṛddhī rasotpattir na pāpāḥ śaradi smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.8) the sound of singing and instruments on mountain-ridges and forest-mountains; crop growth and the production of sap — [these] are not considered inauspicious in autumn.

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.9) śītānilatuṣāratvaṃ nardanaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām | rakṣoyakṣādisattvānāṃ darśanaṃ vāg amānuṣī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.9) Cold winds, frost, the roaring of deer and birds, the sighting of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, and other beings, and non-human speech,

body.text: (AVParis_64,9.10) dīptadhūmarajasdhvastā diṅnāgā vanaparvatāḥ | uccais toyadasomārkā hemante śobhanāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.9.10) directions, world-elephants, forests, and mountains blazing, smoky, dusty, and shattered; the clouds, Moon, and Sun [appearing] high — [these] are remembered as auspicious in early winter.

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.1) ṛtusvabhāvā ete hi dṛṣṭāḥ svartau śubhapradāḥ | ṛtau anyatra ca utpātā dṛṣṭāḥ svartau śubhapradāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.1) These indeed are of seasonal nature; seen in their own season, they are auspicious. [But if] portents are seen in a different season, [even those] seen in their own season [are then re-evaluated as] auspicious [only if in their proper time].

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.2) unmattānāṃ ca yā gāthā bālānāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ ca yat | striyaśca yat prabhāṣante tatra nāsti vyatikramaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.2) The songs of the mad, the actions of children, and what women say — in these there is no transgression [i.e., they are reliable portents].

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.3) pūrvaṃ vadati deveṣu paścād gacchati mānuṣe | nācoditā āg vadati satyā hi eṣā sarasvatī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.3) She speaks first among the gods, and afterwards goes among humans; she does not speak unprompted — for this <s>Sarasvatī</s> is truthful.

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.4) utpātāḥ sarva eva ete kadācid rājamṛtyave | jñeyā deśavināśāya rāhor āgamanāyā vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.4) All these portents sometimes [indicate] the death of a king; they should be known as [portending] the destruction of a region or the approach of <s>Rāhu</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.5) kālāmbudaparisrāvā grahāṇām udayāya vā | svacakraparacakrebhyo bhaye vā samupasthite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.5) The overflow of dark clouds [indicates] the rising of planets; or when danger arises from one's own forces or from enemy forces,

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.6) rāṣṭre senāpatau putre pure vātha purodhasi | amātye vāhane dāre nṛpatau vā palanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.6) [the portents] manifest regarding the kingdom, the commander-in-chief, the prince, the city, the royal priest, the minister, the vehicle, the wife, or the king.

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.7) etān samutthitāṃ jñātvā rājā sabalavāhanaḥ | praṇipatya guruṃ brūyād bhagavan śamayasva me ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.7) Having recognized these [portents] as they arise, the king, together with his army and vehicles, should prostrate before the preceptor and say: 'O Blessed One, bring me peace!'

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.8) bhayam utpātajaṃ sarvaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te | iti uktaḥ śraddadhānena rājñā svahitam icchatā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.8) 'Quell all fear born of portents; tell me what I should do for you.' Thus addressed by the faithful king who desires his own welfare,

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.9) nimittāni samālokya kṛtvā pāvanam āditaḥ | mahāśāntiṃ prayuñjīta sarvopadravanāśinīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.9) [the priest], having examined the omens and performed purification from the beginning, should employ the great pacification rite (<s>mahāśānti</s>) that destroys all calamities,

body.text: (AVParis_64,10.10) sarvarogapraśamanīm utpātaphalanāśinīm | raudrīṃ kuryān mahāśāntiṃ śraddhayā bahudakṣiṇāṃ śraddhayā bahudakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 64.10.10) that which quells all diseases and destroys the effects of portents. One should perform the great <s>Raudrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Rudra</s>) pacification rite with faith and abundant ritual fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_65. sadyovṛṣṭilakṣaṇam)
(AVParis_65,1.1) om atha ato lakṣaṇopāṅge sadyovṛṣṭilakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 65: Signs of Immediate Rainfall) (AVParis 65.1.1) Oṃ. Now, in the supplementary section on signs, we shall explain the signs of immediate rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.2) snigdhavimalataladarśane 'rciṣmaty atitejasi sthūlaraśmau harijvalanasaṃnibhe savitari sadyo varṣati parjanyo viśuddhāsu ca dikṣu kākāṇḍavarṇeṣu giriṣv atirajaskandheṣu hradamagneṣu vimalavipulasnigdhaprasannahṛṣṭapradarśaneṣu nīcair iva jyotirgaṇeṣv anukūleṣu śive śite nīce mārute bhavati cātra ślokaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.2) When the sun appears with an unctuous, clear surface, radiant, exceedingly brilliant, with thick rays, resembling a blazing green fire — <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) rains immediately. And when the directions are clear, the mountains are crow-egg colored with abundant dust-ridges, the lakes are cloudless, clear, expansive, unctuous, serene, and joyful in appearance, the hosts of stars appear as if low, the winds are favorable, auspicious, cool, and low — there is a verse on this:

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.3) pūrvo 'bhrajanamo vāyur itaro 'bhravināśanaḥ | udag janayate vṛṣṭiṃ varṣaty eva ca dakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.3) The east wind generates clouds, while the other (west wind) destroys clouds; the north wind generates rain, and the south wind indeed brings rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.4) abhreṣu timiramakaranaganāganakragrāhaśiṃśumāraśaṅkhadrumakūrmormijhaṣamahiṣavarāhadigdviradanavakumudakhaṇḍākṛtinalakalaśakuḍmalāpīḍatoraṇāvartasvastikavardhamānaravauhvarajatamadrāṇipatākāśvatātyāsthānavividhajalacarapakṣivirutacatuṣpadākāreṣu naktanīlotpalakamalapalāśakomaleṣu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.4) [One should predict immediate rain] when clouds have shapes of darkness, <s>makara</s>s (sea-monsters), serpents, <s>nāga</s>s, crocodiles, <s>grāha</s>s (seizers), dolphins, conches, trees, turtles, waves, fish, buffaloes, boars, directional elephants, clusters of fresh <s>kumuda</s> lotuses, sections of water-pots, buds, crowns, archways, whirlpools, <s>svastika</s>s, <s>vardhamāna</s>s, sounds of camels, silver, banners, flags, horse-stations, various aquatic creatures, bird-calls, and quadruped forms — soft as night-lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>), day-lotuses (<s>kamala</s>), and <s>palāśa</s> leaves.

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.5) [muktā]sphaṭikarajatavaiḍuryāñjanabhramarasarpasaṃnikāśeṣu | kṣaudrakṣīrapalāśadhūma[dūrvā]rajatakanakavidrumaprabheṣ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.5) Resembling [pearls,] crystal, silver, lapis lazuli (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>), collyrium, bees, and serpents; with the radiance of honey, milk, <s>palāśa</s>, smoke, [<s>dūrvā</s> grass,] silver, gold, and coral.

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.6) dviguṇatriguṇadarśaneṣu mūlavatsu viśikhareṣu mahāvarteṣu taralarathanemighoṣeṣu udadhijalanirghoṣasaṃhrādeṣu kṣubdhadundubhininādeṣu kiñjalkāravindasaṃnibheṣu vā kumudamayūragalakālakeṣu cābhrajālāvanādeṣu chinnābhreṣu vā chinnamūleṣu kāleṣu kāñcanamanahśiloupameṣu suvarṇapūrṇeṣu jaleṣv asmin na cābhyantarato deśaśobhiteṣu dakṣiṇamāruteritaparitate grahāntargatastanitagambhīranisvaneṣu ardhāntareṣu sadyovarṣam ādiśet || atra ślokau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.6) When [clouds appear] doubled or tripled in visibility, rooted, with spreading peaks, with great whirlpools, with sounds like trembling chariot-rims, with reverberations like the roar of ocean waters, with the rumbling of agitated drums, resembling the filaments of lotuses, or dark as <s>kumuda</s> lotuses and peacock-necks — with roaring cloud-masses, or with broken clouds, or broken at the roots, at times resembling gold and realgar, filled with golden [hues], in waters not made beautiful from within, driven and scattered by the south wind, with deep thundering sounds within the planets — [in] half-intervals, one should predict immediate rain. Here are two verses:

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.7) udayāstamaye meghā garbhabhūtā divākare | pradīptā iva citrāsu viṣamāsu khakoṭiṣu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.7) At sunrise and sunset, clouds pregnant [with rain], around the sun, blazing as if in the brilliant [stars], in the uneven corners of the sky,

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.8) pañca mārutaparyaṅkā maṇayaḥ kāñcanā iva | yatrayatropalakṣyante tatratatra pravarṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.8) five [clouds] resting on the wind like couches, [shining] like golden gems — wherever these are observed, there it rains.

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.9) ghananicayaṃ virohaṇe vādhirohaṇāstagamane vā savitur dṛṣṭvā ca varṣad udadhijīvarādrariṣṭakavaiḍūryotpalakamalapalāśadhūmaśevālavadhrajabakasaṃnikāśasnigdhaghoṣagambhīragabhastividvanbhaiḥ pravṛddhaiḥ samārutān vañcibhiḥ pravṛddhaskandhaśākhānvitapāvanitalaruhān sadyovarṣam ādiśet || atra ślokau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.9) Having seen a mass of clouds at the rising or the mounting or setting of the sun, and [observing them as] unctuous, deep-sounding, and richly-rayed, resembling ocean creatures, ruddy [minerals], lapis lazuli, lotuses, <s>palāśa</s> leaves, smoke, moss, and herons — growing, with wind, with deceptive [movements], having grown trunks and branches, rooted on pure ground — one should predict immediate rain. Here are two verses:

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.10) antarājitadīptāgnikāñcanāmalasaṃnibhaiḥ | abhraiś cotpalavaidūryaprabhāvāñjanasaṃnibhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.10) With clouds resembling internally conquered blazing fire and pure gold, and resembling lotus, lapis lazuli radiance, and collyrium,

body.text: (AVParis_65,1.11) nīlarśmiprarohantaḥ śākhāvanta iva drumāḥ | yatrayatra pradṛśyante dhruvaṃ tara pravarṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.1.11) sprouting blue rays, like trees with branches — wherever these are seen, certainly there it rains.

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.1) saṃdhyā ca jvalanaravīndīvarakaraṇdatapanīyārkodayaharitālanīlotpalaghṛtamadhubandhujīvakajapāpuṣpakiṃśukarāśisaṃnikāśā tathā drutakanakavidrumasphaṭikavaiḍūryavarṇam uddyotayanti diśaḥ śāntamṛgaśakuniviśeṣāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.1) And when the twilight resembles flame, the sun, blue lotuses, baskets, heated gold, sunrise, yellow orpiment, blue lotuses, ghee, honey, <s>bandhujīvaka</s> flowers, <s>japā</s> flowers, and heaps of <s>kiṃśuka</s> [blossoms]; and [clouds] illuminate the directions with the color of molten gold, coral, crystal, and lapis lazuli; and when animals and birds are peacefully disposed —

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.2) kiṃtanā snigdhā ghanā gabhastimālini saṃprati saṃdhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā nīcair nirmalasnigdhaparidhipariveṣābhravṛkṣapratisūryakā lohitākṣapakṣiptā sārdhaṃ pañcakāvaliptaiś ca mahiṣavṛṣavarāhādidviradajalagaṇair ivācaritaviṣayā atra ślokaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.2) How unctuous and dense [are the clouds] around the garland of rays? Having seen the twilight at a low position, with clear, unctuous halos, coronas, cloud-trees, and mock-suns thrown by the red-eyed [sun], along with five painted [features], and [the sky appearing] as if traversed by groups of water-buffaloes, bulls, boars, elephants, and aquatic creatures — here is a verse:

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.3) sāṃdhyaiś ca pariveṣaiś ca pratighaiḥ pratisūryakaiḥ | jalajaiś cāvṛtānindyaiḥ sadyaḥ saṃdhyā pravarṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.3) With twilight-coronas, with halos, with counter-gleams, with mock-suns, surrounded by flawless water-born [signs] — the twilight [indicates] immediate rainfall.

body.text:
(AVParis_65,2.4) yathālakṣaṇaṃ śastrakāṃsyatāmrāyasānāṃ kledavatāṃ khadyotāni || tatra svedanti kāmahurdhunināś ca uttaṭaprākāragopuragṛhāgādhirohaṇapāṃsusnānam aṇḍajānām
(AVParis_65,2.5) pracaraṇe taḍāgakūpān setubandhākrītāś ca śiśūnāṃ dṛṣṭvā prasaṃkhyāyāś ca citrāviśākhāsvātibahulāṣāḍhāhirbudhnyayāmyasya saṃgrahasaṃpāteṣu mahadvarṣasaṃvṛte ca tryahād ūrdhvaṃ cātra ślokau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.4-5) According to the signs, the moistening of iron, bronze, copper, and steel [objects; also] fireflies [appear] there; they sweat with desire; and [there is] bathing in dust by birds [who climb] river-banks, ramparts, gate-towers, and house-rooftops; and having seen the playing of children in ponds and wells, un-purchased [games]; and at the conjunctions and encounters of [the <s>nakṣatra</s>s] <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Bahulā</s> (Kṛttikā), <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> (Uttarabhādrapadā), and <s>Yāmya</s> (Bharaṇī); and when great rain is imminent, after three days — here are two verses:

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.6) ākrīḍāś caiva matsyānāṃ gavāṃ dṛṣṭvāgamo gṛham | prācuryadaṃśamaśakair dhiṣṇyānāṃ cātha mokṣeṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.6) The playful activities of fish, and the cows' return home; abundance of biting insects and mosquitoes, and the release of [shooting] stars —

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.7) jalājalajasaṃtānān ekatra bilavāsinām | pipīlikāṇḍasaṃkrāntir athoṣṇaṃ cāmbu vṛṣṭaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.7) The migration of ant-eggs of water-dwelling and land-dwelling creatures to one place, from hole-dwellers; and warm water — [these are signs] of rain.

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.8) satkṛtya ca daivajñaṃ palvalakūpataḍāganadītīre || sāddālagṛheṣu deśeṣv ārdravāsārdrapāṇiḥ prṛcchet || sadyovarṣam adiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.8) Having honored the astrologer, at the bank of a pool, well, pond, or river, in places with <s>śāla</s>-tree groves, one should ask [him] with wet clothes and wet hands. He should predict immediate rainfall.

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.9) diśy aiśānyāṃ vā madhurasvarariṣṭavyāharaṇaṃ jalagotrasābhūtaṃ talliṅgānām antarālaṃ bālānāṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā varṣatīti brūyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.9) In the northeastern direction, hearing the sweet-voiced inauspicious utterances of those born of water-lineage and spirits, the signs thereof, [and] the intervals [between them] of young [creatures] — having heard and seen [these], one should say 'It will rain.'

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.10) rātristanito divā vidyudbhir vādyamākṣetre varṇaḥ snigdho dviguṇendracāpa darśane vyomni nirabhre paśuvirāvābhradaṇḍābhasvalpāñ cābhrarājiprādurbhāvaiḥ sadyovṛṣṭir atra ślokāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.10) When it thunders at night [and there is] lightning by day, in a wild-rice field the color is unctuous; when a double rainbow is seen in the cloudless sky; with animal cries, cloud-columns, small radiant cloud-streaks appearing — [these indicate] immediate rain. Here are verses:

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.11) pratisūryako bhaved yas tu raver uttarato yadā | toyaṃ nivārayen nityaṃ dakṣiṇe salilād bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.11) When there is a mock-sun to the north of the sun, it always wards off water; [but] to the south, there is danger from water.

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.12) tridhā nimittasaṃpannā vṛṣṭir bhavati pārthivī | nimitte tāvad ekasmin pañcayojanikaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.12) Endowed with signs in three ways, terrestrial rainfall occurs; with just one sign, it would extend five <s>yojana</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_65,2.13) yeṣuyeṣu nimitteṣu nakṣatreṣu ca vartmani | praśastam iti teṣv eva prādurbhūteṣu varṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.2.13) In whichever signs, in whichever <s>nakṣatra</s>s and paths [they are] declared as auspicious — when those very [signs] appear, it rains.

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.1) viparyayanimittāni pratibandhakarāṇi tu | teṣu śāntiṃ prakurvīta atharvā śamanāya vai ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.1) Signs that are contrary are obstructive; for those, one should perform the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Atharvavedic) pacification rite for quelling [the adverse effects].

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.2) sam ut patantu sūktena pra nabhasveti cāpare | vaitasyaḥ samidho 'nye tu śamīmayyo 'pare viduḥ ||
