body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.2) 'May they fly up together' — with this <s>sūkta</s> (hymn); and others [use] 'Pra nabhasva' (Forth, O cloud!); some [use] fuel-sticks of cane; others know [them to be] of <s>śamī</s> wood.

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.3) [samidhāṃ vaitasīnāṃ tu agnāv arkendhanāhute | ahorātrikahomaḥ syāt parjanyo bahuvarṣadaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.3) [With fuel-sticks of cane, offered into the fire with <s>arka</s>-plant fuel, performing a day-and-night oblation — <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) grants abundant rain.]

body.text:
(AVParis_65,3.4) sam ut patantu sūktena maruto yajate pākayajñavidhānena yathā varuṇaṃ vṛṣṭikāmaḥ || pra nabhasvety ṛcau dve maruto yajate vṛṣṭikāmo yathā varuṇaṃ juhoti ||]
(AVParis_65,3.5) ādadhyāt samidhaḥ plākṣīḥ sakṣīrā ghṛtasaṃyutāḥ | tatas tac chamam āyāti kṛtsnam utpātalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.4-5) ['May they fly up together' — with this <s>sūkta</s>, one worships the <s>Marut</s>s by the <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) procedure, as one desiring rain [worships] <s>Varuṇa</s>. 'Pra nabhasva' — with these two <s>ṛc</s>s, one worships the <s>Marut</s>s; desiring rain, one offers to <s>Varuṇa</s>.] One should place fuel-sticks of <s>plakṣa</s> (fig tree), containing sap, mixed with ghee; then all the portent-signs are pacified.

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.6) aindrīṃ vā vāruṇīṃ vāpi mahāśāntiṃ vidhānataḥ | varṣādau tu prayuñjīta avṛṣṭes tu vināśanīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.6) One should employ the <s>Aindrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>) or <s>Vāruṇī</s> (pertaining to <s>Varuṇa</s>) great pacification rite according to the prescribed procedure at the beginning of the rainy season, as the destroyer of drought.

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.7) vṛṣṭer yāni nimittāni tāny apratihatāni tu | bhavanti vṛṣṭidāyīni sasyavṛddhikarāṇi tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.7) Those signs of rain that are unobstructed — they become rain-giving and promoters of crop growth.

body.text: (AVParis_65,3.8) vaitasānāṃ tu pattrāṇāṃ lakṣaṃ kṣīrasamāyutam | vratānte bhārgavo juhvad avarṣāsv api varṣayed iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 65.3.8) One hundred thousand leaves of cane, mixed with milk — <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Śukra</s>), offering [these] at the conclusion of the vow, would cause rain even during droughts.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_66. gośāntiḥ)
(AVParis_66,1.1) oṃ bhagavan devadeveśa surāsuranamaskṛta | gavāṃ sarveṣu rogeṣu pratijñāteṣu vai prabho ||
body.translated_text: (<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 66: Pacification Rite for Cattle) (AVParis 66.1.1) Oṃ. 'O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods of Gods, worshipped by gods and demons! When all diseases of cattle have been declared, O Lord,

body.text: (AVParis_66,1.2) kathaṃ śāntiṃ dvijaḥ kuryāt kena mantreṇa prokṣaṇam | homamantrāś ca ke proktāḥ kasmiṃs tantre prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.1.2) how should a twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) perform the pacification rite? With what <s>mantra</s> is the sprinkling? What oblation-<s>mantra</s>s are prescribed, and in which ritual system (<s>tantra</s>) should [they] be employed?'

body.text: (AVParis_66,1.3) uvāca paripṛṣṭaḥ san brahmā sarvajagatpatiḥ | śṛṇvantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve gośāntiṃ mahaduttamām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.1.3) Thus questioned, <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of all worlds, spoke: 'May all the sages listen to the great and supreme pacification rite for cattle,

body.text: (AVParis_66,1.4) atharvavihitāṃ samyak sarvarogavināśanīm | yāṃ śrutvā savarogās tu vidravanti sahasraśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.1.4) properly ordained by the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, the destroyer of all diseases; hearing which, all diseases flee by the thousands.'

body.text: (AVParis_66,1.5) goṣṭhamadhye gṛhe vāpi govāṭe gokulāntile | ācāryas tu śucir bhūtvā kārayen maṇḍalaṃ śubham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.1.5) In the middle of a cow-pen, or in a house, or in a cattle-enclosure, or at the border of a herd — the preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>), having become pure, should have an auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s> (diagram) drawn.

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.1) snātaś cāhatavāsāś ca ahorātroṣitaḥ śuciḥ | caturaśraṃ caturdvāram ālikhet tatra maṇḍalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.1) Having bathed, wearing fresh garments, having fasted for a day and night, pure — one should draw there a square <s>maṇḍala</s> with four doors.

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.2) tasya madhye tu deveśaṃ gomayena nidhāpayet | tataḥ kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva gugguluṃ candanāgurum ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.2) In its center, one should place [an image of] the Lord of Gods with cow-dung; then [one should prepare] milk, ghee, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin), sandalwood, and <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood),

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.3) puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni tathā vai sarṣapāṃs tilān | lājāś ca samidhaś caiva samāhṛtya vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.3) fragrant flowers, and also mustard seeds and sesame seeds, parched grain and fuel-sticks — the discerning one should gather [all these].

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.4) prāṇāṃs tu tarpayet tatra dadhikṣīraghṛtādibhiḥ | tataḥ śāntiṃ prayuñjita namaskṛtvā svayaṃbhuvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.4) One should make offerings to the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>s) there with curds, milk, ghee, and the like; then one should perform the pacification rite, having paid homage to the Self-existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>).

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.5) ājyabhāgāntājyatantram abhyātānāni caiva hi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.5) [The ritual follows] the ghee-oblation system up to the ghee-portions, and also the extension-offerings.

body.text: (AVParis_66,2.6) namojñāya sureśāya namas te viśvatomukha | namaḥ kālāya tīkṣṇāya [jaṭilāya] sarvabhūtahitāya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.2.6) 'Homage to the All-knowing One, the Lord of the Gods! Homage to You, O Universal-faced One! Homage to <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the Sharp One, [the Matted-haired One,] and the Benefactor of all beings!'

body.text: (AVParis_66,3.1) tataḥ sarṣapatilalājā ūrdhvāḥ samidhaś ca dadhimadhughṛtāktā juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.3.1) Then one should offer mustard seeds, sesame, parched grain upward, and fuel-sticks anointed with curds, honey, and ghee.

body.text: (AVParis_66,3.2) yajāmi || kālāya svāhā || piṅgalāya tīkṣṇāya jaṭilāya babhrave oṃ bhūr oṃ bhuva oṃ svar oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar jayavijayāya jayādhipataye kapardine karālāya vikaṭāya kaṭiramāṭarāyāṅgirasabārhaspatyakakapilamaṇḍalamuṇḍajaṭilakapāleśvarādhipataye kapardine svāheti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.3.2) 'I worship! To <s>Kāla</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Tawny One, the Sharp One, the Matted-haired One, the Brown One — Oṃ <s>bhūḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>svaḥ</s>, Oṃ <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s> — to the Victorious Conqueror, the Lord of Victory, the Crested One, the Terrible One, the Deformed One, <s>Kaṭiramāṭara</s>, the Lord of <s>Āṅgirasa</s>-<s>Bārhaspatya</s>-<s>Kapila</s>-circle-shaven-matted-skull Lords, the Crested One — <s>svāhā</s>!'

body.text: (AVParis_66,3.3) eṣa karmasu tu gośānteḥ saṃsṛṣṭa ṛṣibhiḥ purā | proktā svayaṃbhuvā caiṣā gośāntis tu hitāya vai ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.3.3) This [ritual] in the rites of cattle-pacification was combined [with other rites] by the sages of old; this cattle-pacification rite, spoken by the Self-existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>), is indeed for [their] welfare.

body.text: (AVParis_66,3.4) yo vipraḥ paṭhatīmāṃ hi gokule cāpi hitāya vai | gāvas tasya pravardhante mahatīṃ cāśnute śriyam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 66.3.4) Whichever <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> recites this in a cattle-herd, indeed for [their] welfare — his cattle prosper, and he attains great prosperity.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_67. adbhutaśāntiḥ)
(AVParis_67,1.1) oṃ puruṣas putradāraṃ vā dhanadhānyam atha api vā | nimittair yair vinaśyeta śāntiṃ tatra nibodhata ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 67: Pacification of Portents)
(AVParis 67.1.1) Oṃ. A person, or his sons and wife, or wealth and grain — learn the pacification for those omens by which [these] are destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.2) indrāyudhaṃ bhavet rātrau dṛśyate yasya kasya cit | darvī kare vā bhidyeta maṇis kumbhas tathā eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.2) If <s>Indra</s>'s weapon (a rainbow) appears at night and is seen by anyone; or if a ladle breaks in one's hand, and likewise a jewel or a pot;

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.3) chattraṃ śayyā āsanaṃ ca eva anyat vā api svayaṃ kva cit | strī hanyāt ca striyaṃ vā api gaur avaghret ulūkhalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.3) An umbrella, a bed, a seat, or anything else [breaks] spontaneously somewhere; or a woman strikes another woman; or a cow sniffs at a mortar;

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.4) śvā pidet gām anaḍvāhaṃ kalis saṃpadyate kule | gajavājino mriyante vivādo rājakīyakas ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.4) A dog bites a cow or an ox; strife arises in the family; elephants and horses die; there is a dispute involving the king;

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.5) kuṭumbam aśubhaṃ sarvam aindrāṇi etāni nirdiśet | śāmyanti yena sarvāṇi nirvapet pāyasaṃ carum ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.5) All of the household [becomes] inauspicious — one should declare these as pertaining to <s>Indra</s>. That by which all [portents] are pacified: one should cook a <s>caru</s> (oblation porridge) of milk-rice.

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.6) samāvaoya ghṛtaṃ tatra āhutiṃ jihuyāt imām | indram id devatātaye sthālīpākasya homayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.6) Having mixed ghee therein, one should offer this oblation: 'To <s>Indra</s> alone, for the worship of the deity' — one should offer a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked oblation).

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.7) indras śacīpatis śakro vajrapāṇis sureāśvaras | sarvādbhutānāṃ śamano mahāvyāhṛtayas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.7) '<s>Indra</s>, husband of <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, thunderbolt-handed, lord of the gods, pacifier of all portents' — and the <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>s (great utterances) likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_67,1.8) hutvā sviṣṭakṛtaṃ ca eva carutantraṃ samāpayet | vimuktotpātadoṣas tu jīvet tu śaradas śatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.1.8) Having offered the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (right-making offering) as well, one should complete the <s>caru</s> ceremony. Freed from the fault of portents, one would live a hundred autumns.

body.text: (AVParis_67,2.1) uddīpikā gṛhe yasya valmīkā madhujālakam | abjānāṃ maṇike śabde tailaṃ sthīyata eva vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.2.1) In whose house there are fireflies, anthills, or a honeycomb; sounds in water-jars; or oil stands [by itself];

body.text: (AVParis_67,2.2) aśubhā vikṛtir dadhnāṃ dugdhānāṃ vā yadā bhavet | akasmāt ca praroheyur bījāni kṛmayas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.2.2) When there is an inauspicious transformation of curds or milk; and seeds or worms sprout without cause;

body.text: (AVParis_67,2.3) kāryo varuṇayāgas tu vāruṇīvidhipūrvakas | ud uttamaṃ pradhānaṃ syāt pañcājyāhutayas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.2.3) A sacrifice to <s>Varuṇa</s> should be performed, preceded by the <s>Vāruṇī</s> ritual; the chief [verse] should be '<s>ud uttamam</s>'; and five ghee-oblations likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_67,2.4) varuṇas pāśapāṇis ca yadāsāṃ patir eva ca | śe.aṃ tu pūrvavat ca eva carutantraṃ samāpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.2.4) '<s>Varuṇa</s>, holder of the noose, and lord of waters' — the rest as before, one should complete the <s>caru</s> ceremony.

body.text: (AVParis_67,2.5) vimuktotpātadoṣas tu jīvet tu śaradas śatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.2.5) Freed from the fault of portents, one would live a hundred autumns.

body.text: (AVParis_67,3.1) gṛhe yasya patet gṛdhra ulūko vā kathaṃ cana | kapotas praviśet ca eva jīvā vā araṇyasaṃbhavās ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.3.1) In whose house a vulture or an owl falls somehow, or a pigeon enters, or creatures born in the forest [enter];

body.text: (AVParis_67,3.2) dhuryau ca patato yuktau gostrījanma ca vaikṛtam | jāyante yamalāni eva ghoras svapnas ca dṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.3.2) And yoked draft-animals fall; and there is a monstrous birth among cows, women, or people; twins are born; and a terrible dream is seen;

body.text: (AVParis_67,3.3) abhidravanti rakṣāṃsi yatra ca eva kumārakān | unnidrako atunidro vā atyalpam atibhojanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.3.3) And <s>Rākṣasa</s>s (demons) attack children; and [one is] sleepless or excessively sleepy; eating too little or eating too much;

body.text: (AVParis_67,3.4) ālasya ca evam eteṣāṃ devatā yama ucyate | nāke suparṇam iti etat sthālīpākasya homayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.3.4) And lethargy — the deity of these is said to be <s>Yama</s>. With '<s>nāke suparṇam</s>' — one should offer a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked oblation).

body.text: (AVParis_67,3.5) yamas pretapatis ca eva daṇḍapāṇis tathā īśvaras | śamanaḥ sarvādbhutānām... ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.3.5) '<s>Yama</s>, lord of the dead, rod-bearing, ruler, pacifier of all portents...'

body.text: (AVParis_67,4.1) anagnir utthito yasya dhūmo vā api gṛhe kva cit | āmaṃ vā jvalate māṃsaṃ bhaveyur visphuliṅgakās ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.4.1) If in anyone's house smoke arises without fire, or anywhere; or raw meat blazes; or there are sparks;

body.text: (AVParis_67,4.2) chattradhvajapatākās ca jvalante toraṇāni ca || āsanaṃ ca eva ;ayyā ca vastrāṇi kusumāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.4.2) And umbrellas, banners, flags, and arched gateways blaze; and seats, beds, garments, and flowers [blaze];

body.text: (AVParis_67,4.3) hastyaśvānāṃ ca pucchāni varṣatyaṅgāravarṣaṇam | akāle ca diśāṃ dāha oṣadhīnāṃ ca pācanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.4.3) And the tails of elephants and horses [blaze]; there is a rain of embers; and out of season, burning of the directions and ripening of herbs;

body.text: (AVParis_67,4.4) hastinyas ca eva madyante agnirūpaṃ tad adbhutam | agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe sthālīpākasya homayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.4.4) And female elephants go into rut — that portent has the form of fire. With '<s>Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe</s>' (We choose <s>Agni</s> as messenger) — one should offer a <s>sthālīpāka</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_67,4.5) agnir hiraṇyapatis ca arciṣpāṇis tathā īśvaras | śamanas sarvādbhutānām... ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.4.5) '<s>Agni</s>, lord of gold, flame-handed, ruler, pacifier of all portents...'

body.text: (AVParis_67,5.1) suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vajraṃ vaiḍūryaṃ mauktikāni ca | pravālavastranāśas ca mitrāṇāṃ ca viparyayas ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.5.1) Gold, silver, diamond, cat's-eye, and pearls, and the destruction of coral and garments, and the reversal of friendships;

body.text: (AVParis_67,5.2) ārambhās ca vipadyante na soddhis karmaṇām api | carur vaiśravaṇas tatra abhi tyaṃ devam ṛk smṛtā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.5.2) And undertakings fail, and there is no success even in actions — [for these] a <s>caru</s> to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>); the <s>ṛk</s> (verse) prescribed is '<s>abhi tyaṃ devam</s>.'

body.text: (AVParis_67,5.3) vaiśravaṇo yakṣapatis arthapāṇis tathā īśvaras | śamanas sarvādbhutānām... ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.5.3) '<s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Yakṣa</s>s, wealth-handed, ruler, pacifier of all portents...'

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.1) atha yasya svanakṣatre ulkā nirghāta eva vā | rāhur grasati candrārkau kabandhaṃ darpaṇe bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.1) Now, if in one's own birth-constellation, a meteor or thunderclap [falls]; <s>Rāhu</s> eclipses the moon or sun; a headless trunk [appears] in a mirror;

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.2) patet svayaṃ vā musalaṃ devatā vā kathaṃ cana | unmīlate ca eva yadā tathā ca api nimīlate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.2) Or a pestle falls by itself; or a deity somehow opens its eyes when it [normally] has them closed, and also closes them [when open];

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.3) prachidyate ca yadi vā tathā vā api prakampate | prayāto vā api dṛśyeta pratisroto nadī vahet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.3) Or [a deity image] is split, or trembles; or a departed [person] is seen; or a river flows upstream;

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.4) vimale na eva arkachāyā pratīpā vā api tu sāyakās | pariveṣas tu anabhreṣu dṛśyate candrasūryayos ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.4) When the sky is clear there is no shadow of the sun; or arrows [fly] backwards; and a halo around the moon and sun is seen when there are no clouds;

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.5) kośāt khaḍgā nirgirante tūṇāt ca eva tu sāyakās | anāhatāni vādyante nadante śabdam āturam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.5) Swords emerge from sheaths, and arrows from quivers; unstruck musical instruments sound, emitting a plaintive sound;

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.6) caruṇā vaiṣṇavena eṣāṃ yāgas kartavyas eva tu | idaṃ viṣṇus pradhānaṃ syāt pañcājyāhutayas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.6) With a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s>) <s>caru</s>, a sacrifice should indeed be performed for these. '<s>idaṃ Viṣṇuḥ</s>' should be the chief [verse]; and five ghee-oblations likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_67,6.7) sarvabhūtapatis viṣnus cakrapāṇis tathā īśvaras | śamanas sarvādbhutānām... ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.6.7) '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of all beings, discus-handed, ruler, pacifier of all portents...'

body.text: (AVParis_67,7.1) ativāto yatra bhavet rūpaṃ vā yatra vaikṛtam | kharakarabhamahiṣā varāhā vyāghrasiṃhakās ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.7.1) Where there is excessive wind, or where there is a monstrous form — donkeys, camels, buffaloes, boars, tigers, and lions;

body.text: (AVParis_67,7.2) gṛdhrās ca tathā gomāyus kṛkalāsā vadanti ca | māṃsapeśaṃ ca rudhiraṃ pāṃsuvṛṣṭis tathā eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.7.2) And vultures, jackals, and chameleons speak; and there is a rain of lumps of flesh, blood, and dust;

body.text: (AVParis_67,7.3) vāyurūpam idaṃ sarvam adbhutaṃ parikīrtitam | vāta ā vātu bheṣajaṃ vāyau ā yāhi darśata iti sthālīpākasya homayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.7.3) All this portent is declared to have the form of wind. With '<s>vāta ā vātu bheṣajam</s>' (may the wind blow medicine) and '<s>vāyau ā yāhi darśata</s>' (come, O visible <s>Vāyu</s>) — one should offer a <s>sthālīpāka</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_67,7.4) vāyur mahān nabhapatir vajrapāṇis tathā īśvaras | śamanas sarvādbhutānāṃ mahāvyāhṛtayas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.7.4) '<s>Vāyu</s>, the great one, lord of the sky, thunderbolt-handed, ruler, pacifier of all portents' — and the <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>s likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_67,7.5) hutvā sviṣṭakṛtaṃ ca eva carutantraṃ samāpayet | vimuktotpātadoṣas tu jīvet tu śaradas śatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.7.5) Having offered the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> as well, one should complete the <s>caru</s> ceremony. Freed from the fault of portents, one would live a hundred autumns.

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.1) atha ced anyaśākhasu kartā bhavati vedavit | japtvā sa ṛgyajuḥsāmnaṃ śatamātraṃ samāhitas ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.1) Now, if the performer belongs to another Vedic branch and is learned in the <s>Veda</s>, having recited one hundred [verses] each from the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> with concentration,

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.2) gāyatryaṣṭaśataṃ japtvā yayajamānas samāhitas | vācayet tam upādhyāyaṃ vastreṇa kanakena vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.2) Having recited the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eight hundred times with concentration, the sacrificer should honor the preceptor with a garment or with gold.

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.3) dṛṣṭāṃ ca eva adbhutaṃ yasmins tat ca api pratipādayet | etās tu dakṣiṇās sarvās śaktiyukto na hāpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.3) And the portent that was seen — that too one should communicate [to the preceptor]. All these gifts one who is able should not omit.

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.4) yajamānas tatsuto vā yas svayaṃ kartum arhati | brāhmaṇāya viśeṣeṇa dadyāt tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ śubhām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.4) The sacrificer, or his son, whoever is himself qualified to perform — to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> especially he should give that auspicious gift.

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.5) japtvā atharvaśiras ca eva kuryāt vipreṣu pūjanam | śaktyā atha bhojanaṃ ca eva kuryāt vipreṣu pūjanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.5) Having recited the <s>Atharvaśiras</s> as well, one should honor the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; and according to one's ability, one should provide a feast and honor the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.6) etad evaṃ samākhyātam adbhutānāṃ viśodhanam | caturṇām api varṇānāṃ yas kuryāt śraddhayā anvitas ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.6) Thus has been declared this purification of portents; whoever of the four <s>varṇa</s>s (social classes) performs it endowed with faith,

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.7) maraṇaṃ na bhavet tasya na duḥkhaṃ na daridratā | sidhyanti sarvakāryāṇi dharme ca asya matir bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.7) Death shall not befall him, nor suffering, nor poverty; all undertakings succeed, and his mind is inclined toward <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).

body.text: (AVParis_67,8.8) etat puṇyaṃ paritraṃ ca devatāyāgapūjanam | sarvaśāntikaṃ ca eva pratipuruṣaṃ nibodhata || pratipuruṣaṃ nibodhata iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 67.8.8) This is meritorious and a protection — the worship and sacrifice to the deities; and this is the universal pacificatory rite, for each individual — know this. Know this for each individual.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_68. svapnādhyāyaḥ)
(AVParis_68,1.1) om athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi yad uktaṃ padmayoninā | upāṅgaṃ śukracārasta śubhāśubhanivedakam ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 68: Chapter on Dreams)
(AVParis 68.1.1) Oṃ. Now I shall expound what was spoken by <s>Padmayoni</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) — the subsidiary [text] of the course of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), the indicator of auspicious and inauspicious [results].

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.2) svapnādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā | śaśaṃsire purā yaṃ hi śaunakāya mahātmane ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.2) I shall expound the chapter on dreams, according to the statement of <s>Kroṣṭuki</s>, which was formerly related to the great-souled <s>Śaunaka</s>

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.3) nimittajñānakuśalāḥ sarvaṃ tasya tu pṛcchataḥ | grahā bhārgavabhaumārkāḥ paittikā dīptitejasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.3) By those skilled in the knowledge of omens, in response to all his questions. The planets <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), and <s>Arka</s> (Sun) are of bilious nature, with blazing radiance.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.4) kaphaprakṛtayo madhyā bṛhaspatibudhendavaḥ | vātaprakṛtayaḥ krūrā rāhuketuśanaiścarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.4) Of phlegmatic constitution and moderate are <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Indu</s> (Moon); of wind-constitution and cruel are <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn).

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.5) teṣāṃ tathā phalaṃ vidyāt saṃnipāte yathākramam | ete nava grahā jñeyā vātapittakaphātmakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.5) One should know their results accordingly in combination, in sequence; these nine planets should be known as having natures of wind, bile, and phlegm.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.6) eṣāṃ prakṛtitulyānāṃ niṣiktānāṃ tu teṣu vai | saṃyogeṣu ca jātānāṃ tulya prakṛtitā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.6) Those of similar constitution, cast into those [planets], and those born in their conjunctions — they have the same constitutional nature.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.7) arkenduprabhavā deham upatiṣṭhanti dehinaḥ | tasmān niṣicyamāneṣu vātapittakapheṣu yaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.7) Born from the sun and moon, they attend upon the body of the embodied being; therefore, when wind, bile, and phlegm are being distributed,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.8) eṣām anyatamo deho yātiriktaḥ prakāśate | pracakṣate sā prakṛtiḥ prakṛtijñānakovidāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.8) Whichever of these [humors] is predominant in the body, that manifests; those skilled in the knowledge of constitutions declare that to be the constitution.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.9) tatra ye mānisvāṅgāni ṛjavaḥ kalahapriyāḥ | uṣṇāḥ kapilaromāṇāaḥ svedanā anavekṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.9) Among them, those with prominent limbs, upright, quarrelsome, hot-tempered, with tawny hair, perspiring, and heedless;

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.10) bahvāśidurbhagāś caiva mṛdvaṅgāḥ śiśirapriyāḥ | lālanāḥ śithilāṅgāś ca priyāś ca priyāś ca lavaṇās tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.10) Eating much yet unfortunate, with soft limbs, fond of cold things, pampered, with loose limbs, and fond of salt;

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.11) tanutvaṅnakharomāṇas tv ācāryās tīkṣṇa eva ca | valīpalitabhūyiṣṭhās tathā khalatino narāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.11) With thin skin, nails, and body-hair, sharp-tempered, mostly with wrinkles and grey hair, and also bald men;

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.12) glayate śuṣyate caiṣām āśu mālyānulepanam | dāhātmikāḥ śaśāṅke 'pi pittaprakṛtayas tu te ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.12) Their garlands and ointments wither and dry up quickly; of burning nature even in moonlight — those are of bilious constitution.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.13) svapne caiva prapaśyanti diśaḥ kanakapiṅgalāḥ | maṇḍalāni samūhāṃś ca dikṣu pītāruṇaprabhān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.13) And in dreams they see directions that are golden-tawny, and circles and masses in the directions with yellow-red radiance,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.14) śṛṅgārimadirān deśāñ śuṣkāṃ malajalāṃ mahīm | śuṣkagulmadrumalatā dahyamānaṃ mahad vanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.14) Amorous and intoxicating regions, earth that is dry with dirty water, dry shrubs, trees, and creepers, a great forest being burned,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.15) viśuṣkāṇi ca vastrāṇi rudhirāṅgāṃs tathaiva ca | dahanādīṃś ca devāṃś ca raktam induṃ sugandhikān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.15) And dried garments, and blood-stained bodies likewise, and fire-like gods, and a red moon, and fragrant [flowers],

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.16) palāśāni ca puṣpāṇi karṇikāravanāni ca | digdāhavidyucchulkāś ca dīpyamānaṃ ca pāvakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.16) And <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest) flowers, and <s>karṇikāra</s> tree groves, directional conflagrations, lightning-flashes, and blazing fire.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.17) bhūyiṣṭhaṃ bhūṣitāś cāpi pibanti subahūdakam | saritsaravanānteṣu kūpaprasravaṇeṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.17) Mostly adorned, they also drink very much water, at the banks of rivers and lakes, at wells and springs.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.18) uṣṇārtāḥ śītakāmās tu nimajjanti pibanti ca | kalahaṃ caiva kurvanti duḥkhāny anubhavanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.18) Afflicted by heat and desirous of cold, they plunge in and drink, and they engage in quarrels and experience sufferings.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.19) strībhiś caiva vimānyante kṣayante klāmayanti ca | ity evaṃ paittikā jñeyāḥ prakṛtisvapnalakṣaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.19) And they are reviled by women, waste away, and become exhausted. Thus should those of bilious nature be known by the characteristics of constitutional dreams.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.20) prakṛtisvapnabhāvaiś ca śleṣmikāṇy api me śṛṇu | snigdhakeśanakhaśmaśrutatatvagroma[bhāṣiṇaḥ] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.20) And hear from me about the phlegmatic [constitution] by the manifestations of constitutional dreams: those with smooth hair, nails, beard, skin, and body-hair [and speech];

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.21) mahodarabhojoraskadīrghakeśanakha[dvijāñ] | vaiḍūryopalabaddhe tu saṃnibhair niyamaiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.21) With large belly, arms, chest, and long hair, nails, [and teeth]; adorned as if set with cat's-eye gems, with beautiful auspicious disciplines;

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.22) sthiropacitasarvāṅgā bhavanti sukhabhāginaḥ | śirodarakaṭiskandhapakṣayor vimalekṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.22) With all limbs firm and well-built, they are partakers of happiness; with clear eyes on head, shoulders, back, waist, and sides;

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.23) priyāḥ priyamvadāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtajñā dṛḍhabhaktayaḥ | cirād gṛhṇanti suciraṃ gṛhītaṃ dhārayanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.23) Dear, speaking pleasantly, heroic, grateful, of firm devotion; they grasp slowly but retain for a very long time what is grasped.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.24) na krudhyanti cirāt kruddhāḥ saṃbhavanty antakopamāḥ | pūjābhir vipulāṃ bhūmim āvahanti kulasya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.24) They do not become angry quickly; when angered, they become like <s>Antaka</s> (Death); by worship they bring vast territory and [glory] to their family.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.25) khyāpayanti ca sarvatra guṇaiś ca vipulair yaśaḥ | māṃśoṣṇatātimadhurapayohārātha suprajāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.25) And they spread fame everywhere with abundant virtues; [fond of] flesh, warm [foods], very sweet [substances], and milk products, and blessed with good offspring.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.26) na cirāc chuṣyate caiṣāṃ toyamālyānulepanam | nimīlitāsyanayanā niḥśabdā niḥprakampinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.26) Their water, garlands, and unguents do not dry up quickly; with closed mouths and eyes, silent, without trembling,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.27) svapanty ekena pārśvena ciraṃ sukhanibodhanāḥ | nātiduḥkhena jīvanti votpadyante sukhena tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.27) they sleep on one side for a long time, awakening pleasantly; they do not live with excessive suffering, but they arise comfortably.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.28) śyāmāḥ śyāmāvadātāś ca śrīmanto 'dṛḍharogiṇaḥ | alpāśidīrghakāmās tu bhavanty arthasahiṣṇavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.28) They are dark-complexioned or dark-fair, handsome, not firmly diseased; of little food [intake], long-lived in desire, and patient in acquiring wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.29) kṣutpipāsāsahāś cāpi kaphaprakṛtayo narāḥ | svapneṣu caiva paśyanti ramyaṃ candanakānanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.29) Men of <s>Kapha</s> (phlegm) constitution are able to endure hunger and thirst; and in dreams they see a lovely sandalwood forest,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.30) vikuḍmalapalāśāni pauṇḍarīkavanāni ca | śubhāś ca śiśiraprāyā nadyaḥ śubhajalāvahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.30) with budding <s>Palāśa</s> trees and groves of white lotuses; and rivers that are auspicious, mostly cool, bearing pure waters,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.31) tuṣāreṇāvṛtāś cāpi himavāghapaṭalāni ca | muktāmaṇisuvāśṛṅgā mṛṇālaphalakāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.31) and [landscapes] covered with frost, and sheets of snow-clouds; [mountains] with peaks of pearls, gems, and fine gold, and slabs of lotus-fiber,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.32) varāhakhaḍgamahiṣā mṛgāś ca rathakuñjarāḥ | spaṣṭatāraṃ tu haṃsāś ca vyopoḍhanti nabhastalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.32) boars, rhinoceroses, buffaloes, deer, chariots, and elephants; and swans clearly singing, flying across the vault of the sky,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.33) kundagokṣīragaurābhir indoḥ kīrṇagabhastiṣu | protphullakumudākārā vyomni sudhāmbusaprabhaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.33) with the moon's scattered rays, white as <s>Kunda</s> flowers and cow's milk; with the appearance of blossoming night-lotuses in the sky, with [hues] resembling nectar-water,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.34) rājahaṃsapratīkāśaṃ śaśāṅkaṃ cāmaladyutim | śubhrāṇi ca vimānāni phalāni madhurāṇi ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.34) the moon resembling a royal swan, of spotless brilliance; and white aerial chariots, and sweet fruits,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.35) kṛtapuṣpopahārāṇi mahānti bhavanāni ca | brāhmaṇān yajñavādāṃś ca dadhikṣīrāmṛtāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.35) and great mansions adorned with flower-offerings; <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, sacrificial discourses, curds, milk, and ambrosia,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.36) striyaś ca paramodāktāḥ suveṣāḥ svabhyalaṃkṛtāḥ | madhuraśvetapītāni prāyaśaś ciram eva tu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.36) and women supremely anointed, well-dressed, beautifully adorned; sweet, white, and yellow [objects] — mostly for a long time indeed

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.37) svapneṣu caivaṃ paśyanti kaphaprakṛtayo narāḥ | prakṛtisvapnabhāveṣu vātikāny api lakṣayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.37) do men of <s>Kapha</s> constitution see these in dreams. In the natural dream-states, one should also note the <s>Vāta</s> (wind) [characteristics]:

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.38) calāś ca calavikrāntāḥ kṣipramkṣipraṃ pralāpinaḥ | suptāḥ pralāpinas tv anye kaṣāyakaṭukapriyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.38) [They are] restless, of restless gait, speaking rapidly and repeatedly; others talk in their sleep, fond of astringent and pungent [tastes],

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.39) tvagromanakhadantoṣṭhapāṇipādatalādiṣu | rūkṣasphuṭitadurdarśā durbalā duḥkhabhāginaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.39) in their skin, body-hair, nails, teeth, lips, palms of hands, soles of feet, and such — rough, cracked, unsightly, weak, and destined for suffering,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.40) kaṭhinopacitāṅgāś ca bhrāntacittāphutekṣaṇāḥ | lāpino mṛdavaḥ krūrā vidyād asthirabuddhayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.40) with hard, compact limbs, with wandering mind and darting eyes; talkative, soft [in manner], cruel — one should know them as of unsteady intellect,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.41) nṛtyagītakathāśīla jambhino duḥkhabhāginaḥ | hrasvalomāḥ suvapuṣo durbalā dhamanās tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.41) habituated to dancing, singing, and stories, given to yawning, destined for suffering; with short body-hair, of fine physique, weak, with [prominent] veins likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.42) kṣāmā bhinnāḥ sadoṣāś ca satataṃ vānavasthitāḥ | hastanakhatvagoṣṭhānāṃ pādānāṃ ca vikāriṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.42) lean, broken, always faulty, and constantly restless; with irregularities of hands, nails, skin, cow-pens, and feet,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.43) akasmāt kopanāś cāpi rodanā dhamānās tathā | paraprakṛtiśīlāś ca valganāsphoṭanapriyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.43) and prone to sudden anger, weeping, and [pulsing] veins likewise; of disposition inclined toward others, fond of leaping and snapping.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.44) durbalāḥ śiśirāś cāpi vātaprakṛtayo naraḥ | svapneṣu caiva paśyanti vātābhravimalā diśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.44) Men of <s>Vāta</s> (wind) constitution are weak and sensitive to cold; and in dreams they see the directions clear of wind-blown clouds,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.45) mārutavegatuṅgāni bhuvanāni vānāni ca | śyāmatārāgrahagaṇaṃ vidhvastārkendumaṇḍalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.45) dwellings and forests [tossed] high by the force of the wind; a group of dark stars and planets, with the disks of sun and moon shattered,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.46) dhārācaradbhir viśvābhaiḥ saṃkulaṃ gaganaṃ ghanaiḥ | bhramantaḥ pakṣisaṃghāś ca mṛgāś codbhrāntayūthapāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.46) the sky crowded with clouds moving in streams, everywhere visible; flocks of birds whirling, and deer with panicked herd-leaders,

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.47) anyāś cāpu śambarāś ca girigahvarakānanāḥ | bhramanti ghnanti dhāvanti ūrdhvebhyaḥ prapatanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.47) and other demons and mountain-caves and forests; they wander, they strike, they run, and they fall from heights.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.48) svapneṣv etāni paśyanti vātaprakṛtayo narāḥ | miśrasvapnasvabhāveṣu saṃnipātātmakāḥ viduḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.48) Men of <s>Vāta</s> constitution see these things in dreams. In mixed dream-natures, one should know [the dreamer as] of <s>Saṃnipāta</s> (combined humors) type.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.49) etās tisraḥ prakṛtayaḥ saṃsṛṣṭāś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.49) These three constitutions [exist], and [also] mixed in every way.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.50) samyak karaṇavijñānaṃ tathā svapnād bhavet phalam | śubhaṃ vāpi aśubhaṃ vāpi nirdeṣṭavyam aśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.50) With correct knowledge of causation, thus the fruit of a dream becomes [clear]; whether auspicious or inauspicious, it should be declared completely.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.51) yenayenendriyārthena viddhaḥ svapiti mānavaḥ | tasyatasyendriyārthasya suptaḥ karmāṇi paśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.51) By whichever sense-object a person is afflicted when he falls asleep, of that very sense-object he sees the actions while sleeping.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.52) prakṛtyākṛtasaṃkalpasaṃbhavā devatāsv api | svapnamālāṃ tu yaḥ paśyed yāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā na tu smaret ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.52) Those [dreams] arising from natural constitution, formed intention, or deities — he who sees a garland of dreams and does not remember it upon seeing —

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.53) naite phalaṃ prayacchanti gargasya vacanaṃ yathā | prakṛtyānūkajān āhur eke śubhaphalodayān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.53) these do not yield fruit, as is the statement of <s>Garga</s>. Some say that dreams arising naturally and from habit have auspicious fruition.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.54) sārasvataṃ yathānūkaṃ saṃghātasaṃśrayaṃ śṛṇu | dṛṣṭvā bhogam asuptavyaṃ tataḥ prāpya śubhaṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.54) Hear the <s>Sārasvata</s> [doctrine]: according to habit and collective association; having seen an enjoyment, one should not sleep [again] — then one obtains the auspicious fruit.

body.text: (AVParis_68,1.55) svapnaprakṛtibhāvaṃ tu jñātvā tattvaṃ samādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.1.55) Having understood the nature and constitution of the dream, one should declare the truth.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.1) gṛhṇīta samudgendvindravāyvagnyarkanadīṃ kṣitim | samudraṃ vāhinīṃ dvīpaṃ laṅghayed vā vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.1) [If one dreams that] one grasps the ocean, the Moon, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the Sun, a river, or the earth; or the ocean, an army, or an island; or leaps over the earth —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.2) vāhinīṃ caturaṅgāṃ ca jīvachattrapatākinīm | dorbhyāṃ ca pratigṛhṇīyāt tathāketuvasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.2) or a four-limbed army with living parasol and banners; or grasps with both arms the earth with [its] banner-staffs;

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.3) ekapuṣkariṇīparṇe sauvarṇe bhāhane 'pi vā | sarpiṣā pāyasaṃ bhuṅkte gāṃ duhan yaś ca budhyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.3) or eats <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) with ghee on a single lotus-leaf or on a golden [plate]; or milks a cow and [then] awakens —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.4) pariveṣaḥ svayaṃ candre yo 'navastravasuṃdharām | parvatāgraṃ samāruhya kṣitiṃ yaś cāvalokayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.4) a halo around the moon of its own accord, [or dreams of] the uncovered earth; or having climbed a mountain peak, looks down upon the earth —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.5) ā kaṇṭhaṃ majjate yo hi mānavaḥ śoṇitārṇave | rathena siṃhayuktena parvataṃ cādhirohati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.5) or a man who sinks up to the neck in an ocean of blood; or mounts a mountain in a chariot yoked with lions —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.6) mahīṃ vā kampayed yas tu cālayed vā punar girīm | śvetam aśvam athāruhya pāṇḍuraṃ vāpu yo gajam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.6) or makes the earth tremble, or shakes a mountain; or riding a white horse or a white elephant —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.7) bhuṅkte puṣkariṇīparṇe pāyasaṃ vāpi sarpiṣā | aṅgavṛddhiṃ śirovṛddhiṃ prāpnuyād yas tu mānavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.7) or eats <s>pāyasa</s> with ghee on a lotus-leaf; or a person who attains growth of limbs or growth of the head —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.8) brāhmaṇo vāpi rājā vā svapne yad abhiṣecayet | rājā tu pārthivo jñeyaḥ kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.8) or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or a king consecrates [him] in a dream — he should be known as an earthly king, as is the statement of <s>Kroṣṭuki</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.9) śiro vā chidyate yasya vimānaṃ śoṇitaṃ tathā | senāpatyaṃ mahac cāyur arthalābhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.9) [If one dreams that] one's head is cut off, or [sees] an aerial chariot, or blood — [this portends] generalship, long life, and gain of wealth likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.10) vibhūṣaṇaṃ ca vidyāṃ ca karṇachedam avāpnuyāt | hastachede labhet putraṃ bāhuchede dhanāgamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.10) Adornment, learning, and the cutting of an ear [in a dream] one obtains; in the cutting of a hand, one gains a son; in the cutting of an arm, acquisition of wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.11) uraḥ sahasralābhaḥ syāt pādachede tathaiva ca | uraḥprajananachede atyantaṃ sukhaṃ dedhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.11) [A dream of] cutting the chest [portends] gain of a thousand; in cutting of the foot likewise; in cutting of the chest and genitals, one attains exceeding happiness.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.12) chatrādarśaphaloṣṇīṣaśuklamālyāgame tathā | matsyamāṃsadadhikṣīrarudhirāgama eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.12) In the appearance of a parasol, mirror, fruit, turban, white garland likewise; and in the appearance of fish, meat, curds, milk, and blood;

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.13) śaktyaṅkuśapatākānāṃ chattrāsidhanuṣāṃ tathā | vimalānāṃ jalānāṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ tu nidarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.13) of spears, goads, banners, parasols, swords, and bows; and of clear waters — the previously stated [auspicious interpretation] is the indication.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.14) sūkarakharavāhyānāṃ vadhaś caikapaśor api | narayuktasya yānasya nikṣiptasya gavasya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.14) [Dreams of] vehicles drawn by pigs or donkeys, the slaughter of even a single animal; of a conveyance yoked by humans, and of a cow lying down —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.15) darśanaṃ cāpy adṛṣṭānām agamyāgamanaṃ tathā | kṣīriṇāṃ phalamvṛkṣāṇāṃ darśanārohaṇāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.15) and the seeing of things unseen, and approach to the unapproachable; and the seeing and climbing of milk-bearing fruit-trees —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.16) viṣadarśanadaṃsparśo dhānyenotsaṅgapūraṇam | dasyubhir hanyamānasya rudataḥ pratibodhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.16) the seeing, biting, and touching of poison; the filling of the lap with grain; and awakening while crying as one is being struck by robbers —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.17) dvijebhyo dadhimāṃsasya lābhaḥ piśitabhakṣane | abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe cāpu śvetamālyānulepanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.17) the obtaining of curds and meat from <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, eating of flesh; and in eating of forbidden food — white garlands and unguents,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.18) ghātanaṃ śvāpadānāṃ ca pāṇau ca rudhirāgamaḥ | arthalābhāya boddhavyaḥ suhṛnmitrasamāgamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.18) the killing of wild beasts, and the arrival of blood in the hand — these should be understood as [portending] gain of wealth; and the meeting of friends and well-wishers.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.19) labhate nātra saṃdeho bhārgavasya vaco tathā | śuklāḥ sumanasaḥ kanyā dadhi gobrāhmaṇaṃ vṛṣam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.19) One obtains [the fruit] — there is no doubt in this, as is the word of <s>Bhārgava</s>. [Seeing] white flowers, a maiden, curds, a cow, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a bull,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.20) daivatāni nṛpādhyakṣāḥ pāṇḍurāṇi gṛhāṇi ca | suhṛdaḥ saphalā vṛkṣā nakṣatrāṇy amalaṃ jalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.20) deities, kings and officials, white houses, friends, fruit-bearing trees, asterisms, clear water,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.21) iṣṭakalyāṇaśabdāś ca śuklāmbaradharāḥ striyaḥ | nabho vimalanakṣatraṃ pāvakaṃ viṣamārciṣam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.21) auspicious and blessed sounds, women wearing white garments, the sky with bright asterisms, a fire with uneven flames —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.22) dṛṣṭvā yas tatkṣaṇaṃ budhyet tasya kalyāṇam ādiśet | vṛkṣān gulmāṃś ca vallīś ca svagṛhe puṣpitā naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.22) he who awakens at that very moment upon seeing [these] — for him one should predict auspiciousness. [Seeing] trees, shrubs, and creepers blossoming in one's own house,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.23) śuklavāsāḥ striyaś cāpi yaḥ paśyec chrīs tu taṃ bhajet | viṣaśoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prītīm āpnoti mānavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.23) and women in white garments — he who sees [these], prosperity shall attend him. A man whose body is smeared with poison and blood attains affection.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.24) dīptāṅgo labhate bhūmiṃ vardhamānāṅga eva ca | parivāryābhirudito bāndhavaiḥ karuṇaṃ naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.24) One with blazing body gains land, and one with growing body likewise; a man surrounded and wept over piteously by relatives —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.25) śokārto labhate tuṣṭiṃ mṛtaś cāyur avāpnuyāt | śuklamālyāmbaradharo dahyamānaḥ pralīyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.25) one afflicted by grief gains satisfaction, and one dead may gain long life. Wearing white garlands and garments, being burned, one dissolves [i.e. auspicious].

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.26) yaḥ svapne saṃbhayed ugraṃ pārakyaṃ so 'rtham āpnuyāt | nāgadantakamudrāṃ ca vīṇāṃ mālāñjanaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.26) He who in a dream fears a terrible stranger gains wealth. [Seeing] an elephant-tooth [bracelet], a seal-ring, a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), a garland, and collyrium likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.27) kāñcanaṃ paśyate yas tu tathā strīṃ labhate naraḥ | uḍḍīyamānān vihagān tathā puṣkariṇīgatān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.27) and he who sees gold — that man obtains a woman. [Seeing] birds flying up, and those gone to a lotus-pond —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.28) mattaṃ kareṇum āruhya parastrīṃ labhate naraḥ | kumārīṃ labhate nārīm āyasair nigaḍair naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.28) mounting a rutting she-elephant — a man obtains another's wife. A man obtains a young woman [if he dreams of] iron fetters.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.29) baddhvā navāṃ tu yo mālām utpālānāṃ vibudhyate | kavāṭale ca saṃyukte tathaivotpalahastake ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.29) He who awakens having tied a fresh garland of blue lotuses; and when a door-panel is joined, and likewise when one holds a blue lotus in hand —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.30) bhṛṅgāro darpaṇo vāpi labdhvā putrāgamaṃ vadet | taḍāgārāmakūpānāṃ purārañjanayor api ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.30) a water-pitcher or a mirror — having obtained [these in a dream], one should predict the arrival of a son. Of reservoirs, gardens, and wells, and of cities and pleasure-grounds,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.31) pūrṇakumbhasya cādeśyaṃ varṣam uttaraṇād bhruvam | cipiṭaḥ kālako nagnaḥ śravaṇo mehate yadi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.31) and of a full water-pot — one should predict rain from the rising of [one's] brow. [If] a flat-nosed, dark, naked, [one with] streaming [ears] urinates,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.32) vidikthaḥ sravate cārmiḥ svapne varṣaṃ samādiśet | sūkarīṃ mahiṣīṃ vāpi hastinīṃ śakunīṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.32) or a low-born one streams with sweat in a dream — one should predict rain. [If] a sow, buffalo-cow, she-elephant, or a hen

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.33) svapne yadā prasūyeta subhikṣaṃ nirdiśet tadā | śayanāsanayānāni gṛhagrāmapurāṇi ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.33) gives birth in a dream — one should predict abundance then. Beds, seats, vehicles, houses, villages, and cities —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.34) yeṣāṃ svapne pralīyante teṣāṃ vṛddhim athādiśet | govṛṣaṃ puruṣaṃ vṛkṣaṃ hastinaṃ parvataṃ gṛham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.34) of whomever these dissolve in a dream, for them one should predict growth. A bull, a man, a tree, an elephant, a mountain, a house —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.35) narasyārohaṇād vṛddhiḥ pāṇḍurāṇi viśeṣataḥ | daivatāni dvijā gāvaḥ pitaro liṅgino grahāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.35) from a person's climbing [these], growth [is predicted]; white ones especially. Deities, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, cows, ancestors, ascetics, planets —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.36) yad vadanti naraṃ svapne tat tathaiva vinirdiśet | saritsarasamudrāṇāṃ taraṇe śokatāraṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.36) what they say to a person in a dream, one should declare that exactly so. In crossing rivers, lakes, and oceans — crossing over grief.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.37) narasya śoṇitaṃ pītvā prakṛtāṇl labhate naraḥ | candrendradhvajasūryāṇāṃ patane nṛpater bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.37) Having drunk a person's blood, a man obtains natural [worldly goods]. In the falling of the Moon, <s>Indra</s>'s banner, or the Sun — danger from the king.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.38) mahārṇavamahendrāṇāṃ kṣobhe kṣobhaṃ vinirdiśet | keśaśmaśrunakhānāṃ ca patane śokasaṃbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.38) In the agitation of great oceans and great mountains, one should predict agitation. In the falling of hair, beard, and nails — the arising of grief.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.39) kṛmiṇatvaṃ bhaved dhanyaṃ kroṣṭuker vacanaṃ yathā | kravyādair damṣṭribhiś cāpi vināśo bhūtavigrahe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.39) Being worm-infested would be auspicious, as is the statement of <s>Kroṣṭuki</s>. By flesh-eaters and fanged [beasts] — destruction; in a conflict with spirits,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.40) śastramuṣṭiprahāreṣu vijānīyāj jvarāgamam | yadyad ujjvalavad dravyaṃ tattat sukhakaraṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.40) in [dreams of] blows by weapons and fists, one should know the approach of fever. Whatever object appears luminous — that shall be happiness-producing.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.41) yadyad virudhyate vāpi svapne tat tasya nirdiśet | [nopānena] prajātānāṃ darśane sthānam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.41) Whatever is contradicted in a dream — one should declare that for the [dreamer]. [In seeing] those born without sandals — one should predict [change of] residence.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.42) upānahabalachattradarśane ca grhe tathā | hasadbhir vā parivṛto nṛtyadbhiḥ svajanair api ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.42) In the seeing of sandals, strength, parasol, and in [one's own] house likewise; or surrounded by laughing and dancing kinsmen —

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.43) saṃyuktaṃ sūkarakharair uṣṭraiḥ kṛṣṇacatuṣpadaiḥ | ratham āruhya yo yāyād akṣatas tu yugaṃdharaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.43) He who would ride a chariot yoked with boars, donkeys, camels, and black quadrupeds — [he will be] unharmed, a yoke-bearer.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.44) prakīrṇakeśo hriyate dakṣiṇenāpareṇa vā | dakṣiṇenāgatā kanyā kālikākulavāsinī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.44) [If] one with disheveled hair is dragged to the south or to the west; [or if] a maiden from the south, a dark-complexioned one dwelling in a [low] family, [appears],

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.45) nīyate puruṣair yaś ca pāśahastair viśeṣataḥ | nirastānāṃ viṣamāṇāṃ pretenākuśalaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.45) and [if] one is led by men holding nooses, especially — for those cast out, poisoned, [or encountering] a corpse, there shall be misfortune.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.46) piṇyākasya tilānāṃ ca karṣāsu lavaṇasya ca | rūḍhaśmaśrunakhānāṃ ca duścelānāṃ ca vāsasām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.46) [The seeing of] oil-cake, sesame seeds, salt in a receptacle, those with overgrown beards, nails, and hair, and those wearing ragged garments,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.47) virāgavāsasāṃ vāpi vikṛtānāṃ tathaiva ca | sarīsṛpāṇāṃ vyālānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ cāpi darśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.47) or those wearing faded garments, or deformed ones likewise, and the seeing of crawling creatures, serpents, and enemies,

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.48) kṛṣṇānāṃ vāpi sarveṣāṃ rājadvijavṛṣād ṛte | darśanaṃ gamanaṃ vāpi śokam āyāsavedanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.48) and of all dark-colored [things] — except for a king, a twice-born, or a bull — [their] seeing or [one's] going [toward them] portends sorrow, distress, and suffering.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.49) padmair vā jalabhāṇḍair vā krīḍitāyāsadarśanam | padmāni vāharet svapne hastachedam avāpnuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.49) [Playing] with lotuses or water-vessels shows fatigue from play; [if] one carries lotuses in a dream, one would suffer the cutting off of a hand.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.50) prasanne tu dhruvaṃ śoko rajjuchede mriyeta saḥ | rūḍhasya srotasā śoko mṛtyuḥ sriotasi naśyataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.50) In clear [water], there is certainly sorrow; in the cutting of a rope, he shall die. For one established [in a current], sorrow from a stream; death when the stream is destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.51) dantā bāhuṃ tathā śīrṣṇo chinnāṃśadravyadarśanam | bhrātaraṃ pitaraṃ vāpi putraṃ vā nāśayanti te ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.51) Seeing the severed parts of teeth, arms, or head — these destroy one's brother, father, or son [respectively].

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.52) dvāre vā sārgale vāpi śayyāṃ śakhāṃ tathaiva ca | svapne yasya pranaśyanti bhāryā tasya vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.52) [If] in a dream, one's door, or its bolt, bed, or couch perishes — that man's wife perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.53) kṛkalāso vṛko vāpi puruṣo vāpi piṅgalaḥ | śayyāṃ yasyādhirohanti bhāryā tasyāpi duṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.53) A lizard, a wolf, or a tawny man — whoever mounts one's bed [in a dream], that man's wife is corrupted.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.54) svapne yo mārayet sarpaṃ śvetapītakalohitam | kṛṣṇasya vā śiraś chindyāt putras tasya vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.54) He who in a dream would kill a serpent — white, yellow, or red — or cut off the head of a black one, that man's son perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.55) rājaputraś ca coraś ca rājabhṛṭyaś ca yo bhavet | tasya svapnāḥ phalaṃ dadyur eteṣu yad udāhṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.55) A prince, a thief, or a king's servant — for him, dreams would yield the fruit that is declared for these [categories].

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.56) yeṣāṃ lābhe bhaved vṛddhis teṣāṃ nāśe guṇo bhavet | yeṣāṃ lābhe bhaved dhānis teṣāṃ lābhe guṇo bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.56) For those whose gain would mean increase, their loss would be beneficial; for those whose gain would mean loss, their gain would be beneficial.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.57) śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu yaḥ svapne punaḥ paśyaty apūjitam | śubhaṃ vāpy aśubhaṃ vāpi yat paścāt tatphalaṃ labhet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.57) He who, having seen something auspicious in a dream, then again sees something inauspicious — whether auspicious or inauspicious, he obtains the fruit of what was [seen] last.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.58) svapnās tu prathame yāme saṃvatsaravipākinaḥ | dvitīye 'ṣṭasu māseṣu tṛtīye tu tadardhabhāk ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.58) Dreams in the first watch of the night ripen in a year; in the second, in eight months; and in the third, in half of that [four months].

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.59) māsiko govisarge tu sadyaḥpākaḥ prabhātike. kālaḥ pañcasv avasthāsu śarvaryāḥ kīrtitaḥ pṛthak ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.59) [A dream] at the time of releasing the cows [early morning] [ripens] in a month; at dawn, it ripens immediately. The time [of fruition] in the five stages of the night has been declared separately.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.60) viprebhyaḥ śaktito dānaṃ śāntiḥ svaṣṭyayanādayaḥ | vināśayanti duḥsvapnaṃ prātaś cāśvatthasevanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.60) Gifts according to one's ability to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, pacification rites, <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictory rituals) and the like — these destroy a bad dream, as does the worship of the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree in the morning.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.61) aśvatthasevā tilapātradānaṃ gosparśanaṃ brāhmaṇatarpaṇaṃ ca | śāntikriyā svastyayanakriyā ca duḥsvapnam etāni vināśayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.61) Worship of the <s>Aśvattha</s>, the gift of sesame and a vessel, the touching of a cow, the satisfying of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the performance of pacification rites, and the performance of <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictory) rites — these destroy a bad dream.

body.text: (AVParis_68,2.62) vasnakanakadānadevapūjāgurugoṣṭhaniṣevitāni kuryuḥ | dvijavṛṣabḥgavāśvapārthivānāṃ darśanam itihāsamaṅgalāḥ syuḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.2.62) One should perform [rites involving] the gift of garments and gold, worship of deities, and attendance at the cow-pen and the <s>guru</s>'s [dwelling]; the seeing of a twice-born, a bull, a cow, a horse, or a king — these along with <s>itihāsa</s> [recitations] would be auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.1) imān dṛṣṭvāśubhān svapnān prātar utthāya satvaraḥ | nadīsaṃgamatoyena mukhaṃ saṃmārjya tattvataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.1) Having seen these inauspicious dreams, rising promptly in the morning, truly washing one's face with water from the confluence of rivers,

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.2) hiraṇyavarṇābhir udakaṃ śaṃtātīyamayobhuvā | abhimantrya prayatnena mukhaṃ saṃmārjya tattvataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.2) having consecrated the water with [the hymn] '<s>Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ</s>' (Golden-hued), the <s>Śāntātīya</s>, and the <s>Ayobhūva</s> [hymns], carefully and truly washing one's face,

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.3) yo na jīvaḥ paro 'pehi vidma te svapna vedanam | rocanā sarṣapā mṛdā samit sakusumaṃ dadhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.3) [reciting] 'O you who are not alive, go away! We know the anguish of your dream.' [One should offer] <s>rocanā</s> (yellow orpiment), mustard seeds, earth, a fire-stick, curds with flowers,

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.4) gām ajaṃ kanakaṃ sattvaṃ kumārīṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śubham | abhivandya nṛpo yāyāt suhṛdāṃś ca manoharān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.4) and having reverenced a cow, a goat, gold, a creature, a maiden, and an auspicious <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the king should go [forth], and [greet] charming friends.

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.5) yadā tu yātrāṃ nṛpatiḥ kartum icched vidhānavit | atha svastyayanaiḥ [saumyaiḥ saumyais tam abhimantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.5) When the king, knowing the proper procedure, wishes to undertake a military expedition, then one should consecrate him with auspicious <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictory) [mantras].

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.6) tataḥ śuklāmbaradharo vāgyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ | tāṃ niśaṃ saṃviśed rājā bhūmau caivābhimantrayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.6) Then, wearing white garments, with restrained speech and controlled senses, the king should lie down on the ground that night and consecrate [it with mantras].

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.7) [anyathaiva hi na svapnadarśanārthanidarśanam] | evam uktvā narapatiḥ prayatātmā tataḥ svapet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.7) [Otherwise, there is indeed no demonstration of the meaning of dream-vision.] Having spoken thus, the lord of men, with purified self, should then sleep.

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.8) praśastasvapnatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tato yāyān narādhipaḥ | svapneṣu vāpraśastreṣu tataḥ śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.8) Having seen auspicious dreams, the king should then set out; if the dreams are inauspicious, then he should undertake a pacification rite.

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.9) māhendrīm amṛtāṃ raudrīṃ kuryād vāpy aparājitām | kauberīṃ vā prayuñjīta ādityāṃ vā sadakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.9) He should perform the <s>Māhendrī</s> (of <s>Indra</s>), the <s>Amṛtā</s> (of immortality), the <s>Raudrī</s> (of <s>Rudra</s>), or the <s>Aparājitā</s> (unconquered); or he may employ the <s>Kauberī</s> (of <s>Kubera</s>), or the <s>Ādityā</s> (of the Sun) with the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.10) rajanikaradivākarau karābhyāṃ spṛśati yadā grasate 'tha vā narendraḥ | lavaṇajalanidhiṃ nadīṃ ca dorbhyāṃ tarati hradāpadakardamaṃ tamo vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.10) When the king touches the Moon and the Sun with his hands, or swallows them [in a dream]; crosses the salt ocean or a river with his arms; [crosses] a pool, water, or mud, or darkness —

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.11) naraturagamahīruhān nagān vā bhavanacarān na virohayed gajān vā | jvalanamaraṇakālavṛddhayogān yadi nṛpa ātmagatāṃś ca paśyatīha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.11) [if in a dream] he mounts men, horses, great trees, mountains, house-roaming [elephants], or elephants; [or] sees the conjunctions of blazing fire, death, time, and growth as pertaining to himself —

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.12) yadi ca nṛpatir ātmano 'bhracārair bhramati mahīṃ sapurāṃ parikṣipet | yadi ca sa ciramagnagātramātro bhramati nṛpo grasate 'tha medinīṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.12) or if the king wanders with cloud-walkers, circumscribes the earth with its cities; or if the king, with his body submerged for a long time, wanders or swallows the earth —

body.text: (AVParis_68,3.13) yadi ca jayati damṣṭriṇo narān vā yadi ca bhavet sitamālyadānadhārī | yadi ca ruditi caivam ādi dṛṣṭvā paraviṣayaṃ hṛṣitas tatas tu yāyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.3.13) or if he conquers tusked beasts or men, or if he becomes a wearer of white garlands and bearer of gifts; or if he weeps — having seen such [things] and the like, he should set out joyfully for the enemy's territory.

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.1) sa kaluṣasalilāvapāṃsumagno madhugh}ṛtatailavasāpradigdhagātraḥ | malinavasanajīrṇaraktavāsā yadi sumanobhir alaṃkṛtaḥ svayaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.1) [But if] he is immersed in turbid water, dust-covered, his body smeared with ghee, oil, or fat, wearing soiled garments, worn-out or red clothes, or [if] he himself is adorned with flowers —

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.2) svapiti jayati khādati prahṛṣṭo vilapati nartati gāyanaprahāsaiḥ | bhavati ca mudito labheta kanyāṃ yadi nṛpatir nayaśo bhavej jayārthī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.2) [if] he sleeps, conquers, eats with delight, weeps, dances with singing and laughter, and is joyful, or obtains a maiden — [then] the king who seeks victory will gain fame and success.

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.3) mayakharasūkaravānarādhirūḍho hṛtamukuṭāṅgadavastracihnanagnaḥ | vinihataturagadvipo narendro yadi patitadhvajavāṃs tato na yāyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.3) [But if] riding a buffalo, donkey, boar, or monkey, with crown, armlets, and garments stripped away, naked, bereft of markings, his horses and elephants slain — if a king's flag is fallen, then he should not set out.

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.4) narapatir aparājitaḥ parair yo yadi ca paraiḥ parihasyate madadbhiḥ | yadi ca bhavati durdṛśograrūpo <atha> na sa īdṛśakaḥ parān prayāyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.4) The king who is unconquered by enemies — if he is mocked by proud enemies [in a dream]; or if he becomes one of terrible, fierce form — then such a one should not go against the enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.5) svapnān dṛṣṭvā śubhān rājā japadbhir abhimantritaḥ | yuktaḥ sa śakunair bhūpa utpātagaṇavarjitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.5) Having seen auspicious dreams, the king, consecrated by those reciting [mantras], accompanied by [favorable] bird-omens, O lord, free from the host of portents,

body.text: (AVParis_68,4.6) sahāyavān susaṃnaddho nimittajñaiḥ samanvitaḥ | sumuhūrte sunakṣatre prayāyād vasudhādhipaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.4.6) with allies, well-armored, accompanied by those skilled in reading omens — the lord of the earth should set out at an auspicious moment and under a favorable <s>nakṣatra</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.1) tailābhyaktaś ca kṛsarāṃ bhuṅkte tailapariplutām | mātaraṃ praviśed yaś ca jvalitaṃ ca hutāśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.1) [If in a dream] one anointed with oil eats <s>kṛsarā</s> (rice-and-sesame porridge) drenched in oil, or enters one's mother or a blazing fire,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.2) prāsadāt parvatāgrād vā pated yaś cāpi mānavaḥ | magnaḥ kardamakūpeṣu jale yaś cāpi naśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.2) or a man falls from a palace or mountain-peak, [or is] submerged in muddy pits, or perishes in water,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.3) drumam unmūlayed yas tu paśyed rājñopasevakam | kumārīvadane yaś ca vānarīṃ vādhigacchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.3) or uproots a tree, or sees one who serves a king, or [sees] the face of a maiden, or mounts a female monkey —

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.4) raktakaṇṭhagate vāpi yasya kaṇṭhe visarjati | vivarṇo vāpi pāśair yo badhyate mriyate tu saḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.4) or [has] a red [mark] at the throat, or discharges at the throat; or one who is pale, or who is bound with nooses — he shall die.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.5) kāṃsyaṃ vā kāṃsyapātrīṃ vā yasya tejo 'dhirohati | acireṇaiva kālena so 'sinā vadhyate naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.5) He upon whose bronze or bronze vessel splendor mounts [in a dream] — within a short time, that man is slain by a sword.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.6) yūpāgram adhiruhyātha nāvāgram adhirohati | acireṇaiva kālena śūlāgraṃ so 'dhirohati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.6) He who climbs the top of a sacrificial post and then mounts the prow of a boat — within a short time, he mounts the point of an impaling stake.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.7) muṇḍaḥ kāṣāyavāso vā śvetaraktapaṭo 'pi vā | svapne yasyādhirohanti vyādhis tasyādhirohati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.7) A shaven-headed one, or one wearing ochre robes, or [one wearing] white or red cloth — whoever mounts [one's body] in a dream, disease mounts that person.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.8) śvā vā ajagaro godhā tarakṣu śalyako 'pi vā | kṛkalāso rurur vyāghro dvīpī yasyādhirohati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.8) A dog, a python, a monitor lizard, a hyena, a porcupine, a chameleon, a <s>ruru</s> deer, a tiger, or a leopard — whoever mounts [one's body],

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.9) ahiś ca raudrajaṭilaḥ śvetaraktapaṭo 'pi vā | svapne yam upatiṣṭhanti vyādhis tam upatiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.9) a serpent, a fierce-matted [ascetic], or one wearing white or red cloth — whomever these attend in a dream, disease attends that person.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.10) mahībhasmapradigdhāṅgo nirāvaraṇa eva ca | samasyānāṃ sajātānām utsavānāṃ ca darśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.10) [If] one's body is smeared with earth or ash, and [one is] without covering; [or the] seeing of assemblies, kinsmen, and festivals,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.11) durgam adhvānagamanam anūpānāṃ ca sevanam | abhyaṅgaś caiva gātrāṇāṃ tilagomayakardamaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.11) traveling a difficult road and frequenting marshy places; and the anointing of the body with sesame, cow-dung, and mud —

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.12) suvarṇamaṇimuktāni bhūṣaṇaṃ rajatāni ca | darśanaṃ vāpy athaiteṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ saṃpraveśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.12) [seeing] gold, gems, pearls, ornaments, and silver — the seeing of even these [portends] the onset of disease.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.13) gāyanaṃ nartanaṃ hāsyaṃ vivāhakaraṇaṃ tathā | ānandaś ca pramodaś ca vyasanasya ca darśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.13) Singing, dancing, laughter, and the performance of a wedding, joy and delight, and the seeing of calamity —

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.14) purāṇaghṛtadigdhāṅgo naro maraṇam āpnuyāt | evam uktā mahotpātā vividhāḥ pūrvacoditaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.14) a man whose body is smeared with old ghee shall obtain death. Thus have been declared the various great portents, as previously stated.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.15) ulkābhedās tathā pañca pariveṣā nava smṛtāḥ | digdāho 'ṣṭavidhaḥ prokto vidyud aṣṭavidhā tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.15) The types of meteors are five, the halos are remembered as nine; the burning of directions is declared as eightfold, and lightning likewise as eightfold.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.16) catvāro bhūmikampāś ca nirghāto 'ṣṭavidhas tathā | viṃśatī dve ca vijñeyā bhedā hy ulkādiṣu smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.16) Earthquakes are four, and thunder is eightfold likewise; twenty-two types should be known as remembered in [the categories of] meteors and the like.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.17) mahotpātāś ca bahavaḥ śāntiyogeṣu kīrtitāḥ | teṣu sarveṣu vidhivac chāntikāmo narādhipaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.17) And the many great portents have been proclaimed in the context of pacification rites; for all of these, the king who desires pacification, according to rule,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.18) atharvāṇaṃ ca vṛṇuyāt sarvaśāstravidaṃ nṛpaḥ | sa vṛto bhayabhītena śamanārthaṃ mahātmanā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.18) should choose an <s>Atharvan</s> priest who knows all the <s>śāstra</s>s. He, being chosen by the great-souled one who is terrified by danger, for the purpose of pacification,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.19) prajānām abhayaṃ samyag dāpayet pṛthivīpatiḥ | anantaraṃ gavāṃ pūjā brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.19) should have the lord of the earth properly grant safety to the people. Immediately thereafter, worship of cows and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s especially,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.20) devatāyatane sadyo dohān bhūmau prakārayet | satataṃ cānulipyas tu puṣpair dhūpair yathoditaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.20) and at the temple of the deity, one should immediately have the milking performed on the ground; and constantly anointing [the temple] with flowers and incense as prescribed,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.21) pradīpair vividhaiḥ śubhraiḥ sarvadikṣuprakalpitaiḥ | tathā balyupahāraiś ca pāyasāpūpasaṃyutaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.21) with various bright lamps arranged in all directions, and with <s>bali</s> (offerings) accompanied by <s>pāyasa</s> (rice-milk pudding) and <s>apūpa</s> (cakes),

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.22) hṛdyair bahuvidhair bhakṣaiḥ sarvadikṣuprakalpitaiḥ | tasminn evāntare śānte goṣṭhe vā jalasaṃnidhau ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.22) with pleasing food-offerings of many kinds, arranged in all directions — in that very interval, [at] a peaceful [place], in a cow-pen or near water,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.23) nirgatya nagarād vāpi śucau deśe samāhitaḥ | vṛṇuyāc chāntitattvajñān utpātavihitāñ śubhān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.23) having gone out from the city, in a clean place, with concentrated mind, one should choose [priests] who know the truth of pacification, [those] blessed [ones] prescribed for [averting] portents.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.24) ṣoḍaśāṣṭau vṛtās te ca puraścaraṇaśodhitāḥ | aṅgāni kuryur anye ca śatasaṃkhyā dvijottamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.24) Sixteen or eight chosen [priests], purified by <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preliminary practice); others, the best of twice-born, numbering a hundred, should perform the auxiliary [rites].

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.25) udayāste sukhāsīnā japaṃ kuryur atandritāḥ | te sadasyā iti proktā vācane yajñakarmaṇi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.25) Seated comfortably at sunrise and sunset, they should perform <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation) untiringly. They are called the assembly-members (<s>sadasya</s>s) in the recitation and sacrificial rites.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.26) teṣāṃ variṣṭhaḥ śāntijña upadraṣṭā manoharaḥ | sarvakarmasu vettā ya ānayet so 'py athādarāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.26) The most eminent among them, the knower of pacification, the charming overseer — he who knows all rites should also be brought with respect.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.27) bhūmiṃ saṃśodhya vidhivat kṛtvā tatra ca maṇḍapam | vidhivat kalpayed vediṃ yajñapātrāṇi ca svayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.27) Having purified the ground according to rule and having constructed a pavilion there, one should prepare the altar and the sacrificial vessels according to rule, by oneself.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.28) evaṃ yathoktavidhinā agnimanthanapūrvakām | mahāśāntiṃ prayuñjīta sarvopadravanāśinīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.28) Thus, according to the prescribed procedure, beginning with the churning of fire, one should perform the <s>Mahāśānti</s> (Great Pacification) rite, which destroys all calamities.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.29) annair vastraiś ca vividhaiḥ saṃyuktāṃ bahudakṣiṇām | kārayitvā mahāśāntiṃ varaṃ gāṃ ca nivedayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.29) Having performed the great pacificatory rite, accompanied by various foods and garments, with abundant gifts, one should offer a choice cow.

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.30) gṛham ābharaṇaṃ chattram anaḍudvājinaṃ tathā | kuñjaraṃ vā tathā dattvā ghaṇtābharaṇabhūṣitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.30) Having given a house, ornaments, an umbrella, a bull, a horse, or an elephant adorned with bells and ornaments,

body.text: (AVParis_68,5.31) mahat sukham avāpnoti kāryasiddhiṃ ca vindati | kāryasiddhiṃ ca vindati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 68.5.31) One obtains great happiness and achieves success in one's undertakings; achieves success in one's undertakings.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_69. atharvahṛdayam)
(AVParis_69,1.1) om upasaṃgamya munayaḥ sarvajñaṃ śāntamānasam | apṛcchan gatamātsyaryaṃ bhṛguṃ brahmavidāṃ varam ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 69: The Heart of the <s>Atharva</s> [Veda])
(AVParis 69.1.1) Oṃ. Having approached the omniscient, tranquil-minded, envy-free <s>Bhṛgu</s>, the best among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, the sages asked:

body.text: (AVParis_69,1.2) kāmā hi bahavo loke saṃsthitā bhinnasādhanāḥ | ekam eva paraṃ teṣāṃ samyak tvaṃ brūhy asaṃśayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.1.2) 'Many desires exist in the world, established with different means [of fulfillment]; declare to us without doubt the one supreme [means] among them all.'

body.text: (AVParis_69,1.3) samāsena pravakṣyāmi yena sarvaṃ pradadyate | atipraśno 'yam udgīrṇas tathāpi kathayāmy aham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.1.3) 'I shall declare in brief that by which everything is bestowed; this is a most extraordinary question raised, yet I shall tell it.'

body.text: (AVParis_69,1.4) sarvārthasādhanārthāya śrutir āṅgirasī hitā | svatejasā prajvalantī hṛdayaṃ tad athārvaṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.1.4) 'For the accomplishment of all purposes, the <s>Āṅgirasī</s> <s>Śruti</s> (the tradition of <s>Aṅgiras</s>) is beneficial; blazing with its own radiance, it is the heart of the <s>Atharvan</s>s.'

body.text: (AVParis_69,1.5) prabhāvaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi upariṣṭād yathāvidhi | duḥsādhyāni nimittāni tāni vedmi hi kāni cit ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.1.5) 'I shall declare its power hereafter, according to prescribed rules; I know certain portents that are difficult to counteract.'

body.text: (AVParis_69,2.1) akāle yasya jāyante dantāḥ keśair vivarjitaḥ | prabhūtalambakeśo vā tathā hīnādhikāṅguliḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.2.1) One whose teeth appear at an untimely [age], who is devoid of hair, or who has excessively long and hanging hair, or who has fewer or more fingers,

body.text: (AVParis_69,2.2) dvidantaś cāpi jāyeta tasya karma svaśākhikam | svaśākhāyāṃ tu yat proktaṃ kuryād vātharvaṇaṃ vidhim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.2.2) Or one who is born with two [rows of] teeth — for him the rite of his own branch [should be performed]; what is prescribed in his own branch, or else one should perform the <s>Ātharvana</s> rite.

body.text: (AVParis_69,2.3) dvimūrdhā vā trinetro vā tathaikākṣir dvināsikaḥ | hīnahasto 'paro hy arthe na tv atharvaśirāḥ sa ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.2.3) One with two heads, or three eyes, or one-eyed, or with two noses, or with a deficient hand — for another purpose, however, that is not the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_69,2.4) kṛtopacāraḥ pañca sapta śuddhātmā sādhyasatkṛtaḥ | sa śāntyudakam ācamya śāntavṛkṣasamīpataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.2.4) Having performed the preparatory rites for five or seven [days], the purified soul, honored by the <s>sādhya</s>s, sipping the pacificatory water near a pacificatory tree,

body.text: (AVParis_69,2.5) śāntavṛkṣasamidbhis tu tilais trimadhurais tathā | homaṃ kuryād atharvā tu tena nandati satkulam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.2.5) With firewood from pacificatory trees, and with sesame and the three sweets, the <s>Atharvan</s> priest should perform the oblation; by that, a good family rejoices.

body.text: (AVParis_69,3.1) na labhed yady atharvāṇaṃ kuryād daśaguṇaṃ svayam | mahāvyāhṛtihomaṃ ca sāvitraṃ japam eva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.3.1) If one cannot obtain the <s>Ātharvana</s> [rite], one should perform it tenfold oneself — the great <s>Vyāhṛti</s> oblation and the <s>Sāvitrī</s> recitation.

body.text: (AVParis_69,3.2) vikṛtāṅgo 'dhikāṅgo vā jāto hīnāṅgo eva vā | kulasyādbhutam atyarthaṃ tad atharvā śamaṃ nayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.3.2) If one is born with deformed limbs, extra limbs, or deficient limbs — this is a great portent for the family; the <s>Atharvan</s> priest should bring it to peace.

body.text: (AVParis_69,3.3) kapyuṣṭrebhagavādīnāṃ jāyante 'ṅgamukhaiḥ samāḥ | yasmin rāṣṭre nṛpas tatra ṣaṇmāsādd hi vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.3.3) [Beings] resembling monkeys, camels, or donkeys in their limbs and faces are born — in whichever kingdom the king [resides], he perishes within six months.

body.text: (AVParis_69,3.4) kapyādayo va jāyante anyasya tulyagātrakāḥ | vṛkṣe 'nyavṛkṣajaṃ puṣpaṃ jāyate phalam eva vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.3.4) Monkeys and the like are born with bodies resembling those of another [species]; or on a tree, a flower or fruit of another tree is born —

body.text: (AVParis_69,3.5) dvijottamam atharvāṇaṃ tatrecchec chāntim ātmanaḥ | kārayeta mahāśāntiṃ rāṣṭrasya ca purasya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.3.5) One should seek peace for oneself from the best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s learned in the <s>Ātharvana</s>; one should have the great pacificatory rite performed for the kingdom and the city.

body.text: (AVParis_69,4.1) upasthite rājyanāśe mahāraurava eva vā | durbhikṣe marake vāpi anāvṛṣṭibhaye 'pi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.4.1) When destruction of the kingdom is at hand, or a great calamity, or famine, or plague, or fear of drought,

body.text: (AVParis_69,4.2) sarvaṃ rāṣṭre vinaśyeta sasyaṃ śalabhamūṣakaiḥ | akasmān nirjalā vā syād aśoṣā vā mahāsarit ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.4.2) When all crops in the kingdom are destroyed by locusts and mice, or when a great river unexpectedly becomes waterless or does not dry up [when expected],
