body.text: (AVParis_69,4.3) tathānyeṣv apu anukteṣu ghoreṣūpasthiteṣu ca | kuryuḥ śāntim atharvāṇo dvijā hy eteṣu bheṣajam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.4.3) And in other terrible [portents] not mentioned [here] that have arisen — <s>Atharvan</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s should perform pacification, for they are the remedy in these [cases].

body.text: (AVParis_69,4.4) labhate rājyayogyo 'pi na rājyaṃ raja^nandanaḥ | paṭhan na labhate vidyāṃ dvijaḥ śṛṇvann api śrutam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.4.4) Even one worthy of kingship does not obtain the kingdom, a prince; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> studying does not obtain learning even while hearing the scriptures;

body.text: (AVParis_69,4.5) ādhitsur api nādhānaṃ kuryād āvāsam eva ca | kanyā pariṇinīṣur vā kāmyeṣv iṣṭapatiṃ na ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.4.5) One desiring to kindle [the sacred fires] cannot perform the fire-establishment or even [build] a dwelling; or a maiden wishing to marry — in desired matters, [one does not obtain] the wished-for husband.

body.text: (AVParis_69,5.1) vandhyā vā mṛtavatsā yā durbhagā strīprasū ca yā | sakṛtprasūtā yā nārī garbhaṃ gṛhṇāti naiva ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.5.1) She who is barren, or whose children die, or who is unfortunate, or who bears only daughters, or who has given birth only once and does not conceive again,

body.text: (AVParis_69,5.2) sūtikāle 'py atikrānte garbhe sphuraṇavaty api | na sūtiṃ labhate yā tu bahuputrīyate ca yā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.5.2) Even when the time of delivery has passed, though the fetus is stirring in the womb, she who does not obtain delivery — and she who desires many sons —

body.text: (AVParis_69,5.3) kṛṣīvalaḥ kṛṣīvalaṃ jayaty āyudhajīvy api | jayāpsur vyavahāre vā saubhāgyaṃ sārvabhautikam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.5.3) A farmer conquers [another] farmer, and one who lives by weapons [conquers] likewise; one desiring victory in a dispute, or universal good fortune —

body.text: (AVParis_69,5.4) athāpahantuṃ bhayam evamādikaṃ yadābhilaṣyet phalam uktam eva vā | tadāṅgirasyaṃ varamantrasaṃpadā sphurantam uccaiḥ śaraṇaṃ vrajed dvijam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.5.4) Then, to ward off such fear, or when one desires the stated result, one should approach a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> as refuge, one who blazes with the wealth of the supreme <s>Āṅgirasī</s> mantras.

body.text: (AVParis_69,5.5) rātrau dvichāyavṛkṣaṃ vā kusvapnaṃ vāpi riṣṭadam | divā grahān nirīkṣeta bhūmikampaivamādikam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.5.5) At night, a tree with double shadow, or a bad dream portending danger; by day, one should observe the planets, earthquakes, and such things.

body.text: (AVParis_69,6.1) jvālādbhutāny atha proktāni yāni ulkādibhedā gaditās tathā ye | svapnādbhutāny api vānyādbhutāni gṛheṣu yāny arthavido vadanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.6.1) The portents of flames that have been declared, and the various types of meteors that have been described, dream-portents and also other portents in houses that the learned describe —

body.text: (AVParis_69,6.2) eteṣu śāntiṃ kurvīta amṛtāṃ vā sadakṣiṇām | raudrīṃ vā vaiśvadevīṃ vā abhayāṃ vāparājitām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.6.2) In these, one should perform the pacificatory rite — the <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal) rite with gifts, or the <s>Raudrī</s> (relating to <s>Rudra</s>), or the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (relating to the All-Gods), or the <s>Abhayā</s> (fearlessness) rite, or the <s>Aparājitā</s> (invincible) rite,

body.text: (AVParis_69,6.3) gobhūhiraṇyavastrānnais tilair vā saphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ | upānacchattrasaṃyuktāṃ gurvābharaṇasaṃyutām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.6.3) Accompanied by [gifts of] cows, land, gold, garments, food, sesame with auspicious fruits, sandals and umbrella, and adorned with heavy ornaments.

body.text: (AVParis_69,6.4) pratipatīyathoktaṃ vā yaḥ kurvīta vidhānvit | etad utpātajaṃ sarvaṃ mahāśāntyā pralīyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.6.4) One who, knowing the rules, performs the rite as prescribed on the new-moon day — all that arises from portents is dissolved by the great pacificatory rite.

body.text: (AVParis_69,6.5) yasya rājño janapade atharvā śāntipāragaḥ | nivasaty api tadrāṣṭraṃ vardhate nirupadravam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.6.5) In whichever king's realm an <s>Atharvan</s> priest who has mastered the pacificatory rites dwells — that kingdom flourishes free from calamities.

body.text: (AVParis_69,7.1) yasya rājño janapade sa nāsti vividhair bhayaiḥ | pīḍyate tasya tad rāṣṭraṃ paṅle gaur iva majjati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.7.1) In whichever king's realm he is not present, that kingdom is afflicted by various fears, sinking like a cow in the mud.

body.text: (AVParis_69,7.2) tasmād rājā viśeṣeṇa atharvāṇaṃ jitendriyam | dānasaṃmānasatkārair nityaṃ samabhipūjayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.7.2) Therefore, the king should especially honor the self-controlled <s>Atharvan</s> priest constantly with gifts, respect, and hospitality.

body.text: (AVParis_69,7.3) nityaṃ ca kārayec chāntiṃ grahaṛkṣāṇi pūjayet | bhūmidohān prakurvīta devatāyataneṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.7.3) He should constantly have pacificatory rites performed and worship the planets and constellations; he should perform earth-offerings at temples of the deities,

body.text: (AVParis_69,7.4) catuṣpatheṣu goṣṭheṣu tīrtheṣv apsu ca kārayet | gotarpaṇaṃ ca vidhivat sarvadoṣavināśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.7.4) At crossroads, in cowpens, at pilgrimage sites, and in waters he should have [rites] performed; and the cow-libation according to rules, which destroys all faults.

body.text: (AVParis_69,7.5) evaṃ tu khyāpayan rājā sarvakālaṃ jitendriyaḥ | anantaṃ sukham āpnoti kṛtsnāṃ bhuṅkte vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.7.5) Thus, a self-controlled king proclaiming [these rites] at all times obtains infinite happiness and enjoys the entire earth.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.1) upasthitaṃ mṛtyum api dvijottamaḥ śamaṃ nayet | adhītyātharvāṅgirasas tādṛśam ādhṛtavrataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.1) The best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, having studied the <s>Ātharvāṅgirasa</s>s, firm in his vows, can bring to peace even approaching death.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.2) dyutiṃ prabhāṃ sadā sphuran mantrapavitravān naraḥ | nṛpe dhanini cānyatra śāntyāptvā dakṣiṇāṃ budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.2) A man sanctified by mantras, always shining with brilliance and radiance; having obtained gifts through pacificatory rites from kings, the wealthy, and others, the wise one,

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.3) sīdan kuṭumbakaḥ poṣaṃ gṛhītvānyat samutsṛjet | triḥ saṃhitāṃ haviṣyādyaṃ japet kṛcchraṃ ca śuddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.3) If a householder is declining, he should take sustenance and abandon other [pursuits]; he should recite the <s>Saṃhitā</s> three times, eat sacrificial food, and perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for purification.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.4) sāvitrīlakṣam ayutaṃ sahasaram atha cottaram | japtvā daśāṃśako homaḥ kāryo doṣānusārataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.4) Having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> one hundred thousand, ten thousand, or a thousand times and more, one should perform the oblation of one-tenth [of the recitations], according to the nature of the fault.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.5) śatīranirmalo yas tu nārcito 'pi dvijottaram | amatsarī nitāntaṃ yaḥ so 'tra śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.5) One who is purified by hundreds [of recitations], who even without being honored [respects] the best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, who is utterly free from envy — he should commence the pacificatory rite.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.6) evaṃvidho 'ṅgirā yatra yāni sādhyāni sādhayet | na nyūnaṃ tatra kiṃcit syād iti tad bhṛgubhāṣitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.6) Where such an <s>Āṅgirasa</s> priest performs whatever rites need to be accomplished, nothing remains deficient — thus declared by <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_69,8.7) laghuśāntyudakavidhinā gāyatryā vāpu atharvakaḥ | kuryāt sarvam idaṃ jānann atharvahṛdayaṃ budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.8.7) With the rite of the minor pacificatory water, or with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Atharvan</s> priest, knowing all this — the heart of the <s>Atharva</s> [Veda] — should perform [the rite], being wise.

body.text: (AVParis_69,9.1) ye na jānanty adhītā api śrutim āṅgirasīṃ dvijāḥ | atharvahṛdayaṃ cāpi na te vedavidaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.9.1) Those <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s who, even though they have studied, do not know the <s>Āṅgirasī</s> tradition and the Heart of the <s>Atharva</s> — they are not considered knowers of the <s>Veda</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_69,9.2) atharvahṛdayaṃ vettā atharvā paramaḥ smṛtaḥ | nātharvaṇe 'py idaṃ deyaṃ guror vidveṣayāyini ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.9.2) One who knows the Heart of the <s>Atharva</s> is considered the supreme <s>Atharvan</s>; this should not be given even to a non-<s>Atharvan</s> who causes hostility toward the teacher.

body.text: (AVParis_69,9.3) anyaśākhyaṃ dvijo mohāt pāṭhayan pravilīyate | atharvahṛdayaṃ buddhvā yaḥ paṭhed bhaktipūrvakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.9.3) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who out of delusion teaches this to one of another branch is destroyed; one who, having understood the Heart of the <s>Atharva</s>, recites it with devotion —

body.text: (AVParis_69,9.4) atharvā nādbhutaṃ tasya śāntir eva sadā bhavet | śāntir eva sadā bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 69.9.4) For that <s>Atharvan</s>, no portent [is feared]; peace alone always prevails; peace alone always prevails.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_70. bhārgavīyāṇi)
(AVParis_70,1.1) oṃ saṃpūjya vidhivat prājñaṃ vidvāṃso munayaḥ purā | apṛcchan bhṛgum avyagraṃ sarvasattvahite ratam ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 70: The <s>Bhārgavīya</s> [Teachings])
(AVParis 70.1.1) Oṃ. Having duly worshipped the wise one, the learned sages of old asked the composed <s>Bhṛgu</s>, who was devoted to the welfare of all beings:

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.2) lokatrayaniviṣṭānām utpātānām anekadhā | bhinnānāṃ śamanaṃ noktaṃ vada tv asaṃśayaṃ mune ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.2) 'The pacification of portents of many kinds occurring in the three worlds has not been told to us — declare it without doubt, O sage.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.3) pratyuvāca bhṛgur viprān śṛṇutāhitamānasaḥ | utpātaśamanatritvaṃ kathyamānam asaṃśayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.3) <s>Bhṛgu</s> replied to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s: 'Listen with attentive minds to the essence of portent-pacification being told, without doubt.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.4) tatra viprān pravakṣyāmi duriṣṭaśamanakṣamān | atharvāṅgiraso vede vidhijñān sarvakarmaṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.4) 'There I shall declare the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s capable of pacifying evil portents — those who know the rules of all rites in the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> Veda.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.5) ahiṃsāsatyadākṣiṇyaśaucaśraddhāsamanvitāḥ | śrutismṛtisadācārāḥ kulaśīlavayo 'nvitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.5) 'Endowed with non-violence, truthfulness, generosity, purity, and faith; devoted to <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and righteous conduct; possessing [good] family, character, and age.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.6) teṣām ekaḥ pradhānatve yaḥ śānto dvijasattamaḥ | bhṛgvaṅgirovid atyarthaṃ śuciḥ syāt sādhusaṃmataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.6) 'Among them, one who is pre-eminent as the chief — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the highest order who is peaceful, exceedingly learned in the [traditions of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, pure, and approved by the virtuous.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.7) brahmāṇaṃ taṃ nṛpaḥ kuryād dhotāraṃ sarvavedinam | evam ukte bhṛguṃ viprāḥ procur vigatakalmaṣam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.7) 'The king should appoint him as the <s>Brahman</s> priest and as the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), one who knows all the <s>Veda</s>s.' When this was said, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, free from sin, asked <s>Bhṛgu</s>:

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.8) hotāro bhūmibhartṝṇāṃ mahāśānteḥ prakīrtitāḥ | nanu kṣīṇe vidvan svadharmapracyute 'pi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.8) '<s>Hotṛ</s> priests of kings have been declared for the great pacificatory rite; but, O learned one, when [the king's merit] is exhausted, or when he has fallen from his own <s>dharma</s> —'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.9) tatra śāntau prayuktāyāṃ kasya śāntiphalaṃ bhavet | nṛpo 'py adhārmikaḥ kuryād brahmaṇas tarpaṇaṃ purā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.9) 'When the pacificatory rite is employed there, whose would be the fruit of pacification? Even an unrighteous king should first perform the propitiation of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.10) tataḥ kṛtā mahāśāntī rājānaṃ pāti sarvataḥ | sa vṛtaḥ pāvanaṃ gacched dvijānāṃ pāvanāya vai ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.10) 'Then the great pacificatory rite, when performed, protects the king from all sides; the chosen [priest] should proceed for the purification of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s indeed.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,1.11) dvādaśāhaṃ vrataṃ tatra payomūlaphalāśanaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.1.11) 'A twelve-day observance there, [subsisting] on milk, roots, and fruits.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,2.1) trīṇi tryahāṇi kurvīta payomūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ | anaśnaṃś ca tryahaṃ dhīraḥ sa puraścaraṇo bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.2.1) 'One should observe three periods of three days each with milk, roots, and auspicious fruits; and the steadfast one, fasting for three days — that constitutes the preliminary observance.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,2.2) tathaikonaṃ śataṃ nṝṇāṃ śuśrūṣūṇām akalmaṣam | anuktavac ca tryahaṃ tat karmaṇaḥ karaṇe kṣamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.2.2) 'Likewise, ninety-nine men, eager to learn, free from blemish, and silent for three days — that makes [them] fit for performing the rite.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,2.3) kṛcchraṃ cāpi hitaṃ kṛtvā kuryuḥ karma samāhitāḥ | śuddhātmāno japair homair vaidikair vītamatsarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.2.3) 'Having also performed the beneficial <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), they should perform the rite with concentration; with purified souls, through Vedic recitations and oblations, free from envy.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,2.4) tataḥ paraṃ purodhaḥsu divyaṃ tatram avāpnuyāt | grahātithyaṃ ca saṃrabhya diśāṃ yāgaṃ ca sarvataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.2.4) 'Thereafter, among the chief priests, one would attain the divine [status]; and having prepared the hospitality for the planets, and the sacrifice to all directions,

body.text: (AVParis_70,2.5) nakṣatreṣu ca sarveṣu yāgaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ | tato 'mṛtamahāśāntyā sthāpayet padmasaṃbhavam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.2.5) And having performed the sacrifice to all the constellations according to rules, then with the <s>Amṛta-Mahāśānti</s> (great immortal pacificatory rite), one should install the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>).'

body.text: (AVParis_70,3.1) sāvitryā lakṣahomaṃ tu bhaume tiṣṭhed viśāradāḥ | kuryur deyaṃ ca dānānāṃ viprebhyo yasya yat priyam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.3.1) 'The experts should perform the <s>Sāvitrī</s> oblation of one hundred thousand on an earthen [altar]; and one should give as gifts to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s whatever is dear to each.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,3.2) gobhūmikāñcanāśvānāṃ ratnānāṃ dhānyavāsasām | rathānāṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca dānaṃ kāmam ataḥ param ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.3.2) 'Gifts of cows, land, gold, horses, jewels, grains, garments, chariots, and elephants — and beyond this, as one desires.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,3.3) tuṣyeyur yena vā viprāḥ saṃbhavo yasya yasya hi | tat tat sarvam upādeyam eṣa dānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.3.3) 'By whatever the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s would be pleased, whatever is within the means of each — all that should be offered; this is the prescribed rule of giving.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,3.4) dadyāc ca gurave grāmaṃ dhenuṃ vāsoyugaṃ tathā | alaṃkāraiś ca saṃpūjya prīṇayet prītamānasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.3.4) 'One should give the preceptor a village, a cow, and a pair of garments; and having honored [him] with ornaments, one should gratify him with a pleased heart.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,3.5) anena vidhinā bhaumam adbhutaṃ śamayed guruḥ | eṣa eva vidhir jñeyo viyatye 'py adbhutāśraye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.3.5) 'By this prescribed procedure, the preceptor should pacify the earthly portent; this same rule should be known for portents originating from the sky as well.'

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.1) viśeṣo 'yaṃ tu sāvitryā daśalakṣāṃs tu homayet | homasamāhitamanāḥ kuryāc ca ghṛtakambalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.1) The special [rule] for the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (<s>Gāyatrī</s>) is: one should offer ten hundred-thousand oblations; with mind concentrated on the oblation, one should also offer a ghee-blanket.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.2) dhenūnāṃ dvādaśaṃ deyaṃ śataniṣkasamanvitam | gurave dīyamānaṃ tac chamayaty ambarādbhutam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.2) Twelve cows should be given, accompanied by a hundred <s>niṣka</s>s (gold coins); that [gift], when given to the preceptor, pacifies atmospheric portents.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.3) divyādbhuteṣu kartavyaḥ koṭihomasamanvitaiḥ | gosahasraṃ ca dātavyaṃ gurave dakṣiṇāvidhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.3) For celestial portents, the rite should be performed accompanied by ten-million oblations; a thousand cows should be given — [this is] the rule of gift to the preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.4) eṣa prokto vidhiḥ samyag divyāniṣṭavipatkare | subhikṣakṣemasaṃpattyā prajānāṃ puṣṭivardhanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.4) This rite has been properly declared for averting celestial inauspicious calamity; it promotes prosperity and welfare for the people through abundance of food and security.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.5) koṭihomeṣu sarveṣu dravyabhedāśrayaṃ phalam | śāntipuṣṭyabhicārārthaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.5) In all the ten-million oblations, the result depends on the difference of materials; for the purpose of pacification, prosperity, and sorcery — hear as I declare them.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.6) saumyavṛkṣāśrayāḥ kāryāḥ samidhaḥ śāntim icchatā | arkakāśmaryanimbānāṃ samidbhiḥ śatruśātanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.6) Fuel-sticks from auspicious trees should be used by one desiring pacification; with fuel-sticks of <s>arka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and <s>nimba</s> (neem) — destruction of enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.7) durnāmakaṇṭakambūnāṃ samidbhiś ca viśeṣataḥ | bhagnasphuṭitavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalaṃ śatrunibarhaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.7) With fuel-sticks of ill-named, thorny, and stunted [trees] especially; and of broken and cracked trees — the result is the annihilation of enemies.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.8) bilvapadmotpalānāṃ tu śucideśaprarohiṇām | sarvadā sarvakāmāṃs tu homaiḥ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.8) But with <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), lotus, and <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) growing in pure places, a person always obtains all desires through oblations.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.9) tilavrīhiyavādīnāṃ dadhno madhughṛtasya ca | payogodhūmaśālīnāṃ hotā śāntiṃ samārabhet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.9) With sesame, rice, barley and the like, curd, honey, and ghee, milk, wheat, and <s>śāli</s> (fine rice) — the offerer should undertake the pacificatory rite.

body.text: (AVParis_70,4.10) sarveṣāṃ haviṣāṃ caiva ghṛtaṃ śāntikaraṃ smṛtam | sarvadravye ghṛtaṃ tasmād dhome prakṣepam arhati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.4.10) Of all oblation materials, ghee is known as the pacifying agent; therefore, ghee in all materials deserves to be added to the oblation.

body.text: (AVParis_70,5.1) yajñopavītinā kāryaṃ śāntikarma vipaścitā | upavītaṃ tu pitryeṣu sarveṣv eva samārabhet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.5.1) The pacificatory rite should be performed by the learned one wearing the sacred thread; but in all rites pertaining to the ancestors, one should begin with the [left-shoulder] <s>upavīta</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70,5.2) madhvājyadadhidugdheṣu bhakṣyamāṇe vilepane | yantravāhanaśastreṣu bhavaneṣv āyudheṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.5.2) In honey, ghee, curd, and milk being consumed, and in ointment, in machines, vehicles, and weapons, in buildings and armaments,

body.text: (AVParis_70,5.3) darpaṇe bhaktapātre ca maṇimuktāphaleṣu ca | bhūṣaṇeṣu tathānyeṣu śayyāyām āsaneṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.5.3) In mirrors, food-vessels, gems, and pearls, in ornaments and other things, in beds and seats —

body.text: (AVParis_70,5.4) kākolūkakapotānāṃ madhor vā darśanaṃ bhavet | anyeṣāṃ cāpraśastānām āgamo mṛgapakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.5.4) If there is the appearance of crows, owls, pigeons, or honey; or the approach of other inauspicious animals and birds;

body.text: (AVParis_70,5.5) aśvetānāṃ ca puṣpāṇāṃ sarīsṛpagaṇasya ca | vasālohitamāṃsānām asthimajjāśiroruhām ||5 ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.5.5) And of non-white flowers, and of the group of reptiles, and of fat, blood, flesh, bones, marrow, and hair;

body.text: (AVParis_70,6.1) akasmāc caiva saṃghāte darśane nakhabhasmanām | rasānyatve rasānāṃ ca durgandhe vānimittaje ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.6.1) And if without cause there is a gathering, or the sight of nails and ashes; or an alteration of tastes, or an inexplicable foul odor;

body.text: (AVParis_70,6.2) padmapuṣpākṛtir yatra dṛśyate madhusarpiṣi | kṛsarāpāyase caiva kṣayas tasya dhanāyuṣoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.6.2) Where a lotus-flower shape is seen in honey and ghee, or in <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-sesame porridge) or milk-rice — that [portends] destruction of his wealth and life.

body.text: (AVParis_70,6.3) ghṛte vā madhudadhni vā yadā padmākṛtir bhavet | svastiko vāpi dṛśyeta tadā maraṇam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.6.3) When a lotus-shape or a <s>svastika</s> appears in ghee, honey, or curd — then one should predict death.

body.text: (AVParis_70,6.4) vikāro yatra dṛśyeta kṣīrodanahavihṣu vā | śrotriyāya tu tad dadyād bhāvaiva śamayen naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.6.4) Where a transformation is seen in milk, water, or oblation-materials — one should give that to a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; a person should pacify [it] through devotion.

body.text: (AVParis_70,6.5) yatrasthaṃ cādbhutaṃ paśyet tatrāpi pratipādayet | kuryād vā vāruṇīṃ śāntiṃ parameṇa samādhinā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.6.5) And wherever one sees a portent, there too one should communicate [it]; or one should perform the <s>Vāruṇī</s> pacificatory rite with supreme concentration.

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.1) anyākṛtiṣu vāpy etad ye sthāne śāntikārakāḥ | teṣām athākṣayaṃ vidyād āyuṣārthadhanena vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.1) In other forms also — those places where pacificatory rites [are performed] — for them one should know imperishability of lifespan, prosperity, and wealth.

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.2) calite jvalite pāte sphurita utpatite tathā | mahājanagajāśvānāṃ sthāne vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.2) When there is trembling, blazing, falling, throbbing, or leaping up — in the quarters of great assemblies, elephants, and horses — one should know great danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.3) tatra yudhyanti jātīnāṃ bhayaṃ tat syād asaṃśayam | tatrāpi cārthanicayaiḥ paśubhir vidyayāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.3) There, people of [different] castes fight — that danger is beyond doubt; there too, with accumulations of wealth, with cattle, or with learning,

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.4) utpātaśamanārthaṃ tu ye kriyā na prayuñjate | narāḥ kṣipraṃ vinaśyante sānvayāḥ saparicchadāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.4) Those people who do not employ rituals for the pacification of portents — they perish quickly along with their descendants and possessions.

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.5) viprāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ kāryaṃ sahasrasyāyutasya vā | balipuṣpopahāraiś ca devatānāṃ prasādanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.5) Feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s should be done — a thousand or ten thousand; and the propitiation of the deities with offerings of food, flowers, and gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_70,7.6) kartavyaṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ śāntikarma vipaścitā | evaṃ kṛte bhayaṃ sarvaṃ tatkṣaṇād eva naśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.7.6) The pacificatory rite should be performed properly by the learned one; when done thus, all fear is destroyed at that very moment.

body.text: (AVParis_70,8.1) śubhāśubhasthitaṃ caiva munayo bhṛgum abruvan | sa pratyuvāca puruṣu saṃvatsarasamāśraye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.8.1) The sages asked <s>Bhṛgu</s> about the auspicious and inauspicious conditions; he replied regarding the persons [years], based on the year.

body.text: (AVParis_70,8.2) śītoṣṇavṛṣṭikāleṣu vītadoṣeṣu sarvadā | saṃvatsarākhyaḥ puruṣo nirupadrava ucyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.8.2) In the cold, hot, and rainy seasons, when they are always free from defects, the year is called a person free from calamity.

body.text: (AVParis_70,8.3) yadi nirghātabhūkampadigdāhādivivarjitaḥ | ketubhiś caiva yujyeta yadi vādityakīlakaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.8.3) If it is free from thunderclaps, earthquakes, directional conflagrations, and the like, yet if it is conjoined with comets, or with solar pegs,

body.text: (AVParis_70,8.4) anyair vā lokanāśārthair adbhutair nāśanākulaiḥ | tata eṣa viśuddhātmā puruṣaḥ sukham edhate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.8.4) Or with other portents causing destruction of the world, filled with ruin — then this pure-souled person [year] prospers happily.

body.text: (AVParis_70,8.5) atha cet sa bahuvidhair adbhutaiḥ parisaṃyutaḥ | saṃvatsaraṃ bhavec chīghraṃ kuryus tacchamanaṃ budhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.8.5) But if that [year] is accompanied by manifold portents, the wise should quickly perform its pacification for the year.

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.1) tatra śāntiṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm | divyatantravid ācāryo yayā phalam avāpnuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.1) I shall now declare the pacificatory rite that destroys all sins; by which the teacher learned in the celestial treatise would obtain the result.

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.2) pūrvaṃ tāvad viśuddhātmā sa puraścaraṇo bhavet | devatānāṃ tato yāgaṃ yathāśruti samācaret ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.2) First, the pure-souled [priest] should undertake the preliminary observance; then he should perform the sacrifice to the deities according to the scriptures.

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.3) yāgaṃ kṛtvā grahāṇāṃ tu nakṣatrāṇāṃ tataḥ param | ṛtūn athārtavāṃś caiva mahādevagaṇādhipān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.3) Having performed the sacrifice to the planets, then next to the constellations; then the seasons, and the seasonal [deities], and the leaders of <s>Mahādeva</s>'s hosts,

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.4) diśaś ca vidiśaś caiva yamendravaruṇāṃs tathā | viśveśvaraṃ ca viṣṇuṃ ca yajetādbhutakarma ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.4) And the directions and intermediate directions, and <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> likewise; and <s>Viśveśvara</s> (Lord of All) and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the portent-ritual;

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.5) sūryācandramasāv agniṃ sarvān grahagaṇāṃs tathā | vāyuṃ tathāśvinau caiva mahāśāntiṃ vidhānataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.5) The sun and moon, <s>Agni</s>, all the hosts of planets likewise, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the two <s>Aśvin</s>s — the great pacificatory rite according to prescribed rules

body.text: (AVParis_70,9.6) kuryād devādṛto dhīmān evaṃ doṣaḥ praśāmyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.9.6) Should be performed by the wise one, favored by the gods; thus the fault is pacified.

body.text: (AVParis_70,10.1) śvetaṃ vā bhavati payo vilohitaṃ vā pītaṃ vā bhavati hi kṛṣṇapiṅgalaṃ vā | utpātaḥ phalati yathā catuḥprakāras tat sarvaṃ śṛṇuta samāsato mayoktam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.10.1) When rain becomes white, or blood-red, or yellow, or dark-tawny — the portent produces results of four kinds; hear all that stated by me in summary.

body.text: (AVParis_70,10.2) viprāṇāṃ bhavati hi śuklam ambudoṣe rājānaṃ sapadi nihanti lohitaṃ ca | pītaṃ ced bhavati nihanti vaiśyavargaṃ śūdrāṇāṃ bhavati hi kṛṣṇapiṅgadoṣe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.10.2) White [rain portends] defect in clouds for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; red immediately strikes the king; if yellow, it strikes the <s>Vaiśya</s> class; for <s>Śūdra</s>s, there is the defect of dark-tawny [rain].

body.text: (AVParis_70,10.3) bījaṃ yatra praroheta phalam atha pramādataḥ | etad atyadbhutaṃ nāma dampatyos tu vināśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.10.3) Where a seed sprouts, or fruit [appears] through negligence — this is a great portent called the destruction of the married couple.

body.text: (AVParis_70,10.4) apūjanāt tu pūjyasya tathāpūjyasya pūjanāt | antaḥkaraṇadoṣāc ca hetoḥ śāntir na jāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.10.4) From not honoring the honorable, and from honoring the dishonorable, and from the defect of the inner faculty — pacification does not arise from that cause.

body.text: (AVParis_70,10.5) tasmād vedārthaśāstrajñān vītarāgān amatsarān | paricārakamukhyāṃś ca kārayet kuśalān dvijān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.10.5) Therefore, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s who know the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>s and <s>śāstra</s>s, free from passion and free from envy, chief among attendants and skilled — these should be engaged.

body.text: (AVParis_70,11.1) vicāritaṃ ca vidvadbhir niścitaṃ sudhiyā punaḥ | deśakālasamāyuktaṃ karma kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.11.1) Deliberated by the learned and determined again by the wise, the discerning one should perform the rite suited to the place and time.

body.text: (AVParis_70,11.2) codite karmaṇy anyasmin nānyat kuryād vidhānavit | na ca prārabhya karmāṇi sthātavyaṃ kva cid antare ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.11.2) When engaged in one prescribed ritual, the knower of rules should not perform another; and having begun rituals, one should not stop anywhere in between.

body.text: (AVParis_70,11.3) nāpi kurvīta matimān kadā cit karmasaṃkaram | kurvaṃs tu na tathā karma doṣam utpādayed bhṛśam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.11.3) Nor should the wise one ever make a mixture of rituals; for one performing a rite improperly would generate severe fault.

body.text: (AVParis_70,11.4) anyathākaraṇe doṣān samīkṣya tu bahūn iha | saṃkalpavān na samāptiḥ [sāvīryākṛtikarmaṇī] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.11.4) Considering the many faults in improper performance — [without] determination there is no completion [of a rite with the required form and efficacy].

body.text: (AVParis_70,11.5) dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ tu kārtsnyena tataḥ śāntiṃ samārabhet | asamīkṣya tu kurvāṇo na śāntiṃ labhate naraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.11.5) Having seen a portent in its entirety, then one should undertake the pacificatory rite; performing it without careful examination, a person does not obtain pacification.

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.1) vātikasya yathā vaidyaḥ paittikasya ca niścaye | rogasya bhaiṣaje datte karmasiddhim avāpnuyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.1) Just as a physician, upon determining the wind-type or bile-type disease, achieves success when the medicine is given,

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.2) tasmāt tāvat parīkṣeta yāvan niṣpannam adbhutam | asadasyasadasyānāṃ kartuḥ kārayitus tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.2) So one should examine until the portent has fully manifested; [the fault of] unqualified and qualified [performers], and of the agent and the instigator,

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.3) viguṇaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tu karma kuryād upadravam | viśeṣato nihanyeta kartāraṃ saparicchadam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.3) A rite performed deficiently would cause calamity; it would especially destroy the performer along with his possessions.

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.4) hetuśrutaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ ca tasmāt sāguṇyam ācaret | saguṇe ca kṛte tasmin sarvasaṃpad bhaved dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.4) [A rite] based on what is heard and what is seen — therefore one should perform it with full qualifications; and when done with full qualifications, all prosperity is certain.

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.5) aśokapuṣpair home tu madhukṣīrasamanvitaiḥ | prāpnoti sukṛtair vipro gandharvapadam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.5) With oblations of <s>aśoka</s> flowers accompanied by honey and milk, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through meritorious [acts] attains the supreme realm of the <s>Gandharva</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_70,12.6) brahmādistambaparyantaṃ yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ samīhate | tat tat prāpnoty ayatnena satyam etad dvijottamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70.12.6) Whatever desire one has, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — all that one obtains effortlessly; this is true, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_70b. gārgyāṇi)
(AVParis_70b,1.1) oṃ praṇamya viṣṭarāsīnāṃ brahmāṇaṃ kavisattamam | praṇamya śirasā devaṃ gautamaḥ paryapṛcchata ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 70b: The <s>Gārgya</s> [Teachings])
(AVParis 70b.1.1) Oṃ. Having bowed to <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme sage seated on [his] grass seat, bowing with his head, <s>Gautama</s> questioned [him].

body.text: (AVParis_70b,1.2) adbhutāni suraśreṣṭha prajānām ahitāya vai | śamanaṃ ca tathā teṣāṃ prabrūhi vinayena me ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.1.2) 'O best of the gods, portents [arise] for the harm of the people; the pacification of those — declare it to me with humility.'

body.text: (AVParis_70b,1.3) tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ | abravīt paramaḥ prītaḥ sarvotpātapratikriyām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.1.3) Having heard that speech of his, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds, supremely pleased, declared the counter-measures for all portents.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,1.4) śṛṇu vatsa yathānyāyaṃ dvādaśādhyāyasaṃgraham | pracyamānam aśeṣaṃ taṃ vātavaikṛtanoditam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.1.4) 'Hear, my child, in proper order, the compendium of twelve chapters, this entire [text] being recited, prompted by wind-transformations.'

body.text: (AVParis_70b,1.5) yasmāc ca vāyur valavāñ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvādbhutodbhavaḥ | tasmāt tam eva prathamaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvidhi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.1.5) 'Since the wind is powerful and foremost [among] the sources of all portents, therefore I shall declare it first, according to the prescribed rules.'

body.text: (AVParis_70b,2.1) yānti yānāny ayuktāni vinā nṛbhis tathā | yuktāni vā na gacchanti narendrāṇāṃ mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.2.1) Vehicles go unyoked, without men likewise; or yoked, they do not go — great danger to kings.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,2.2) bheryo mṛdaṅgāḥ paṭahā vādyante vāpy anāhatāḥ | āhatāś ca na vādyante acalāni calanti vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.2.2) Drums, <s>mṛdaṅga</s>s, and kettledrums sound unstruck; and struck ones do not sound; immovable things move;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,2.3) araṇye tūryanirghoṣo yadi śrūyeta nābhasaḥ | śarīraṃ vyathate tatra yadi vā veśmani śrutaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.2.3) If the sound of musical instruments is heard from the sky in a forest — the body suffers there; or if heard in a dwelling;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,2.4) śrūyante ca mahāśabdā gītagāndharvanisvanāḥ | śarīraṃ bādhyate tatra vyādhir vā sumahān bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.2.4) And great sounds are heard — singing and <s>Gandharva</s> music; the body is afflicted there, or a very great disease occurs.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,2.5) koṣṭhe vā patate yatra hastād darvī kadā cana | patate musalaṃ cāpi śūrpaṃ vā dhūyate yadi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.2.5) When a ladle falls from the hand into the storehouse at any time, or a pestle falls, or if a winnowing basket is shaken [by itself],

body.text: (AVParis_70b,3.1) golāṅgalānāṃ saṃsargo vikāraś candrasūryayoḥ | nārīṃ vā dhayate nārī jāyate tumulaṃ bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.3.1) Contact with langur monkeys, a transformation of the moon and sun; or a woman suckles [another] woman — tumultuous fear arises.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,3.2) pratyāharanti sarpanti stambhaprāsādapādapāḥ | śayanāsanayānāni niyataṃ nṛpater vadhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.3.2) Pillars, palaces, and trees retract and creep — [as do] beds, seats, and vehicles — certain death of the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,3.3) vāti cākālilo vāyur ghoraḥ śarkarakarṣaṇaḥ | pātayan vṛkṣaveśmāni kalpānta iva bhīṣaṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.3.3) An untimely wind blows, terrible, dragging gravel, felling trees and buildings, frightful as the end of an age.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,3.4) saptāham atha vā pakṣaṃ nibadhnāty atidāruṇam | tryahād yadi na varṣeta ghoraṃ śastrabhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.3.4) For a week or a fortnight it rages exceedingly terribly; if it does not rain after three days, there will be terrible fear from weapons.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,3.5) vāyavyeṣv eva nṛpatir vāyuṃ saptabhir arcayet | dvāv imāv iti tisro hi japtavyāḥ prayatair dvijaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.3.5) With the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind-deity) [rites], the king should worship <s>Vāyu</s> with seven [verses]; the three [verses] '<s>dvāv imau</s>' should be recited by purified <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,4.1) bahvannadakṣiṇo homaḥ kartavyo 'tiprayatnataḥ | vāyavyām eva śāntau ca vāyoḥ savitur āvapet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.4.1) Oblation with abundant food and gifts should be performed with great effort; in the wind-pacificatory rite, one should offer to <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,4.2) ādāv ante ca madhye ca tathaivam anuyojayet | gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād vāyavīśāntisiddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.4.2) At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle — thus one should employ [the rites]; one should give a gift to the preceptor for the success of the wind-pacification.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,4.3) yamakaṃ jāyate puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vā yamakaṃ yadi | kumudotpalapadmāni ekanāle bahūny api ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.4.3) When a twin flower is born, or if twin fruit [appears]; <s>kumuda</s>s (night lotuses), <s>utpala</s>s (blue lotuses), and <s>padma</s>s (lotuses) — many on a single stalk;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,4.4) bahuśīrṣā dviśīrṣā vā tathānyaprasavā api | yavā vā vrīhayo vāpi svāmino maraṇāya te ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.4.4) Many-headed or two-headed, and also other [abnormal] growths; whether barley or rice — these portend the death of the master.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,4.5) ekavṛkṣe ca saṃpaśyen nānātvaṃ phalapuṣpayoḥ | vyatyāsam anyathātvaṃ vā paracakrāgamo bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.4.5) If one observes on a single tree diversity of fruits and flowers, reversal or alteration — there will be an invasion by a foreign army.

body.text:
(AVParis_70b,5) [The manuscripts contain no khaṇḍikā five.]
(AVParis_70b,6.1) anṛtu phalapuṣpaṃ vā na yathartu phalanti vā | oṣadhīvīrudho vāpi janamārabhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text:
(AVParis 70b.5) [The manuscripts contain no chapter five.]
(AVParis 70b.6.1) Flowers or fruits out of season, or [plants] not bearing fruit in their proper season; herbs and creepers likewise — there will be fear of plague among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,6.2) atha dhānyaviparyāse abhadraṃ cāpi śaṃsati | tilā vā samatailāḥ syuḥ surātailā bhavanti vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.6.2) Now, in the reversal of grains, it also foretells misfortune; sesame seeds may be oily, or liquor may become oily;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,6.3) agrāmyaṃ kārayet puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vā vikṛtaṃ nṛpaḥ | dhānyānāṃ vaikṛte kṣetraṃ saha sasyena dāpayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.6.3) If a non-cultivated [plant] produces flowers, or fruit becomes deformed — the king should give away the field together with its crops upon the alteration of grains.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,6.4) sauryaṃ caruṃ puṣpaphale vikṛte paśum eva ca | kṣaitrapatyaṃ ca bhaumaṃ ca nirvapet sasyavaikṛte ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.6.4) A <s>saurya</s> (solar) oblation when flowers and fruits are deformed, and an animal [sacrifice] as well; a <s>kṣaitrapatya</s> (field-lord) and <s>bhaumya</s> (earth) [oblation] should be offered when crops are altered.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,6.5) sauryī śāntiḥ prayoktavyā sauryair mantrair yathāvidhi | uccā patantam ity ṛgbhyāṃ garbhaṃ tu parikīrtitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.6.5) The <s>saurī</s> (solar) pacificatory rite should be employed with solar <s>mantra</s>s according to prescribed rules; with the two <s>ṛc</s> verses beginning '<s>uccā patantam</s>' — the conception [of the rite] is declared.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.1) bhaumena cānuvākena garbhayet sasyavaikṛte | sadakṣiṇair dvijair bhuktaiḥ kartāraṃ cārcayet tataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.1) With the <s>bhaumya</s> (terrestrial) <s>anuvāka</s> (recitation section), one should conceive [the rite] when crops are altered; then, with twice-born [priests] who have been fed and given gifts, one should honor the performer.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.2) pureṣu yeṣu dṛśyante pādapā devacoditāḥ | rudanto vā hasanto vā sravanto vā bahūn rasān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.2) In the cities where trees, impelled by the gods, are seen — weeping or laughing or exuding many saps;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.3) arogā vā nivāte ca śākhā muñcanty asaṃbhrame | phalaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā bālā darśayantīti hāsanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.3) Or when healthy [trees] in a calm [place] shed their branches without agitation; when [trees] display fruits, flowers, and also young shoots — that indicates calamity.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.4) sarvāvasthāṃ darśayantaḥ phalapuṣpam anārtavam | [kṣipraṃ tatra bhayaṃ ghoraṃ ghoraṃ pravaryteta caturvidham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.4) [Trees] displaying all conditions — fruits and flowers out of season; [swiftly, terrible fear of four kinds would arise there;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.5) sarpān matsyān pakṣiṇo vā yatra devaḥ pravarṣati | tatra sasyopaghātaḥ syād bhayaṃ vātipravartate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.5) Where the god rains down serpents, fish, or birds — there will be destruction of crops, or fear exceedingly arises.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.6) surāsavaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ sarpis tailaṃ tathā dadhi | yatra varṣati parjanyaḥ kṣudragas tatra jāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.6) Where <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain god) rains down liquor, <s>āsava</s> (fermented drink), honey, ghee, oil, and curds — there a minor calamity arises.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.7) ulkātārāś ca dhiṣṇyeṣu yadāṅgārāṃś ca varṣati | tadā vyādhibhayaṃ ghoraṃ teṣu deśeṣu nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.7) When meteors and stars fall upon the constellations, and when it rains embers — then one should predict terrible fear of disease in those regions.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.8) nārācāḥ śaktayaḥ khaḍgāḥ pradīpyante yadā muhuḥ | tadā śastrabhayaṃ ghoraṃ teṣu deśeṣu nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.8) When arrows, spears, and swords blaze up repeatedly — then one should predict terrible fear of weapons in those regions.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.9) pumān aśvo gajo vāpi yadā yatra pradīpyate | naśyanti sevakās tatra pradhānaś ca vinaṅkṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.9) When a man, horse, or elephant catches fire anywhere — servants perish there, and the chief will be destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.10) yatra sravec caityavṛkṣaḥ sahasā vividhān rasān | pṛthakpṛthak samastān vā tat pravakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.10) Where a sacred tree suddenly exudes various saps — separately or all together — I shall declare the signs of that.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.11) ghṛte madhuni dugdhe ca ghṛte dugdhe tathāmbhasi | kṣaudre madhuni pānīye ghṛte caivāparaṃ payaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.11) In ghee, in honey, in milk; in ghee, in milk, and in water; in mead, in honey, in water; and in ghee again, milk —

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.12) yatraitac ca mahotpātaṃ vṛkṣeṣu syāt sudāruṇam | surāsave mithobhedaḥ śoṇite śastrapātanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.12) Where this great portent occurs among trees, most terrible; [exuding] liquor and wine [portends] mutual discord; [exuding] blood, the fall of weapons;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.13) taile pradhānā vadhyante bhakte kṣudbhayam ādiśet | anṛtau cet phalaṃ yatra puṣpaṃ vā dṛśyate drume ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.13) [Exuding] oil — the chiefs are slain; [exuding] food, one should predict fear of famine; if out of season, where fruit or flowers are seen on a tree,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.14) dhruvaṃ syād daśame māsi rājñas tatra viparyayaḥ | puṣpe puṣpaṃ bhaved yatra phale caiva tathā phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.14) Certainly in the tenth month there will be reversal for the king there; where flower [grows] upon flower, and likewise fruit upon fruit,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.15) parṇe parṇaṃ vijānīyāt tatra nānāvidhaṃ bhayam | śuklena vāsasā yatra caityavṛkṣaḥ samāvṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.15) One should recognize leaf upon leaf — there [arises] manifold fear; where a sacred tree is covered with white cloth,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.16) brāhmaṇānāṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ tadā tīvraṃ vinirdiśet | raktavastrāvṛtaiś cānyaiḥ kṣatraiyāṇāṃ mahābhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.16) Then one should predict severe, terrible fear for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; and when covered by others with red garments — great fear for <s>Kṣatriya</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.17) pītavastraiś tu vaiśyānāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ kṛṣṇavāsasaiḥ | nīlaiḥ sasyopaghātāya miśrais tu mṛgapakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.17) With yellow garments, [fear] for <s>Vaiśya</s>s; for <s>Śūdra</s>s, with black garments; with blue [garments], destruction of crops; with mixed [garments], [fear] for animals and birds.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.18) vivarṇair vāyavas tīvrāḥ paraṃ syur daśamāsataḥ | daivatāni pralapanti yasya rāṣṭre hasanti vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.18) With discolored [garments], fierce winds — the effect occurring after ten months; in whose kingdom the deities prattle or laugh,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.19) udīkṣante puro vāpi tatra vidyān mahad bhayam | vihasanti nimīlanti liṅgāni vikṛtāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.19) Or gaze toward the city — there one should know great fear; [if they] laugh, close their eyes, and [their] forms are distorted,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.20) māsāntareṇa jānīyāt tatra tatra mahad bhayam | yatra citram udīkṣeta gāyate ceṣṭate muhuḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.20) One should know great fear there within an interval of months; where a painting gazes [outward], sings, or moves repeatedly,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.21) eteṣv aṣṭasu māseṣu rājño maraṇam ādiśet | citrāṇi yatra liṅgāni tathaivāyatanāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.21) Within these eight months one should predict the death of the king; where images, <s>liṅga</s>s (sacred symbols), and likewise temples,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.22) vikāraṃ kuryur atyarthaṃ tatra vidyān mahābhayam | utpāṭanaṃ tadāgānāṃ saraso vā fires tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.22) Undergo excessive transformation — there one should know great fear; uprooting of reservoirs, or of lakes, or fires likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.23) samuddeśe pradīpyante vidyāt tatra bhayaṃ mahat | yatra vṛkṣā akālīnaṃ darśanaṃ phalapuṣpayoḥ] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.23) Blaze up in [various] locations — one should know great fear there; where trees [show] untimely appearance of fruits and flowers,]

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.24) kṣīraṃ snehaṃ surāṃ raktaṃ madhu toyaṃ sravanti vā | śūṣyanty arogāḥ sahasā śuṣkā ruhanti vā punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.24) Or exude milk, oil, liquor, blood, honey, or water; or healthy [trees] suddenly wither, or withered ones sprout again;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,7.25) uttiṣṭhanti niṣīdanti tat pravakṣyāny ataḥ param ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.7.25) [Trees] rise up or sink down — I shall declare [the meaning of] that hereafter.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,8.1) hasane dehanāśaḥ syād yodhā naśyanti śakhayā | saṃbhramo deśanāśāya phalī śilpikṣayāya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.8.1) Laughter [of trees portends] destruction of the body; warriors perish through [shedding of] branches; agitation [portends] destruction of the region; bearing fruit, destruction of artisans.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,8.2) bālānāṃ maraṇaṃ kuryād bālānāṃ phalapuṣpatā | svarāṣṭrabhedaṃ kurute phalapuṣpam anārtavam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.8.2) Bearing fruit and flowers [in young trees] causes the death of children; [such] fruiting and flowering out of season brings discord in one's own kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,8.3) kṣayaḥ kṣīrasrave jñeyaḥ snehe durbhikṣalakṣaṇam | vāhanāpacayaṃ madye rakte saṃgrāmam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.8.3) Exuding milk indicates destruction; [exuding] oil is a sign of famine; [exuding] wine, loss of vehicles; [exuding] blood, one should predict battle.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,8.4) madhusrāve bhaved vyādhir jalasrāve na varṣati | arogā yadi śuṣyante vidyād durbhikṣalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.8.4) Exuding honey would bring disease; exuding water [means] it will not rain; if healthy [trees] wither — one should know [it as] a sign of famine.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,8.5) bhedaḥ svapatitotthāne rudatsv annakṣayo bhavet | jalpane dhananāśaḥ syād gulmavallīlatāsu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.8.5) Discord [arises] when [a fallen tree] rises again; when [trees] weep, destruction of food occurs; when [they] chatter, destruction of wealth — [this applies] also to shrubs, creepers, and vines.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,9.1) pūjitānāṃ jalasrutau rājño mṛtyuṃ samādiśet | ācchādayitvā taṃ vṛkṣāṃ gandhamālyair vibhūṣayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.9.1) When venerated [trees] exude water, one should predict the death of the king; having covered that tree, one should adorn it with fragrant garlands;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,9.2) bhojanaṃ cātra viprāṇāṃ madhusarpiḥsamanvitam | chattradhvajaṃ ca dātavyaṃ parṇahomas tathā param ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.9.2) And feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s there, accompanied by honey and ghee; an umbrella and banner should be given, and then an oblation of leaves.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,9.3) mantrair auṣadhasaṃyuktair bhvoradāban ataḥ param | baliṃ caivopahārāṃś ca gītanṛtyaṃ samantataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.9.3) With <s>mantra</s>s combined with herbs — hereafter [the procedure]; and offerings and presentations likewise, singing and dancing all around.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,9.4) gandhamālyaṃ ca dhūpaṃ ca dīpaṃ dadyāt tathaiva ca | bhakṣabhojyānnapānaṃ ca rudrasyopaharen niśi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.9.4) Fragrant garlands, incense, and lamps should be given likewise; food, eatables, provisions, and drink should be offered to <s>Rudra</s> at night.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,9.5) pākaś ca daśame māsi śukrasya vacanaṃ yathā | bṛhaspatis tathāditye bruvete yat tathaiva tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.9.5) The ripening [of results occurs] in the tenth month, as declared by <s>Śukra</s>; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Āditya</s> also declare the same.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,10.1) raudrī caivātra kartavyā vṛkṣādbhutavināśinī | durave dakṣiṇāṃ dadyān niṣkaṃ bhūmiṃ ca tatra vai ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.10.1) The <s>Raudrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Rudra</s>) [pacificatory rite] should be performed here, which destroys tree-portents; as a gift, one should give a gold coin and land there.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,10.2) akālaprasuvo nāryaḥ kālātītāḥ prajās tathā | saṃbaddhayugmaprasavā dviyugmaprasavā api ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.10.2) Women who give birth prematurely, or those whose [delivery] time is overdue; those who bear conjoined twins, or those who bear double twins;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,10.3) amānuṣāṇi ruṇḍāni saṃjāyante yadā striyām | atyaṅgāni anaṅgāni hīnāṅgāny atha vā punaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.10.3) When non-human headless [forms] are born from a woman; with extra limbs, without limbs, or with deficient limbs;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,10.4) catuṣpatpakṣisadṛśāny ardhamānuṣavanti ca | vināśas tatsya deśasya kulasya ca vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.10.4) Resembling quadrupeds or birds, or half-human — one should predict the destruction of that region and that family.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,10.5) aprāptavayaso garbho dvicatuṣpatstriyo 'pi vā | vidhvastaṃ vikṛtaṃ cāpi prajāyeta bhayāya tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.10.5) If a woman who has not reached [proper] age conceives, or a woman [bearing] two or four legs — [the birth] ruined or deformed — that portends danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,11.1) tāny āśu parabhūmiṣu tyaktavyāni śubhārthibhiḥ | śāntiś cātra prakartavyā brāhmaṇair brahmavādibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.11.1) Those [deformed offspring] should be quickly abandoned in foreign lands by those desiring welfare; and the pacificatory rite should be performed there by <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s who know the <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,11.2) vaḍavā hastinī gaur vā yadi yugmaṃ prasūyate | vijātaṃ vikṛtaṃ vāpi ṣaṇmāsair mriyate nṛpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.11.2) If a mare, cow-elephant, or cow gives birth to twins, or [the offspring is] misborn or deformed — the king dies within six months.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,11.3) apatyāni ca yūthebhyas tyājyāni parabhūmiṣu | svāmino nagaraṃ yūtham anyathā tu vināśayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.11.3) The offspring should be abandoned from the herds in foreign lands; otherwise it would destroy the master, the city, and the herd.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,11.4) viyoniṣu yadā yānti ṃśrībhāvaḥ prajāsv api | kharoṣṭrahayamātaṅgāḥ pakṣiṇo vā na sādhu tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.11.4) When [animals] go to those of other species — [there is] loss of prosperity among the people also; donkeys, camels, horses, elephants, or birds [mating abnormally] — that is not auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,11.5) akāle vāpi mādyante kāle vāpu amadā yadi | śivoṣṭrahayamātaṅgāḥ pakṣiṇo vā na sādhu tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.11.5) If [animals] become excited out of season, or if they are not excited in the proper season; dogs, camels, horses, elephants, or birds — that is not auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,12.1) athānaḍvān anaḍvāhaṃ dhenur dhenuṃ pibed yadi | śunī vā dhayate dhenuṃ śunīṃ dhenur athāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.12.1) Now, if a bull suckles a bull, or a cow [suckles] a cow; or if a bitch suckles a cow, or a cow [suckles] a bitch;

body.text: (AVParis_70b,12.2) [tiryagyonau mānuṣī vā paracakrāgamo bhavet | amānuṣā mānuṣāṇi jalapante prāṇino yadi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.12.2) [If a human woman [gives birth] in an animal womb — there will be invasion by a foreign army; if non-human creatures speak to humans,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,12.3) viceṣṭāṃ vā virāvaṃ vā māsena mriyate nṛpaḥ] | catuṣpatpakṣibhujagān mānuṣī janayed yadi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.12.3) Or [display] strange movements or cries — the king dies within a month.] If a human woman gives birth to quadrupeds, birds, or serpents,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,12.4) tiryagyonau mānuṣaṃ vā paracakrāgamo bhavet | jaṅgame sthāvaraṃ jātaṃ sthāvare vātha jaṅgamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.12.4) Or if a human [is born] in an animal womb — there will be invasion by a foreign army; if a movable [being] is born as stationary, or a stationary [being] as movable,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,12.5) tasmin yoniviparyāse paracakrāgamo bhavet | tyāgo vivāso dānaṃ vā dattvāpy āśu śubhaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.12.5) In that reversal of species, there will be invasion by a foreign army; [by] abandonment, exile, or giving [it] away — auspiciousness quickly arises.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,13.1) sthālīpākena yaṣṭavyaṃ paśunā vā purohitaḥ | prājāpatyena mantreṇa yajed bahvannadakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.13.1) The <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) should sacrifice with a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) or with an animal; with <s>Prājāpatya</s> (relating to <s>Prajāpati</s>) <s>mantra</s>s he should sacrifice, with abundant food and gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,13.2) yāmyākarmaprayogas tu prathamaṃ tatra dṛśyate | prājāpatyāṃ tataḥ śāntiṃ prājārthī kārayen nṛpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.13.2) The <s>Yāmya</s> (relating to <s>Yama</s>) ritual procedure is seen first there; then the king desiring offspring should have the <s>Prājāpatya</s> pacificatory rite performed.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,13.3) ādāv ante ca madhye ca śāntāv uktas tu tadgaṇaḥ | ārogyaṃ ca śivaṃ caiva deśe tasmin nṛpe bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.13.3) At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle — in the pacificatory rite, that group [of deities] is invoked; health and auspiciousness will arise in that region for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,13.4) yatrādbhutāni dṛśyante vicitrāṇi samantataḥ | susamṛddho 'pi deśaḥ sa kṣipram eva vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.13.4) Where wondrous portents are seen of various kinds all around — even a very prosperous region quickly perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,13.5) rājaveśmasu vaikṛtye prāsādadhvajatoraṇe | autpātikāni dṛśyante rājñas tatra mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.13.5) When distortions [appear] in the royal palaces, in the mansions, banners, and gateways — portentous [signs] are seen — there is great fear for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,14.1) prāsādatoraṇāṭṭāladvāraprāsādaveśmanām | akasmāt patanaṃ teṣāṃ rājamṛtyukaraṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.14.1) The sudden falling of mansions, gateways, watchtowers, doors, palaces, and dwellings — that is declared to cause the death of the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,14.2) devarājadhvajānāṃ ca patanaṃ bhaṅga eva vā | niṣevaṇaṃ vā kravyādaiḥ..........prabhraṣṭair vītaraśmikaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.14.2) The falling or breaking of banners of gods and kings; or their being frequented by carrion-eaters... [text corrupt]... with fallen, rayless [luminaries];

body.text: (AVParis_70b,15.1) prabhraṣṭagrahanakṣatrair diśaḥ sarvāḥ samākulāḥ | saṃdhyā cobhayathā dīptā tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.15.1) With fallen planets and constellations, all directions in turmoil; and the twilight blazing on both sides — there one should know great fear.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,15.2) yadi vā dīryate 'kasmād bhūmiś chidrībhaved yadi | prakampate 'timātraṃ vā sarveṣu ca bhayāya tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.15.2) If the earth suddenly splits open, or if the ground becomes perforated; or if it trembles excessively — that portends fear for all.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,15.3) rakṣaḥpataṃgaiḥ panthāno na vahanti bhayānvitāḥ | rakṣorūpāṇi dṛśyante na ca rakṣā gṛheṣv api ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.15.3) The paths do not function, [being beset] by demonic moths, [travelers are] filled with fear; forms of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s are seen, and there is no protection even in houses.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,15.4) saṃpraviṣṭaiḥ piśācair vā rakṣobhir vāpi tannibhaiḥ | acirān nagaraṃ tatra janamāreṇa māryate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.15.4) With <s>Piśāca</s>s (flesh-eating demons) or <s>Rākṣasa</s>s (demons) or similar [beings] having entered — soon that city is destroyed by plague among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,15.5) ṛtavas tu viparyastā brāhmaṇāś ca vidharmiṇaḥ | nakṣatrāṇi viyogīni bhayam īdṛk pradarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.15.5) The seasons are reversed, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s are unrighteous; the constellations are disjoined — such is the indication of danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,16.1) apūjyā yatra pūjyante na pūjyante ca pūjitāḥ | pūjyeṣv adānaniṣṭhā ca bhayam īdṛk pradarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.16.1) Where the unworthy are honored and the worthy are not honored, and there is no devotion to giving among the venerable — such is the indication of danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,16.2) nādīyante na pūjyante brāhmaṇā balibhiḥ surāḥ | na caivātmīyadharmeṣu ratiṃ kurvanty adharmataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.16.2) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s are not revered, nor are the gods honored with offerings; and they do not take delight in their own duties, [acting] unrighteously.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,16.3) bhinnāḥ kauṭilyabahulā gajāḥ puruṣavājinaḥ | kalahe syur nirutsāhāḥ sasatyāḥ satyavarjitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.16.3) Elephants, men, and horses, broken and full of crookedness, would be spiritless in battle, though allied [they are] devoid of truth.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,16.4) śīlācāravihīnāś ca madyamāṃsānṛtapriyāḥ | nagnapāṣaṇḍabhūyiṣṭhā vināśe paryupasthite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.16.4) Devoid of good conduct and virtuous behavior, fond of liquor, meat, and falsehood, abounding in naked heretics — when destruction is at hand.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,16.5) mahābaliṃ mahāśāntiṃ bhojyāni sumahānti ca | prājāpatyaṃ mahendraṃ ca mahādevam athāpi vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.16.5) A great offering, a great pacificatory rite, and very great feasts; the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [rite], the <s>Māhendra</s>, or that of <s>Mahādeva</s> also —

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.1) aindrasthāne tu māhendrīṃ raudre raudrīṃ prayojayet | gavām aṣṭaśataṃ dadyād viprebhyo manujādhipaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.1) In the station of <s>Indra</s>, one should employ the <s>Māhendrī</s> [rite]; in the <s>Raudra</s> [station], the <s>Raudrī</s>; the lord of men should give eight hundred cows to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.2) gurave tu śataṃ niṣkaṃ prajāsv evaṃ śivaṃ bhavet | anāvṛṣṭyātivṛṣṭyā vā durbhikṣeṇa bhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.2) And a hundred <s>niṣka</s>s of gold to the preceptor — thus there will be well-being for the people; from drought or excessive rain, danger may arise from famine.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.3) akālavarṣo rogāya ativṛṣṭir bhayāya ca | anabhraṃ varṣate 'kasmād vaidyutaṃ garjitaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.3) Untimely rain [portends] disease; excessive rain, danger; when it rains suddenly from a cloudless [sky], likewise lightning and thunder,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.4) anabhre vāpi nirghātaḥ patito rājamṛtyave | tīkṣṇaṃ ca varṣaty anṛtau ṛtuṣv eva na varṣati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.4) A thunderbolt falling from a cloudless sky [portends] death of the king; and when it rains harshly out of season, and does not rain in the proper seasons,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.5) yadā coṣṇe bhavec chītaṃ śīte coṣṇaṃ tathaiva ca | dṛṣṭo bhāvas tu vikṛto na yathartu svarūpakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.5) When it becomes cold in the hot [season] and hot in the cold [season] likewise, the observed natural state is distorted, not in accordance with its seasonal character —

body.text: (AVParis_70b,17.6) anārogyaṃ bhavec caiva prajānām iti nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.17.6) One should declare that there will be ill-health among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.1) saptarātraṃ yadā varṣet prabaddhaṃ pākaśāsanaḥ | anṛtau tasya deśasya pradhānasya vadho dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.1) When <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (Indra) rains continuously for seven nights out of season, the death of the chief of that land is certain.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.2) śoṇitaṃ varṣate yatra tatra śastrabhayaṃ bhavet | majjāsthisnehamāṃsaṃ vā janamārībhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.2) Where it rains blood, there will be danger from weapons; if marrow, bones, fat, or flesh [rain down], there will be danger of pestilence among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.3) aṅgārapāṃsuvṛṣṭes tu nagaraṃ tad vinaśyati | phalaṃ puṣpaṃ śamīdhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ vā bhayāya tat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.3) From a rain of embers and dust, that city is destroyed; fruit, flowers, <s>śamī</s> grain, or gold [raining] portends danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.4) jantavo dīnavikṛtāḥ palālo 'pi vināśanaḥ | chidrāvartāḥ plavaṅgaś ca sasyānām ativardhanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.4) Creatures distressed and deformed, even chaff [raining], portend destruction; whirlpools with holes, floating [objects], and excessive growth of crops,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.5) anabhre vā divā rātrau śvetam indrāyudhaṃ bhavet | pūrvapaścāduttare vā dakṣiṇe vāpi dṛśyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.5) In a cloudless [sky], by day or night, if a white rainbow appears — whether seen in the east, west, north, or south —

body.text: (AVParis_70b,18.6) susamṛddham api sthānaṃ durbhikṣeṇa vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.18.6) Even a very prosperous place is destroyed by famine.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.1) yady anabhre 'pi vimale sūryachāyā na dṛśyate | na nirabhre pratīpā vā tatra deśabhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.1) If in a cloudless, clear [sky] the shadow of the sun is not seen, or [if it appears] reversed when the sky is cloudless — there will be danger to that region.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.2) sūryendravāyuparjanyā yaṣṭavyā varṣavaikṛte | annāni sahiraṇyāni dhānyaṃ gāvaś ca dakṣiṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.2) <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Parjanya</s> should be worshipped when there is an anomaly of rainfall; food along with gold, grain, and cows [should be given] as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual gifts).

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.3) vaiśvadevī ca kartavyā sarvādbhutavināśinī | gurave ca hayaḥ śvetaḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.3) The <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> [rite] should also be performed, which destroys all portents; and a white horse marked with all auspicious signs [should be given] to the preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.4) śataṃ niṣkaṃ suvarṇasya dātavyaṃ vā gavāṃ śatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.4) A hundred <s>niṣka</s>s of gold should be given, or a hundred cows.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.5) athāto 'gnivaikṛtam adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmo yathovāca bhagavāñśukraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.5) Now we shall expound the chapter on fire-portents, as the blessed <s>Śukra</s> declared.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.6) anindhano 'gnir dīpyeta yatra tūrṇam aghasvanaḥ | na dīpyate sendhano vā sarāṣṭraṃ pīḍayen nṛpam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.6) Where fire blazes without fuel, quickly with a dreadful sound, or does not blaze even with fuel — it would afflict the king along with his kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,19.7) prajvaled dadhi māṃsaṃ vā tathā dūrvāpi kiṃ cana | agniṃ vinā yadāśuṣkaṃ niyataṃ nṛpater vadhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.19.7) If curd, meat, or <s>dūrvā</s> grass or anything else ignites, [and] without fire when it is dry — the death of the king is certain.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,20.1) prāsādaṃ toraṇaṃ dvāraṃ prākāraṃ kāśyapaṃ gṛham | śayanāsanayānaṃ ca dhvajaṃ chattraṃ sacāmaram ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.20.1) A palace, gateway, door, rampart, the house of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, a bed, seat, vehicle, banner, parasol, and fly-whisk —

body.text: (AVParis_70b,20.2) anagninā yadi dahed vidyutā vāpi nirdahet | saptāhābhyantare tatra niyataṃ nṛpater vadhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.20.2) If any of these burns without fire, or is consumed by lightning — within seven days the death of the king is certain.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,20.3) aniśāyāṃ tamāṃsi syur yadi vā pāṃsavo rajaḥ | dhūmāś cānagnijā yatra tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.20.3) If at night there should be darkness, or dust and dirt, or smoke not produced by fire — one should know great danger there.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,20.4) rātrau divā cānabhre vā yadi jvālā pradṛśyate | garhitaṃ jyotiṣāṃ caiva darśanaṃ vā bhaven niśi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.20.4) At night or by day, in a cloudless [sky], if flames are seen, or if there is a condemned sighting of luminous bodies at night,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,20.5) purāṇāṃ caiva patanaṃ jvalatāṃ ca muhurmuhur | dṛśyate 'nyac ca sahasā tatrāpy agnibhayaṃ vadet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.20.5) And the falling of ancient [walls] and things blazing again and again, or if something else is seen suddenly — there too one should declare danger from fire.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,21.1) prāsādādiṣu caityeṣu yadi dhūmo vināgninā | bhavaty agnir adhūmo vā tathaivātibhayāvahaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.21.1) In palaces, temples, and other sacred places, if there is smoke without fire, or fire without smoke — that likewise is very fear-inducing.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,21.2) jvalanti yadi śastrāṇi vinamanty unnamanti vā | kośebhyo vāpi niryānti saṃgrāmas tumulo bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.21.2) If weapons blaze, bend, or rise up, or come out of their sheaths by themselves — there will be a tumultuous battle.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,21.3) pradīpyante ca sahasā catuṣpatpakṣimānuṣāḥ | vṛkṣā vā parvatā vāpi tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.21.3) And if four-footed animals, birds, or humans suddenly catch fire, or trees or mountains likewise — one should know great danger there.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,21.4) śayanāsanayāneṣu keśaprāvaraṇeṣu ca | dṛśyate 'tīva sahasā tatrāpy agnibhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.21.4) On beds, seats, vehicles, in hair and garments, if [fire] is suddenly seen exceedingly — there too the danger of fire will arise.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,21.5) garjanty āyudhaśastrāṇi vinamanty unnamanti vā | dhanunā saha vā bāṇāḥ saṃgrāmas tumulo bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.21.5) Weapons and arms roar, bend, or rise up, or arrows [fly] together with the bow — there will be a tumultuous battle.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,22.1) samidbhiḥ kṣīraṛkṣāṇāṃ sarṣapais tu ghṛtena ca | hotavyo 'gniḥ svakair mantraiḥ mantraiḥ suvarṇaṃ cātra dakṣiṇā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.22.1) With fuel-sticks of milk-bearing trees and mustard seeds mixed with <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter), the fire should be offered into with proper <s>mantra</s>s; gold is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) here.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,22.2) pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā miśraṃ dvijātīn bhojayet tataḥ | tebhya eva yathāśaktyā dakṣiṇāṃ dāpayen nṛpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.22.2) One should then feed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s with <s>pāyasa</s> (rice pudding) mixed with <s>ghṛta</s>; to them the king should give <s>dakṣiṇā</s> according to his ability.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,22.3) agnir bhūmyām iti tribhir āgneyaṃ tatra kārayet | gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadyān niṣkam aśvaṃ ca sundaram ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.22.3) With the three [verses beginning] '<s>agnir bhūmyām</s>,' one should perform the <s>Āgneya</s> (fire-related) [rite]; one should give to the preceptor as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> a <s>niṣka</s> [of gold] and a fine horse.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.1) gārgyeṇoktaṃ pravakṣyāmi kṛtsnam utpātalakṣaṇam | bhūmikampo bhaved yatra devatāpratimā haset ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.1) I shall declare what was spoken by <s>Gārgya</s>, the complete characteristics of portents: where there is an earthquake, where a divine image laughs,

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.2) devatā bhramate yatra mṛtyus tatra vinirdiśet | garjanaṃ vāpi kūpānām upasargas tu jāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.2) Where a deity moves about — there one should declare death; or when there is rumbling from wells — a calamity arises.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.3) pratisrotavahā nadyo bhavanti ca kathaṃ cana | ṣaḍbhir māsair vijānīyāt paracakrābhimarśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.3) If rivers somehow flow against their current, within six months one should know an invasion by a foreign army.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.4) akālajaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ śītoṣṇatvam akālajam | anyaṃ svāminam icchanti nadyaś cākālasaṃbhavāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.4) Untimely fruit and flowers, unseasonable cold and heat — the rivers, appearing out of season, desire another master.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.5) acalaṃ ca calaṃ yatra calaṃ vā<py> acalaṃ bhavet | rājā vinaśyate tara deśo vāpi vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.5) Where that which is immovable becomes movable, or the movable becomes immovable — the king perishes there, or the land itself is destroyed.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.6) divā tārā yatra paśyec chvetaḥ pakṣy atha vā bhavet | rātrau cendrāyudhaṃ paśyed deśabhaṅgaṃ vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.6) Where one sees stars by day, or a white bird appears, and if one sees a rainbow at night — one should declare the destruction of the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.7) śaśakaṃ jambukaṃ vāpi sūkaraṃ hariṇaṃ tathā | sthānamadhye yadā paśyec chūnyaṃ bhavati niścayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.7) When one sees a hare, jackal, boar, or deer in the middle of a settlement — it will certainly become deserted.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.8) araṇyamṛgajātīyāḥ svayaṃ yānti nṛpālayam | tat sthānaṃ tu bhavec chūnyaṃ bhagnaprākāratoraṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.8) When creatures of forest-animal species come of their own accord to the king's abode, that place becomes deserted, with broken ramparts and gateways.

body.text:
(AVParis_70b,23.9) prākāraveśmabhiṭṭīṣu toraṇe gokule 'pi vā | madhūni yatra dṛśyante tatra vai kasya kiṃ phalam ||........................
(AVParis_70b,23.10) kālanaṣṭapathaṃ sīmāṃ tṛṇavallīsamākulām | sa deśo mānuṣair mukto mṛgāṇāṃ gocaro bhavet ||
body.translated_text:
(AVParis 70b.23.9) Where honeycombs are seen on ramparts, house-walls, gateways, or in cow-pens — what fruit [portends] for whom there?
(AVParis 70b.23.10) A land whose paths are lost to time, whose boundaries are overgrown with grass and creepers — that land, abandoned by humans, becomes the domain of wild animals.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.11) pratyādityaṃ yadā paśyet pure devakule 'pi vā | api śakrasamo rājā abdamadhye vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.11) When one sees a counter-sun in a city or even in a temple — even a king equal to <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) perishes within a year.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.12) vāpīkūpataḍāgeṣu nadyāṃ vā tarate śilā | rājabhaṅgaṃ bhavec caiva cauravyādhibhayaṃ tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.12) In tanks, wells, and reservoirs, or in a river, if a stone floats — there will be the fall of the king, and danger from thieves and disease likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.13) rājagāmiṣu puṣpeṣu vastreṣv ābharaṇeṣu ca | anagninā yadi dahet parighaṃ tatra vai dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.13) If royal flowers, garments, and ornaments burn without fire — a calamity is certainly [portended] there.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.14) tat pātaparityakta kadā cid api budhasyādayaṃ bhavati | dahanaṃ pavanajalamaraṇarogarakṣakṣayāya buddhivāk karoti budhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.14) That which is abandoned by falling — the rising of <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) sometimes occurs; the wise one performs [rites] for the destruction of burning, wind, water, death, disease, <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, and decline through intelligence and speech.

body.text: (AVParis_70b,23.15) tatra kuryān mahāśāntim amṛtāṃ viśvabheṣajīm ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70b.23.15) There one should perform the great pacificatory rite, the immortal, universal remedy.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_70c. bārhaspatyāni)
(AVParis_70c,22.1) om āsīnaṃ tu himavati bṛhaspatiṃ sukhāvaham | gautamaḥ paripṛcchati vinayāt saṃśitavrataḥ ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 70c: The <s>Bārhaspatya</s> [Teachings])
(AVParis 70c.22.1) Oṃ. <s>Gautama</s>, of disciplined vows, with humility questioned <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the bestower of happiness, who was seated on the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas).

body.text: (AVParis_70c,22.2) katham agniḥ parīkṣyo 'yaṃ mantrakarmaṇi śobhanaḥ | svarūpaṃ jñāpaya tvaṃ hi śubhāśubhanibodhane ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.22.2) 'How is this fire to be examined in the auspicious ritual act? Reveal its true nature for understanding the auspicious and inauspicious.'

body.text: (AVParis_70c,23.1) bṛhaspatiḥ pratyāha taṃ gautam || śvetaḥ sugandhiḥ padmābho nirbhūmo dundubhisvanaḥ | asakto 'muṭitaśikhaḥ snigdhotthāyī pradakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.23.1) <s>Bṛhaspati</s> replied to that <s>Gautama</s>: 'White, fragrant, lotus-colored, smokeless, with the sound of a drum, detached, with unbroken flame-tips, smooth-rising, and turning to the right —

body.text: (AVParis_70c,23.2) hūyamānaḥ pradīptaḥ syād dīptatejāḥ sukhapradaḥ | śāntikarmaṇi yatrāgnir niyataṃ siddhilakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.23.2) When offered into, it should be blazing, of brilliant radiance, bestowing happiness; where such fire [appears] in a pacificatory rite, that is certainly the mark of success.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,23.3) svastikā vardhamānā ca śrīvatsā ca pradakṣiṇā | jvālārūpeṇa dṛśyeta sā vai śrīḥ sarvatomukhī ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.23.3) If in the form of a <s>svastika</s>, <s>vardhamāna</s>, or <s>śrīvatsa</s>, turning to the right — if seen in the form of flames, that is <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) facing all directions.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,23.4) yadā hotra prasannena hūyamāno yathā śikhī | ghoṣam utpādayan snigdhaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tad vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.23.4) When the fire, offered into by a serene priest, produces a smooth, rich sound — one should declare that as auspicious.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,23.5) dīptaś ca ratnasaṃkāśaḥ kṣemo dundubhivad ghanaḥ | dhūmaḥ praśasto bhavati svārthasiddhikaro nṛṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.23.5) Blazing and jewel-like in appearance, auspicious, deep-sounding like a drum — the smoke is declared praiseworthy, bringing fulfillment of one's aims for people.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,24.1) snigdhaghoṣo 'lpadhūmaś ca gauravarṇo mahān bhavet | piṇḍitārcir vapuṣmān vā pāvakaḥ siddhikārakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.24.1) With a smooth sound, little smoke, and golden color, the fire would be great; with consolidated flames or radiant form — the fire brings success.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,24.2) yadā tv agniḥ sarvadikthā jvālāgraiḥ spṛśate haviḥ | tadāsya nṛpatiḥ śīghraṃ pararāṣṭraṃ ca mardati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.24.2) When the fire touches the oblation with flame-tips from all directions, then the king quickly crushes the enemy kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,24.3) tiṣṭhantaṃ sthāvaraṃ snigdhaṃ śrūyate yatra gītakam | vācaḥ prasannā homeṣu maṅgalyāś caiva siddhaye ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.24.3) Where singing is heard from the fire standing still, stable, and smooth, and voices during oblations are serene and auspicious — [that leads] to success.
