body.text: (AVParis_70c,24.4) kokilasya māyurasya bhāsasya kuralasya ca | homeṣu śravaṇaṃ caiva prādakṣiṇyaṃ ca śasyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.24.4) During oblations, the hearing of [the sounds of] a cuckoo, peacock, blue jay, or <s>kurala</s> bird, and [their] circumambulation to the right, is praised.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,24.5) śatapattrā rudantī ca cāṣasya nandanaṃ tathā | rambhaṇaṃ caiva dhenūnāṃ havaneṣu praśasyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.24.5) The cry of a <s>śatapatra</s> (woodpecker), the weeping [call of a bird], and the delight of a blue jay likewise, and the lowing of cows during oblations — [all these] are praised.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,25.1) padmavaiḍūryanikāśā vāditrāṇāṃ ca nisvanāḥ | gāvaḥ savarṇavatsā ca dṛṣṭā home praśasyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.25.1) [If flames appear] resembling lotuses and emeralds, with sounds of musical instruments, and cows with calves of the same color are seen during an oblation — [that] is praised.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,25.2) vikāsipadmasadṛśaḥ prasannārcir hutāśanaḥ | susamānābhir arcābhiḥ snigdhābhir anupūrvaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.25.2) The sacrificial fire, resembling a blooming lotus, with serene flames, with smooth flames rising in due order —

body.text: (AVParis_70c,25.3) gambhīraṃ nardate yatra tad agryaṃ siddhilakṣaṇam | akṣatān phalapuṣpāṇi vardhamānam apāṃ ghaṭam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.25.3) Where it roars deeply — that is the supreme mark of success; unbroken grains, fruits, flowers, and a brimming water-pot —

body.text: (AVParis_70c,25.4) dṛṣṭvā vā yadi vā śrutvā karmasiddhiṃ samādiśet | pīṭhachattradhvajanibhā jvālā vāraṇasaṃnibhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.25.4) If seen or heard, one should declare the success of the ritual; flames resembling thrones, parasols, and banners, and [flames] resembling elephants —

body.text: (AVParis_70c,25.5) praśastā ujjvalāś caiva vajrakuṇḍalasaṃnibhāḥ | pradakṣiṇagatiḥ śrīmān agniḥ kartur manoharaḥ | yasya syād vijayaṃ kuryāt kṣipraṃ narapater dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,25.5) Praised, radiant, resembling diamond earrings; the fire moving clockwise, glorious, captivating the mind of the performer — for whomever this occurs, it would bring victory to the king swiftly and certainly.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,26.1) bhūmyāṃ meghābhivṛṣṭānāṃ madhupāyasasarpiṣām | kṛṣṇavartmā sugandhiḥ syāj jayaṃ kṣitipater vadet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,26.1) The fire, [having the fragrance] of honey, milk-rice, and ghee rained upon the earth from the clouds, the dark-pathed [fire] being fragrant — one should declare victory for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,26.2) śaṅkhasvastikarūpāṇi cakrarūpaṃ tathā gadā | śiromālā ca dṛśyeta tad vai vijayalakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,26.2) Forms resembling a conch, <s>svastika</s>, disc, and mace; and if a garland atop [the flame] is seen — that indeed is the mark of victory.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,26.3) ghṛtavarṇanibhas tv agniḥ snigdhaghoṣo mahāsvanaḥ | citrabhānuḥ prasanno vā niyataṃ siddhilakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,26.3) The fire resembling the color of ghee, with a smooth and deep sound, <s>Citrabhānu</s> (the brilliant one) being serene — that is certainly the mark of success.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,26.4) mṛgapakṣiṇa āraṇyāḥ praviśanti yadā puram | grāmyā vā tyaktvā nagaram araṇyaṃ yānti nirbhayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,26.4) When wild animals and birds enter the city, or domestic ones, leaving the town, go to the forest fearlessly,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,26.5) divā rātricarā vāpi rātrau vāpi divācarāḥ | divā vā puramadhyasthā ghoraṃ vāśyanti nirbhayāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,26.5) Those that roam by night [appearing] during the day, or those that roam by day [appearing] at night, or those dwelling in the middle of the city by day cry out terribly without fear,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.1) rājadvāre puradvāre śivā vāpy aśubhaṃ vadet | [tyaktvāraṇyaṃ ca tiṣṭhanti nagaraṃ mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.1) At the king's gate or the city gate, a jackal declares inauspicious [omens]; [wild animals and birds, leaving the forest, remain in the city].

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.2) āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe vāpi śūnyaṃ bhavati tatpuram | [tyaktvā siṃhāḥ sahariṇā mūṣikaṃ sūkaraṃ rurum ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.2) In <s>Āṣāḍha</s> or <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> [months], that city becomes deserted; [when] lions together with deer, mice, boars, and <s>ruru</s> deer,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.3) dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭān nagare śūnyaṃ bhavati tatpuram] | abhivācaṃ vadante ca paśavyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.3) Are seen having entered the city, that city becomes deserted. And animals and birds cry out ominously,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.4) śyenā gṛdhrā bakāḥ kākāḥ sarve maṇḍalacāriṇaḥ | vāśante bhairavaṃ yatra tad apy āśu vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.4) Hawks, vultures, herons, crows — all moving in circles, where they cry out terrifyingly — that [place] too quickly perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.5) niśāyāṃ bahavaḥ śvāno roruvanti yadā tu te | hanyamānā na gacchanti tatra vāso na rocate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.5) When many dogs howl during the night, and when beaten do not leave — dwelling in that [place] is not advisable.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.6) prāsādadhvajaśālāsu prākāradvāratoraṇaiḥ | gardabhaṛśyabhāsānāṃ piṇḍān dṛṣṭvā puraṃ tyajet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.6) Upon seeing droppings of donkeys, bears, and vultures on palaces, banner-halls, ramparts, gates, and arches — one should abandon the city.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.7) pūrvamukhaś ca saṃdhyāyām apraśāntasvaro mṛgaḥ | grāmīṇaghātaṃ śaṃset sa grāmaṇyapraticārataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.7) A deer facing east at twilight, with an unquiet voice, would foretell the slaughter of the village folk, due to the village chief's response.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.8) grāmadvāre ca vāśyeta vanād āgatya jambukaḥ | tīkṣṇasvareṇa mahatā diṣṭo grāmavadho hi saḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.8) And if a jackal, having come from the forest, cries at the village gate with a loud, sharp voice — that is a portent of the destruction of the village.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.9) yad yāti veśma kapotaḥ praviśeta viśeṣataḥ | rājaveśmany ulūko vā tat tyājyam acirād gṛham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.9) When a pigeon enters a house, especially entering [uninvited], or an owl [enters] a royal palace — that house should be abandoned immediately.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,27.10) akasmād veśmaprākāre prāsāde toraṇe dhvaje | patanti bahavo gṛdhrāḥ kākolūkā bakaiḥ saha ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,27.10) Suddenly upon the walls of the house, on the palace, archway, or banner, many vultures fall together with crows, owls, and herons.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,28.1) athāpy eteṣu sthāneṣu madhu saṃjāyate yadā | nalinī caiva valmīkaḥ ṣaṇmāsair mriyate nṛpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,28.1) And moreover, when honey is produced in those places, or a lotus pond or an anthill [appears] — the king dies within six months.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,28.2) mṛgaḥ paśur vā pakṣī vā sūkaro vāpi vāśyate | yadi cotthāya śṛṇute sa manuṣyo vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,28.2) If a deer, domestic animal, bird, or boar cries out, and one rises and listens to it — that person perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,28.3) kākamūṣikamārjārāñ śvapataṃgān bhayāvahān | atīva bahuśo dṛṣṭvā durbhikṣeṇa kṣayaṃ vadet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,28.3) Having seen crows, mice, cats, dogs, and moths in terrifying and excessive numbers — one should declare destruction through famine.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,28.4) śvānaḥ śivābhir vāśyanto bhramantaḥ puramadhyataḥ | asthīni vā mṛtādīnāṃ janamārabhayaṃkarāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,28.4) Dogs howling with jackals, roaming through the middle of the city, [carrying] bones and [parts] of the dead — [these are] terrifying [portents] of plague among the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,28.5) kāṣṭhaṃ vā yadi vā śṛṅgaṃ gṛhītvā śunakaḥ svayam | grāmamadhyena dhāvan syāt tathaivāhur mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,28.5) If a dog, having seized a piece of wood or a horn by itself, runs through the middle of the village — they likewise declare great danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,29.1) purohitas tu kurvīta kāpotīṃ śāntim uttamām | devāḥ kapota iti ca sūktaṃ tatra samādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,29.1) The <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) should perform the supreme <s>kāpotī śānti</s> (pigeon-pacificatory rite); he should prescribe the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) '<s>devāḥ kapota</s>' (O gods, the pigeon) for that [purpose].

body.text: (AVParis_70c,29.2) āvāpe vyatiṣaṅge ca upariṣṭāc ca hūyate | kāmikāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād gurur vā yena tuṣyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,29.2) In the throwing, entanglement, and above — oblations are offered; one should give the desired <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee), or whatever satisfies the preceptor.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,29.3) devatārcāḥ pranṛtyanti dīpyanti prajvalanti vā | udvijanti rudante vā prasvidyante hasanti vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,29.3) When images of deities dance, blaze, or burst into flame, become agitated, weep, or perspire, or laugh,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,29.4) uttiṣṭhanti niṣīdanti pradhāvanti pibanti vā | ejanti vikṣipante vā gātrapraharaṇadhvajān ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,29.4) Rise up, sit down, run, or drink, tremble or hurl away their limbs, weapons, and banners,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,29.5) avāṅmukhā vadante vā sthānāt sthānaṃ vrajanti vā | vapante vāgnim udakaṃ snehaṃ raktaṃ payo vasām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,29.5) Speak face downward, or move from one place to another, or emit fire, water, oil, blood, milk, or fat,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,30.1) jalpanti vā niśvasanti viceṣṭante rudanti vā | citraṃ saṃvīkṣyate yatra gātrair vāpi viceṣṭitaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,30.1) Talk, sigh, move about, or weep; where something extraordinary is observed through their bodily movements,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,30.2) yatraite saṃpradṛśyante vikārāḥ sahasotthitāḥ | liṅgāyatanacaityeṣu tatra vāso na rocate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,30.2) Where these disturbances are seen arising suddenly in <s>liṅga</s>s, temples, and <s>caitya</s>s (sacred monuments) — dwelling there is not advisable.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,30.3) rājño vā vyasanaṃ tatra sa vā deṣaḥ pralīyate | kṣucśastramaraṇair vāpi kiṃ cit tatrābhiśasyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,30.3) Either calamity befalls the king there, or that region is destroyed; or through famine, weapons, and death, something [terrible] is portended there.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,30.4) devatāyatanair vāpi prayātāḥ sumahotsavaiḥ | japahomaś ca kalpantā sīdatāṃ ca same pathi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,30.4) And those who set out with great festivals for the deity temples — <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>homa</s> (oblation) are prescribed, and for the afflicted ones on level ground,

body.text: (AVParis_70c,30.5) same pātam akasmāc ca udāsīnāṃ tathaiva ca | dṛśyate tad vināśāya rājño janapadasya vā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,30.5) A sudden fall on level ground, and of those who are indifferent likewise — this is seen as portending destruction of the king or the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.1) yatra prasthāni bhūtāni liṅgasyāyatanāni ca | tatra śāmyanti ghorāṇi japahomaś ca kalpate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.1) Where spirits are established and where there are shrines of the <s>liṅga</s> — there the terrible [portents] are pacified, and <s>japa</s> and <s>homa</s> are prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.2) prasādaḥ puṇḍarīkaṃ vā viśīryeta pateta vā | vātavajrahato vāpi puramukhye bhayaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.2) If a palace or a lotus [ornament] crumbles or falls, or is struck by wind or lightning — great danger befalls the chief of the city.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.3) pitāmahasya dharmeṣu yan nimittaṃ dvijeṣu tat | aśvakrāntāgniyāneṣu yāni tāni purohite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.3) In the rules of <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Grandfather [<s>Brahmā</s>]), what pertains to portents for <s>dvija</s>s (twice-born) — those concerning horse-movements and fire-conveyances belong to the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest).

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.4) paśūnāṃ rudrajaṃ jñeyaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ lokapālajam | jñeyaṃ māṇḍalikānāṃ ca yat tat skandaviśākhayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.4) For animals, [portents] should be known as originating from <s>Rudra</s>; for kings, from the <s>Lokapāla</s>s (world-guardians); and for regional rulers, those [portents] belong to <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Viśākha</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.5) laukikaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ jñeyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca sarvadā | senāpatau gaṇeśānāṃ gāndharvaṃ saciveṣu ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.5) The public [portents] should be known as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and to the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s (all-gods) always; for the commander-in-chief, [they belong] to the <s>Gaṇeśa</s>s (lords of hosts), and for ministers, to the <s>Gandharva</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.6) devapreṣyaṃ nṛpapreṣye devastrīṇāṃ nṛpastriyām | kāśyapaṃ yantraprāsāde vāstoṣpatyaṃ pure sthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.6) [Portents] of divine messengers [apply] to the king's messengers; of divine women, to the king's women; the <s>Kāśyapa</s> [doctrine applies] to mechanical structures and palaces; the <s>Vāstoṣpatya</s> (pertaining to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>) to the established city.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,31.7) kumārīṣu kumārījaṃ kumāreṣu kumārajam | yakṣarākṣasanāgaiś ca yathoktaiḥ pānakarma ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,31.7) For maidens, [portents] originate from <s>Kumārī</s>; for young men, from <s>Kumāra</s>; and with <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, and <s>Nāga</s>s — the rites of libation as prescribed.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.1) athātaḥ sarvasarvasamucchayaḥ ekam adhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmo yathovāca bhagavān bṛhaspatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.1) Now, the compendium of all [portents]: we shall explain one chapter, as the blessed <s>Bṛhaspati</s> declared.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.2) yad dvādaśabhir adhyāyair vyākhyānaṃ parikīrtitam | tat samāsena bhūyo 'pi śṛṇu paryāyam āgatam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.2) What has been explained and declared through twelve chapters — hear that again in summary, the cycle having come [full circle].

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.3) parājito rāhunipīḍitamaṇḍalo vivarṇaḥ saṃdhyāvikṛto niḥprabho yadā | astamanaṃ yāti divākaraḥ tadāśu vidyāt subrahmajanakṣayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.3) When the day-maker (<s>Sūrya</s>), defeated, with his orb afflicted by <s>Rāhu</s>, discolored, distorted at twilight, devoid of radiance, sets — then one should quickly know the destruction of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> people.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.4) gṛhīto rāhuṇā sārdham uttiṣṭhati divākaraḥ | tadā dharmaphalaṃ kṣīṇaṃ kalim āviśate prajā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.4) When the day-maker rises still seized by <s>Rāhu</s> — then the fruit of <s>dharma</s> diminishes, and the people enter the age of <s>Kali</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.5) amukto rāhuṇā sārdham uttiṣṭhati yadā śaśī | tadā dharmaphalaṃ kṣīṇaṃ kalim āviśate prajā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.5) When the moon rises still unreleased by <s>Rāhu</s> — then the fruit of <s>dharma</s> diminishes, and the people enter the age of <s>Kali</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.6) amukto rāhuṇā sārdham astaṃ gacchati candramāḥ | tadā tato bhayaṃ vidyān mṛtyum āviśate prajā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.6) When the moon sets still unreleased by <s>Rāhu</s> — then one should know danger from that; death overtakes the people.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.7) avādyamānāḥ paṭahāḥ pravadanti muhurmuhuḥ | śastrāṇi vāhanāni ca jvalanty aśubhadāruṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.7) Drums sound repeatedly without being struck; weapons and vehicles blaze with inauspicious terror.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.8) vātaprakopo rajasānuviddhā diśaś ca saṃdhyā ca ghanānuyātā | drakṣanti saṃdhyā yadi pañcavarṇā bhayāni rājñaḥ prativedayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.8) When the wind rages, the directions are pervaded with dust, and twilight is followed by dense clouds — if they see a twilight of five colors, [these portents] announce dangers to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.9) anabhre stanate yatra nabhogulma gulmāyate | kṣipraṃ vidravate rāṣṭraṃ daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.9) Where it thunders in a cloudless [sky], where cloud-masses form clusters — the kingdom is quickly scattered for fifteen years.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.10) anabhre patate vidyud darśayed vāghanotthitām | anabhre vāpi nirghātaḥ patito rājamṛtyave ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.10) Lightning falls from a cloudless sky, or displays itself risen from the clouds; a thunderbolt too falling from a cloudless sky [portends] the death of the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.11) yady ahni vāteṣu mahendrarekhā mahendracāpaḥ samudeti rātrau | tadā bhayaṃ pārthivamaṇḍalānāṃ vadanti śāstrārthavido dvijendrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.11) If <s>Mahendra</s>'s streak [appears] among the winds by day, and <s>Mahendra</s>'s bow (rainbow) rises at night — then the learned <s>dvija</s>s (twice-born) versed in the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>s declare danger to the circles of kings.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.12) nikalkayukto niśi sendracāpo vivardhamānaḥ samudeti rātrau | viśīryamāṇā patate tatholkā tadā bhayaṃ pārthivamaṇḍalānām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.12) When [the rainbow], marked with dark spots, rises at night with <s>Indra</s>'s bow, growing [in intensity], and a meteor falls disintegrating — then there is danger to the circles of kings.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.13) muñcanti nāgā rudhiraṃ karaiś ca lomāni dīpyanti turaṃgamāṇām | dīpyanti khaḍgāni ca khecarāṇi cihnāni rājñaḥ prativedayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.13) Elephants shed blood from their trunks, the hairs of horses blaze, and swords and aerial [weapons] blaze — [these] signs announce [danger] to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.14) girivarapatanaṃ svabhūmicālaḥ pratibhayatā ca tathaiva mānuṣāṇām | vikṛtajananam uktim ugravācā mahati bhaye mṛgapakṣiṇo vadanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.14) The falling of great mountains, earthquakes, and likewise the terror of human beings; monstrous births and fierce speech — animals and birds [also] speak of great danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.15) chattre gṛhe vāsarathe dhvaje ca dhūmaḥ samuttiṣṭhati yasya cāgniḥ | sa pārthivaḥ kṣīnamanuṣyakośaḥ prāpnoti nāśaṃ ca janakṣayaṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.15) That king from whose parasol, house, chariot, or banner smoke rises, and [whose] fire [dies] — he, with diminished men and treasury, meets destruction and loss of people.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.16) mahormibhiḥ svair vitatair jaloghair nadyaḥ svakūlāc ca haranti vṛkṣān | yadi pratisrotavahās tadā syur vināśanā deśaparā nṛpasya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.16) Rivers carry away trees from their own banks with great waves and spreading floods; if they flow against the current — then there is destruction of the king's country.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.17) yadā tu ghāte ca divākaraprabhāḥ svareṇubhir vāpi vidhūmasaṃbhramāḥ | na tasya vāsaṃ viṣaye vadanti āhur gaṇānāṃ ca vivṛddhināśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.17) When the splendor of the sun is [obscured] in the fog, [or there are] confusions of dust and smoke — they declare no dwelling in his domain; they say there is growing destruction of the multitudes.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.18) hutāśanasy jvalanaṃ niredhaṃ tathā na caiva jvalate ca sedhmā | .......... bhayāni rājñaḥ prativedayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.18) When the fire blazes without fuel, and the fuel does not burn — .......... [these portents] announce dangers to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.19) śiloccayānāṃ ca śilānipātaḥ puradrumāṇāṃ ca viṣāṇapātaḥ | caityadrumāṇāṃ ca tathaiva pāto bhayāni rājñaḥ prativedayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.19) The falling of rocks from mountains, the falling of branches from city trees, and likewise the falling of sacred trees — [these] announce dangers to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.20) acālyavatsāḥ puragopureṣu bhramanti gāvaḥ kṛtaraudraśabdāḥ | mṛṇālabāddhāś ca gajā bhavanti bhayāni rājñaḥ prativedayanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.20) Cows with calves that cannot be restrained roam on city gates making terrible sounds; and elephants become [tameable] by lotus-fiber bonds — [these portents] announce dangers to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.21) prāsādagopuramukhāś ca patanti yatra indradhvajotthitavanaspativājināṃ ca | teṣāṃ vadanti pacanāni sukhāvahāni saumyādi saṃprabhayatā ca tathādiśanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.21) Where palace and gate facades fall, and [where] festival poles, trees, and horses [fall] — they declare the roasting [destruction] of those, bringing ease [to enemies]; and they indicate danger beginning with auspicious [omens turned ominous].

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.22) ūrdhvaṃ vilokya nagaraṃ pratisaṃniviṣṭāḥ sūryodaye khalu rudanti śivātiraudram | gṛdhrāś ca maṇḍalasamutpatitā bhramanti prāptaṃ bhayaṃ janapadasya samādiśanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.22) Having looked upward at the city, jackals settled [there] at sunrise howl most terrifyingly; and vultures fly about rising in circles — they indicate that danger has arrived for the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.23) daṇḍāśaniḥ patati yatra savisphuliṅgā bhūḥ kampate dinakarasya bhavet praśāntiḥ | candhre ca yatra vikṛtaṃ ca bhaved aśāntaṃ māsāt samudbhavati tatra bhayo 'tighoraḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.23) Where the thunderbolt falls with sparks, the earth quakes, and the sun loses its light; and where there is disturbance and unrest regarding the moon — within a month, most terrible danger arises there.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.24) caityadrumāṇāṃ rudhiraprakopāḥ kabandhayānāni bhavanti yatra | saṃdhyāsu rakṣo 'dhipater janānāṃ prabhūti rājño 'tibhaye bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.24) Where there are eruptions of blood from sacred trees, and headless torsos travel about; at twilights, [portents] of the lord of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s [appear] to the people — [these] occur when extreme danger to the king is imminent.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.25) vṛṣṭir yadā varṣati reṇuvarṣais tatopariṣṭād dharitālavarṣam | tataḥ paraṃ varṣati śailavarṣaṃ tadā balaṃ naśyati pārthivasya ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis_70c,32.25) When it rains with showers of dust, then above with showers of yellow orpiment, then further with showers of stones — then the army of the king perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.26) āraṇyo grāmavāsī mṛgaśakunigaṇo grāmavāsī vanānte gṛdhrāṇāṃ saṃnipāto narapatibhavane gopure vā pure vā | yatra syān mānuṣīṇāṃ kharakarabhamukhānekarūpā prasūtis tatsthāne jīvitārthī sthitim ati kurute naiva pātaiḥ praduṣṭe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.26) Wild animals dwelling in the village, flocks of beasts and birds, village-dwellers at the forest's edge, an assemblage of vultures at the king's palace, at the gate, or in the city — where women give birth to offspring of various forms with the faces of donkeys, camels, and the like, in that place one who desires life should not remain at all, as it is corrupted by [such] portents.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.27) prayānti devāḥ sahasāyatasthā vanāni vā yatra patanti bhūmau | sthānāni mucyanti nadanti ke cit tathā paraṃ śoṇitajagdhagātrāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.27) The gods who have stood firm suddenly depart, or where trees fall to the ground, sacred sites are abandoned, some cry out, and moreover their bodies are consumed and smeared with blood.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.28) utpātasaṃghair atyugraiḥ kṣātrahāniḥ prajāyate | lokānāṃ pīḍanaṃ caiva rogacaurāgnisaṃbhavam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.28) By exceedingly fierce groups of portents, destruction of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> order arises; and affliction of the people occurs, born of disease, thieves, and fire.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.29) agnīnāṃ saṃpradoṣāḥ pratibhayajananā dīpyamānā diśaś ca madhyāhne cāntarikṣe grahagaṇakhacitā gṛdhrasaṃghaiḥ prakīrṇāḥ | nirghātaiḥ pāṃsuvarṣaiḥ satatamalinatā bhūpracālaś ca ghoro devānāṃ cāśrupāto nṛpatibhayakarā rāṣṭranāśāya caite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.29) The corruption of [sacred] fires, the directions blazing with fear-generating [flames], and at midday in the atmosphere [the sky] studded with hosts of planets and scattered with flocks of vultures; by thunderbolts, showers of dust, constant impurity, and terrible earthquakes, and the weeping of the gods — these cause fear to kings and [lead to] the destruction of the kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.30) śivādaye yatra divākarasya jvālāvimucy ūrdhvamukhī praroditi | samāvṛtā vāyasagṛdhrasaṃghais tadā bhayaṃ vedavido vadanti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.30) Where a she-jackal, releasing flames, cries upward facing toward the sun, surrounded by flocks of crows and vultures — then those who know the <s>Veda</s>s declare danger.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.31) rudanti nāgās tu vimuktahastā vimuktadantās turagā rudanti | rudanti nāryaś ca samāgame ca tadā bhayaṃ syāc chrutiliṅgamūlam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.31) Elephants cry with trunks outstretched, horses cry with teeth bared; and women cry at gatherings — then there shall be danger rooted in scriptural signs.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.32) yadā tu vastrāṇi varadrumāṇāṃ prakāśavṛṣṭyā nipatanti mūrdhni | samīkṣya pātaṃ ca yathārthadṛṣṭaṃ bhayāya rāṣṭrasya nṛpasya vidyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.32) When garments of excellent trees fall upon one's head through a luminous shower, having observed the fall as a true sign, one should know [it portends] danger to the kingdom and the king.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.33) śakaṭādyāni yānāni yadāyuktāni saṃcalet | tadā janapade vidyān mahābhayam upasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.33) When vehicles such as carts move while unyoked, then one should know that great danger has arrived in the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.34) yathaiva nityaṃ dṛśyante tathaiva samudāharet | na tasyātikramaḥ kaś cid akṛte śāntikarmaṇi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.34) Just as [portents] are regularly seen, so should one declare [their results]; there is no overcoming of those, if the pacificatory rite is not performed.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.35) kṣayo janapadastrīṇāṃ vidyād gajapurohite | japaṃ homaṃ ca śāntiṃ ca utpāteṣu prayojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.35) One should know destruction of the women of the realm when [portents appear] regarding the elephant and the royal priest; one should employ chanting, oblation, and pacificatory rites for portents.

body.text: (AVParis_70c,32.36) viśeṣeṇāmṛtāṃ kuryād bṛhaspativaco yathā | homaṃ lakṣamitaṃ kuryāj japed vā vedasaṃhitām | dānāni tu hiraṇyāni śāntikarmaṇi yojayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 70c.32.36) Especially one should perform the immortality [rite] according to the word of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; one should perform a hundred thousand oblations, or chant the <s>Veda</s> collection; and one should employ gifts of gold in pacificatory rites.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_71. auśanasādbhutāni)
(AVParis_71,1.1) papracchośanasaṃ kāvyaṃ nāradaḥ paryavasthitaḥ | divyāṃś caivāntarikṣāṃś ca utpātān pārthivāṃs tathā ||
body.translated_text:
(Pariśiṣṭa 71: The <s>Auśanasa</s> Portents)
(AVParis 71.1.1) <s>Nārada</s>, having stationed himself, questioned <s>Uśanas Kāvya</s> about celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents.

body.text: (AVParis_71,1.2) ṛtūnāṃ ca viparyāse tathaiva mṛgapakṣiṇām | amānuṣāṇāṃ vyāhāre sthāvarāṇāṃ vyatikrame ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.1.2) Regarding the reversal of seasons, and likewise of animals and birds; regarding the utterances of non-human beings, and the transgression of stationary things;

body.text: (AVParis_71,1.3) yonivyatikare caiva māṃsaśonitavarṣaṇe | anagnijvalane caiva tathā yānānusarpaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.1.3) And regarding cross-breeding of species, and rain of flesh and blood; and regarding spontaneous combustion, and likewise the self-movement of vehicles;

body.text: (AVParis_71,1.4) śastraprajvalane caiva caityaśuṣkavirohaṇe | liṅgāyatanacitrāṇāṃ rodane garjane tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.1.4) And regarding the blazing of weapons, and the sprouting of dried sacred trees; and regarding the weeping and rumbling of images and shrines;

body.text: (AVParis_71,1.5) udapānataḍāgābān jvalane garjane 'pi vā | matsyasarpadvijātīnāṃ rasānāṃ ca pravarṣaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.1.5) Regarding the blazing or rumbling of wells, ponds, and waters; and the raining down of fish, serpents, birds, and various fluids;

body.text: (AVParis_71,2.1) āyudhānāṃ prajvalane garjane ca viśeṣataḥ | puṣpe phale ca vṛkṣāṇām akāle ca virohaṇe ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.2.1) Regarding the blazing of weapons and especially their rumbling; and regarding the flowering and fruiting of trees out of season, and their sprouting [at wrong times];

body.text: (AVParis_71,2.2) prāsādādrivimānānāṃ prākārāṇāṃ ca kampane | gītavāditraśabdāś ca yatra syur animittataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.2.2) Regarding the trembling of palaces, mountains, aerial chariots, and ramparts; and where sounds of song and musical instruments arise without cause;

body.text: (AVParis_71,2.3) ye cānye ke cid utpātā jāyante vikṛtātmakāḥ | teṣāṃ phalaṃ ca kālaṃ ca tattvenācakṣva bhārgava ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.2.3) And whatever other portents of distorted nature arise — their results and timing, declare them truly, O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_71,2.4) sa tasmai pṛcchate samyaṅ nāradāyāśanāḥ kaviḥ | trividhān apy athotpātān vyākhyātum upacakrame ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.2.4) To him who thus asked, to <s>Nārada</s>, the poet son of <s>Uśanas</s> then undertook to explain the three types of portents.

body.text: (AVParis_71,2.5) yadā śīte bhavaty uṣṇam uṣṇe śītam atīva ca | navamāsāt paraṃ vidyāt teṣu deśeṣu vai bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.2.5) When in winter there is heat, and in summer excessive cold, after nine months one should know danger in those regions.

body.text: (AVParis_71,3.1) yatrānṛtau prabaddhena tryahād ūrdhvaṃ pravarṣati | tasmin deśe pradhānasya puruṣasya vadho bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.3.1) Where it rains continuously for more than three days out of season, in that region the killing of a prominent person shall occur.

body.text: (AVParis_71,3.2) kokilāś ca mayūrāś ca akāle madabhāginaḥ | saṃsargaṃ vāpi gaccheyur vidyāj jānapadaṃ bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.3.2) If cuckoos and peacocks become intoxicated out of season, or engage in mating, one should know [there will be] danger to the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_71,3.3) ruravaś caiva raudrāś ca pṛṣatā hariṇās tathā | yeṣu deśeṣu dṛśyante tān araṇyāya nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.3.3) <s>Ruru</s> deer, fearsome ones, spotted deer, and <s>hariṇa</s> deer — in whichever regions they are seen, one should designate those [regions] for wilderness.

body.text: (AVParis_71,3.4) pradhānāś caiva vadhyante pakṣe saptadaśe tathā | tasmiñ janapade caiva mahad utpadyate bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.3.4) And prominent persons are slain in the seventeenth fortnight likewise; in that realm too, great danger arises.

body.text: (AVParis_71,3.5) gāvo 'śvāḥ kuñjarāḥ śvānaḥ kharoṣṭrā vānaroragāḥ | nakulāḥ pakṣiṇo vyālāḥ sūkarā mahiṣā mṛgāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.3.5) Cows, horses, elephants, dogs, donkeys, camels, monkeys, serpents, mongooses, birds, wild beasts, boars, buffaloes, and deer —

body.text: (AVParis_71,4.1) sattvāny etāni jalpanti yeṣu deśeṣu mānuṣam | teṣu deśeṣu rājā tu ṣaṣṭhe māsi vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.4.1) These creatures speak in human [language] in whichever regions — in those regions the king perishes in the sixth month.

body.text: (AVParis_71,4.2) utpātā vikṛtātmāno dṛśyante yatra tatra vai | deśe bhavati śīghraṃ hi ṣaṇmāsād bhayam uttamam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.4.2) Portents of distorted nature are seen wherever they may be; in that region swiftly, within six months, supreme danger occurs.

body.text: (AVParis_71,4.3) āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ yadā yatra prasarpati | vipakṣāt tatra tatsvāmī bhayaṃ prāpnoti dāruṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.4.3) When a seat, bed, or vehicle creeps forward on its own, from enemies the owner thereof incurs terrible danger.

body.text: (AVParis_71,4.4) dhānyakoṣṭhāyudhāgārāḥ pāṣāṇāḥ kūpaparvatāḥ | etāni yatra sarpanti vikṛtāni vadanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.4.4) Granaries, weapon-stores, stones, wells, and mountains — wherever these creep and speak in distorted forms,

body.text: (AVParis_71,4.5) bahu vā jāyate tīvraṃ tasmin deśe bhayaṃ mahat | trīn māsān parakāle tu śeṣe saumyātikaṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.4.5) Much or intensely arises in that region great danger; within three months in the adversary's time, but the remainder has an auspicious result.

body.text: (AVParis_71,5.1) deśe vā yadi vā grāme yonivyatikaro bhavet | tatra saṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃ mahad utpadyate bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.5.1) In a region or village where cross-breeding of species occurs, there, after a year, great danger arises.

body.text: (AVParis_71,5.2) gaur aśvaṃ vaḍavā vāpi yasmin deśe prasūyate | abhyantareṇa tadvarṣād rājño maraṇam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.5.2) A cow gives birth to a horse, or a mare [gives birth to one], in whichever region — within that year one should foretell the death of the king.

body.text: (AVParis_71,5.3) mānuṣī janayed yatra tṛṇādān vividhān paśūn | ṣaṇmāsotthaṃ bhayaṃ tīvraṃ tatra tūtpadyate mahat ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.5.3) Where a human woman gives birth to various animals such as grass-eaters, intense danger arises there, great and arising after six months.

body.text: (AVParis_71,5.4) paracakrāgamaṃ caiva nirdiśed iha śāstravit | saṃgrāmāś cātra vipulā jāyante vikṛtātmakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.5.4) And the knower of the <s>śāstra</s>s should foretell the invasion of an enemy army; and great battles of distorted nature arise therein.

body.text: (AVParis_71,5.5) sarpaṃ vā pakṣiṇaṃ vāpi janayed yatra mānuṣī | pracalas tasya deśasya ṣaṇmāsāt tu paraṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.5.5) Where a human woman gives birth to a serpent or a bird, the destruction of that region shall occur after six months.

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.1) uṣṭraṃ vā yā prasūyeta vānaraṃ vāpi mānuṣī | anyad vā jaṅgamaṃ kiṃ cit sthāvaraṃ vāpi kiṃ cana ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.1) Or a human woman who gives birth to a camel, or a monkey, or any other moving or stationary creature whatsoever —

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.2) rogeṇa śastrapātena durbhikṣeṇa ca pīḍitaḥ | sa deśo vyathate śīghraṃ rājā tatra vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.2) That region, afflicted by disease, fall of weapons, and famine, suffers quickly; the king there perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.3) amānuṣī mānuṣaṃ vā mānuṣī vāpy amānuṣam | prasūyate tu jānīyāt paracakrāgamaṃ dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.3) A non-human [creature] gives birth to a human, or a human woman to a non-human — one should know [this portends] the certain invasion of an enemy army.

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.4) caturakṣaṃ dviśīrṣaṃ vā gātrair nyūnādhikais tathā | vyañjanaiś copasaṃpannaṃ mānuṣī yā prasūyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.4) Four-eyed, two-headed, or with limbs deficient or excessive, endowed with [unusual] marks — [that which] a human woman gives birth to —

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.5) dvisaṃvatsaraparyantād rājā tatra vinaśyati | uṣṭro vṛṣo vāpy aśvo vā gajo vā yatra jāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.5) Within two years the king there perishes. Or where a camel, bull, horse, or elephant is born [from a human woman],

body.text: (AVParis_71,6.6) pakṣān māsāc ca bhavati rājñas tatra bhayaṃ mahat | paracakrasamutthaṃ vā sa deśo bhayam ṛcchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.6.6) Within a fortnight or a month, great danger befalls the king; arising from an enemy army, that region encounters danger.

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.1) yonivyatikaraṃ yatra kuryur evaṃvidhaṃ striyaḥ | gaur vā sūyet tathānyāni tatra rājyaṃ vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.1) Where women produce such cross-breeding of species, or a cow gives birth [to anomalous offspring] and likewise other [animals] — there the kingdom perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.2) vasanti yeṣu deśeṣu teṣu vidyān mahad bhayam | tasmād etāni sattvāni rājā kṣipraṃ pravāsayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.2) In whichever regions they dwell, in those one should know great danger; therefore the king should quickly banish these creatures.

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.3) aśvā kiśoraṃ janayec chṛṅgiṇaṃ yatra tatra tu | ādiśen maraṇaṃ rājño varṣābhyantara eva hi ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.3) Where a mare gives birth to a horned foal, there one should foretell the death of the king within the year itself.

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.4) māghe budhe ca mahiṣī śrāvaṇe vaḍavā divā | siṃhe gāvaḥ prasūyante svāmino mṛtyudāyakāḥ | iti śāstrasamuccayāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.4) When a queen buffalo [gives birth] in <s>Māgha</s> and [on the day of] Mercury, a mare by day in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and cows give birth in [the month of] Leo — [these are] death-bringing to the master. Thus from the collection of <s>śāstra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.5) nārī kharavṛṣoṣṭrāśvāñ śunaḥ sūkaragardabhān | rākṣasān vā piśācān vā yadāpy evaṃ prasūyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.5) When a woman gives birth to donkeys, bulls, camels, horses, dogs, boars, asses, <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, or <s>Piśāca</s>s —

body.text: (AVParis_71,7.6) vyāpadyante 'tra dhānyāni sasyāni ca dhanāni ca | caturvidhaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ kṣipraṃ tatra pravartate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.7.6) Grains, crops, and wealth perish there; fourfold terrible danger quickly arises in that place.

body.text: (AVParis_71,8.1) vadhyante hi pradhānās tu sārdhamāsāṣṭame tathā | vyādhīṃś ca teṣu deśeṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.8.1) And prominent persons are slain, likewise in the eighth [month] and a half; and in those regions one should foretell diseases for three years.

body.text: (AVParis_71,8.2) anagnir jvalate yatra deśe tūrṇam anindhanaḥ | yo rājā tasya deśasya sadeśaḥ sa vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.8.2) Where a fireless [conflagration] blazes quickly without fuel in a region, whatever king [rules] that region — he perishes along with his territory.

body.text: (AVParis_71,8.3) māṃsavarṣeṇa maghavā yatra deśe pravarṣati | asthīni rudhiraṃ majjāṃ vasāṃ caiteṣu vai dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.8.3) Where <s>Indra</s> rains down a rain of flesh in a region — bones, blood, marrow, and fat — in those [places] certainly,

body.text: (AVParis_71,8.4) paracakrāgamaḥ śīghraṃ vijñeyas tu mahad bhayam | āhavāś cātra jāyante vipulā vikṛtātmakāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.8.4) The invasion of an enemy army should quickly be recognized as great danger; and great battles of distorted nature arise therein.

body.text: (AVParis_71,8.5) aṅgāravālukādhānyaṃ yatra devaḥ pravarṣati | kṣipraṃ tatra bhayaṃ ghoraṃ pravarteta caturvidham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.8.5) Where the rain-god showers embers, sand, and grain, there swiftly terrible fourfold danger arises.

body.text: (AVParis_71,9.1) sarpān matsyān pakṣiṇo vā yatra devaḥ pravarṣati | tatra sasyopaghātaḥ syād bhayaṃ cātipravartate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.9.1) Where the rain-god showers serpents, fish, or birds, there destruction of crops shall occur, and danger arises exceedingly.

body.text: (AVParis_71,9.2) surāsavaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ sarpis tailaṃ payo dadhi | yatra varṣati parjanyaḥ kṣudrogas tatra jāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.9.2) Liquor, spirits, honey, ghee, oil, milk, and curds — where the cloud rains [these], minor disease arises there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,9.3) ulkātārāś ca dhiṣṇyeṣu yadāṅgārāṃś ca varṣati | tadā vyādhibhayaṃ ghoraṃ teṣu deśeṣu nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.9.3) When meteors, stars, and firebrands rain down upon [their] stations, then one should foretell terrible danger from disease in those regions.

body.text: (AVParis_71,9.4) pumān aśvo gajo vāpi yadā yatra pradīpyate | daśamāsāt paraṃ tatra jānīyād rāṣṭrasaṃplavam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.9.4) When a man, a horse, or an elephant spontaneously catches fire, after ten months one should recognize the ruin of the kingdom.

body.text: (AVParis_71,9.5) nārācāḥ śaktayaḥ khaḍgāḥ pradīpyante yadā muhuḥ | tadā śastrabhayaṃ ghoraṃ teṣu deśeṣu nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.9.5) When iron arrows, spears, and swords blaze repeatedly, then one should foretell terrible danger from weapons in those regions.

body.text: (AVParis_71,10.1) caityavṛkṣāḥ prabhajyante visvaraṃ vinadanti ca | prahasanti prasarpanti gāyanti ca rudanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.10.1) Sacred trees break apart, cry out discordantly, laugh, creep, sing, and weep.

body.text: (AVParis_71,10.2) āgamaḥ paracakrasya teṣu cāpadyate tvaram | sacakrā vāpi naśyanti pradhānaś cātra vadhyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.10.2) The invasion of an enemy army befalls those [regions] swiftly; or those with their armies perish, and prominent persons are slain there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,10.3) yatra sravec caityavṛkṣaḥ sahasā vividhān rasān | pṛthakpṛthak samastān vā tat pravakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.10.3) Where a sacred tree suddenly exudes various fluids, separately or all together — I shall declare the characteristics of that.

body.text: (AVParis_71,10.4) ghṛte madhuni dugdhe ca ghṛte dugdhe tathāmbhasi | kṣaudre madhuni taile vā vyādhayaḥ syuḥ sudāruṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.10.4) [If it exudes] ghee, honey, milk, or ghee, milk, and water, or honey, mead, or oil — there shall be very terrible diseases.

body.text: (AVParis_71,10.5) surāsave mithobhedaḥ śoṇite śastrapātanam | taile pradhānā vadhyante bhakṣe kṣudbhayam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.10.5) [If it exudes] liquor or spirits, mutual dissension; blood, the fall of weapons; oil, prominent persons are slain; food, one should foretell danger from famine.

body.text: (AVParis_71,11.1) anṛtau cet phalaṃ yatra puṣpaṃ vā sūyate drumaḥ | vidyād dvādaśame māsi rājñas tatra viparyayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.11.1) Where a tree bears fruit or flowers out of season, one should know the reversal of fortune for the king in the twelfth month.

body.text: (AVParis_71,11.2) puṣpe puṣpaṃ bhaved yatra phale vā syāt tathā phalam | parṇe parṇaṃ vijānīyāt tatra jānapadaṃ bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.11.2) Where a flower [grows] upon a flower, or likewise a fruit upon a fruit, or a leaf upon a leaf — one should recognize danger to the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_71,11.3) śuklena vāsasā yatra caityavṛkṣaḥ samāvṛtaḥ | brāhmaṇānāṃ bhayaṃ ghoram āśu tīvraṃ vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.11.3) Where a sacred tree is covered with a white garment, one should foretell terrible and swift danger to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_71,11.4) raktavastrāvṛtaiś cānyaiḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahad bhayam | pītavastrais tu vaiśyānāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ kṛṣṇavāsasaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.11.4) And when covered by others with red garments — great fear for <s>Kṣatriya</s>s; with yellow garments, [fear] for <s>Vaiśya</s>s; for <s>Śūdra</s>s, with black garments.

body.text: (AVParis_71,11.5) nīlaiḥ sasyopaghātaḥ syāc citrais tu mṛgapakṣiṇām | vivarṇair vyādhayas tīvrāḥ paraṃ syur daśamāsataḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.11.5) With blue [garments], destruction of crops; with variegated [garments], [fear] for animals and birds; with discolored [garments], severe diseases — the effect occurring after ten months.

body.text: (AVParis_71,12.1) daivatāni prasarpanti yatra rāṣṭre hasanti vā | udīkṣante 'tha rodhāṃsi tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.12.1) Where the deities creep about in a kingdom, or laugh, or gaze at embankments — there one should know great fear.

body.text: (AVParis_71,12.2) vihasanti nimīlanti gāyanti vikṛtāni ca | māṃsaśonitagandhāni yatra tatra mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.12.2) [If they] laugh, close their eyes, sing, and [display] distorted [forms]; where [there are] smells of flesh and blood — there great fear.

body.text: (AVParis_71,12.3) yatra citram udīkṣeta gāyate ceṣṭate muhuḥ | eteṣv aṣṭasu māseṣu rājño maraṇam ādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.12.3) Where a painting gazes [outward], sings, or moves repeatedly — within these eight months one should predict the death of the king.

body.text: (AVParis_71,12.4) citrāṇi yatra liṅgāni tathaivāyatanāni ca | vikāraṃ kuryur atyarthaṃ tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.12.4) Where images, <s>liṅga</s>s (sacred symbols), and likewise temples undergo excessive transformation — there one should know great fear.

body.text: (AVParis_71,12.5) udapānaṃ taḍāgaṃ vā saraḥ parvata eva vā | samuddeśeṣu dīpyante vidyād bhayam upasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.12.5) A well, a reservoir, a lake, or a mountain itself — [when these] blaze up at [various] locations — one should know that danger is imminent.

body.text: (AVParis_71,13.1) [prahaseyuḥ staneyur vā] śvā vā mārjāravad vadet | tasya deśasya rājā tu pīḍām āpnoti dāruṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.13.1) [If they laugh or rumble,] or if a dog speaks like a cat — the king of that region incurs terrible affliction.

body.text: (AVParis_71,13.2) śaṅkhavaiṇavatūryāṇāṃ dundubhīnāṃ ca nisvanaḥ | deśe yatra bhṛśaṃ tatra rājadaṇḍo nipātyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.13.2) The sound of conches, bamboo flutes, and <s>dundubhi</s> (war drums) — wherever [heard] intensely in a region, the king's punishment descends there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,13.3) yasya rājño janapade nityodvignāḥ prajāḥ kṣayam | gacchanti na citrāt tatra vināśam api nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.13.3) In whose kingdom the people, constantly distressed, go to ruin — there one should predict destruction before long.

body.text: (AVParis_71,13.4) yasya rājño janapade nityam eva gavāṃ kṣayaḥ | bhayaṃ tatra vijānīyād acirāt samupasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.13.4) In whose kingdom there is constant decline of cattle — one should know that danger is imminent before long.

body.text: (AVParis_71,13.5) yasya rājño janapade nadī vahati kardamam | kāṣṭhaṃ tṛṇaṃ copalaṃ vā mṛtamatsyān grahāṃs tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.13.5) In whose kingdom a river carries mud, wood, grass, stones, dead fish, and crocodiles likewise,

body.text: (AVParis_71,14.1) madyaṃ kṣaudraṃ ca māṃsaṃ ca sarpis tailaṃ payo dadhi | anyarājāgamabhayaṃ tatra deśe samādiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.14.1) And liquor, honey, flesh, ghee, oil, milk, and curds — one should predict fear of invasion by another king in that region.

body.text: (AVParis_71,14.2) yasya rājño janapade pratisroto nadī vahet | māsāṣṭakāj jānapadaṃ bhayaṃ syāc chastrapāṇinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.14.2) In whose kingdom a river flows against its current — from the eighth month, there shall be danger to the people from one bearing weapons.

body.text: (AVParis_71,14.3) kūpo vā garjate yatra yadā vāpy avadīryate | lohitaṃ vātha pūyaṃ vā bhayaṃ tatra vinirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.14.3) Where a well rumbles, or where [a pond] collapses; or [exudes] blood or pus — one should predict danger there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,14.4) āyudhāni pradhāvanti tīvraṃ pratyāharanti ca | tūṇīrāt sahasā bāṇā udgiranti nadanti ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.14.4) Weapons rush forward violently and withdraw sharply; arrows suddenly leap out of quivers and roar;

body.text: (AVParis_71,14.5) svabhāvataś ca pūryante dhanūmṣi prajvalanti ca | saṃgrāmo dāruṇas tatra deśe bhavati biścitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.14.5) And bows string themselves of their own nature and blaze — a terrible battle in that region is certain.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.1) akāle puṣpavantaś ca phalavantaś ca pādapāḥ | dṛśyante yasya rāṣṭreṣu tasya nāśo vibhāvyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.1) Trees bearing flowers and fruits out of season are seen in whose kingdom — its destruction is foreseen.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.2) vṛkṣā vallyaś ca taruṇā yatra syuḥ phalapuṣpadāḥ | akāle cāpi dṛśyeyus tatra vidyān mahad bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.2) Where trees, creepers, and young [plants] bear fruits and flowers out of season and are also seen [thus] — there one should know great fear.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.3) prāsādāni vimānāni prajvalanti tu yatra vai | dṛḍhāni ca viśīryante yasya sa mriyate 'cirāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.3) Where palaces and aerial mansions blaze up; and sturdy [structures] crumble — he [the king] dies before long.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.4) vadanty araṇye tūryāṇi śrūyante vyomni nityaśaḥ | nivaseta tadā rājā samāgamya diśo daśa ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.4) Instruments speak in the forest; [sounds] are heard in the sky constantly — then the king should dwell having assembled [forces from] the ten directions.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.5) yasya veśmani śrūyante gītavāditranisvanāḥ | akasmān mriyate samyag dhanaṃ cāsya vilupyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.5) In whose dwelling the sounds of songs and musical instruments are heard — he dies suddenly and completely, and his wealth is plundered.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.6) śaṅkhavaiṇavavīṇāś ca bherīmurajagomukhāḥ | vādyamānāḥ pradṛśyante deśe yatrāpy aghaṭṭitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.6) Conches, bamboo flutes, <s>vīṇā</s>s, <s>bherī</s>s (kettledrums), <s>muraja</s>s (barrel drums), and <s>gomukha</s>s (horn instruments) — where these are seen sounding though untouched,

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.7) saṃbhṛtyaiva tato bhāram anyaṃ janapadaṃ vrajet | mṛgavāṃs tu sa deśo hi vāyuś cātropajāyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.7) Having gathered one's belongings, one should proceed to another territory; that region indeed becomes [infested] with wild animals, and wind arises there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.8) anāhatā dundubhayo vāditrāṇi vadanti ca | chidrāṇi ca gṛhe yasya sa śīghraṃ bhayam ṛcchati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.8) When <s>dundubhi</s>s (war drums) unstruck and instruments sound, and there are holes in whose house — he quickly encounters danger.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.9) devarājadhvajānāṃ ca patanaṃ bhaṅga eva vā | kravyādānāṃ praveśaṃ ca rājñaḥ pīḍākaraṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.9) The falling or breaking of banners of gods and kings; and the entry of carrion-eaters — [this] would cause affliction to the king.

body.text: (AVParis_71,15.10) vājivāraṇamukhyānām akasmān maraṇaṃ bhavet | itarakṣamāpates tatra vijñeyā satvarāgatiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.15.10) When prominent horses and elephants die suddenly — one should recognize the swift approach of danger from the adversary there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,16.1) aśvatthe puṣpite kṣatraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpy udumbare | plakṣe vaiśyāś tu pīḍyante nyagrodhe dasyavas tathā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.16.1) When the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) flowers, [danger to] the <s>Kṣatriya</s> [class]; for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, the <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig); when the <s>plakṣa</s> (wave-leaf fig) [flowers], <s>Vaiśya</s>s are afflicted; with the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan), the <s>Dasyu</s>s (barbarians) likewise.

body.text: (AVParis_71,16.2) śvetam indrāyudhaṃ viprān raktaṃ kṣatriyanāśanam | vaiśyānāṃ pītakaṃ rātrau kṛṣṇaṃ śūdravināśanam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.16.2) A white rainbow [portends danger to] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; a red one, destruction of <s>Kṣatriya</s>s; for <s>Vaiśya</s>s, a yellow one at night; a dark one, destruction of <s>Śūdra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_71,16.3) nirghāte bhūmikampe ca caityaśuṣkavirohaṇe | deśapīḍāṃ vijānīyāt pradhānaś cātra vadhyate ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.16.3) In the event of thunderclaps, earthquakes, or the sprouting of a withered sacred tree — one should know affliction to the region, and a prominent person is slain there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,16.4) indrayaṣṭir bhajyate vā viśasto vā paśur vrajet | yadā tadā vijānīyād rājñaḥ pīḍām upasthitām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.16.4) When <s>Indra</s>'s staff is broken, or a slaughtered animal moves — then one should know that affliction for the king is imminent.

body.text: (AVParis_71,16.5) pitāmahe vāsudeve somadharmāryameṣv api | nimittam aśubhaṃ yatra brāhmaṇānāṃ bhayāvaham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.16.5) In [the images of] the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Aryaman</s> — where an inauspicious portent [appears], it portends fear for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.1) bṛhaspatau vā śukre vā pāvake pākaśāsane | yāni rūpāṇi dṛśyante vidyāt tāni purohite ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.1) In [the images of] <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire), or <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — whatever forms are seen, one should know [they pertain to] the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest).

body.text:
(AVParis_71,17.2) mahādeve kubere ca tathā skandaviśākhayoḥ | nimittaṃ tat pārthiveṣu vijñeyaṃ saṃpravartitam || [akasmād dṛśyate yat tu nimittaṃ saṃprakīrtitam ||]
(AVParis_71,17.3) devānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca ratho yatra nimajjati | bhayaṃ tatra vijānīyāt pārthivasyāśuradbhutam ||
body.translated_text:
(AVParis 71.17.2) In [the images of] <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and likewise <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Viśākha</s> — that portent should be understood as pertaining to kings. [Whatever portent is seen suddenly — that is declared.]
(AVParis 71.17.3) Wherever the chariot of gods or kings sinks — there one should know a swift and terrible danger for the king.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.4) some ca vāsudeve ca varuṇe pākaśāsane | yad bhayaṃ dṛśyate tadd hi jñeyaṃ bhāṇḍādhike kane ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.4) In [the images of] <s>Soma</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — whatever danger is seen, that should be known as [pertaining to] the treasurer.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.5) vāte prājāpatau caiva viśvakarmaṇi caiva hi | pravartate yan nimittaṃ taj jānapadikaṃ bhavet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.5) In [the images of] <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Prājāpati</s>, and <s>Viśvakarman</s> — whatever portent arises, that pertains to the people of the province.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.6) kumārīṣu kumārīṇāṃ kumārāṇāṃ kumārajam | tathā preṣyeṣu sarveṣu kalpayec chāstrataḥ phalam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.6) Among maidens, [the portent pertains to] maidens; among boys, to boys; and among all servants, one should determine the result according to the <s>śāstra</s>s.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.7) indrāṇi varuṇānī ca bhadrakālī mahābalā | vīramātā ca yad brūyus tad rājamahiṣībhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.7) What <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Varuṇānī</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s> the mighty, and <s>Vīramātā</s> (Mother of Heroes) declare — that [portends] danger to the chief queen.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.8) ekaivāsāṃ tathā cānyā yāś cānyā devatāḥ striyaḥ | kuryur nimittaṃ tat strīṇāṃ pradhānānāṃ ca nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.8) [Whether] one alone of these, or another, and whatever other female deities — if they produce a portent, one should predict [danger] for prominent women.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.9) gandharveṣu nimittaṃ yat tad anyeṣu pradṛśyate | senāpatīnāṃ bhayakṛt sacivānāṃ bhayāya ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.9) Whatever portent [appears] among <s>Gandharva</s>s — that is seen to manifest in others; it causes fear for army commanders and portends danger for ministers.

body.text: (AVParis_71,17.10) rakṣapannagayakṣeṣu liṅgasyāyataneṣu ca | yathārūpaṃ yathākarma puruṣeṣu vyavasthitam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.17.10) Among <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, <s>Nāga</s>s (serpent-beings), and <s>Yakṣa</s>s, and in <s>liṅga</s>s and temples — according to [their] form and function, [the portent] is determined [to apply] to the corresponding persons.

body.text: (AVParis_71,18.1) dakṣiṇeṣu śarīreṣu devatānāṃ ca veśmasu | sarveṣv aṅgeṣu nārīṇāṃ tulyaṃ syād ubhayor bhayam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.18.1) On the right sides of the bodies of the deities and in their abodes; on all limbs of women — the danger would be equal for both.

body.text: (AVParis_71,18.2) svaśarīre yathotpātā vihitā daivacintakaiḥ | tathaiva parisaṃkhyeyaṃ sarvatraiva śubhāśubham ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.18.2) Just as portents upon one's own body have been prescribed by the diviners, so too should the auspicious and inauspicious be reckoned everywhere.

body.text: (AVParis_71,18.3) māṇibhadrādayo yakṣā gandharvāś citrasenayaḥ | tadbhayaṃ tu pradhānānām amātyānāṃ vibhāvayet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.18.3) <s>Māṇibhadra</s> and other <s>Yakṣa</s>s, and <s>Gandharva</s>s [led by] <s>Citrasena</s> — their [portents indicate] danger for the prominent ones and ministers, one should discern.

body.text: (AVParis_71,18.4) yeṣu deśeṣu dṛśyeta daivateṣu śubhāśubham | te ca deśā vinaśyanti rājā vātha vinaśyati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.18.4) In whichever regions auspicious or inauspicious [signs] are seen upon the deities — those regions perish, or the king himself perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_71,18.5) brāhmaṇā yatra vadhyante grāme rāṣṭre 'tha vā pure | rājadhānīṣu vā yatra tad abhāvasya lakṣaṇam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.18.5) Where <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s are slain — in a village, kingdom, or city, or in royal capitals — that is the sign of ruin.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.1) yatrābalaṃ vadhyamānaṃ rājā naivābhirakṣati | tatra daivakṛto daṇḍo nipataty āśu rājani ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.1) Where the king does not protect the weak who are being killed — there the divinely ordained punishment swiftly falls upon the king.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.2) chattradhvajapatākāsu devasthāne gṛheṣu ca | dvārāṭṭālaka^harmyeṣu [kārayedd homavācanam] ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.2) Upon umbrellas, banners, and flags, in temples and houses, at doorways, watchtowers, and mansions — [one should have] oblations and recitations performed.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.3) yatra prakṛtibhūtāni liṅgāni vikṛtāni ca | devatāś cāpi nadyaś ca kṣarakṣāmamahīruhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.3) Where the natural forms, the <s>liṅga</s>s, are distorted, and the deities, rivers, and withered, barren trees [also],

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.4) senā caiva na dṛśyeta hastyaśvaiś ca padātibhiḥ | hīnāṅgā vikṛtāṅgā vā pralayaṃ tatra nirdiśet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.4) And where the army with elephants, horses, and infantry is not seen; or [beings] with deficient or distorted limbs [appear] — one should predict dissolution there.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.5) stambhavṛkṣā dhvajā yatra sraveyū rudhirāmbu ca | dhūmayeyur jvaleyur vā mantriṇāṃ tatra vai vadhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.5) Where pillars, trees, and banners exude blood and water, or smoke, or blaze — there indeed the ministers are slain.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.6) jagatsvāmini jānīyād yadi ced divi jāyate | āntarikṣaṃ tu deśe syād bhaumaṃ sasyopatiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.6) If [the portent] arises in the sky, one should know [it pertains to] the Lord of the World; if in the atmosphere, it pertains to the region; if terrestrial, it affects the crops.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.7) bhāryāyāṃ vāhane putre kośe senāpatau pure | purohite narendre vā patate daivam aṣṭadhā ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.7) Upon the wife, vehicle, son, treasury, army commander, city, <s>purohita</s> (royal priest), or king — the divine [portent] falls in eight ways.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.8) māhendrīm amṛtāṃ raudrīṃ vaiśvadevīm athāpi vā | utpāteṣu mahāśāntiṃ kārayed bahudakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.8) The <s>Māhendrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>), <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal), <s>Raudrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Rudra</s>), or <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (pertaining to All-Gods) — for portents, one should have the great pacificatory rite performed with abundant gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_71,19.9) śāmyanti yena ghorāṇi yogakṣemaṃ ca jāyate | rājāno muditās tatra pālayanti vasuṃdharām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 71.19.9) By which terrible [portents] are pacified and well-being arises — kings, delighted there, protect the earth.

body.text:
(Pariśiṣṭa_72. mahādbhutāni)
(AVParis_72,1.1) atha mahādbhutāni vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
(<s>Pariśiṣṭa</s> 72: Great Portents)
(AVParis 72.1.1) Now we shall explain the great portents.

body.text:
(AVParis_72,1.2) kṣipravipākīny amoghāni ghorāṇi grahopahatam ulkābhihataṃ grastaṃ nirastam upadhūpitaṃ vā yadā syāj janmanakṣatraṃ karmanakṣatram abhiṣecanīyajanapadanakṣatram
(AVParis_72,1.3) eteṣu kṣipram eva mahāśāntim amṛtāṃ kārayed rājāṣṭame ca candramasaḥ sthāne <vajre> ca devopasṛṣṭe skambhe vā

children.text: (AVParis_72,1.4) atha vā nānāvarṇe bahurūpe śṛṅgiṇi cāditye kīlavati c[ādbhutāny] ulkābhihate
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.1.4) Or when the sun has multiple colors, many forms, or horns, or has a spike — [these are] portents — [also] when struck by a meteor,

children.text: (AVParis_72,1.5) kacandha eva niśvasati hasati bhramati
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.1.5) When a headless torso breathes, laughs, or wanders about,

children.text: (AVParis_72,1.6) hāse bhāse nāde śabde vāsane ca vaiśvānare 'prajvalite 'ntarikṣe bhasmāsthyaśmāṅgārā vīthī cendradhanuṣi rātrau vīdhra eva tu ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.1.6) [Portents include:] laughter, radiance, rumbling, sounds, and smells; when the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (sacred fire) does not blaze; when ashes, bones, stones, and embers [fall] in the atmosphere; the Milky Way [appearing] as a rainbow at night; and a clear [sky appearing otherwise].

body.translated_text:
(AVParis 72.1.2) [These are] swift in ripening, infallible, and terrible — when the birth-constellation, the action-constellation, or the consecration-constellation of a province is struck by a planet, hit by a meteor, eclipsed, cast down, or obscured.
(AVParis 72.1.3) In these [cases], the king should quickly have the great <s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal) pacificatory rite performed, also in the eighth station of the moon, and when the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) or the divine pillar is afflicted.

body.text:
(AVParis_72,2.1) candrārkau yasya rāṣṭre pariviṣyetātāṃ tān vipakṣān parolakasaṃsthāñ janapadāṃs
(AVParis_72,2.2) tathaiva kākakapotakaṅkagṛdhrayakṣarākṣasapiśācaśvāpadeṣu naktaṃ vadatsv abhivadatsu gāyatsu rāyatsu vā cakradhvajaveśmāvasathaprāsādāgre
(AVParis_72,2.3) vāpīkūpa udapāne codgirati nadati vidyotati vā
(AVParis_72,2.4) rathayantravāraṇapravahaṇavāditrādiṣūlkādayo 'ṅgārā dhūmo 'rcir vā prādurbhāve
(AVParis_72,2.5) liṅgaṃ viliṅge rājñaḥ
(AVParis_72,2.6) kālolūkakṛkalāsaśyenanipatite rājachattre bhagne dhvaje cakrasya rājño daṇḍe rājñaś ca dante

children.text: (AVParis_72,2.7) hastinyāṃ ca mattāyāṃ grāme ca prasūtāyām
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.2.7) And when a cow-elephant in musth [gives birth], or [gives birth] in a village;

children.text: (AVParis_72,2.8) rājarathaś ca rājādhirūḍho bhagnākṣaḥ saptarātrād rājño hanti purohitam amātyaṃ senāpatiṃ jāyāṃ hastinaṃ mahiṣīṃ kumāraṃ rājānam eva vā ṛdhnuyād ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.2.8) And when the king's chariot, with the king mounted upon it, has its axle broken — within seven nights it strikes the king's <s>purohita</s>, minister, army commander, wife, elephant, chief queen, prince, or the king himself. He who knows thus succeeds.

children.text: (AVParis_72,2.9) dvādaśaṃ śataṃ gavāṃ dhenūnāṃ kaṃsavasanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ niṣko 'śva etāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.2.9) Twelve hundred milch cows, a bronze vessel, gold, a <s>niṣka</s> (gold coin), a horse — these are the [ritual] gifts.

body.text: (AVParis_72,3.1) nānutpanneṣu daiveṣu rājñāṃ śāntir vidhīyate | asthāneṣu kṛtā śāntir nimittāyopapadyate | tasmāt sthānaṃ samuddiśya kārayec chāntim ātmanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.3.1) Pacificatory rites for kings should not be performed when divine [portents] have not arisen; a pacification performed in wrong circumstances becomes the cause of [further] portents; therefore, having identified the [correct] circumstance, one should have the pacificatory rite performed for oneself.

body.text:
(AVParis_72,3.2) sarpasamitau vāyusaṃbhrame udakaprādurbhāvagamaneṣu
(AVParis_72,3.3) dhanuḥsaṃdhyolkāpariveṣavidyuddaṇḍāśaniparighaparidhinirghāte
(AVParis_72,3.4) rajovarṣam upalavarṣaṃ dadhimadhughṛtakṣīravarṣaṃ majjārudhira<varṣam> varṣati
(AVParis_72,3.5) hīnagabhastī dve mārge vīthyau vittakṣaye somasya kṣaye 'pūrṇapūraṇe kṣayasyāvabhāsāḥ sadyo 'pararātrād digdāhopadhūpanam
(AVParis_72,3.6) grahavaiṣamyam ārohaṇam ākramaṇaṃ gandharvanagaraṃ mārutaprakopas tithikaraṇamuhūrtanakṣatragrahādīnāṃ somaviyogaḥ
(AVParis_72,3.7) pratisrotogāminyo nadyaḥ prāsādatoraṇadhvajeṣu vāyasasamavāyā vṛkaśakaṭārohaṇaṃ vṛṣadaṃśātimārjanam ulūkapratigarjanaṃ śyenagṛdhrādīnāṃ dhvajābhilapanam
(AVParis_72,3.8) vikṛtāś ca mānuṣāmānuṣaprabhavāḥ strībālavṛddhapralāpāḥ pradīptendrayaṣṭipādabhagne 'dravyeṣv ekavṛkṣe dvichāye pratichāye parivṛktam
(AVParis_72,3.9) ata ūrdhvam [chāyo] 'kasmāc caityavṛkṣastambhapatane virohatsv aviroheṣv achinnaparṇaprapātāc chuṣkaśākhino drumā dhūmarajodakaprādurbhāvagamaneṣu vanaspatiṣu
(AVParis_72,3.10) bahuśastrabhaṅga indrakīlagopurāṭṭālakadhvajādīnāṃ bhaṅga ucitānāṃ vyucchedane 'nucitānāṃ pravardhane dṛḍhabhaṅgesu
(AVParis_72,3.11) śuṣkavirohe gṛhe valmīke śayanadeśe darhastambotpattau mitravirodhe 'mitraprītau ca devatārcayo tathachedane
(AVParis_72,3.12) yatra rājāprasādamukhaḥ paureṣu ca bhṛtyādiṣu bhavati bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
(AVParis_72,3.13) yadā tu pratipat somo vikṛtyā vikṛto bhavet | anudbhinno vilūno vā rājño maraṇam ādiśet ||
(AVParis_72,3.14) āyudhākārarūpāṇi śvetavarṇākṛtīni ca | pañcavarṇāni cābhrāṇi tathā daṇḍanibhāni ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.3.14) Clouds having the appearance and form of weapons, or white-colored shapes, or five-colored [clouds], and likewise those resembling staffs —

body.text: (AVParis_72,3.15) yadā candrārkayor madhye kṛṣṇaṃ bhavati maṇḍalam | sa śaṅkur iti vijñeyo grahaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.3.15) When a dark circle appears between the moon and the sun, that is to be known as the <s>Śaṅku</s> (peg) — a planet of utmost ferocity.

body.text: (AVParis_72,3.16) tatra rājño vadhaṃ vidyāt sarvabhūtabhayāvaham | tatra kuryān mahāśāntim amṛtāṃ viśvabheṣajīm iti ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.3.16) There one should know the death of the king, [which is] fear-inspiring to all beings; there one should perform the great pacificatory rite, the immortal, universal remedy.

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.1) atha yasminn eva janapade gobrāhmaṇasūtasāṃvatsaravaidyānāṃ parivrājakacāraṇavānaprasthabrahmacāriṇāṃ vāpi saṃkaraḥ pravartate tad adbhutaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.1) Now, in whatever region the intermixing of cows, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>Sūta</s>s, astrologers, physicians, wandering ascetics, bards, forest-hermits, and celibate students takes place — that one should know as a portent.

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.2) karmasaṃkaraṃ yajñasaṃkaraṃ vyavahārasaṃkaraṃ ca yatra ca dharmo 'dharmeṣa pīḍyate tad adbhutaṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.2) Where there is intermixing of rituals, intermixing of sacrifices, and intermixing of customary practices, and where <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) is oppressed by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) — that one should know as a portent.

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.3) teṣām ajñātaprāyaścittaṃ yad ajñātam anāmnātam iti madhye juhuyāt puruṣasūktaṃ ca teṣv akṛtaprāyaścitteṣu mahādbhutāni prādurbhavanti ||
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.3) For them the expiation for the unknown — that which is unknown and not handed down by tradition — one should offer into the midst [of the fire] the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>; in those [cases] where expiation has not been performed, great portents manifest.

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.4) divyānīty ācakṣate devagṛheṣv atha hasanti gāyanti rudanti krośanti prasvidyanti pradhūmāyanti prajvalanti prakampanty unmīlayanti nimīlayanti lihitaṃ sravanti parivartayanti vā
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.4) They are called 'divine' — in the temples of the gods: when [images] laugh, sing, weep, cry out, sweat, emit smoke, blaze, tremble, open their eyes, close their eyes, shed fluid when scratched, or turn around —

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.5) teṣām prādurbhāvagamaneṣv anyarājāgamanaṃ vā vidyād udagraṃ vā[ṅgegam] avṛṣṭiśastrabhayaṃ bubhukṣāmāraṃ jānapadam amātyānāṃ rājño vināśam
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.5) At their appearance and disappearance, one should know [it portends] the coming of another king, or uprising, or danger from drought, weapons, famine, plague — regional [calamity], destruction of ministers, and of the king.

children.text: (AVParis_72,4.6) teṣu sarveṣu bhṛgvaṅgirovidam ity uktaṃ sa catuṣpatha īśānaṃ prapadyeta || oṃ prapadye bhūḥ prapadye bhuvaḥ prapadye svaḥ prapadye janat prapadya iti prapadyeta
children.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.6) In all these [cases], what was declared by <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> [applies]: at a crossroads one should surrender to <s>Īśāna</s>: 'Oṃ, I take refuge in <s>Bhūḥ</s>, I take refuge in <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, I take refuge in <s>Svaḥ</s>, I take refuge in <s>Janat</s>' — thus one should take refuge.

body.text: (AVParis_72,4.7) kapilānām aṣṭaśatasya kṣīreṇa pāyasaṃ śrapayitvā kapilāsv alabhyamānāsu dogdhrīṇāṃ śatasya kṣīreṇa pāyasaṃ śarapayitvā prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāya paristīrya barhī raudreṇa gaṇena śāntā juhuyāt || sarpir juhuyāt pāyasaṃ juhuyāc chuklāḥ sumanasa upahared brāhmaṇān bhaktenopepasanti tā eva gā dadyād rājyaṃ vā parimitakālaṃ tasya parituṣṭaye gosahasraṃ kartre dadyād grāmavaraṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.4.7) Having prepared <s>pāyasa</s> (rice pudding) with the milk of eight hundred tawny cows — and if tawny ones are unavailable, with the milk of a hundred milch cows — having placed the fuel-wood facing east and spread the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), one should offer oblations, pacified, with the <s>Raudra gaṇa</s> [hymns]; one should offer <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter), offer <s>pāyasa</s>, present white flowers, and feast <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s with food. Those very cows should be given [as gifts], or the kingdom for a limited period, for his [the priest's] satisfaction; one should give a thousand cows and an excellent village to the performer.

body.text: (AVParis_72,5.1) atha yatraitac chayane vātha vastre vā jāyate yad dhutāśanaḥ | etad atyadbhutaṃ nāma sarvakṣayakaraṃ nṛṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.5.1) Now, wherever on a bed or on a garment this [fire] arises — that which is the devourer [fire] — this is called the 'supremely wondrous' portent, causing the destruction of all for people.

body.text: (AVParis_72,5.2) atra brāhmīṃ mahāśāntiṃ kārayed bahudakṣiṇām | bahvannāṃ bahusaṃbhārām anūcānasudakṣiṇām | rājyakāmo 'rthakāmo vā pūjayet tu bṛhaspatim ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.5.2) Here one should have the great <s>Brāhmī</s> pacificatory rite performed, with abundant <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (gifts), with abundant food and many provisions, with proper fees for the learned; one who desires sovereignty or wealth should worship <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

body.text: (AVParis_72,5.3) sṛjanti devā divyādbhutāni prāg upasargāt pratibodhanārtham | kāryāṇi vighnāni tathā janānāṃ karmākule varṇasamākule ca ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.5.3) The gods send forth divine portents prior to calamity, for the purpose of awakening; likewise obstacles to the undertakings of people, when actions are confused and classes are intermixed.

body.text: (AVParis_72,5.4) daivyopasṛṣṭena balena kāryaṃ kārya ca śāntiḥ praṇipatya devān | tatopasargād vighnāt pramucyate divi ced aniṣṭaṃ na punaḥ sa kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.5.4) The task should be accomplished through the power sent by the gods, and pacification should be performed, bowing to the deities; then one is freed from calamity and obstruction, and if there is misfortune in the heavens, may it not recur.

body.text: (AVParis_72,5.5) pṛthivyām antarikṣe ca divi cāpy upalakṣayet | ceṣṭitaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ rutaṃ ca mṛgapakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.5.5) On the earth, in the atmosphere, and in the sky one should observe the movements of all beings and the cries of animals and birds.

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.1) grāme kule vā yadi vāpi deśe rājany amātyeṣu tathā dvijeṣu | bhāvaḥ paśūnāṃ vikṛto virūpas tad adbhutaṃ tasya deśasya vidyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.1) In a village, family, or in a region, among the king, ministers, or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s — if the condition of cattle is distorted and deformed, one should know that as a portent for that region.

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.2) amātyabhedo vividhaikaśīrṣa ekadviśīrṣe bhavati dvirājyam | apādahaste mriyate hy amātyo jāte kavandhe nṛpatir vinaśyet ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.2) An anomaly among ministers: [a child born] with a single head of various [forms], or with one or two heads — [the latter portends] dual sovereignty; one born without hands or feet — the minister dies; when a headless trunk is born, the king perishes.

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.3) yadādhikāṅgo yadi vāṅgahīno bhavet paśūnāṃ vikṛto virūpaḥ | strīṇāṃ tathaiva vikṛto virūpas tad adbhutaṃ tasya deśasya vidyāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.3) When [an offspring] has excess limbs or is deficient in limbs, when cattle are distorted and deformed, when women likewise [give birth to] distorted and deformed [offspring] — one should know that as a portent for that region.

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.4) anāsyaṃ vāpy anoṣṭhaṃ vā jāyate ced vidūlakam | arūpam asarūpaṃ vā jāyate ced vidūlakam ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.4) If a kitten is born without a mouth, or without lips, or formless, or of wrong form —

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.5) adharādīnn acakṣur vā jāyate ced vidūlakam | etad atyadbhutaṃ nāma rāṣṭre rājyakṣayamkaram ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.5) If a kitten is born with a lower [jaw deformity], or without eyes — this is called the 'supremely wondrous' portent, causing the destruction of the kingdom in the realm.

body.text: (AVParis_72,6.6) tam adbhiḥ snātaṃ surabhiṃ sugandhiṃ gatāsum agnau juhuyād ghṛtāktam | ganeṇa raudreṇa ghṛtaṃ ca hutvā tathā mahātmā śivam asya kuryāt ||
body.translated_text: (AVParis 72.6.6) That [creature], bathed with water, made fragrant and sweet-smelling, lifeless, smeared with <s>ghṛta</s>, should be offered into the fire; having offered <s>ghṛta</s> with the <s>Raudra gaṇa</s> [hymns], the great-souled one should thus make auspiciousness for him.
